entry.summary: This paper analyzes whether aggregate spectral invariants can accelerate continuous subgraph matching over dynamic graphs, proving that lazily-maintained spectral bounds lose pruning power within four touching updates while exact maintenance is affordable when selective, and proposes a dynamic spectral index. It matters for the theory and practice of efficient pattern matching in evolving graph databases.

entry.title: Accuracy and Satisfaction in Multi-Turn LLM Dialogues for NFR Assessment

author.name: Ali Pourghasemi Fatideh, Wilder Baldwin, Maria Dhakal, Collin McMillan, Sepideh Ghanavati

entry.summary: This paper investigates accuracy and conversational quality of multi-turn LLM dialogues for assessing software non-functional requirements (NFRs), which are vague and context-dependent, going beyond single-turn functional correctness benchmarks. It matters because current evaluation benchmarks for developer assistants ignore the multi-turn collaborative reasoning needed for NFR assessment.

entry.title: RAVEN: A Regime-Aware Variable-context Expert Network for Financial Time Series Forecasting

author.name: Cheng He, Zhenyu Guan, Xijie Liang, Defu Lian, Jiajia Li, Enhong Chen, Patrick P. C. Lee, Geng Hu, Zehao Chen

entry.summary: Proposes RAVEN, a regime-aware mixture-of-experts framework for financial time series forecasting that adaptively determines the optimal look-back context per sample using nested contiguous windows. Addresses the mismatch between fixed context windows and non-stationary price processes.

entry.title: Zero-Shot Test-Time Canonicalization using Out-of-Distribution Scoring

author.name: Dominik Lindner, Johann Schmidt, Tom Siegl, Martin Becker, Sebastian Stober

entry.summary: Reframes test-time canonicalization for affine-robust classification as out-of-distribution scoring, undoing input transformations to map to a canonical form without retraining the classifier. Explores the previously unexamined design space of scoring functions and optimizers.

entry.title: Does My Embedding Reflect That $A = B$? Evaluating Mathematical Equivalence in Embedding Models

author.name: Jiaying Ye, Samarth Rao, Leo Carlin, Kedar Chintalapati, Saharsh Bhargava, Rachit Jaiswal, Michael Zhou, Jared Darlington, Jarod Alper, Vasily Ilin, Henry Kvinge

entry.summary: Introduces the MELD dataset of mathematically equivalent but lexically different statement pairs to test whether embedding models capture mathematical equivalence across subfields and formalisms. Motivated by the need to navigate between mathematical languages such as Lean and natural language.

entry.title: Sentence-Level Contextual Entrainment in Large Language Models

author.name: Yang Liu, Chenhui Chu

entry.summary: Extends the phenomenon of contextual entrainment in LLMs from the token level to the sentence level, showing across 26 models and two datasets that sentences in the prompt (even counterfactual ones) significantly increase their own probability during generation. Provides insight into how context biases model outputs.

entry.title: AVOC: Enhancing Hour-Level Audio-Video Understanding in Omni-Modal LLMs via Retrieval-Inspired Token Compression

author.name: Yijing Chen, Wenhui Tan, Xiaoyi Yu, Yuyue Wang, Xin Cheng, Kaisi Guan, Hao Jiang, Xiangyang Li, Guojie Zhu, Ruihua Song

entry.summary: Proposes AVOC, a framework for hour-level audio-video understanding in omni-modal LLMs that reframes multimodal token compression as a top-K retrieval problem, retrieving a compact query-relevant token subset within a fixed context budget. Draws on classical information-retrieval criteria for token selection.

entry.title: OmniPath: A Multi-Modal Agentic Framework for Auditing Wheelchair Accessibility

author.name: ASM Mobarak Hossain, Nadim Mahmud, Vaskar Raychoudhury, Md Osman Gani

entry.summary: OmniPath is a multimodal agentic system that fuses OpenStreetMap topology with high-density aerial LiDAR to virtually audit pedestrian path accessibility for wheelchair users in 0.5-meter increments. It matters for proactive accessibility mapping that conveys how a path physically feels to travel rather than just where it exists.

entry.title: Cost-Optimal Decision Diagrams for Stochastic Boolean Function Evaluation

author.name: Xia Zong, Tuomo Lehtonen, Jussi Rintanen

entry.summary: This paper presents the first practical exact branch-and-bound algorithm for constructing cost-optimal deterministic evaluation strategies for stochastic Boolean function evaluation under variable acquisition costs and a probability distribution over truth assignments. It matters for cost-sensitive decision-making such as medical diagnosis where acquiring each piece of information has different cost.

entry.title: A Survey on Federated Causal Discovery and Inference

author.name: Xianjie Guo, Yuwei Wang, Guodu Xiang, Xiaoli Tang, Kui Yu, Han Yu, Qiang Yang

entry.summary: Provides a systematic survey of federated causal discovery and inference, organizing the emerging field through a multi-dimensional taxonomy. Addresses privacy-preserving collaborative causal analysis across distributed institutions.

entry.title: From Spatial to Spectral: An Efficient, Frequency-Guided Feature Representation Learner for Small Object Detection

author.name: Yuhan Rui, Shihan Qiao, Yibin Lou, Mingxi Yu, Yutong Wan, Yanqiao Chen, Dongsheng Hou, Zhen Cao, Athena Zhuoming Zhong, Qi Hao

entry.summary: Proposes a frequency-guided feature representation framework that shifts small object detection from spatial to spectral processing, recovering fragile high-frequency cues without expensive upscaling. Generalizes across CNN and Transformer detectors.

entry.title: Blockwise Policy-Drift Gating for On-Policy Distillation

author.name: Liwen Zheng, Haiyun Jiang

entry.summary: Introduces blockwise policy-drift gating, a lightweight student-only drift controller for on-policy distillation under rollout reuse. Reweights position losses based on log-probability shifts without changing teacher targets.

entry.title: Inclusive Interactive Collisions for Multi-View Consistent Compositional 3D Generation

author.name: Chang Liu, Mingwen Shao, Xiang Lv, Xinyuan Chen, Lingzhuang Meng, Qiao Zhang, Zhengyi Gong, Jinghao Hu

entry.summary: Proposes I2C-3D, an optimization-based method for multi-view consistent compositional 3D generation that models reasonable interactions between Gaussian primitives and reduces cross-view hallucinations from Score Distillation Sampling. Addresses multi-object 3D asset generation.

entry.title: Average Rankings Mask Per-Subject Optimality: A Friedman-Nemenyi Benchmark of EEG Motor-Imagery BCI Decoders

author.name: Xavier Vasques, Paul Barbaste, Olivier Oullier

entry.summary: This benchmark study evaluates 1,056 EEG motor-imagery BCI decoding configurations across three datasets using Friedman-Nemenyi statistical testing, showing that average rankings mask per-subject optimality. It challenges the common claim that any single decoding pipeline is broadly preferable.

entry.title: FlowPipe: LLM-Enhanced Conditional Generative Flow Networks for Data Preparation Pipeline Construction

author.name: Kunyu Ni, Lei Cao, Jie He, Xiaotong Zhang, Jianfeng Jin, Junyu Dong, Yanwei Yu

entry.summary: FlowPipe formulates automated data preparation pipeline construction as conditional generative flow network sampling enhanced by LLMs, addressing weak credit assignment, poor dataset context injection, and inefficient exploration in prior Multi-DQN methods. It targets the combinatorial difficulty of synthesizing cleaning and feature transformation operator sequences.

entry.title: Reconstructing GRACE Terrestrial Water Storage with Spatio-Temporal Graph Neural Networks: An Application to South America

author.name: Lukas Arzoumanidis, Lara Johannsen, Klara Middendorf, Annette Eicker, Youness Dehbi

entry.summary: This work reconstructs monthly GRACE-like terrestrial water storage anomalies back to 1940 over South America using spatio-temporal graph neural networks learning from ERA5 meteorological forcing. It extends the short satellite record for climate-scale analyses beyond prior grid-cell regression and CNN approaches.

entry.title: DREG: A Layer-Wise Jacobian Regularization as a General-Purpose Penalty

author.name: Rowan Martnishn

entry.summary: DREG is a layer-wise Jacobian/derivative regularization penalty studied through a fully-crossed factorial sweep of 960 experiments across activations, regularizers, datasets, and seeds. It achieves the highest clean-regime accuracy among tested regularizers and ranks second in noise robustness behind spectral normalization.

entry.title: Learning the Koopman Operator using Attention Free Transformers

author.name: Mohammed Nagdi, Evangelos-Marios Nikolados, Alexey Yermakov, Mars Gao, Nathan Kutz, Filippo Menolascina

entry.summary: This work learns Koopman operators with autoencoders augmented by an attention-free latent memory block that aggregates a short window of past latents in linear time to correct drift in long-horizon rollouts. It improves robustness on systems with switching, continuous spectra, or strong transients.

entry.title: A Time-Reparameterized Cumulative Intensity Extrapolation Sampler for Discrete Flow Matching

author.name: Feiyang Fu, Hehe Fan

entry.summary: TR-CIE is a sampler for discrete flow matching that improves generation quality under limited function evaluations via schedule-based time reparameterization and cumulative intensity extrapolation. It targets efficient sampling beyond standard tau-leaping discretizations.

entry.title: Computational references are not experiments: pre-registered validation of machine-learned sodium-cathode voltages

author.name: Krishna Teja Vepa

entry.summary: A pre-registered validation study showing that ML screens for sodium-ion cathode voltages trained against computed references carry systematic errors that fail when checked against experiment-anchored values. Emphasizes rigorous pre-registration and documents how computational references differ from experiments.

entry.title: Autonomous Video Generation with Counterfactual Controllability for Self-Evolving World Models

author.name: Xin Wang, Wenxuan Liu, Tongtong Feng, Wenwu Zhu

entry.summary: Argues that video generation yields only a partial, implicit world model and proposes autonomous video generation with counterfactual controllability to identify which variables are controllable. Aims toward self-evolving world models that go beyond passive visual prediction.

entry.title: MotifGen: Spatiotemporal interpolation of misaligned satellite images via multi-source generative modeling, in an application to tropical cyclones

author.name: Cl\'ement Dauvilliers (Inria), Claire Monteleoni (Inria)

entry.summary: Introduces MotifGen, the first generative model for spatiotemporal interpolation of misaligned, irregularly-timed, multi-source satellite microwave imagery, applied to tropical cyclone monitoring. Handles heterogeneous instruments with varying characteristics that change across samples.

entry.title: EXPO-SQL: Execution-based Clause-level Policy Optimization for Text-to-SQL

author.name: Jaehoon Lee, CheolWon Na, Suyoung Bae, Jin-Seop Lee, Jihyung Lee, YunSeok Choi, Jee-Hyong Lee

entry.summary: Proposes EXPO-SQL, an execution-based clause-level policy optimization method for text-to-SQL that assigns fine-grained clause-level rewards by identifying erroneous clauses, rather than uniform query-level rewards. Provides denser learning signals for correct SQL generation.

entry.title: Beyond Logprobs: A Multi-Signal Confidence Engine for LLM-Based Document Field Extraction

author.name: Nitesh Kumar

entry.summary: Presents ExtractConf, a cross-domain field-agnostic confidence engine for LLM document field extraction, arguing that log-probabilities, verbalized confidence, and self-consistency all collapse to over-confidence at practical thresholds. Combines multiple signals to reliably separate trustworthy from untrustworthy extractions for automation-versus-review decisions.

entry.title: Prob-BBDM: a Probabilistic Brownian Bridge Diffusion Model for MRI sequence image-to-image translation

author.name: Martin Valls (UFR SFA), Pascal Bourdon (UFR SFA), Christine Fernandez-Maloigne (LabCom I3M), Guillaume Herpe (CHU Poitiers -- Radio, DACTIM-MIS), David Helbert (UFR SFA)

entry.summary: MVG-KAN is a multi-view geo-wind guided Kolmogorov-Arnold Network for short-term PM2.5 forecasting that incorporates wind-direction-dependent pollutant transport beyond distance-only or correlation-based graphs. It matters for public health protection and air-quality early warning given the complex coupled factors driving PM2.5 variation.

entry.title: Synergizing Physically Constrained MCMC and Chemical-Informed Gaussian Processes for Reaction Network Discovery

author.name: Runzhe Liu, Zihao Wang, Wenbo Yang, Shengyang Tao

entry.summary: Combines physically constrained MCMC topology sampling with chemical-informed Gaussian processes to discover interpretable reaction networks from sparse, noisy time-series. Integrates conservation laws and thermodynamic screening into a gray-box workflow.

entry.title: Decentralized Coordination of Autonomous Traffic Through Advanced Air Mobility Corridors

author.name: Jasmine Jerry Aloor, Hamsa Balakrishnan

entry.summary: Shows that autonomous aircraft can learn to self-organize into corridor flows in decentralized settings for Advanced Air Mobility, contrary to the belief that corridor-based operations are inefficient without central management. Uses learning-based coordination for fixed-wing aircraft.

entry.title: RASC+: Retrieval-Constrained LLM Adjudication for Clinical Value Set Authoring

author.name: Sumit Mukherjee

entry.summary: Presents RASC+, a stage-wise retrieval-constrained LLM adjudication approach for clinical value set authoring, optimizing candidate-pool recall then constrained LLM selection. Improves on poorly suited zero-shot generation for large version-controlled clinical code systems.

entry.title: DynaWM: Dynamics-Aware Distillation with World Model and Momentum Targets for Smooth Locomotion over Continuous Stairs

author.name: Haidong Hou, Zhangguo Yu, Hengbo Qi, Jianlin Zhang

entry.summary: Proposes DynaWM, a dynamics-aware distillation framework using a world model regularizer and momentum target encoder for smooth bipedal-wheeled robot locomotion over continuous stairs. Enhances terrain geometry encoding and stabilizes knowledge transfer.

entry.title: Exact Schur-Sylvester Dimensionality Reductions for Non-Smooth Stochastic Complexity and Manifold Sampling

author.name: Trenton Lau, Gary P. T. Choi

entry.summary: This paper presents an exact, mathematically equivalent reformulation that bypasses cubic-scaling bottlenecks in computing the Normalized Maximum Likelihood codelength for non-smooth estimators like Lasso, using block Schur complement and Sylvester's determinant identity. It reduces complexity in manifold-constrained projection and volume integration for a geometric MCMC sampler.

entry.title: When Top-1 Fails: Calibrating LoRA Monitors for Masked Diffusion LMs

author.name: Lucky Verma, Pratik Yadav

entry.summary: This paper tests top-1 argmax concentration as a collapse-warning diagnostic during LoRA/PEFT fine-tuning of discrete diffusion language models, finding it fires for all 816 configurations while zero actual collapses occur, giving zero precision. It identifies pre-equilibrium saturation as the cause and evaluates max LoRA gradient norm as a better parameter-side signal.

entry.title: Hessian-augmented Supervised Learning for Hamilton-Jacobi-Bellman PDEs

author.name: Mat\'ias G\'omez-Aedo, Behzad Azmi, Yuyang Huang, Dante Kalise, Karl Kunisch

entry.summary: Develops a Hessian-augmented supervised learning method for approximating value functions in Hamilton-Jacobi-Bellman PDEs by generating training data of values, gradients, and Hessians via Pontryagin's principle and Riccati equations. The added derivative information substantially reduces sample complexity.

entry.title: Harmonic: Hierarchical State Space Models for Efficient Long-Context Language Modeling

author.name: Petr Nyoma

entry.summary: Presents Harmonic, a hierarchical state-space model stacking three recurrent levels at progressively slower timescales where each level receives prediction errors from below. Reports outperforming comparable Transformer and Mamba baselines on long-context language modeling and successful training at 64K tokens where baselines run out of memory.

entry.title: Measuring User's Mental Models of Speech Translation in Human-AI Collaboration

author.name: HyoJung Han, Nishant Balepur, Jordan Boyd-Graber, Marine Carpuat

entry.summary: Studies users' mental models of speech translation systems via a cross-lingual question-answering framework where users either accept MT output or request professional re-translation. Finds users develop stronger mental models with practice, especially with some source-language knowledge, predicting where systems are likely to fail.

entry.title: Tractable Reasoning and Conjunctive Query Answering for Defeasible DL-Lite under Rational Closure

author.name: Giovanni Casini (CNR - ISTI, University of Cape Town), Umberto Straccia (CNR - ISTI)

entry.summary: This paper studies reasoning under Rational Closure for the core and horn variants of the DL-Lite description logic family, providing a plug-in architecture over standard classical reasoners for instance checking and conjunctive query answering with minimal overhead. It matters for efficient non-monotonic reasoning over defeasible knowledge in lightweight ontologies.

entry.title: Matching Tasks to Objectives: Fine-Tuning and Prompt-Tuning Strategies for Encoder-Decoder Pre-trained Language Models

author.name: Ahmad Pouramini, Hesham Faili

entry.summary: This study explores how diverse pre-training objectives affect encoder-decoder language model performance on generation and question answering, introducing a Match Task to Objective (MTO) framework with automated methods to determine the appropriate objective and prepare task-related data for adaptation. It matters for aligning pre-training and fine-tuning objectives with downstream tasks like commonsense retrieval and completion.

entry.title: VeriPilot: An LLM-Powered Verilog Debugging Framework

author.name: Yihan Wang, Cheng Liu, Jiazheng Zhang, Lei Zhang, Long Cheng, Xiaowei Li, Huawei Li

entry.summary: Presents VeriPilot, an LLM-powered Verilog debugging framework using golden reference models to enable fine-grained fault localization beyond simple test-output feedback. Addresses long dependency chains in hardware code.

entry.title: Infinitesimal Causality

author.name: Sridhar Mahadevan

entry.summary: This paper introduces a categorical account of infinitesimal causality in Frobenius Markov categories with tangent-bundle semantics, treating interventions as tangent deformations of copy/discard structure. It defines categorical causal sufficiency through the compatibility of algebraic and geometric Frobenius structures.

entry.title: Task Decomposition for Efficient Annotation

author.name: Nupoor Gandhi, Emma Strubell

entry.summary: This paper proposes decomposing complex structured annotation tasks into subtasks distributed across heterogeneous annotators including models and humans, rather than end-to-end annotation by single annotators. It aims to make high-quality structured annotation more cost-efficient.

entry.title: Real vs. Complex Spectral Bases for Neural Operators: The Role of Green's Function Alignment

author.name: Jason Sulskis, Sathya Ravi

entry.summary: Introduces the Hartley Neural Operator (HNO), a real-valued counterpart to Fourier Neural Operators that uses the Discrete Hartley Transform to avoid complex arithmetic and conjugate-symmetry redundancy. Analyzes how spectral basis choice interacts with Green's function alignment for PDE solving.

entry.title: Difference-Making without Making a Difference

author.name: Sander Beckers

entry.summary: This philosophy-of-causation paper shows that Andreas and Gunther's most recent factual difference-making definition of actual causation instantiates all three of their supposedly competing account types, arguing these are distinctions without a difference and undermining all seven of their accounts. It matters for the foundations of causal reasoning by clarifying conceptual confusion in definitions of actual causation.

entry.title: Coordinate-Queryable Neural Field Reconstruction for EEG Spatial Super-Resolution with Unseen-Electrode Generation

author.name: Hongjun Liu, Leyu Zhou, Zijianghao Yang, Chao Yao

entry.summary: Reformulates EEG spatial super-resolution as learning a shared conditional scalp field via implicit neural representations, enabling robustness to random missing channels and generation of unseen electrode positions. Addresses brittleness of fixed channel-mapping methods.

entry.title: JupOtter: Cell-Level Bug Detection in Jupyter Notebooks

author.name: Lukas Ottenhof, Thibaud Lutellier

entry.summary: Presents JupOtter, a bug detection system for Jupyter Notebooks with notebook-specific tokenization, cell-level bug prediction, and a new 21,000-notebook labeled dataset. Targets the rising problem of buggy notebooks on platforms like GitHub.

entry.title: MedPCFM: Improving Medical Point Cloud Completion by Integrating Point Transformers and Flow Matching

author.name: Kamil Kwarciak, Marek Wodzinski

entry.summary: MedPCFM introduces a flow-matching approach backed by Point Transformer v3 for medical point cloud completion, used in anatomical reconstruction. It is evaluated on skull and mandibular defect datasets, achieving state-of-the-art generative completion performance.

entry.title: Beyond U-Net: A Latent-Representation-Aligned Skip-Free Backbone for Flow-Matching Speech Enhancement

author.name: Wangyi Pu, Michele Scarpiniti

entry.summary: This work proposes a skip-free encoder-decoder backbone for flow-matching speech enhancement guided by latent representation alignment, avoiding U-Net skip connections that may transfer noise-correlated features to the decoder. It aligns bottleneck and decoder representations with clean latent features.

entry.title: Flow-Corrected Thompson Sampling for Non-Stationary Contextual Bandits

author.name: AmirHossein Naghdi, Ali Baheri

entry.summary: Proposes Flow-Corrected Thompson Sampling for non-stationary linear contextual bandits, transporting past rewards to the present via an explicit drift model with confidence weights reflecting transport reliability. Handles linear drift, periodic variation, and regime switches in a unified template.

entry.title: EERLoss: A Novel Loss Function for Training Deep Biometric Models. A Case Study in Keystroke Dynamics

author.name: Nahuel Gonzalez, Marta Robledo-Moreno, Ivan DeAndres-Tame, Ruben Vera-Rodriguez, Ruben Tolosana

entry.summary: Introduces EERLoss, a subdifferentiable and arbitrarily accurate approximation to the Equal Error Rate for directly training deep biometric models, aligning the training objective with the evaluation metric. Validated on the challenging keystroke-dynamics verification task.

entry.title: Layer-wise Probing of wav2vec 2.0 and Whisper for Consonant Cluster Reduction in African American English

author.name: Hamid Mojarad, Kevin Tang

entry.summary: Conducts layer-wise probing of wav2vec2 and Whisper to study how consonant cluster reduction in African American English is represented, finding that reduced segments retain cues to their underlying cluster identity. Relevant to understanding ASR disparities affecting AAE speakers.

entry.title: Exploring Dualistic Meta-Learning to Enhance Domain Generalization in Open Set Scenarios

author.name: Xiran Wang, Jian Zhang, Lei Qi, Yang Gao, Yinghuan Shi

entry.summary: Proposes a dualistic meta-learning strategy (MEDIC) for open-set domain generalization that addresses the imbalance causing over-rejection of out-of-distribution data from known classes. Performs joint domain-class matching.

entry.title: Token Complexity of Certifying Stochastic-Oracle Reliability

author.name: Jie Wang

entry.summary: Develops certification token complexity, the minimum expected token cost to certify whether a stochastic oracle meets a target reliability level, building on the Stochastic-Oracle Turing Machine framework. Constructs an SPRT-based certification machine with controlled error probability.

entry.title: Structural Kolmogorov-Arnold Convolutions: Learnable Function on the Values or the Filter Shape as Parameter-Efficient Alternative to Per-Edge Convolutional KANs

author.name: Stefano Mereu, Oleksandr Kuznetsov, Gabriele Marchello, Alessandro Galdelli, Emanuele Frontoni, Adriano Mancini, Ferdinando Cannella

entry.summary: This work proposes structural Kolmogorov-Arnold convolutions that place learnable univariate functions in the convolution structure (on values or filter shape) rather than per-edge, offering a more parameter-efficient alternative to per-edge convolutional KANs. It explores three realizations along a single design axis.

entry.title: Paying to Know: Micro-Transaction Markets for Verified Product Information in Agentic E-Commerce

author.name: Filippos Ventirozos, Matthew Shardlow

entry.summary: This paper envisions agentic e-commerce as a micro-transaction market where buyer agents pay fractions of a cent to progressively unlock verified product information, arguing the bottleneck shifts from matching products to acquiring trustworthy decision-relevant data. It builds on emerging agent-native micro-payment rails like x402 and AP2.

entry.title: Federated Survival Analysis in Healthcare: A Multi-Model Evaluation on Cross-Institutional Heterogeneous Breast Cancer Data

author.name: Natalia Moreno-Blasco, Anusha Ihalapathirana, Pekka Siirtola, Miguel Fernandez-de-Retana

entry.summary: This paper systematically evaluates federated survival analysis on a cross-institutional, naturally heterogeneous breast cancer cohort, comparing Cox proportional hazards, DeepSurv, and other models under privacy-preserving federated learning. It examines effectiveness for time-to-event modeling under realistic data heterogeneity.

entry.title: A Physics-Informed Fourier-Wavelet Transformer for Multiscale Computational Fluid Dynamics Surrogate Modeling

author.name: Somyajit Chakraborty, Ming Pan, Xizhong Chen

entry.summary: Proposes a physics-informed Fourier-wavelet transformer for next-step velocity-field reconstruction in CFD surrogate modeling, combining hybrid spectral encoding with PDE-residual-biased self-attention and self-supervised physics pretraining. Targets better capture of localized multiscale flow structures.

entry.title: Dirac-Frenkel dynamics with inertia for nonlinearly parametrized solutions of evolution problems

author.name: Matteo Raviola, Benjamin Peherstorfer

entry.summary: Adds inertia to Dirac-Frenkel dynamics for nonlinearly parametrized evolution problems (e.g., neural networks, mixture models), preserving useful parameter-velocity information in weakly informed directions while following standard dynamics in well-informed ones. Proves well-posedness and provides a posteriori error bounds.

entry.title: Ground Then Rank: Revisiting Knowledge-Based VQA with Training-Free Entity Identification

author.name: Qian Ma, Qiong Wu, Zhengyi Zhou, Yao Ma

entry.summary: Revisits knowledge-based VQA with a training-free Ground-Then-Rank approach that separates entity-level identification from fact-level evidence ranking, rather than coupling them in a single re-ranking stage. Targets the entity and evidence grounding bottlenecks in multimodal RAG.

entry.title: Prague Dependency Treebank -- Consolidated 2.0: Enriching a Complex Annotation Scheme

author.name: Marie Mikulov\'a, Ji\v{r}\'i M\'irovsk\'y, Milan Straka, Pavl\'ina Synkov\'a, Jan \v{S}t\v{e}p\'anek, Barbora \v{S}t\v{e}p\'ankov\'a, Jan Haji\v{c}

entry.summary: Presents the second consolidated version of the Prague Dependency Treebank (PDT-C 2.0), a uniformly annotated nearly 4-million-token multi-layer Czech language resource with linked meaning representations, coreference, and discourse relations, plus compatible lexicons. Concludes a nearly 30-year resource-development project.

entry.title: BluTrain: A C++/CUDA Framework for AI Systems

author.name: Adhitya Charan, Adwaid Suresh, Anuj Kumar, Aparna A, Dhanakumar K, Dharun M S, Dinesh G, Goutham Kumar Reddy K, Harshini V M, Jenifa D, Jona Delcy C A, Kathirvel S, Killi Uma Maheswara Rao, Kiruthik Kanna M, Kurra Vishnu Sai, Madhumithaa G K, Navin Kumar V, Ram Charan Golla, Revathi T, Rishikkanth R, Sanjay Krishna M V, Surendra Vendra

entry.summary: BluTrain is a lightweight, architecture-general deep learning training framework built from first principles in standard C++ and core CUDA, implementing every layer natively to give absolute control over hardware expression while abstracting systems complexity. It matters because at scale, throughput, memory footprint, and numerical fidelity depend more on hardware expression than architecture.

entry.title: Event-Aligned Analysis of Multi-Rater Pain Assessments Using Continuous Wearable Physiology

author.name: Saba A. Farahani, Elahe Khatibi, Thomas D. Hughes, Ariana M. Nelson, Hung Cao, Amir M. Rahmani

entry.summary: Proposes a rater-aware, event-aligned framework for pain assessment that preserves the identity of different raters (patients, nurses, clinicians) rather than assuming a single ground truth. Aligns wearable physiology to pain-change events and finds rater-dependent physiological differences.

entry.title: Promise and challenges of heart chamber segmentation from non-contrast CT scans using contrastive unpaired image translation: a feasibility study

author.name: Jing Wang, Tong Yu, Hao-En Lu, Zixue Zeng, Joseph K. Leader, Xin Meng, Jianbing Zhu, Jiantao Pu

entry.summary: Develops ChameleonNet, using contrastive unpaired image translation to synthesize non-contrast CT from contrast CT, then trains segmentation of four heart chambers on synthetic images. Evaluates feasibility of heart chamber segmentation without contrast agents.

entry.title: Offline Reinforcement Learning for Warehouse SLAM Throughput Control

author.name: Tina Dongxu Li, Mouhacine Benosman, Rajat Kumar, Kevin Tan, Ken Meszaros, Trevor Dardik

entry.summary: Presents an algorithm-agnostic offline RL framework for optimizing SLAM throughput control in warehouse fulfillment, with history-informed state representation, action abstraction for delayed effects, and a reward capturing upstream and downstream metrics. Balances throughput with stability.

entry.title: RetiSEM: Generalising Causal Models for Fragmented Biomedical Data

author.name: Inam Ullah, Imran Razzak, Shoaib Jameel

entry.summary: RetiSEM is a domain-constrained structural equation modeling framework for causal graph recovery and mediation analysis on fragmented, incomplete biomedical data, organizing variables into biologically informed blocks with forbidden-edge constraints. It is evaluated on synthetic benchmarks and a real NHANES setting.

entry.title: Systematic Exploration of 4-Expert Heterogeneous Mixture-of-Experts via Automated Pipeline Search

author.name: Yashkumar R Lukhi, Harsh Rameshbhai Moradiya, Radu Timofte, Dmitry Ignatov

entry.summary: This work presents an automated large-scale search pipeline for heterogeneous 4-expert mixture-of-experts architectures within the LEMUR dataset ecosystem, replacing manual design with a deterministic code-assembly generator. A 28-day campaign generated 4,463 candidates with 1,021 evaluated, surfacing findings about heterogeneous MoE design.

entry.title: Constrained Variable Projection for Structured Problems

author.name: Emanuele Zangrando, Sara Venturini, Francesco Rinaldi, Francesco Tudisco

entry.summary: Develops a constrained variable-projection framework for separable nonlinear least-squares problems by casting it as bilevel optimization with convex constraints on the remaining variables. Derives exact reduced-gradient formulas compatible with automatic differentiation and a conditional-gradient algorithm.

entry.title: RE4: Transformation-aware Imitation of Object Interactions Using Manipulation Modes

author.name: Arsh Chawla, Rahul Shome

entry.summary: Presents RE4, a transformation-aware imitation learning framework for object-interaction tasks that repurposes principled manipulation theories (manipulation modes) to preserve both performance and interpretability. Uses lightweight self-supervised pose estimation from demonstration data.

entry.title: Same Lesson, Different Story: Cross-Lingual Reconstruction of Cultural Narratives in Large Language Models

author.name: Jory Alshaalan, Haya Albaker, Abeer Aldayel, Aljawharah Alabdullatif, Rehab Alahmadi

entry.summary: Introduces a multilingual narrative framework using 414 proverbs across 15 languages and four LLMs to generate 13k narratives, assessing whether models preserve culturally grounded meaning when equivalent moral lessons are conveyed through distinct cultural forms. Examines cross-lingual reconstruction of cultural narratives.

entry.title: Neuromorphic Speech Enhancement with Dual-Branch Spiking Neural Networks

author.name: Taiyu Meng, Wenbin Jiang, Haoyi Zhang, Yuhan Zhou, Haibing Yin

entry.summary: Proposes GSU-DBNet, a dual-branch spiking neural network with a gated spiking unit for energy-efficient neuromorphic speech enhancement. Jointly models magnitude and complex spectra to narrow the gap with ANN-based methods.

entry.title: Towards Version-aware Operations and Transaction Memories for Multi-layer MeMo

author.name: Peiran Li

entry.summary: Proposes a version-aware operation layer for MeMo multi-layer correlation matrix memory language models, compiling high-level operations like replace, rollback, and trace into MeMo-native primitives. Explores reducing retraining when knowledge changes by editing explicit memories.

entry.title: DTT-BSR+: A Generative-Regression Cascade for Music Source Restoration

author.name: Youran Ni, Shihong Tan, Yuzhu Wang, Gongping Huang

entry.summary: Proposes DTT-BSR+, a two-stage generative-regression cascade for music source restoration that decouples distribution fitting from signal reconstruction. Improves multi-mel SNR over single-stage approaches across all stems.

entry.title: Entity Resolution via Batched Oracle Queries

author.name: Lorenzo Balzotti, Donatella Firmani, Luca Gagliardelli, Giovanni Simonini

entry.summary: This paper formalizes batched entity resolution, where an oracle clusters only a limited batch of records at a time and no batch contains all records of an entity, proving optimal batch selection is NP-hard and giving an optimal solution under a natural condition. It evaluates a pay-as-you-go approach on six datasets.

entry.title: Toward Self-Evolution-Ready Workflow Harnesses: A Reversible Migration Path and Convertibility Taxonomy for Expert LLM Pipelines

author.name: Yimo Lin, Zhen Zhang, Yibin Li

entry.summary: This paper proposes a reversible Strangler-Fig migration path and a three-tier convertibility taxonomy to refactor static expert LLM-plus-script workflows into composable, typed, auditable, and self-evolving stages. It addresses the unsolved problem of migrating legacy production workflows toward adaptive agents.

entry.title: It's Complicated: On the Design and Evaluation of AI-Powered AAC Interfaces

author.name: Blade Frisch, Will Wade, Dylan Gaines, Michelle Kinsella, Betts Peters, Tamara Broderick, Keith Vertanen

entry.summary: This paper examines the complicated nature of designing and evaluating AI-powered augmentative and alternative communication interfaces, arguing current metrics fail to capture the intersectional and nuanced needs of users. It explores six AAC problem spaces and proposes more robust evaluation methods.

entry.title: PROTECT-90: A Fault Dataset for Power System Protection

author.name: Julian Oelhaf, Georg Kordowich, Christian Bergler, Andreas Maier, Johann J\"ager, Siming Bayer

entry.summary: Releases PROTECT-90, an open EMT-simulated benchmark of 9,022 short-circuit episodes on a standardized 90kV double-line topology with digital-fault-recorder-like measurements for power-system protection research. Fills a gap in standardized, reproducible high-voltage waveform datasets.

entry.title: L3Cube-MahaPOS: A Marathi Part-of-Speech Tagging Dataset and BERT Models

author.name: Hariom Ingle, Ronit Ghode, Ishwari Gondkar, Jidnyasa Harad, Raviraj Joshi

entry.summary: Introduces L3Cube-MahaPOS, a gold-standard manually annotated POS-tagging dataset of 32,354 Marathi sentences plus BERT models, addressing the lack of resources for this widely-spoken but under-resourced language. Tackles Marathi's rich morphology, free word order, and code-mixing challenges.

entry.title: From Task-Guided Conversational Graphs to Goal-Oriented Dialogue Runtimes

author.name: Mariano Garralda-Barrio

entry.summary: Introduces the Goal-Oriented Dialogue Runtime, a framework-neutral design pattern treating goals, lifecycle state, and resumption contracts as first-class runtime objects for conversations with interdependent objectives. Addresses conversational continuity in LLM workflows.

entry.title: End-to-End Radar and Communication Modulation Recognition with Neuromorphic Computing

author.name: Xiaohu Li, Chongxiao Qu, Caiyong Lin, Chenxiao Dou, Wei Hua

entry.summary: Proposes EMRFormer, an end-to-end spiking neural network with adaptive spike encoder and integer leaky integrate-and-fire neurons for energy-efficient radar and communication modulation recognition. Targets neuromorphic hardware constraints.

entry.title: Uniform Sampling from High-dimensional Spectral Norm Balls

author.name: Michael R. Metel

entry.summary: Proves that singular values of matrices sampled uniformly from the unit spectral norm ball converge to 1 almost surely as dimensions grow, justifying a simple sampling method for high-dimensional matrices. Motivated by ML optimization applications at LLM scale.

entry.title: Model selection with proper scoring rules on data sets of time series

author.name: Giorgio Corani, Stefano Damato, Dario Azzimonti, Lorenzo Zambon

entry.summary: Analyzes model selection between probabilistic time-series models using proper scoring rules, showing that conflicting decisions from mean score, median score, and mean rank arise from skewness in the score distribution. Studies how criteria behave as test-set size grows.

entry.title: QuechuaTok: Morphological Boundary Accuracy as a Necessary Metric for Tokenizer Evaluation in Agglutinative Low-Resource Languages

author.name: Maria Contreras

entry.summary: Presents QuechuaTok, a benchmark comparing four tokenization strategies for Southern Quechua and argues that morphological boundary accuracy is a necessary metric beyond fertility rate for agglutinative low-resource languages. Uses a finite-state morphological analyzer as silver standard.

entry.title: Meet UD_Czech-PDTC: A Large and Genre-Rich Treebank in Universal Dependencies

author.name: Marie Mikulov\'a, Barbora \v{S}t\v{e}p\'ankov\'a, Daniel Zeman, Jan \v{S}t\v{e}p\'anek, Milan Straka, Jan Haji\v{c}

entry.summary: Describes the conversion of the consolidated Prague Dependency Treebank (PDT-C) to Universal Dependencies, producing UD_Czech-PDTC, a large genre-rich Czech treebank more than twice the size of the original PDT. Documents the numerous subtle differences between the two annotation schemes.

entry.title: Exploring Academic Influence of Algorithms by Co-occurrence Network Based on Full-text of Academic Papers

author.name: Yuzhuo Wang, Chengzhi Zhang, Min Song, Seong Deok Kim, Youngsoo Ko, Juhee Lee

entry.summary: This study constructs large-scale algorithm co-occurrence networks from the full text of NLP papers to analyze the collective influence of algorithms through their interconnections rather than in isolation. It matters for scientometrics and understanding how algorithmic ideas propagate and gain influence in AI research.

entry.title: Reentrant value fields as delayed coupled reaction-diffusion systems on finite graphs

author.name: Karsten Bohlen

entry.summary: This paper describes a dynamical system coupling a symbolic field to a geometric field via a bipartite Hilbert-Schmidt kernel, formulated as a retarded functional differential equation, proving well-posedness, a compact global attractor, and delay-independent global stability under a coupling condition. It matters as a mathematical framework for stability in coupled symbolic-geometric reaction-diffusion-like systems on finite graphs.

entry.title: Audio-visual Contrastive Alignment for Diffusion-based Visual-conditioned Speech Enhancement

author.name: Colombe Mboungou (MULTISPEECH), Mostafa Sadeghi (MULTISPEECH), Jean-Eudes Ayilo (MULTISPEECH), Romain Serizel (MULTISPEECH)

entry.summary: Augments diffusion-based audio-visual speech enhancement with a contrastive cross-modal alignment loss to encourage stronger use of visual cues. Keeps the posterior sampling framework unchanged while improving fusion.

entry.title: Predicting Poets' Origins from Verse: A Computational Analysis of Regional Linguistic Fingerprints in the Complete Tang Poems

author.name: Chi-Sheng Chen, Hung-Yun Liu

entry.summary: Applies computational text analysis to predict the geographic origin of Tang-dynasty poets from their verse, achieving 0.69 accuracy on north/south classification using n-gram TF-IDF and interpretable features. Reveals regional linguistic fingerprints.

entry.title: Deep Learning Approaches for 3D Medical Scene Completion: From Geometric Modeling to Generative Paradigms

author.name: Afifa Khaled, Said Jadid Abdulkadir, Majdy Mohamed Eltayeb Eltahir

entry.summary: Systematic review of deep learning approaches for 3D medical scene completion from 2016 to 2026, tracing evolution from voxel semantic completion to generative diffusion priors with Gaussian splatting. Surveys representation paradigms across the field.

entry.title: Poster: Exploring the Limits of Audio-Based Detection of Turkish Phone Call Scams

author.name: Arda Eren, Micheal Cheung, Youqian Zhang, Grace Ngai, Eugene Yujun Fu

entry.summary: This poster explores audio-based detection of Turkish phone-call scams, introducing the first public multimodal dataset of 100 aligned audio-transcript scam and benign conversation pairs. It evaluates seven LLMs across audio, transcript, and transcript-plus conditions for low-resource scam detection.

entry.title: AI-PAVE-Br: Leveraging Large Language Models for Enhanced Product Attribute Value Extraction through a Golden Set Approach

author.name: Murilo Gazzola, Hugo Gobato Souto, Samuel Silva, J\'ulia Schubert Peixoto, Felipe Siqueira, Andr\'e Luis Pedroso de Morais, Caio Gomes

entry.summary: AI-PAVE-Br is an LLM-based system for high-accuracy product attribute value extraction tailored to Portuguese-language Brazilian e-commerce catalogs, paired with a curated Golden Set benchmark for reproducible evaluation. It addresses linguistic nuance gaps in non-English product data extraction.

entry.title: Parallel Manifold Steering: Efficient Adaptation of Large Associative Memories via Residual Energy Shaping

author.name: Kanishk Awadhiya

entry.summary: Introduces H-Res, a hierarchical residual steering method that adapts frozen Transformers by reshaping their energy landscape rather than modifying weights (LoRA) or clogging the prompt buffer (VPT). Frames Transformers as Dense Associative Memories to address the plasticity-stability tradeoff in adaptation.

entry.title: Zero-Shot Neural Priors for Generalizable Cross-Subject and Cross-Task EEG Decoding

author.name: Baimam Boukar Jean Jacques, Brandone Fonya, Nchofon Tagha Ghogomu, Pauline Nyaboe, Kipngeno Koech

entry.summary: Develops a zero-shot cross-subject and cross-task EEG decoding framework benchmarking CNN, hybrid LSTM, and a Transformer foundation model on the Healthy Brain Network dataset. Proposes a progressive unfreezing strategy to adapt the Transformer for regression while avoiding catastrophic forgetting.

entry.title: Stochastic Expectation Maximization for Robust State-Space Radio Interferometric Imaging

author.name: Nawel Arab, Mohammed Nabil El Korso, Isabelle Vin, Pascal Larzabal

entry.summary: Proposes a robust Stochastic Approximation EM algorithm for linear state-space models under compound-Gaussian (heavy-tailed) noise, replacing the standard E-step with Monte Carlo Gibbs sampling of latent states and noise texture. Applied to radio interferometric imaging affected by RF interference.

entry.title: Extended pseudo-spectral physics-informed neural networks for phase-field models

author.name: Callum Marsh, Radek Erban, Andreas Munch

entry.summary: Develops an extended pseudo-spectral physics-informed neural network framework for inverse identification of phase-field models, simultaneously recovering the bulk chemical potential and unknown gradient coefficients from transient snapshot data. Demonstrated on the Cahn-Hilliard equation.

entry.title: Transformation Behavior of Images in Latent Space

author.name: Christian Z\"ollner (Department of Applied Tumor Biology Institute of Pathology Heidelberg University Hospital), Mozzam Motiwala (Department of Applied Tumor Biology Institute of Pathology Heidelberg University Hospital), Aysel Ahadova (Department of Applied Tumor Biology Institute of Pathology Heidelberg University Hospital), Gerrit Anders (Leibniz Institut f\"ur Wissensmedien), Robert H\"uneburg (National Center for Hereditary Tumor Syndromes University Hospital Bonn, Department of Internal Medicine I University Hospital Bonn), Jacob Nattermann (National Center for Hereditary Tumor Syndromes University Hospital Bonn, Department of Internal Medicine I University Hospital Bonn), Matthias Kloor (Department of Applied Tumor Biology Institute of Pathology Heidelberg University Hospital)

entry.summary: This paper investigates how classical image transformations affect the latent space of histopathology encoder networks, comparing pathology-specific encoders from Lunit and Bioptimus against Meta's models. It assesses embedding variance and invariance to label-irrelevant transformations.

entry.title: Low-rank Updates in Slowly Time-varying Graphs for Spatial-Temporal Signal Interpolation

author.name: Saghar Bagheri, Gene Cheung, Tim Eadie, Antonio Ortega

entry.summary: Proposes low-rank modeling of the difference between consecutive adjacency matrices to represent slowly time-varying graphs, jointly interpolating signals and estimating evolving graph structure for spatial-temporal data. Combines graph smoothness priors with a low-rank update constraint.

entry.title: MorfFlex: Handling Rich Morphology

author.name: Jaroslava Hlav\'a\v{c}ov\'a, Marie Mikulov\'a, Barbora \v{S}t\v{e}p\'ankov\'a, Milan Straka, Jan Haji\v{c}

entry.summary: Presents MorfFlex, a morphological dictionary architecture for languages with rich inflection and derivation, instantiated as MorfFlex CZ with over 100 million wordforms and 1 million lemmas. Uses inflectional and derivational patterns to dramatically compress the otherwise enormous dictionary.

entry.title: Exploring the relationship between human-centric AI and firm idiosyncratic risks

author.name: Zhen-Yuan Ralph Liu (CUMT), Yu-Ting Wang (NFU), Jia-Jia Yan (NEOMA), Shivam Gupta (NEOMA), Mihalis Giannakis

entry.summary: This paper investigates how human-centric AI strategies affect firms' idiosyncratic financial risk, integrating situated AI theory with socio-technical systems theory to argue that HCAI reduces AI-related ethical risks and aligns stakeholder expectations. It matters for understanding investor reactions to corporate AI strategies during the current technological transition.

entry.title: Random coloured digraphs defined by a Markov logic network

author.name: Yasmin Tousinejad, Vera Koponen

entry.summary: Theoretical study of Markov Logic Networks defining probability distributions over coloured digraphs, showing convergence behavior of first-order sentences under weight scaling by 1/n. Contributes to statistical relational AI foundations.

entry.title: Integrated Sensing and Communications for Real-time Avatar Control in XR over 5G

author.name: Nabeel Nisar Bhat, Javad Sameri, Rreze Halili, Rafael Berkvens, Maria Torres Vega, Jeroen Famaey

entry.summary: Proposes a multimodal sensing architecture for XR avatar control combining 5G mmWave integrated sensing and communication with surface electromyography for full-body pose capture. Addresses limitations of camera and controller-based interaction.

entry.title: Lightweight Transformer Models for On-Device Fault Detection: A Benchmark Study on Resource-Constrained Deployment

author.name: Disha Patel

entry.summary: Benchmarks traditional ML methods against lightweight transformers (DistilBERT, TinyBERT variants, MobileBERT) for on-device fault detection across three industrial datasets, evaluating accuracy, model size, latency, and INT8 quantization. Provides deployment-focused tradeoff analysis.

entry.title: Neural Network-Based Parametric Model Reduction for Predicting Turbulent Flow for Different Vehicle Geometries

author.name: Kazuto Ando, Rahul Bale, Akiyoshi Kuroda, Makoto Tsubokura

entry.summary: This work develops a neural network-based parametric model order reduction method to predict turbulent flow over different vehicle geometries, reducing computational cost for aerodynamic simulations. It targets industrial CFD bottlenecks in vehicle body design.

entry.title: Adaptive Machine Learning Framework for UAV Trajectory Optimization in O-RAN

author.name: Chenrui Sun, Swarna Bindu Chetty, Gianluca Fontanesi, Mahnaz Arvaneh, Walid Saad, Hamed Ahmadi

entry.summary: This paper proposes a UAV trajectory optimization framework integrating continual transfer learning within the O-RAN architecture for 6G aerial coverage, maintaining a library of pretrained models and selecting the most relevant one for fast adaptation. It minimizes retraining time in new environments.

entry.title: Visualizing "We the People": Bridging the Perception Gap through Pluralistic Data Storytelling

author.name: Lisa Schirch, Beth Goldberg

entry.summary: This paper argues that traditional binary data storytelling fuels political polarization and proposes pluralistic AI-enabled visualization that emphasizes nuance, opinion distribution, and intergroup commonalities. It examines deliberative technologies via a Jigsaw We the People case study.

entry.title: A Comparative Study of Bayesian Contextual Bandits for Real-Time Warehouse Sorter Optimization

author.name: Tina Dongxu Li, Mouhacine Benosman, Ken Meszaros, Trevor Dardik

entry.summary: This study compares three hybrid machine learning frameworks including Bayesian contextual bandits for real-time sorter diversion optimization in a high-volume e-commerce warehouse, where static cost-function weights fail to adapt to dynamic conditions. It evaluates linear regression and bandit approaches for adaptive material handling control.

entry.title: Reasoning as Attractor Dynamics: Latent Memory Retrieval via Gibbs-Weighted Energy Minimization

author.name: Kanishk Awadhiya

entry.summary: Reframes LLM reasoning as attractor dynamics in a Dense Associative Memory, positing that correct reasoning chains correspond to flat wide minima while hallucinations are sharp unstable minima. Proposes a Gibbs-weighted energy minimization retrieval mechanism over sampled reasoning paths.

entry.title: Deep numerical schemes for systems of Ergodic BSDEs with applications to regime-switching forward utilities

author.name: Guillaume Broux-Quemerais (LMM), Sarah Kaakai (LAGA), Anis Matoussi (LMM), Wissal Sabbagh (LMM)

entry.summary: Introduces two neural-network-based numerical schemes for solving systems of coupled ergodic Backward Stochastic Differential Equations, motivated by optimal strategies in regime-switching forward-utility models. Links the ergodic BSDE system to a multidimensional BSDE with random terminal time.

entry.title: An Agnostic Machine Learning Model of Photosynthetic Habitability

author.name: Callum Gray, Cassandra Hall, Stefano Santabarbara, Klaus Schmidt-Rohr, Andrew Ringham, Edward Gillen, Thomas J. Haworth, Christopher D. P. Duffy

entry.summary: Introduces an organism-agnostic model of the Photosynthetic Habitable Zone grounded in thermodynamics and redox chemistry rather than Earth-centric light-response curves. Uses a generalized photochemical reaction model to estimate where photosynthesis could be driven on exoplanets.

entry.title: A Synthetic Reliability-Aware PINN Benchmark for Offshore Wind Turbine Support-Structure Monitoring with Bayesian Inverse Identification

author.name: Puneet Kant, Monika Tanwar

entry.summary: Presents Digi Turbine, a synthetic reliability-aware physics-informed neural network benchmark for offshore wind turbine monopile monitoring, embedding a Euler-Bernoulli beam equation with Winkler soil foundation and coupling Bayesian inverse identification with reliability screening. Targets fast state estimation from sparse measurements.

entry.title: CN-NewsTTS Bench: a target-level automatic benchmark for raw-input Chinese news TTS pronunciation

author.name: Shijun Luo

entry.summary: Introduces CN-NewsTTS Bench, an open target-level automatic benchmark for evaluating whether Chinese news text-to-speech systems correctly pronounce dense written forms like scores, model names, ranges, units, percentages, and mixed Chinese-Latin-digit names from raw text. Uses a three-ASR ensemble for fixed transcripts and automatic target evaluation.

entry.title: AutoSpecNER: A Fine-Grained Named Entity Recognition Dataset for Vehicle Specification Extraction

author.name: Jordan Lee, Filippos Ventirozos, Abdirahman Abdullahm, Ioanna Nteka, Peter Appleby, Matthew Shardlow

entry.summary: Introduces AutoSpecNER, an expert-annotated fine-grained NER dataset of 659 vehicle advertisements with over 10,000 entities across 15 categories, benchmarking rule-based, fine-tuned encoders, and LLMs. DeBERTa achieves 90% micro-F1, outperforming rule-based and the strongest LLM baseline.

entry.title: Ensemble Feature Selection and Harris Hawks Optimization for Explainable Mental Health Risk Prediction in Female Sex Workers

author.name: Ahnaf Atef Choudhury, Md. Parvej Hoque Palash, Shahriar Siddique Ayon, Ramkrishna Saha, Abdullah Al Mamun

entry.summary: This paper proposes a hybrid predictive model combining ensemble feature selection (ANOVA and mutual information) with Harris Hawks optimization-tuned logistic regression and explainable AI to predict mental health risk among female sex workers. It matters as an application of swarm intelligence to mental health prediction in a marginalized, high-risk population.

entry.title: Evaluating LLM Usage for Efficient and Explainable Numerical and Classified Implicit Sentiment Analysis of Product Desirability

author.name: Sherri Weitl-Harms, John Hastings

entry.summary: Presents an LLM-based framework for scoring implicit product desirability sentiment from qualitative feedback, achieving Pearson correlations up to 0.97 against expert labels. Offers an interpretable, scalable alternative to explicit review scores.

entry.title: A Unified Framework for Runtime Verification and Model-Based Diagnosis in LOLA

author.name: Raik Hipler, Martin Leucker, Patrick Rodler

entry.summary: Presents a unified framework integrating runtime verification and model-based diagnosis within the LOLA stream specification language. Enables continuous online fault localization alongside detection without separate toolchains.

entry.title: The Measurable Majority

author.name: Lawrence S. Moss, Arthur Paul Pedersen

entry.summary: Theoretical study of strict majority reasoning in finite electorates using social decision frames, providing a coherence criterion and a sound, complete minimal logic. Connects majority representability to finitely additive measures.

entry.title: Rapid FinFET Modelling Using an Autoencoder

author.name: Amit Sarkar Suman Sau, Swagata Mandal

entry.summary: Presents a machine learning framework using an autoencoder to compress FinFET current-voltage curves into a low-dimensional latent space encoding device physics, with explicit bias-voltage input for efficient semiconductor device modeling. Reconstructs I-V curves and extracts key device metrics.

entry.title: SURGELLM: Rethinking Multi-Task Evaluation through Task-Aware Feature Gating with Class-Balanced Normalization

author.name: Noor Islam S. Mohammad, Ulug Bayazit

entry.summary: SURGELLM introduces a unified transformer framework with three lightweight modules to address mismatched inductive biases, class imbalance, and lexical knowledge conditioning in fine-tuned encoders across heterogeneous NLP tasks. The components include a surgical feature gate, task-conditioned prefix tokens, and instance-weighted normalization.

entry.title: Machine Learning Modeling for Real-Time Melt Pool Monitoring in Laser Powder Bed Fusion Additive Manufacturing: A Hybrid Approach

author.name: Inioluwa Emmanuel, Zhuo Yang, Ho Yeung, Xinyao Zhang

entry.summary: This study develops a binary image classification framework distinguishing normal and abnormal melt pool images for real-time monitoring in laser powder bed fusion additive manufacturing, benchmarking transfer learning models against hybrid random forest approaches. It evaluates accuracy and inference time against control and hardware constraints.

entry.title: Managing Task Execution for Unknown Workloads in Batteryless IoT: A Hardware-Agnostic Evaluation

author.name: Samer Nasser, Henrique Duarte Moura, Ritesh Kumar Singh, Maarten Weyn, Jeroen Famaey

entry.summary: Proposes two hardware-agnostic dynamic scheduling strategies for batteryless energy-harvesting IoT devices: a model-free RL agent and an on-the-fly approximated prediction method that treat applications as black boxes. The approaches avoid reliance on static thresholds or pre-measured task profiles for managing volatile harvested energy.

entry.title: Prediction of Viscoelastic Droplet Impact Dynamics Using a Vision Transformer-Based Approach

author.name: Diego A. de Aguiar, Cassio M. Oishi

entry.summary: Investigates a Video Vision Transformer (ViViT) to predict the temporal evolution of viscoelastic droplets impacting solid surfaces from volume-fraction fields, as a fast surrogate for expensive fluid simulations. Targets applications in inkjet printing, spray cooling, and pharmaceutical processing.

entry.title: Automated Residual Plot Assessment With the R Package autovi and the Shiny Application autovi.web

author.name: Weihao Li, Dianne Cook, Emi Tanaka, Susan VanderPlas, Klaus Ackermann

entry.summary: Presents an R package (autovi) and Shiny app using a computer-vision model to automate the visual assessment of residual plots for linear-model diagnostics, predicting a visual signal strength score. Reduces the manual effort and subjectivity of the lineup protocol.

entry.title: ModTGCN: Modularity-aware Graph Neural Networks for Text Classification

author.name: Rajarshi Misra, Aditya Sharma, Vinti Agarwal, Hari Om Aggrawal

entry.summary: Proposes ModTGCN, a modularity-aware graph neural network for text classification that adds a modularity-based auxiliary objective on a document-document similarity graph to promote class-coherent communities and reduce over-smoothing. Decouples the heterogeneous TextGCN graph for scalability.

entry.title: MIND: multimodal integration with neighbourhood-aware distributions

author.name: Unknown

entry.summary: This Nature Communications paper introduces MIND, a method for integrating multiple data modalities using neighbourhood-aware probability distributions, which appears aimed at combining heterogeneous datasets (likely single-cell or multi-omics data given the venue) while preserving local structure across modalities. The approach matters for fields that must fuse complementary measurements into a coherent representation, though limited metadata is available to confirm the exact domain.

entry.title: Dimensionality Reduction of QAOA Parameter Space with Kernel PCA for Max-Cut

author.name: Sidharth Brahmandam, Vayd Ramkumar

entry.summary: Investigates Kernel PCA with RBF kernels for dimensionality reduction of QAOA parameter spaces in Max-Cut problems, improving over linear PCA at higher circuit depths where the optimal-parameter manifold becomes nonlinear. Targets the parameter-optimization bottleneck in near-term quantum algorithms.

entry.title: Heterogeneous 2D/1D Signal Representation Fusion for Underwater Acoustic Modulation Recognition Under Distribution Shift

author.name: Ronglai Qian, Liang An, Xiaoyan Wang, Qing Fan, Ziwei Huang, Yang Ye

entry.summary: Introduces a benchmark and fusion model for underwater acoustic modulation recognition that combines 2D time-frequency and 1D statistical signal representations under distribution shift. Addresses robustness across SNR and environment changes.

entry.title: The impact of generative artificial intelligence on academic development of Chinese students in humanities and social sciences

author.name: Lei Fan, Fangxue Liu

entry.summary: Surveys the impact of generative AI on academic development of Chinese humanities and social science students via a large-scale survey across four dimensions. Examines usage patterns, learning effects, challenges, and curricular preferences.

entry.title: Context-Aware Prediction of Student Quiz Performance with Multimodal Textbook Features

author.name: Samin Khan

entry.summary: This study tests whether lightweight content features (text and image complexity) extracted from CourseKata chapter-review questions improve prediction of end-of-chapter quiz scores beyond a student's prior performance. Adding content features improved quiz prediction by about 9 percent across nearly 5,000 observations.

entry.title: QC-SMOTE: Quality-Controlled SMOTE for Imbalanced Classification

author.name: Parth Upman, Shreyank N Gowda

entry.summary: Proposes QC-SMOTE, a quality-controlled oversampling framework that scores minority-sample reliability using neighborhood trustworthiness and generates synthetic samples via an IPQ-guided best-of-K strategy. Aims to avoid low-quality synthetic samples in noisy or overlapping regions.

entry.title: UOL@IDEM at BEA 2026 Shared Task 1: Neural Fusion and Feature-Rich Modeling for L1-Aware Vocabulary Difficulty Prediction

author.name: Nouran Khallaf, Serge Sharoff

entry.summary: Describes a closed-track submission to the BEA 2026 shared task on L1-aware vocabulary difficulty prediction, combining multilingual contextual embeddings with engineered features (frequency, cognate similarity, MLM predictability) for Spanish, German, and Chinese. Reports RMSE scores improving over official baselines.

entry.title: Engineering Reliable Autonomous Systems: Challenges and Solutions

author.name: Marie Farrell, Matt Luckcuck, Angelo Ferrando, Rafael C. Cardoso, Natasha Alechina, Marco Autili, Diana Benjumea Hernandez, Luciana Brasil Rebelo dos Santos, Daniela Briola, Ana Cavalcanti, Christian Colombo, Louise A. entry.summary: Workshop report capturing discussions on engineering reliable autonomous systems, bringing together formal methods and agent-robotics communities. Identifies challenges and solutions for deploying trustworthy autonomous systems.

entry.title: An LLM-based Two-Stage Transformer Framework for Cross-Domain Bearing Fault Diagnosis with Limited Data

author.name: Jinghan Wang, Feng Cheng, Wentao Wu, Hang Li, Gaoliang Peng, Tianchen Liu

entry.summary: Presents a two-stage transfer learning framework using a lightweight GPT-2-style Transformer for cross-domain bearing fault diagnosis under heterogeneous, limited-data industrial conditions. Uses pre-trained encoder weights and fault prototype embeddings as explicit knowledge carriers.

entry.title: Transformer-Based Language Models Across Domain Verticals: Architectures, Applications and Critical Assessment

author.name: Guruprakash J, Krithika L. B

entry.summary: A review organizing transformer-based language model families into a taxonomy (encoder-only, decoder-only, encoder-decoder, long-context, etc.) and surveying post-2023 developments including instruction tuning, RLHF, DPO, mixture-of-experts, and retrieval augmentation. Aims to help practitioners separate durable ideas from incremental noise.

entry.title: Best Preprocessing Techniques for Sentiment Analysis

author.name: Saranzaya Magsarjav, Melissa Humphries, Jonathan Tuke, Lewis Mitchell

entry.summary: Systematically examines the order in which text preprocessing techniques are applied for Twitter sentiment analysis, finding tokenization most impactful, spelling correction least, and that negation should be preserved when removing stop words. Fills a gap on preprocessing ordering effects.

entry.title: What Does ODRL Mean? A Cross-Level Ontological Grounding of Permissions, Prohibitions, and Duties in UFO-L

author.name: Daham M. Mustafa, Christoph Lange, Giancarlo Guizzardi, Diego Collarana, Christoph Quix, Stefan Decker

entry.summary: This paper provides an ontological grounding of ODRL permissions, prohibitions, and duties using the UFO-L legal core ontology, distinguishing conduct-level and competence-level normative positions. It articulates a Cross-Level Design Principle for normative languages with violable consequential norms.

entry.title: Machine Learning and Deep Learning for Exoplanet Detection and Atmospheric Characterization with JWST and the Upcoming Ariel Mission

author.name: Muallim Yakubu, Vwavware Oruaode Jude

entry.summary: A review synthesizing ML/DL applications to exoplanet detection and atmospheric characterization in the context of JWST and the upcoming Ariel mission. Covers classical algorithms through deep learning for transit identification, vetting, and spectral retrieval.

entry.title: Aspect-Based Sentiment Evolution and its Correlation with Review Rounds in Multi-Round Peer Reviews: A Deep Learning Approach

author.name: Ruxue Hana, Haomin Zhoua, Jiangtao Zhong, Chengzhi Zhang

entry.summary: A heavily theoretical study of stochastic quantum neural networks for adversarially robust network intrusion detection, examining whether per-gate stochastic deactivation (true quantum dropout) can regularize where depolarizing channels fail and deriving tighter robustness bounds. Encodes neural noise via a Lindblad master equation.

entry.title: A Hybrid Quantum-Classical Approach for Melt Pool Prediction in Laser Powder Bed Fusion

author.name: Matthew M. Sato, Kincho H. Law

entry.summary: Demonstrates a hybrid quantum-classical model with a quantum feature encoder for predicting melt pools in laser powder bed fusion additive manufacturing. Aims to improve process-parameter feature extraction for quality assurance.

entry.title: Automatic Part-of-Speech Tagging of Arabic-English Dictionary Senses through WordNet

author.name: Diaa M. Fayed, Aly A. Fahmy, Mohsen A. Rashwan, Wafaa K. Fayed

entry.summary: Proposes an algorithm to automatically POS-tag senses of the Al-Mawrid Arabic-English bilingual dictionary by transferring English translation-equivalent POS tags from Princeton WordNet after disambiguation. Enables linking bilingual dictionaries to WordNet and standardizing into WordNet-LMF format.

entry.title: Research Summary: June 23, 2026

author.name: AATF AI News Aggregator

entry.summary:
Today's research spans foundational RL theory, embodied AI, scientific modeling, and a heavy concentration of safety and security findings.

Theory & Foundations

  • Inverting the Bellman Equation (Foerster et al.) proves value-based RL agents trained across rich reward sets implicitly encode a unique, accurate world model, bridging model-free and model-based RL.
  • Unsupervised disentanglement work shows local Jacobian orthogonality enforces identifiability, challenging long-standing impossibility intuitions for nonlinear generative models.

Embodied & Scientific Models

  • NVIDIA's Vesta (Fan, Kautz, Zhu) unifies localization, spatial reasoning, navigation, and long-horizon planning into a single embodied generalist foundation model.
  • Atomistic Language Models (MIT, Gomez-Bombarelli) combine an atomistic encoder, LLM, and denoising diffusion for SOTA materials understanding and generation.
  • GEOPHYS (Simoncelli, Torr, Laptev, Klindt) captures physical plausibility via five geometric properties of frozen image-encoder embeddings, validated against EEG.

Safety & Security

  • Knowledge editing does not truly erase facts; edited knowledge resurfaces under adversarial elicitation, with mechanistic analysis exposing the illusion of erasure.
  • A preregistered 2,610-participant study finds warning labels shift perceptions of sycophantic AI but fail to reduce its actual influence.
  • Import AI 462 reports a ~19,000-conversation study showing AI reliably out-persuades expert humans on politically charged topics.
  • The Watermark Shortcut shows provenance watermarking sabotages audio deepfake detectors, which latch onto watermarks rather than synthesis artifacts.
  • A mechanistic account links prompt injection success to how chat-template tags encode conversational roles in the residual stream.
entry.content:
Today's research spans foundational RL theory, embodied AI, scientific modeling, and a heavy concentration of safety and security findings.

Theory & Foundations

  • Inverting the Bellman Equation (Foerster et al.) proves value-based RL agents trained across rich reward sets implicitly encode a unique, accurate world model, bridging model-free and model-based RL.
  • Unsupervised disentanglement work shows local Jacobian orthogonality enforces identifiability, challenging long-standing impossibility intuitions for nonlinear generative models.

Embodied & Scientific Models

  • NVIDIA's Vesta (Fan, Kautz, Zhu) unifies localization, spatial reasoning, navigation, and long-horizon planning into a single embodied generalist foundation model.
  • Atomistic Language Models (MIT, Gomez-Bombarelli) combine an atomistic encoder, LLM, and denoising diffusion for SOTA materials understanding and generation.
  • GEOPHYS (Simoncelli, Torr, Laptev, Klindt) captures physical plausibility via five geometric properties of frozen image-encoder embeddings, validated against EEG.

Safety & Security

  • Knowledge editing does not truly erase facts; edited knowledge resurfaces under adversarial elicitation, with mechanistic analysis exposing the illusion of erasure.
  • A preregistered 2,610-participant study finds warning labels shift perceptions of sycophantic AI but fail to reduce its actual influence.
  • Import AI 462 reports a ~19,000-conversation study showing AI reliably out-persuades expert humans on politically charged topics.
  • The Watermark Shortcut shows provenance watermarking sabotages audio deepfake detectors, which latch onto watermarks rather than synthesis artifacts.
  • A mechanistic account links prompt injection success to how chat-template tags encode conversational roles in the residual stream.

entry.title: Inverting the Bellman Equation: From $Q$-Values to World Models

author.name: Alistair Letcher, Mattie Fellows, Alexander D. Goldie, Jonathan Richens, Jakob N. Foerster, Oliver Richardson

entry.summary: This paper proves that value-based RL agents trained over a sufficiently rich set of reward functions implicitly encode a unique, accurate world model, and introduces P-learning to extract that model as an inverse of Q-learning. It bridges the model-free versus model-based dichotomy with theoretical conditions on goal/reward diversity.

entry.title: Vesta: A Generalist Embodied Reasoning Model

author.name: Johan Bjorck, Zhiqi Li, Yunze Man, Jing Wang, An-Chieh Cheng, Sifei Liu, Shihao Wang, Zhiding Yu, Abhishek Badki, Stan Birchfield, Valts Blukis, Yevgen Chebotar, Siyi Chen, Sicong Leng, Yu-Cheng Chou, Tianli Ding, Boyi Li, Zhengyi Luo, Hang Su, Jonathan Tremblay, Tingwu Wang, Bowen Wen, Jimmy Wu, Xianghui Xie, Hanrong Ye, Hongxu Yin, K. R. Zentner, Liangyan Gui, Yu-Xiong Wang, Yuke Zhu, Linxi "Jim" Fan, Jan Kautz

entry.summary: Vesta is a unified embodied generalist foundation model from NVIDIA that consolidates localization, spatial reasoning, navigation, and long-horizon planning into a single model with a multimodal memory harness. It beats individual SOTA baselines by over 20% on average across diverse benchmarks.

entry.title: GEOPHYS: The Geometry of Physical Plausibility

author.name: Christian Intern\`o, Alexander Pondaven, Habon Issa, Fabio Pizzati, Francesco Pinto, Markus Olhofer, Ivan Laptev, Philip Torr, Eero P. Simoncelli, Barbara Hammer, David Klindt

entry.summary: GEOPHYS argues that physical plausibility is implicitly captured by five geometric properties of frozen image-encoder embeddings, enabling fast physics-violation detection that correlates with human EEG responses. It claims SOTA without MLLM judges or training modifications.

entry.title: Warning labels shift perceptions of sycophantic AI, but not its influence

author.name: Lujain Ibrahim, Myra Cheng, Cinoo Lee, Pranav Khadpe, Desmong Ong, Dan Jurafsky, Diyi Yang

entry.summary: A preregistered experiment with 2,610 participants tests whether warning labels mitigate sycophantic AI's influence in interpersonal-conflict discussions. Labels shift perceptions (reducing trust and perceived objectivity) but do not reliably reduce sycophancy's actual influence on judgment.

entry.title: Exposing the Illusion of Erasure in Knowledge Editing for LLMs

author.name: Advik Raj Basani, Anshuman Chhabra

entry.summary: Demonstrates that knowledge editing in LLMs does not truly erase facts; edited knowledge resurfaces under adversarial elicitation. Mechanistic analysis shows low-rank updates redistribute rather than overwrite knowledge, acting as suppression rather than deletion.

entry.title: Atomistic Language Models Understand and Generate Materials

author.name: Sathya Edamadaka, Krithik Ramesh, Ju Li, Rafael G\'omez-Bombarelli

entry.summary: Introduces Atomistic Language Models that unify a pretrained atomistic encoder, an LLM, and a denoising diffusion model so a single backbone can understand structures, generate materials from text, and optimize crystals. Achieves SOTA on crystal structure prediction and de novo generation.

entry.title: Import AI 462: Superpersuasion; self-sustaining AI; paths to ASI

author.name: Jack Clark

entry.summary: Jack Clark's newsletter highlights a large study (nearly 19,000 conversations) finding AI systems are reliably more persuasive than expert humans on policy and donation decisions, even when humans prepared extensively and were incentivized. It also covers self-sustaining AI and paths to ASI.

entry.title: Unsupervised Disentanglement Without Compromises : How Functional Orthogonality Enforces Identifiability

author.name: Mathieu Cyrille Simon, Pascal Frossard, Christophe De Vleeschouwer

entry.summary: This paper proves that imposing local orthogonality on the Jacobian of the generative mapping yields identifiability of general nonlinear generative models without statistical independence or causal assumptions, given a full factor-combination domain. Experiments with orthogonality-regularized normalizing flows confirm reliable factor recovery.

entry.title: The Watermark Shortcut: How Provenance Marking Sabotages Audio Deepfake Detection

author.name: Nicolas M. M\"uller, Pascal Debus

entry.summary: Reveals that provenance watermarking of synthetic speech creates a spurious shortcut where deepfake detectors latch onto watermarks rather than learning genuine artifacts. Identifies three failure modes including watermarked fakes evading detection and real watermarked voices being flagged as fake.

entry.title: A Mechanistic Explanation of Prompt Injection (and why you should study roles)

author.name: Charles Ye

entry.summary: Presents a mechanistic theory that prompt injection succeeds because of how LLMs encode conversational roles via chat template tags, using this to construct new attacks and explain interpretability findings. The authors advocate for a new research subfield studying the science of roles.

entry.title: Protein contacts are already in the attention: a single-forward-pass alternative to the Categorical Jacobian

author.name: Rome Thorstenson

entry.summary: This work shows protein contact signals reconstructed by the Categorical Jacobian (about 19L forward passes) are already concentrated in a small subset of attention heads, recoverable in a single forward pass by averaging top-K contact-relevant heads selected on as few as 10 labeled proteins. It matches or beats CJ across bidirectional protein language models.

entry.title: MuPPET: A Benchmark for Contextual Privacy of LLM Assistants in Multi-Party Conversations

author.name: Elena Sofia Ruzzetti, Cornelius Emde, Sangdoo Yun, Seong Joon Oh, Martin Gubri

entry.summary: Introduces MuPPET, a benchmark testing whether LLM assistants leak private information in multi-party conversations like group chats, where one disclosure reaches all members at once. Finds models leak substantially more in multi-party settings than single-interlocutor ones, exposing an unmeasured privacy risk.

entry.title: Discretizing Reward Models

author.name: Vijay Viswanathan, Shiqi Wang, Devamanyu Hazarika, Chirag Nagpal, Tongshuang Wu, Graham Neubig, Yuning Mao

entry.summary: Shows that continuous-scoring reward models are often oversensitive, assigning different scores to equally good responses, which can lead to bad RL policies. Proposes discretizing reward models, with theoretical and empirical support.

entry.title: Superhuman AI for Generals.io Using Self-Play Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Matej Straka, Viliam Lis\'y, Martin Schmid

entry.summary: Presents a superhuman self-play RL agent for Generals.io, a real-time imperfect-information strategy game, reaching #1 on the 5000+ player leaderboard and beating top humans. A key enabler is a JAX-native simulator achieving roughly 10,000x speedup over prior tools.

entry.title: Brittle model organisms obstructs deception elicitation work

author.name: Advik

entry.summary: Shows that finetuning-based auditing methods for deception model organisms can inadvertently erase the very hidden behaviors they aim to measure, producing an illusion of success. Using secret side constraint organisms, the authors find models stop following hidden constraints while still claiming to, inflating intervention effectiveness.

entry.title: ConnectomeBench2: A Unified Benchmark for Automated Connectomic Proofreading

author.name: Jeff Brown, Tim Farkas, Gleb Razgar, Edward S. Boyden

entry.summary: ConnectomeBench2 releases a unified multi-species dataset of over 716,000 expert-labeled proofreading decisions with 4.5 million images across mouse, human, zebrafish, and fly connectomes, and trains a single Vision Transformer reaching human-level accuracy for split error correction and merge identification. Targets the rate-limiting proofreading step in connectomics.

entry.title: Detecting Malicious Agent Skills in the Wild using Attention

author.name: Bacem Etteib, Daniele Lunghi, T\'egawend\'e F. Bissyand\'e
