entry.summary: Presents Locate-and-Judge, an attention-based two-stage detector for malicious agent skills—third-party instruction packages that execute with user privileges. Argues prompt-injection defenses fail here because skills are themselves trusted instructions.

entry.title: Learning through Internalization

author.name: Nikolaos Tsilivis, Nirmit Joshi, Marko Medvedev, Julia Kempe, Nati Srebro

entry.summary: Studies internalization processes by which transformers absorb explicit chain-of-thought procedures into their weights, examining which semiautomata are harder to internalize and the resulting degradation of out-of-distribution performance. Provides the first provable analysis of successful internalization for learning parities.

entry.title: Massive Activations Are Architecturally Robust: A Controlled Scratch/Commitment Residual Stream Test

author.name: Maruthi Vemula (University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill)

entry.summary: Tests whether massive activations in transformers are removable artifacts of residual stream overloading by introducing Ledger Residuals that split the stream into a mutable scratch and protected accumulator. Finds massive activations remain, suggesting they are architecturally robust and functional.

entry.title: Safe to Check, Unsafe to Use: Relinking at the Compression Boundary of LLM Agents

author.name: Zesen Liu, Zihan Zhang, Dongdong She

entry.summary: This paper identifies relinking, a compression-boundary vulnerability where summarization-based prompt compressors act as confused deputies, combining distributed benign fragments into a complete malicious instruction. Unlike prompt injection, no explicitly malicious payload need appear in the source.

entry.title: The Language-Energy Divide: Measuring Energy Costs of Multilingual LLM Inference

author.name: Naihao Deng, Alissa Shen, Yiming Feng, Joan Nwatu, Jae-Won Chung, Mosharaf Chowdhury, Yulong Chen, Rada Mihalcea

entry.summary: This systematic study measures inference energy across languages, finding per-output-token energy varies up to 8.3x and total energy for fixed requests up to 179x between English and Pashto. The disparity is driven by higher per-token costs for complex scripts and more tokens needed per content.

entry.title: Learning Process Rewards via Success Visitation Matching for Efficient RL

author.name: Raymond Tsao, Andrew Wagenmaker, Sergey Levine

entry.summary: Proposes transforming sparse outcome rewards into dense process rewards by training a discriminator between successful and unsuccessful episodes, then incentivizing the policy to match successful state-action visitations. Addresses credit assignment for efficient RL.

entry.title: Sakana Fugu Technical Report

author.name: Yujin Tang, Edoardo Cetin, Jinglue Xu, Qi Sun, Stefan Nielsen, Vincent Richard, Haruto Goda, Iaroslav Tymchenko, Nhan Nguyen, Hyunin Lee, Mari Ashiga, Shashank Kotyan, So Kuroki, Tarin Clanuwat

entry.summary: Sakana Fugu is a family of orchestrator models trained to understand queries and dynamically devise agentic scaffolds that coordinate a team of specialized LLM agents, achieving state-of-the-art results beyond any individual agent. Aims to combine the specializations of different frontier LLMs into a collective system.

entry.title: Towards Understanding the Power and Limits of the Muon Optimizer: A River-Valley Perspective

author.name: Tianqi Shen, Jinji Yang, Runze Shi, Jianhao Ma, Jiaye Teng, Ziye Ma

entry.summary: Develops a trajectory-level theory using a mixed-spiked matrix sensing model to explain when the Muon optimizer outperforms Adam and when its gains are mixed in LLM training. Provides a river-valley loss-landscape perspective on Muon's strengths and limits.

entry.title: Local Causal Attribution of Chain-of-Thought Reasoning

author.name: Dennis Wei, Yannis Belkhiter, Erik Miehling, Radu Marinescu

entry.summary: Proposes AttriCoT, a black-box method that builds a structural causal model over units of a chain-of-thought trace to attribute each unit's causal influence on output log-probabilities using O(U) forward passes. Aims to improve transparency and safety of LLM reasoning.

entry.title: Naturally learned behaviors in deep MLPs resist detection by both human and learned algorithms

author.name: emanuelr

entry.summary: Investigates whether secrets memorized by MLPs can be recovered from weights or black-box queries, a toy version of eliciting hidden behaviors in LLMs. Finds that hard-negative training plus depth makes memorized secrets resistant to input-optimization attacks, while learned weight-readers only modestly help.

entry.title: Comparing Transformers and Hybrid Models at the Token Level

author.name: Yanhong Li, William Merrill

entry.summary: Compares matched transformer and hybrid attention-recurrent language models at the token level using Olmo 3 open weights, stratifying loss differences to identify which data and capabilities drive hybrid gains. Connects empirical results to theoretical state-tracking advantages.

entry.title: Evaluation Awareness Is Not One Capability: Evidence from Open Language Models

author.name: Nilesh Nayan, Aishwarya Sampath Kumar, Rishiraj Girmal, Shivani Anilkumar, Sankaran Vaidyanathan, David A. Nader Palacio, Reshmi Ghosh, Soundararajan Srinivasan

entry.summary: Characterizes evaluation awareness across 37 open-weight models and seven families through eight experiments, finding detection is moderate and training-driven, and that detection shifts safety behavior (hard refusal drops 5.8 points under hypothetical framing). Argues evaluation awareness is not a single capability.

entry.title: A-Evolve-Training: Autonomous Post-Training of a 30B Model

author.name: Zhan Shi, Bing He, Yisi Sang, Hanqing Lu

entry.summary: Reports an autonomous post-training system that runs the full human-in-the-loop loop for a 30B Nemotron model across multiple weeks with no human intervention, reaching near-top human performance on a public leaderboard. Notably the loop detected and corrected its own degrading dev metric.

entry.title: LLM-Guided Test-Time Discovery of Quantum-Chemical Approximation Algorithms

author.name: Masaya Hagai, Yuta Suzuki, Tomoya Murata, Shuhei Kurita, Masaki Adachi

entry.summary: LADeQ is an LLM-guided workflow that discovers, implements, and benchmarks new quantum-chemical approximation algorithms at test-time, going beyond agents that merely orchestrate fixed tools. It targets methodological innovation at the frontier of chemical space.

entry.title: A large-scale foundation model enables simulation-to-real adaptation for nuclear magnetic resonance-based molecular structure analysis

author.name: Chen Yang, Zheng Fang, Hanyu Sun, Fanjie Xu, Hongxin Xiang, Hanyu Gao, Xiangxiang Zeng, Yuqiang Li, Xiaojian Wang, Jun Xia

entry.summary: UltraNMR is a large-scale foundation model for NMR spectroscopy trained on 158 million simulated 1H and 13C spectra with domain-specific pretraining objectives, enabling simulation-to-real adaptation for molecular structure analysis. It addresses experimental data scarcity.

entry.title: B[FM]$^2$: Brain Foundation Model via Flow Matching with SplitUNet

author.name: Jaedong Hwang, Kathleen Zhang, Wei Dai, Konstantinos Kontras, Maarten Vanmarcke, Maarten De Vos, Ila Fiete, Paul Pu Liang

entry.summary: B[FM]^2 is an EEG foundation model that pretrains directly on raw multi-channel signals using continuous-time flow matching with a SplitUNet, avoiding patching, tokenization, or masking that fragment brain rhythms. It aims for better single-backbone transfer across clinical and BCI tasks.

entry.title: SwarmX: Agentic Scheduling for Low-Latency Agentic Systems

author.name: Yeqi Huang, Yanwei Ye, Guomin Chen, Wenhao Su, Bin Gong, Jialian Li, Zhan Lu, Yangshen Deng, Xuan Sun, Le Xu, Luo Mai

entry.summary: This study tests whether LLM hyperparameter-optimization advisors actually outperform classical baselines under a budget-matched, multi-seed protocol on tabular benchmarks. It finds the advisor's apparent advantage comes from a fixed default warm-start configuration, not from LLM reasoning.

entry.title: Is Agent Code Less Maintainable Than Human Code?

author.name: Shaswat Patel, Betty Li Hou, Arun Purohit, Kai Xu, Jane Pan, He He, Valerie Chen

entry.summary: CodeThread constructs controlled experiments from repository-level benchmarks to assess whether agent-generated code is less maintainable when future agents build on it. Across four frontier coding agents and four benchmarks, agents resolve tasks less effectively when building on prior agent code than on human code.

entry.title: BioMatrix: Towards a Comprehensive Biological Foundation Model Spanning the Modality Matrix of Sequences, Structures, and Language

author.name: Qizhi Pei, Zhimeng Zhou, Yi Duan, Yiyang Zhao, Wei Li, Han Guo, Liang He, Chengping Li, Chang-Yu Hsieh, Conghui He, Rui Yan, Lijun Wu

entry.summary: Presents BioMatrix, described as the first multimodal foundation model natively integrating sequences, structures, and natural language for both molecules and proteins in a single decoder-only architecture. Closes the gap between native multimodality and broad entity coverage in biological foundation models.

entry.title: HyperQuant: A Rate-Distortion-Optimal Quantization Pipeline for Large Language and Diffusion Models

author.name: Yuval Domb, Hadar Sackstein, Tomer Solberg

entry.summary: HyperQuant is a unified post-training quantization pipeline combining Hadamard transforms, optimal packing, and entropy coding for weights and KV cache of LLMs and diffusion transformers. Reports outperforming recent schemes at 3-5 bits and near-lossless quantization of a 19B video DiT.

entry.title: Scheduling Thoughts: Learning the Order of Thought in Diffusion Language Models

author.name: Jiawei Xu, Minghui Liu, Aakriti Agrawal, Yifan Chen, Furong Huang

entry.summary: Studies the order in which masked diffusion language models unmask tokens, deriving a tractable bound on decoding mismatch and casting order selection as policy optimization. Proposes Self-Aware Scheduling using GRPO to learn the order of thought with a frozen denoiser.

entry.title: Tapered Language Models

author.name: Reza Bayat, Ali Behrouz, Aaron Courville

entry.summary: Tapered Language Models challenge uniform parameter allocation across depth, showing that under a fixed budget allocating more capacity to earlier layers and less to later ones improves perplexity. Builds on evidence that later layers refine rather than transform the residual stream.

entry.title: Demystifying Numerical Instability in LLM Inference: Achieving Reproducible Inference for Mission-Critical Tasks with HEAL

author.name: Zhenting Zhu, Lucas Thai, Shan Yu, Yicheng Liu, Yifan Qiao, Chenxi Wang, Harry Xu, Junyi Shu

entry.summary: HEAL achieves reproducible LLM inference for mission-critical tasks by diagnosing that output divergence across GPUs stems from truncation errors during 16-bit downcasting at kernel boundaries. Provides a system avoiding the prohibitive cost of a global FP32 pipeline.

entry.title: Robustness Cannot be Reduced to Regularization: Studying Adversarial Training Beyond the Linear Case

author.name: David A. R. Robin (LAMSADE, Dauphine), Rafael Pinot (LPSM, Jussieu), Yann Chevaleyre (LAMSADE, Dauphine)

entry.summary: Formally proves that adversarial training cannot be reduced to a regularized risk equivalence for two-layer networks, unlike the established linear case. This delimits when efficient regularization-based adversarial training methods can apply.

entry.title: Causal Gaussian Processes for Robust Treatment Effect Evaluation with Unobserved Confounding

author.name: Junzhe Zhang, Jingyuan Chen, Elias Bareinboim

entry.summary: Introduces causal Gaussian processes for robust treatment effect evaluation over continuous treatments and outcomes under unobserved confounding, requiring only basic temporal ordering. Uses a universal discretization of exogenous domains to approximate causal models.

entry.title: SkyJEPA: Learning Long-Horizon World Models for Zero-Shot Sim-to-Real Control of Quadrotors

author.name: Pratyaksh Rao, Wancong Zhang, Randall Balestriero, Yann LeCun, Giuseppe Loianno

entry.summary: SkyJEPA applies a Joint Embedding Predictive Architecture to learn long-horizon latent world models for high-frequency quadrotor control, enabling zero-shot sim-to-real transfer and avoiding autoregressive error amplification. It extends JEPA-style modeling from kinematic planning to real-time agile control.

entry.title: What are Key Factors for Updates in RL for LLM Reasoning?

author.name: Peidong Wang, Demi Wang, Xufang Luo, Jiahang Xu, Xiaocui Yang, Shi Feng, Yuqing Yang, Dongsheng Li

entry.summary: Provides theoretical analysis of RLVR updates, showing off-policy degree (gradient steps per rollout) substantially alters importance sampling ratio distributions and clipping, changing which tokens dominate updates. Aims to explain divergent and contradictory algorithmic choices in RL for reasoning.

entry.title: Tmax: A simple recipe for terminal agents

author.name: Hamish Ivison, Junjie Oscar Yin, Rulin Shao, Teng Xiao, Nathan Lambert, Hannaneh Hajishirzi

entry.summary: Presents Tmax, the strongest open RL recipe for terminal-using agents, achieving 27% on Terminal-Bench 2.0 with only 9B parameters, outperforming larger models. Uses a novel data-generation taxonomy combining difficulty control, personas, and verifier diversification.

entry.title: Black-Box Forensics for Conversational LLM Agents

author.name: Isadora White, Yasaman Jafari, Taylor Berg-Kirkpatrick

entry.summary: Studies black-box forensics for conversational LLM agents, achieving 98% accuracy in attributing the base model behind an endpoint and fingerprinting shared system prompts. Aims at accountability for LLM-enabled scams.

entry.title: Trajectory Forcing: Structure-First Generation with Controllable Semantic Trajectories

author.name: Merve Kocabas, Gege Gao, Bernhard Sch\"olkopf, Andreas Geiger

entry.summary: Proposes Trajectory Forcing, a trajectory-centric generative framework that makes the diffusion/flow generation path explicit, semantic, and editable, progressing from global layout to fine detail in structured stages. Treats intermediate states as interactive objects rather than hidden computation.

entry.title: Robot Self-Improvement via Human-Video Dynamics Models

author.name: Hanzhi Chen, Anran Zhang, Simon Schaefer, Kejia Chen, Shi Chen, Daniel Cremers, Oier Mees, Stefan Leutenegger

entry.summary: Shows that human videos can be used to learn embodiment-agnostic action, dynamics, and value representations that transfer across robot embodiments, enabling robots to evaluate, correct, and autonomously improve their own attempts. Investigates whether human-video priors support embodied practice and learning from failure, not just policy initialization.

entry.title: Not all features are created equal

author.name: enricobottazzi

entry.summary: Proposes AIR, an auto-interpretability router that uses sentence embeddings to classify interpretability features into input/abstract/output categories and routes appropriate activation examples to an auto-interpreter. Claims more accurate and cheaper feature explanations than OpenAI or Neuronpedia baselines.

entry.title: PrivacyAlign: Contextual Privacy Alignment for LLM Agents

author.name: Manveer Singh Tamber, Abhay Puri, Marc-Etienne Brunet, Perouz Taslakian, Jimmy Lin, Spandana Gella

entry.summary: PrivacyAlign centers human judgment in agentic privacy alignment, releasing a dataset of 1,350 samples with 3,516 detailed annotations capturing contextual judgments about appropriate sharing. It addresses the unreliable proxies used by prior privacy training and evaluation.

entry.title: Revelio: Cost-Efficient Agentic Memory Safety Vulnerability Detection For Repository-Scale Codebases

author.name: Yiwei Hou, Hao Wang, Muxi Lyu, Marius Momeu, Eric Nguyen, Taige Yang, Koushik Sen, Dawn Song, David Wagner

entry.summary: Presents Revelio, a cost-efficient agentic framework for memory-safety vulnerability discovery in repository-scale codebases that combats hallucination by generating executable Proofs-of-Vulnerability verified by deterministic sanitizers. Uses cheap LLMs plus static analysis to generate and rank hypotheses.

entry.title: What Does a Chemical Language Model Know About Molecules?

author.name: Christian Kenneth, Etowah Adams, Liam Bai, Gerard JP van Westen

entry.summary: Applies sparse autoencoders to the MolFormer chemical language model to mechanistically examine how molecular representations are built across layers. Finds early layers track position and grammar while later layers encode pharmacologically relevant substructure features.

entry.title: Kamera: Unified Position-Invariant Multimodal KV Cache for Training-Free Reuse

author.name: Bole Ma, Jan Eitzinger, Harald Koestler, Gerhard Wellein

entry.summary: Kamera introduces a position-invariant multimodal KV cache enabling training-free reuse of previously encoded video frames and screenshots regardless of context position. Identifies and recovers the cross-chunk conditioning that naive reuse loses, important for multi-hop reasoning.

entry.title: CELEUS: Certifiable and Efficient LLM Evaluation via E-Processes

author.name: Zhijian Zhou, Zesheng Ye, Zhaorun Chen, Bo Li, Feng Liu

entry.summary: CELEUS provides certifiable, anytime-valid LLM evaluation using e-processes, addressing how existing sequential evaluation methods lose coverage guarantees when confidence intervals are repeatedly updated to decide stopping. Bridges theoretical rigor with practical evaluation.

entry.title: Toward Open Weight Models Without Risks: Separating Public and Private Capabilities in LLMs

author.name: Charbel El Feghali, Arkil Patel, Nicholas Meade, Spandana Gella, Verna Dankers, Siva Reddy

entry.summary: Proposes Tiered Language Models, where a single set of released open weights supports multiple capability levels: a default public configuration behaving conventionally while gating sensitive capabilities. Aims to enable open-weight release without the jailbreak risks of suppression or the closed-service incompatibility of mediated access.

entry.title: FlowDPG: Deterministic Policy Gradient on Flow Matching Policies for Real-World Manipulation

author.name: Kexin Shi, Junyao Shi, Poorvi Hebbar, Zhuolun Zhao, Tarun Amarnath, Yifan Su, Shikhar Bahl, Deepak Pathak

entry.summary: FlowDPG is a DDPG-style off-policy RL method tailored for flow matching policies that distills critic gradients into the velocity field, avoiding the prohibitive backpropagation-through-time along the ODE. It combines demonstration-driven and critic-driven velocity components for real-world manipulation.

entry.title: LLM-Driven Feature Discovery

author.name: Josh Engels

entry.summary: Describes an exploratory LLM-driven feature discovery method that uses an autorater to generate features from transcript pieces, embeds and clusters them, and labels clusters to surface model behaviors in deployment or RL distributions. It aims to find novel behaviors and surprising correlations qualitatively.

entry.title: Fara-1.5: Scalable Learning Environments for Computer Use Agents

author.name: Ahmed Awadallah, Sahil Gupta, Yash Lara, Yadong Lu, Hussein Mozannar, Akshay Nambi, Zach Nussbaum, Yash Pandya, Aravind Rajeswaran, Corby Rosset, Alexey Taymanov, Luiz do Valle, Vibhav Vineet, Spencer Whitehead, Andrew Zhao

entry.summary: Fara-1.5 (FaraGen1.5) is a scalable data pipeline for computer-use agents combining environments, multi-model solver harnesses, and verifiers, using both live and synthetic environments plus a user simulator. From a strong Microsoft team, it addresses the cost of collecting human demonstration data.

entry.title: Can Reasoning Models Detect Changes to their Chains of Thought?

author.name: Sathvik Napa, Utkarsh Singh, Chengyuan Xue, Miriam Wanner, William Walden

entry.summary: The authors test whether reasoning models can detect edits to their own chains of thought (prefilled or modified during/after reasoning), finding only modest detection accuracy and poor ability to identify how the CoT was changed. This matters for the validity of CoT interventions and safety monitoring.

entry.title: Imitation from Heterogeneous Demonstrations using Grounded Latent-Action World Models

author.name: Tianyou Wang, Anson Lei, Joe Watson, Ingmar Posner

entry.summary: This paper proposes grounding action representations in prediction so that actions producing the same environmental effect share a representation regardless of source, enabling imitation from heterogeneous demonstrations without hand-engineered alignment. It uses a grounded latent-action world model for visuomotor policy learning.

entry.title: Beyond the Next Step: Variable-Length Latent World Models for Long-Horizon Planning

author.name: Tianqi Du, Qi Zhang, Yifei Wang, Yisen Wang

entry.summary: Variable-length Latent World Models (VLWMs) learn to predict future latent states over variable horizons rather than single steps, addressing compounding errors and training-planning mismatch in JEPA-style world models for long-horizon planning. It aligns training objectives with downstream planning.

entry.title: All Routes Lead to Collapse

author.name: K. R. Balasubramanian

entry.summary: Argues that attention sinks, representation collapse, and norm stratification are not transformer-specific pathologies but general consequences of content-based routing under a fixed similarity metric. Gives a reframing identity showing softmax attention is blind to key magnitude and tests predictions across nine transformers and graph attention routers.

entry.title: Measuring & Mitigating Over-Alignment for LLMs in Multilingual Criminal Law Courts

author.name: Arthur Wuhrmann, Gaetan Stein, Daniel Brunner, Andrei Kucharavy

entry.summary: Studies over-alignment where LLM guardrails wrongly refuse legitimate legal work involving descriptions of violent or sexual offenses, hampering Swiss court translation and summarization. Introduces TF-RefusalBench, a multilingual benchmark, and mitigation methods.

entry.title: Scaling Linear Mode Connectivity and Merging to Billion Parameter Pretrained Transformers

author.name: Tianyi Li, Zhiqiang Shen

entry.summary: Proposes a scalable framework for linear mode connectivity and model merging at billion-parameter scale using functionality-preserving weight transformations and a dual learning procedure where both models jointly learn alignment toward a shared interpolation path. Extends LMC-based merging beyond prior small-scale limits.

entry.title: Reward-free Pretraining for Reinforcement Learning via Occupancy Coverage Maximization

author.name: Marco Prattic\`o, Pietro Novelli, Massimiliano Pontil, Carlo Ciliberto

entry.summary: Proposes a reward-free pretraining method for RL that maximizes occupancy coverage to learn transferable exploration policies without needing access to extrinsic rewards. This addresses sparse-reward challenges especially relevant to multi-task, meta-, and continual RL settings.

entry.title: RocketPFN: Accurate Time Series Classification via In-Context Learning

author.name: Franco Martino O'Rourke, Ana Trisovic, Dimitris Bertsimas

entry.summary: Presents RocketPFN, a training-free time series classification pipeline combining Rocket random convolutional features with in-context classification via TabPFN v2.5, matching the strongest published method HC2 in mean accuracy. Achieves fast inference without target-data training.

entry.title: On the Curse of Dimensionality in Private Sparse Covariance Estimation and PCA

author.name: Syamantak Kumar, Shourya Pandey, Purnamrita Sarkar, Kevin Tian

entry.summary: Studies high-dimensional differentially private sparse covariance estimation and PCA, showing a poly(k, log d) sample complexity is achievable for PCA under additional eigenvector sparsity, while investigating when the curse of dimensionality is inherent. Provides matching upper and lower bounds.

entry.title: Provably Efficient Policy-Reward Co-Pretraining for Adversarial Imitation Learning

author.name: Tian Xu, Zexuan Chen, Zhilong Zhang, Yi-Chen Li, Chenyang Wang, Lei Yuan, Yang Yu

entry.summary: Provides a systematic theoretical analysis of pretraining's role in adversarial imitation learning, identifying reward error as the dominant suboptimality source and the previously overlooked absence of reward pretraining. Introduces principled policy-reward co-pretraining algorithms.

entry.title: Drowning in Routine: Signal Dilution in Multi-Turn Agent Training

author.name: Yann Pernot (Mila - Qu\'ebec AI Institute, Polytechnique Montr\'eal), Vi Retault (Polytechnique Montr\'eal)

entry.summary: Identifies signal dilution in multi-turn agent training, showing that low decision density (fraction of consequential turns) governs credit-assignment difficulty more than horizon length, with signal-to-noise scaling as the inverse square root of decision density. Provides analysis relevant to GRPO-style trajectory-level estimators.

entry.title: Factored Gossip DiLoCo: Reducing Blocking Communication in DiLoCo

author.name: Chamin Hewa Koneputugodage, Thalaiyasingam Ajanthan, Sameera Ramasinghe, Hadi Mohaghegh Dolatabadi, Shamane Siriwardhana, Gil Avraham, Violetta Shevchenko, Karol Pajak, James Snewin, Alexander Long

entry.summary: Introduces Factored Gossip DiLoCo, which relaxes exact synchronization in distributed training to approximate gossip-based mixing, separating a non-blocking overlapping step from a blocking agreement step. Improves robustness to stragglers and communication failures for low-bandwidth training.

entry.title: Adam Converges in Nonsmooth Nonconvex Optimization

author.name: Zijian Liu

entry.summary: This paper proves convergence of the Adam optimizer in nonsmooth nonconvex settings, which better reflect real neural network training than the smooth analyses common in prior work. It seeks to explain Adam's empirical success across diverse problems.

entry.title: Factual Retrieval in LLMs Is a Redundant, Distributed and Non-Contiguous Process

author.name: Hail Hochman, Natalie Shapira, Yoav Goldberg

entry.summary: Investigates how LLMs transform entity representations to retrieve attributes, using iterative layer patching on LLaMA 3.1 8B and Qwen3 8B. Finds factual retrieval paths are non-contiguous, layer-skipping, and redundant with multiple functionally equivalent paths.

entry.title: Deeper is Not Always Better: Mitigating the Alignment Tax via Confident Layer Decoding

author.name: Xuanming Zhang, Sining Zhoubian, Yuxuan Chen, Tianyi Tang, An Yang, Sean Du, Chujie Zheng, Fei Huang, Dayiheng Liu, Gao Huang, Jingren Zhou

entry.summary: Reveals a Guess-Refine-Perturb dynamic where final LLM layers perturb refined intermediate predictions toward generic alignment-preferred tokens. Proposes Confident Decoding, a training-free method selecting reliable near-final layers via entropy-guided backward search to mitigate alignment tax.

entry.title: NullFlow: One-Step Generative Reconstruction

author.name: Xiao Shi, Edward P. Chandler, Chicago Y. Park, Shirin Shoushtari, Ulugbek S. Kamilov

entry.summary: Proposes NullFlow, a one-step generative reconstruction framework that confines the generative flow to a measurement-consistent subspace, eliminating separate data-fidelity corrections and enabling single-evaluation sampling. Proves the average velocity yields a one-step posterior sampler.

entry.title: Wh0: Generative World Models as Scalable Sources of Egocentric Human Hand Manipulation Data

author.name: Yangtao Chen, Zixuan Chen, Peiyang Wang, Yong-Lu Li, Jing Huo, Jieqi Shi, Yang Gao

entry.summary: Wh0 uses generative video world models conditioned on language, objects, and scenes to synthesize a 50k-episode dataset of egocentric human-hand manipulation, addressing the scale-versus-alignment tradeoff in dexterous manipulation data. It aims to unlock pretrained dexterous VLA capabilities without expensive teleoperation.

entry.title: LIBERO-Safety: A Comprehensive Benchmark for Physical and Semantic Safety in Vision-Language-Action Models

author.name: Rongxu Cui, Zongzheng Zhang, Jingrui Pang, Haohan Chi, Jinbang Guo, Saining Zhang, Shaoxuan Xie, Xin Jin, Yao Mu, Jiaolong Yang, Guocai Yao, Xianyuan Zhan, Ya-Qin Zhang, Hao Zhao

entry.summary: LIBERO-Safety is a parametric safety benchmark that procedurally generates safety-critical manipulation scenarios with a keypose-driven data pipeline yielding nearly 20,000 collision-free demonstrations. A cross-paradigm evaluation of ten VLA and embodied foundation models reveals a critical generalization-versus-safety tension.

entry.title: Advocates Can Influence LLM Values By Editing Wikipedia

author.name: jonahmattwoodward

entry.summary: Summarizes a study showing that strategically editing Wikipedia articles, which are heavily weighted in LLM training data, can measurably shift how models respond on specific topics like animal welfare. It demonstrates a low-cost data-poisoning-adjacent vector for advocacy groups to influence model values.

entry.title: MIRAGE: Stealthy Visual Prompt Injection for Vulnerability Detection in Web Agents

author.name: Xuelong Dai, Jianyu Ma, Boyang Ma, Biwei Yan, Yijun Yang, Yue Zhang

entry.summary: MIRAGE studies stealthy visual prompt injection against MLLM web agents under realistic constraints where an attacker controls only a small legitimate region like an ad slot. It reveals practical vision-based vulnerabilities in browser automation agents.

entry.title: GroundShot: Visually Consistent Multi-Shot Long Video Generation via Entity-Grounded Shot Scheduling

author.name: Yixuan Lai, Tianjia Shao, Kun Zhou, Weijia Dou, Siyu Zhu, Jingdong Wang

entry.summary: GroundShot is a training-free, model-agnostic agentic framework for visually consistent multi-shot long video generation that builds entity-level visual memory from accepted shots and schedules generation to preserve entity appearance. It leverages the insight that the first clear appearance sets the consistency ceiling.

entry.title: Local LLM Agents as Vulnerable Runtimes:A Source-Code Audit of the Agent Runtime Layer

author.name: Zhengsong Zhang, Zongze Li, Jiawei Guo, Haipeng Cai

entry.summary: Conducts a source-code security audit of the agent runtime layer in local LLM agents (prompt builder, parser, tool dispatcher, skill loader, memory writer, permission gate), an implementation boundary unexamined by prior prompt-injection or black-box studies. Treats local agents as privileged, vulnerable runtimes.

entry.title: Keyless Attention: Value-Space Routing and Value-Only Caching for Efficient Transformers

author.name: Xin Gao

entry.summary: Keyless Attention eliminates the key projection, operating over queries and values only with a value-space routing matrix, yielding a value-only cache that halves KV cache memory while matching decode throughput. It frames standard attention as depth-2 and Keyless as a depth-m factorization of the attention bilinear form.

entry.title: DiT-Reward: Generative Representations for Text-to-Image Reward Modeling

author.name: Yuanming Yang, Guoqing Ma, Bo Wang, Yuan Zhang, Wei Tang, Chenyi Li, Haoyang Huang, Nan Duan

entry.summary: DiT-Reward converts a pretrained text-to-image diffusion transformer into a reward model for evaluating generated images by aggregating text-conditioned representations across layers. Outperforms HPSv3 on preference benchmarks under the same training data.

entry.title: Right Knowledge, Wrong Answer: Test-Time Steering for Temporal Fact Conflicts in Open-Weight Language Models

author.name: Elias Hossain, Sourav Saha, Umesh Chandra Biswas, Sanjeda Sara Jennifer

entry.summary: Formalizes Parametric Temporal Conflict where LLMs store both outdated and superseding facts but elicit the outdated one, and introduces Temporal Attractor Steering, a test-time intervention to steer toward newer facts without retraining. Builds an 8,746-record benchmark across four open-weight models.

entry.title: Who Checks the Citations? Benchmarking Legal Hallucination Detection

author.name: Patty Liu, Dominik Stammbach, Peter Henderson

entry.summary: This study benchmarks legal hallucination detection by introducing a taxonomy of citation hallucinations grounded in real court filings and a dataset of 1,300 brief excerpts with injected errors, finding over 1,000 real filings with fabricated citations and a year-over-year increase. It evaluates five models in agentic and non-agentic settings for catching fabricated citations.

entry.title: Cloak: Zero-Shot Cross-Embodiment Manipulation by Masking the End-Effector from the VLA

author.name: Michael Piseno, Guy Tevet, C. Karen Liu

entry.summary: Cloak is a training recipe for zero-shot cross-embodiment VLA transfer that masks the robot's own end-effector from its wrist camera using a real-time rendered geometric mask, enabling embodiment-agnostic visual reasoning. Trained on a single gripper dataset, it transfers zero-shot to unseen embodiments without new data collection.

entry.title: What Shapes Emergent Misalignment? Insights from Training Dynamics, Model Priors, and Data

author.name: Yuchen Zhang, Anietta Weckauff, Diego Garcia-Olano, Maksym Andriushchenko

entry.summary: Investigates what shapes emergent misalignment, where narrow fine-tuning leads to broad misalignment, by examining training dynamics, model priors, and data. Explores relationships between in-domain loss and out-of-domain alignment scores across datasets and model families.

entry.title: AI Alignment From Social Choice Perspectives

author.name: Daniel Halpern, Evi Micha, Ariel D. Procaccia, Benjamin Schiffer, Itai Shapira, Shirley Zhang

entry.summary: A survey examining AI alignment from human feedback through the lens of social choice theory, framing feedback aggregation under conflicting human judgments as a social choice problem. It identifies failure modes in the aggregation layer and a broader design space for handling disagreement.

entry.title: ChainWorld: Composing Long-Horizon Desktop Workloads from Atomic OSWorld Tasks

author.name: Vincent Siu, Manasi Sharma, Dawn Song, Daniel Yue Zhang, Chenguang Wang

entry.summary: ChainWorld converts atomic OSWorld desktop tasks into longer multi-step workloads to test whether computer-use agents can sustain state across objectives, comparing single-turn versus multi-turn presentation. Even strong agents top out near 31% chain completion, exposing a major gap in long-horizon desktop automation.

entry.title: Governance Decay: How Context Compaction Silently Erases Safety Constraints in Long-Horizon LLM Agents

author.name: Shiyang Chen

entry.summary: This paper shows that context compaction in long-running agents can silently delete in-context governance constraints, causing agents to perform later prohibited tool actions, a failure termed Governance Decay. The ConstraintRot benchmark measures violations rising from 0% with the policy in full context to about 30% after compaction across seven model families.

entry.title: MotionPyramid: Hierarchical Motion Representation and Residual Interfaces

author.name: Gao Zhu, Zaishuo Xia, Yubei Chen

entry.summary: MotionPyramid introduces a hierarchical action representation for humanoid control that learns multi-scale motion structure via recursive latent decoders, from immediate motor commands to longer-horizon skills. It draws an analogy to perceptual hierarchies for motion.

entry.title: FirstPass: Grounding AI Scientific Judgment in Multi-Round Editorial Outcomes

author.name: Prabhjot Singh, Somnath Luitel, Manmeet Singh, Josh Durkee

entry.summary: FirstPass introduces a dataset of 3,668 complete multi-round peer-review dialogues from Nature Communications across five scientific domains, and fine-tunes Qwen2.5-7B for review generation, reviewer updating, and editorial judgment. It moves beyond CS-only, single-round review evaluation.

entry.title: FOCA: Future-Oriented Conditioning for Data-Efficient Vision-Language-Action Adaptation

author.name: Duc Minh Nguyen, Nghiem Tuong Diep, Binh Gia Nguyen, Trong-Bao Ho, Doanh Le, Tan Q. Nguyen, Thien-Loc Ha, Nhiem Tran, Bao Thach, Nhat X. Tran, Tuan A. Tran, Artur Habuda, Philip Lund M{\o}ller, Tran Nguyen Le, Daniel Sonntag, Matthias Niepert, Khoa D. Doan, Vu Duong, Hung Ngo, Minh N. Vu, Duy M. H. Nguyen, An Thai Le, Ngo Anh Vien

entry.summary: FOCA is a future-oriented conditioning framework for data-efficient adaptation of Vision-Language-Action models under few-shot imitation, combining explicit prediction of task-grounded future interaction embeddings with implicit alignment to future goals. It addresses sharp performance degradation with fewer demonstrations.

entry.title: Latent Personal Memory: Represent personal memory as dynamic soft prompts

author.name: Debrup Das, Avinash Amballa, Yashas Malur Saidutta, Vijay Srinivasan, Vivek Kulkarni, Srinivas Chappidi

entry.summary: Latent Personal Memory represents user history as a compact matrix of interpretable latent slots mapped via shared cross-attention into dynamic soft prompts prepended to a frozen LLM. It outperforms LoRA and prompt tuning on PersonaMem and LoCOMO benchmarks across Qwen3 backbones.

entry.title: Scalable Hierarchical Attention Transformers for Multi-Turn Jailbreak Detection in Long Conversations

author.name: Chenhui Hu, Muhammed Salih, Sudipto Guha, Subramanian Srinivasan

entry.summary: Introduces an efficient hierarchical attention transformer for multi-turn jailbreak detection that encodes individual turns into compact representations and applies a lightweight conversation module to capture cross-turn escalation without expensive long-context concatenation. Achieves F1 of 0.9394 on 14,038 conversations, outperforming Claude Opus 4.7.

entry.title: MEDLAYXPLAIN: Benchmarking the Expert-Lay Gap in Medical Vision-Language Models

author.name: Han Jang, Junhyeok Lee, Songsoo Kim, Chae Young Lim, Hyeonjin Goh, Heeseong Eum, Kyu Sung Choi

entry.summary: MedLayXPlain introduces a 122K-sample multimodal benchmark for medical lay-language generation, evaluating whether medical vision-language models can translate expert findings into patient-accessible descriptions. It is motivated by the Cures Act mandate for immediate patient access to imaging results.

entry.title: LambdaMark: Semantic Audio Watermarking for Robustness and Radioactivity

author.name: Kexin Li, Xiao Hu, Ilya Grishchenko, David Lie

entry.summary: LambdaMark introduces semantic audio watermarking that embeds signals into higher-level representations rather than waveforms or spectrograms, targeting both robustness to signal manipulations and radioactivity (transfer to downstream finetuned models). It defends against voice cloning and impersonation.

entry.title: Decodable but Not Faithful: Coupling Natural-Language Rationales to Programmatic Verifiers

author.name: Vatsal Ananthula, Adarsh Kumarappan

entry.summary: This work introduces verifier-coupled reasoning, inserting inline claims into reasoning traces and training a consistency head to predict programmatic verifier outputs from rationale hidden states. The central finding is a gap between decodability and faithfulness: verifier info becomes decodable but generation is not guaranteed faithful.

entry.title: Steer, Don't Solve: Training Small Critic Models for Large Code Agents

author.name: Shubham Gandhi, Yiqing Xie, Atharva Naik, Ruichen Zhu, Carolyn Rose

entry.summary: This work freezes a large code agent and trains a small critic providing intra-trajectory steering feedback via supervised fine-tuning, rather than post-hoc scoring of completed trajectories. The critic trained on CWM-32B trajectories transfers to unseen agents on SWE-bench Verified with consistent gains.

entry.title: Harness-MU: A Safe, Governed, and Effective Harness for Multi-User LLM Agents

author.name: Wangxuan Fan, Xiaoyu Nie, Zhongxiang Dai

entry.summary: Harness-MU enforces multi-user, multi-principal governance constraints for LLM agents by treating authorization, restriction, and instruction precedence as deterministic runtime variables enforced by execution rather than probabilistic prompt-based safeguards. It addresses the mismatch between single-user training and multi-principal collaborative deployment.

entry.title: A Verifiable Search Is Not a Learnable Chain-of-Thought

author.name: Harsh Patel

entry.summary: This paper shows that not every short verifiable program can be taught to a model as a learnable chain-of-thought, identifying a class of procedures (e.g., backtracking search in cryptarithm) that fail to install via LoRA distillation while forward-computable tasks transfer well. It distills generator-derived solvers into a 30B Nemotron model across nine reasoning tasks.

entry.title: Modularized Reinforcement Learning on LLMs: From MDP Creation to Exploration and Learning

author.name: Zhao Yang, Yuxuan Jiang, Ting-Chih Chen, Lincen Yang, Annie Wong, Chao Gao, Jacob E. Kooi, Zhong Li, Jiayang Shi, Kevin Qiu, Qi Huang, Xinrui Zu, Shiping Yang, Hengyuan Zhang, Ngai Wong, Filip Ilievski, Shujian Yu, Aske Plaat, Zhaochun Ren, Mark Hoogendoorn, Vincent Fran\c{c}ois-Lavet

entry.summary: A survey organizing reinforcement learning for LLM post-training around three stages: MDP creation, exploration, and learning, situating PPO and GRPO within the broader RL design space. Highlights underexplored alternatives in reward, state/action definition, and exploration.

entry.title: Quantifying Theoretical AI Alignment Guarantees: Receiver-Utility Bounds in Bayesian Persuasion

author.name: Eric Yachbes, Eva Tardos

entry.summary: Provides theoretical AI alignment guarantees via a Bayesian persuasion model, bounding how much useful information can reach a human receiver when a strategic AI sender optimizes a misaligned objective. Derives receiver-utility bounds relative to fully aligned communication.

entry.title: Curriculum Reinforcement Learning Can Incentivize Reasoning Capacity in LLMs Beyond the Base Model

author.name: Pengxiang Cai, Tianchen Fang, Xiaohan Li, Qingyuan Zeng, Guocong Li, Jintai Chen

entry.summary: Presents a boundary-aware Curriculum RL approach that uses pass@k sampling to locate the base model's reasoning capacity boundary and then applies curriculum learning to push beyond it. Challenges the view that RLVR only reallocates probabilities among existing trajectories without expanding capacity.

entry.title: Field-level weak lensing cosmology with $<100$ simulations using multifidelity simulation-based inference

author.name: Alex A. Saoulis, Kiyam Lin, Niall Jeffrey, Maximilian von Wietersheim-Kramsta, Davide Piras, Alessio Spurio Mancini, Ana M. G. Ferreira, Benjamin Joachimi

entry.summary: Performs realistic weak-lensing cosmological inference using field-level neural compression and simulation-based inference with fewer than 100 N-body simulations via multifidelity methods. Extracts more cosmological information than standard two-point statistics under tight compute.

entry.title: Open Problem: Is AdamW Effective Under Heavy-Tailed Noise?

author.name: Dingzhi Yu, Hongyi Tao, Yuanyu Wan, Luo Luo, Lijun Zhang

entry.summary: Poses an open problem on whether AdamW converges under heavy-tailed gradient noise, which characterizes real LLM pretraining, where existing theory only covers finite-variance regimes. Proves a positive weighted-metric benchmark while leaving the general question open.

entry.title: AIR: Adaptive Interleaved Reasoning with Code in MLLMs

author.name: Cong Han, Xiaohan Lan, Haibo Qiu, Yujie Zhong

entry.summary: AIR empowers multimodal LLMs with adaptive interleaved code-based reasoning via reinforcement learning on code-augmented numerical computation tasks. Goes beyond visual-only tool use to handle numerical computation that prior approaches could not.

entry.title: CoorDex: Coordinating Body and Hand Priors for Continuous Dexterous Humanoid Loco-Manipulation

author.name: Sikai Li, Shuning Li, Zhenyu Wei, Yunchao Yao, Chenran Li, Mingyu Ding

entry.summary: CoorDex converts high-dimensional body and dexterous hand control into coordinated latent residual control, enabling continuous dexterous loco-manipulation on the move rather than stop-and-go. Distills motion-tracking teachers into proprioception-conditioned latent priors.

entry.title: Horizon Adaptive Offline Policy Learning via Value Stitching

author.name: Kexin Zheng, Xianyuan Zhan, Xintao Yan

entry.summary: VAST replaces fixed-horizon value backups with dynamic horizon composition (value stitching) for offline policy learning, addressing accumulating bias in TD learning and rigidity of n-step or Q-chunking methods. Aims to capture complex value structures in long-horizon multi-stage tasks.

entry.title: Dead-Direction Signatures: A Cheap Spectral Reading of Singular Complexity

author.name: Tejas Pradeep Shirodkar, P. J. Narayanan

entry.summary: Introduces Dead-Direction Signatures, cheap closed-form spectral readings of a network's singular complexity using activation matrices or Fisher-Gram matrices, replacing expensive SGLD chains for estimating the local learning coefficient. Grounded in singular learning theory.

entry.title: Does RoPE Prevent or Degrade Retrieval Heads? A Mechanistic Analysis Across Model Families

author.name: Cengizhan Bayram

entry.summary: Mechanistically investigates whether rotary position embeddings prevent or degrade retrieval heads across four open-weight 7-8B models and a wide range of the theta base parameter. Confirms retrieval heads are causally necessary, with masking collapsing recall.

entry.title: Post-Training Speech Enhancement Language Models with Perceptual Rewards

author.name: Fr\'ed\'eric Berdoz, Luca A. Lanzend\"orfer, Antonis Asonitis, Roger Wattenhofer

entry.summary: Applies Group Sequence Policy Optimization with multi-metric perceptual rewards (DNSMOS, WER, UTMOS) to post-train autoregressive speech enhancement language models, directly optimizing non-differentiable quality metrics. Achieves SOTA on the DNS2020 benchmark.

entry.title: HERALD: High-Throughput Block Diffusion LLM Serving via CPU-GPU Cooperative KV Cache Retrieval

author.name: Omin Kwon, Doyeon Kim, Jongseok Park, Seung Yul Lee, Ion Stoica, Jae W. Lee

entry.summary: Introduces HERALD, a CPU-GPU cooperative KV cache retrieval system for block diffusion LLM serving that exploits consistent top-k KV relevance across denoising steps to enable sparse offloading. Targets throughput limits of long-context diffusion LLMs.

entry.title: A Framework for Directed Acyclic Hypergraph Learning

author.name: Zhiyuan Dong, Carlos Mundo-Levano, Wei Qian, Daniel Lau, Gonzalo R. Arce

entry.summary: Develops a framework for learning Directed Acyclic Hypergraphs from observational data to capture joint parental causal influences beyond pairwise relationships, using a generalized SEM with a differentiable acyclicity constraint via tensor t-products. Extends continuous DAG learning to higher-order causal structure.

entry.title: Causal Variational Deep Embedding: A Family of Interventional Generators for Confounded Images

author.name: Jingyuan Chen, Kangrui Ruan, Junzhe Zhang

entry.summary: Proposes CauVaDE, a family of interventional generative models for confounded images that, rather than assuming a single causal mechanism, represents a feasible region of interventional distributions consistent with weaker assumptions. Built on an augmented structural causal model.

entry.title: Mat-Pref: Verifiable-Reward Training Improves Compositional Reasoning in Inorganic Materials

author.name: Sarrah R. Mikhail Leung, Taehan Kim, Jeongbin Park

entry.summary: Introduces Mat-Pref, a benchmark of 10,837 ionic-substitution questions across inorganic structure families grounded in DFT, with splits isolating in-distribution, held-out-family generalization, and cross-property transfer. Tests whether RLVR gains in materials reflect transfer versus memorization.

entry.title: Asymptotic Signal Subspace Recovery in Softmax Attention Models

author.name: Lan V. Truong

entry.summary: Studies a stylized softmax-attention model where a query vector is learned by stochastic gradient ascent, deriving the limiting ODE governing learning dynamics and establishing rigorous signal subspace recovery. Advances theoretical understanding of how attention identifies relevant tokens.

entry.title: Escaping the Variance Trap: Jacobian-Free Dynamics for Root-Finding Bilevel Optimization

author.name: Zhiyu Li, Xi Xuan, Davide Carbone

entry.summary: Identifies a variance trap when stochastic root-finding problems (entropy tuning, GAN equilibration) are forced into squared-residual minimization, where implicit Jacobian terms act as noise amplifiers. Proposes a Jacobian-free two-time-scale stochastic approximation solution for root-finding bilevel optimization.

entry.title: Scalable Maximum Entropy Reinforcement Learning for Diffusion Policies via Adjoint Matching

author.name: Serge Thilges, Onur Celik, Denis Blessing, Emiliyan Gospodinov, Gerhard Neumann

entry.summary: Introduces a simulation-free algorithm for optimizing diffusion policies in online RL using adjoint matching from stochastic optimal control, avoiding costly backpropagation through the diffusion process. Targets maximum-entropy RL with diffusion policies.

entry.title: Substitution-Based Analysis of Structural Novelty for Generative Models of Materials

author.name: Masahiro Negishi, Aron Walsh

entry.summary: Develops a workflow to assess whether AI-generated inorganic crystals are genuinely novel or just duplicates/elemental substitutions of training structures. Finds 81-92% of valid metastable generated crystals are reproducible by conventional substitution.

entry.title: Go-with-the-Track: Video Compositing and Motion Control with Point Tracking

author.name: Koichi Namekata, Yash Kant, Zhizheng Liu, Ryan D Burgert, Yuancheng Xu, Kuan Heng Lin, Emmett Steven, Julien Philip, Li Ma, Andrea Vedaldi, Paul Debevec, Ning Yu

entry.summary: Presents Go-with-the-Track, a video model unifying point-track motion control and multi-reference image compositing via reference-anchored point-tracks establishing frame-to-reference correspondences. Targets precise filmmaking control over content insertion and motion.

entry.title: Interleaved Speech Language Models Latently Work In Text

author.name: Talia Sternberg, Gallil Maimon, Yossi Adi

entry.summary: Using the logit lens, this work analyzes interleaved speech-text language models and reveals an implicit transcription phase where spoken-word text tokens become decodable in intermediate layers despite no speech-recognition training. It provides interpretability insight into how the two modalities interact internally.

entry.title: Diffusion Models Adapt to Low-Dimensional Structure Under Flexible Coefficient Choices

author.name: Changxiao Cai, Yuchen Jiao, Gen Li

entry.summary: This paper proves that diffusion models robustly adapt to low-dimensional data structure across a broad class of update-coefficient choices, requiring roughly O(k/epsilon) iterations independent of ambient dimension for epsilon-accurate samples. It shows adaptation is not sensitive to precise coefficient choices.

entry.title: AutoDex: An Automated Real-World System for Dexterous Grasping Data Collection

author.name: Mingi Choi, Gunhee Kim, Jisoo Kim, Taeksoo Kim, Taeyun Ha, Jongbin Lim, Hanbyul Joo

entry.summary: AutoDex is an automated real-world system that closes the full dexterous-grasping data-collection loop, including perception under severe hand-object occlusion, execution, labeling, and reset without human intervention. It verifies candidate grasps on real hardware to certify contact validity at scale.

entry.title: Finetuning with Scientific Data Increases Hallucinations: A Multi-domain Factuality Evaluation of LLMs

author.name: Raia Abu Ahmad, Nikolas Rauscher, Ekaterina Borisova, Fabio Barth, Georg Rehm, Sebastian M\"oller

entry.summary: Introduces SciFactCheck, a 2,500-prompt benchmark across five scientific domains measuring three hallucination types, and finds that scientific fine-tuning paradoxically increases hallucinations. Uses controlled minimal-pairing to compare 18 fine-tuned models against base versions.

entry.title: Are Multilingual Models Actually Improving? Isolating True Cross-Lingual Transfer

author.name: Prasoon Bajpai, Eleftheria Briakou, Colin Cherry, Preethi Jyothi, Vihari Piratla

entry.summary: Argues existing cross-lingual transfer measures conflate transfer with source-language accuracy gains, proposing a Hardness Adjusted Transfer score. Analysis across 20 models and 3 benchmarks finds transfer in small models isn't broken and progress with scale is slower than expected.

entry.title: Does the Same Token Mean the Same State? MoE Routing as Signal for Reasoning Control

author.name: Kang Chen, Minshen Yu, Junjie Nian, Yaoning Wang, Yixin Cao, Yugang Jiang

entry.summary: Shows that in sparse MoE models, the same emitted token id does not imply the same router state; expert routing separates task context, history, and reasoning effort. Operationalizes this as Routing Agreement Decoding for test-time reasoning control near answer-boundary anchors.

entry.title: Honeyquest for LLMs: Rethinking Cyber Deception for AI Attackers

author.name: Kerri Prinos, Lilianne Brush, Cameron Denton

entry.summary: Examines whether LLMs can reliably self-report that their prior response was elicited by an adversarial prefill attack, across ten instruction-tuned models (3B-70B) and four safety benchmarks. Finds no model reliably recognizes compromised outputs (27.3% average claim rate), with signal tied to refusal direction.

entry.title: OTTER: A Red-Teaming System for Toxicity-Evading Jailbreak Prompt Optimization

author.name: Jerry Wang, Hsin-Ling Hsu, Yi-Cheng Lai, Nai-Chia Chen, Fang Yu

entry.summary: Presents OTTER, a black-box red-teaming framework that decouples surface toxicity from adversarial intent by replacing as few as five tokens, raising average attack success from 7.0% to 84.0% on 457 AdvBench prompts across four GPT models. Provides the first quantitative analysis of the toxicity-bypass relationship.

entry.title: Uncertainty-based Debiasing and Unlearning for Decontamination

author.name: Guangzhi Sun, Xiao Zhan, Mark Gales

entry.summary: Proposes a sample-level evaluation framework for benchmark decontamination using distributional distance metrics and an uncertainty-based debiasing/unlearning method. Aims to recover uncontaminated model behavior without requiring a clean reference model.

entry.title: SCOPE: Scale-Consistent One-Pass Estimation of 3D Geometry

author.name: Zheng Zhang, Lihe Yang, Tianyu Yang, Chaohui Yu, Yixing Lao, Xiaoyang Guo, Biao Gong, Fan Wang, Hengshuang Zhao

entry.summary: Presents SCOPE, a one-pass method for scale-consistent 3D geometry estimation from long monocular videos using viewpoint-invariant alignment, appearance-invariant learning, and frequency-modulated positioning for extrapolation. Maintains accuracy and temporal consistency across hundreds of frames.

entry.title: CoDMD: Copula-aware Distribution Matching Distillation for Fast Video Generation

author.name: Wenhu Zhang, Kun Cheng, Changyuan Wang, Shiyao Li, Yuechen Zhang, Wenbo Li, Jiajun Zha, Jingyi Zhang, Kang Zhao, Jiaya Jia

entry.summary: Introduces CoDMD, a copula-aware extension of Distribution Matching Distillation for few-step video generation that regularizes relational geometry across batch elements and frames. It addresses layout instability, oversaturation, and broken motion under low NFE budgets.

entry.title: Surgical Anatomy Recognition with Context Learning using Foundation Representations

author.name: Ronald L. P. D. de Jong, Tim J. M. Jaspers, Raf A. H. Vervoort, Aron F. H. A. Bakker, Yiping Li, Jip L. Tolenaar, Jelle P. Ruurda, Willem M. Brinkman, Josien P. W. Pluim, Marcel Breeuwer, Daan de Geus, Fons van der Sommen

entry.summary: Introduces ATLAS-120k, a large-scale clip-level surgical segmentation dataset with over 120,000 annotated frames across 14 procedures, plus a foundation-representation model framework for anatomy recognition in minimally invasive surgery. Uses a scalable expert-guided annotation pipeline.

entry.title: Unmasking LAION-5B: Age, Gender, Race, and Emotion Biases in Large-Scale Image Datasets

author.name: Iris Dominguez-Catena, Daniel Paternain, Mikel Galar

entry.summary: Performs a comprehensive analysis of demographic and stereotypical biases (age, gender, race, emotion) in the LAION-5B image-text dataset using FairFace, DeepFace, and Emo-AffectNet. Reveals substantial overrepresentation of young White males and other systematic biases.

entry.title: World Action Models: A Survey

author.name: Qiuhong Shen, Shihua Zhang, Yue Liao, Qi Li, Zhenxiong Tan, Shizun Wang, Shuicheng Yan, Xinchao Wang

entry.summary: A survey of World Action Models (WAMs), embodied predictive-action models, that clarifies boundaries between world models, video generation models, vision-language-action policies, and WAMs, organizing existing work along two complementary axes. Provides a common conceptual account for a rapidly expanding field.

entry.title: MeshFlow: Mesh Generation with Equivariant Flow Matching

author.name: Qi Sun, Kiyohiro Nakayama, Jing Nathan Yan, Qixing Huang, Alexander Rush, Leonidas Guibas, Gordon Wetzstein, Jing Liao, Guandao Yang

entry.summary: Proposes MeshFlow, an equivariant flow-matching model that generates triangle meshes directly as permutation-invariant triangle soups, avoiding autoregressive serialization. Modifies the Diffusion Transformer to respect mesh symmetries.

entry.title: OpenHLM: An Empirical Recipe for Whole-Body Humanoid Loco-Manipulation

author.name: Yingdong Hu, Haodong Zhu, Boyuan Zheng, Yihang Hu, Tong Zhang, Zunhao Chen, Junming Zhao, Ruiqian Nai, Yang Gao

entry.summary: OpenHLM presents an empirical recipe for building whole-body native vision-language-action models for humanoid loco-manipulation, mapping language and pixels directly to all degrees of freedom. Through systematic one-variable-at-a-time experiments across teleoperation, VLA design, and co-training, it offers practical findings for unified upper-lower-body control.

entry.title: Asymmetric physics enables efficient learning in quadrupedal robot swarms

author.name: Yuang Zhang, Yunlong Song, Zhihao He, Zelin Ni, Kangyu Wang, Tianchi Liu, Yu Hu, Feng Yu, Danping Zou, Weiyao Lin

entry.summary: Shows that asymmetric physics enables efficient end-to-end learning of vision-based decentralized control in large quadrupedal robot swarms, where standard sampling-based RL becomes inefficient when vision, dense interaction, and contact-rich locomotion are learned jointly. It reproduces animal-like collective navigation in cluttered environments.

entry.title: NLA explanations can be shortened without harming reconstruction

author.name: loops

entry.summary: Reports that natural language autoencoder explanations of LLM activations can be shortened by roughly 40% via a small RL length penalty with minimal loss in reconstruction fidelity. This suggests much of the explanation length is not essential for faithful reconstruction.

entry.title: When Do Intrinsic Rewards Work for Code Reasoning? A Comprehensive Study

author.name: Xiaolong Jin, Xuandong Zhao, Wenbo Guo, Xiangyu Zhang, Dawn Song

entry.summary: A comprehensive empirical study of whether intrinsic reward methods (majority voting, confidence scores) that work for math reasoning transfer to code generation, given code's structural complexity and execution-based verification. From a strong Berkeley/Purdue team including Dawn Song.

entry.title: CheXpercept: A Benchmark for Evaluating Expert-Level Lesion Perception in Chest X-rays

author.name: Geon Choi, Hangyul Yoon, Nalee Kim, Jeong Yun Jang, Hyunju Shin, Hyunki Park, Sang Hoon Seo, Edward Choi

entry.summary: CheXpercept is a sequential multi-level perception benchmark for chest X-ray VLMs mirroring radiologist workflow across coarse detection, fine contour evaluation, and semantic attribute extraction, with 10,400 expert-reviewed QA items. It moves beyond disease-presence classification to evaluate visual grounding.

entry.title: PoLAR: Factorizing Extent and Mode in Latent Actions for Robot Policy Learning

author.name: Youngjoon Jeong, Jihwan Yu, Minsoo Jo, Junha Chun, Taesup Kim

entry.summary: PoLAR factorizes latent actions into transition extent (radius) and transition mode (direction) via a polar radial structure instantiated in hyperbolic space, using temporal offset as a weak proxy for extent. It disentangles representations that prior latent action pretraining methods conflate.

entry.title: Fixed RAG Compression Collapses Measured Reader Scaling

author.name: Sugam Panthi, Rabab Abdelfattah

entry.summary: Demonstrates that fixed RAG compression evaluated on few readers is misleading: across 20 readers compression gain decreases with reader strength, flips model rankings, and hides reader upgrades. Argues compressed evidence layers are not evaluation-neutral.

entry.title: LangMAP: A Language-Adaptive Approach to Tokenization

author.name: Clara Meister, Suchir Salhan, Andrzej Szablewski, Pietro Lesci, Paula Buttery, Tiago Pimentel

entry.summary: Proposes LangMAP, extending UnigramLM to produce language-specific tokenization from a single shared multilingual vocabulary, usable when training from scratch or adapting a pretrained model's tokenizer without changing its vocabulary. Improves tokenization quality without retraining.

entry.title: SATURN: Symbolic Spatial Reasoning for Multi-Perspective Grounding

author.name: Danial Kamali, Tanawan Premsri, Shreya Rajpal, Amir Zadeh, Chuan Li, Parisa Kordjamshidi

entry.summary: Proposes SATURN, a neuro-symbolic framework for perspective-aware compositional spatial reasoning that reconstructs approximate 3D scenes, derives soft perspective-aware predicates, and composes them with a training-free symbolic executor. Introduces 3D FORCE, a diagnostic benchmark controlling reasoning depth and viewpoint.

entry.title: Path-dependent program induction under resource constraints explains human sequence learning

author.name: Hanqi Zhou, David G. Nagy, Peter Dayan, Charley M. Wu

entry.summary: Integrates rate-distortion theory with program induction to model how humans build reusable knowledge from sequences under cognitive resource limits, using a hierarchical Adaptor Grammar. Validated against human melodic sequence-learning experiments.

entry.title: Democratizing and accelerating AI-driven pathology research through agentic intelligence

author.name: Jiabo Ma, Cheng Jin, Yihui Wang, Hao Jiang, Ling Liang, Yingxue Xu, Junlin Hou, Zhengrui Guo, Zhengyu Zhang, Yifei Xia, Hongyi Wang, Fengtao Zhou, Zhe Xu, Huajun Zhou, Jiarui Ouyang, Qian Zeng, On Ki Tang, Eunhyang Park, Carolyn Glass, Ronald Cheong Kin Chan, Li Liang, Hao Chen

entry.summary: PathLab is an autonomous agentic framework translating natural-language research objectives into validated computational pathology workflows by composing domain-specific skills, evaluated across 12 datasets. It lowers the technical barrier for pathology research.

entry.title: Calibration Is Not Control: Why LLM-Agent Oversight Needs Intervention

author.name: Chubin Zhang, Zhenglin Wan, Xingrui Yu, Jingxuan Wu, Qi Wen, Pengfei Zhou, Wangbo Zhao, Ivor Tsang

entry.summary: Argues that calibration is insufficient for LLM-agent oversight, formalizing target error and proposing intervention advantage, the expected utility gain from intervening rather than continuing, as the correct decision object. Two prefixes with the same risk may require different actions based on recoverability.

entry.title: Learning the ARTS of Search for Automated Discovery

author.name: Gurusha Juneja, Arnav Kumar Jain, Deepak Nathani, William Yang Wang, Xin Eric Wang

entry.summary: ARTS deploys a reasoning language model to navigate the hypothesis-experiment search tree for automated discovery, separating hypothesis merit from execution quality and diagnosing why prior attempts failed instead of pruning history. It improves over MCTS-style heuristics.

entry.title: Human vs Machine Mathematical Difficulty on Project Euler: An Experimental Analysis

author.name: David Holmes, Johannes Schmitt

entry.summary: Using 3840 attempts across 50 Project Euler problems and 26 model configurations, this study tests whether AI token cost scales with human solve time via a power law, finding exponents below 1 and thus not supporting an earlier prediction that machines find hard human problems disproportionately costly. It is a clean empirical scaling analysis.

entry.title: Geometry-Aware Online Scheduling for LLM Serving: From Theoretical Bound to System Practice

author.name: Li Kong, Qi Qi, Yinyu Ye, Zijie Zhou

entry.summary: This work proposes geometry-aware online scheduling for LLM serving, introducing a Smallest Volume First algorithm (and a 1-bit variant) that models the 2D spatio-temporal growth of KV-cache memory rather than relying on time-only heuristics like Shortest Job First. It provides theoretical bounds and system practice.

entry.title: PlanBench-XL: Evaluating Long-Horizon Planning of LLM Tool-Use Agents in Large-Scale Tool Ecosystems

author.name: Jiayu Liu, Qihan Lin, Cheng Qian, Rui Wang, Emre Can Acikgoz, Xiaocheng Yang, Jiateng Liu, Zhenhailong Wang, Xiusi Chen, Heng Ji, Dilek Hakkani-T\"ur

entry.summary: PlanBench-XL is an interactive benchmark of 327 retail tasks over 1,665 tools that evaluates whether agents can iteratively discover and chain tools under retrieval-limited visibility, with an optional blocking mechanism simulating missing or failing tools. It probes long-horizon planning in large tool ecosystems.

entry.title: MindAlign: Decoding Inner Speech from fMRI Signals via Multimodal Embedding Alignment under Limited Data

author.name: Muxuan Liu, Ichiro Kobayashi, Satoshi Nishida

entry.summary: MindAlign proposes a two-stage brain-to-language framework that decodes inner speech from fMRI signals by aligning neural activity to a shared multimodal semantic space, without fine-tuning the underlying language model. It addresses data scarcity and inter-subject variability in non-invasive brain decoding.

entry.title: Video2Code: Generating Interactive Webpages from UI Videos via Action-Aware Revisit

author.name: Mingde Xu, Zhen Yang, Yan Wang, Yu Wang, Xijun Liu, Zijun Dou, Wenyi Hong, Xiaotao Gu, Bin Xu, Jie Tang

entry.summary: Video2Code generates interactive webpages from UI interaction videos by recovering executable state transitions, addressing state-transition misalignment that sparse sampling causes. It uses an action-aware revisit mechanism to capture short action boundaries.

entry.title: Beyond 'One Language, One Script': Quantifying Orthographic Bias in Multilingual VLMs with PuMVR

author.name: Prabhjot Singh, Bhushan Pawar, Madhu Reddiboina

entry.summary: PuMVR is the first benchmark quantifying script-dependent bias in multilingual VLMs using 375 culturally grounded Punjabi tasks across Gurmukhi, Shahmukhi, and Roman scripts. It exposes a substantial Script Gap where models solve puzzles in one script but fail equivalents in others.

entry.title: Formally Verified Code Synthesis for Structured Data Translation in a Medical Internet of Things

author.name: Colin Samplawski, Adam D. Cobb

entry.summary: Presents an LLM-powered evolutionary code synthesis system with an integrated formal verification step for structured data translation in medical IoT, demonstrated on translating a pulse oximeter's JSON schema to FHIR format. Guarantees generated code meets predefined requirements.

entry.title: A3C3: AI Algorithm and Accelerator Co-design, Co-search, and Co-generation

author.name: Selin Yildirim, Yingbing Huang, Deming Chen

entry.summary: A3C3 is a holistic methodology that jointly optimizes neural network architectures and their hardware accelerator implementations through co-design, co-search, and co-generation. It parameterizes both algorithmic and hardware spaces to overcome inefficiencies of separate-stage design flows.

entry.title: Whose Agent Are You? Multi-Layer Fingerprinting and Attribution of Autonomous Web Agents

author.name: Dayeon Kang, Hyejun Jeong, Jade Sheffey, Pubali Datta, Amir Houmansadr

entry.summary: Demonstrates multi-layer fingerprinting of autonomous web agents using network-layer characteristics and browser interaction behavior to distinguish AI agents from humans and traditional crawlers across six agent frameworks. Addresses the inadequacy of robots.txt against indiscriminate scraping.

entry.title: Is Our Benchmark Enough? An Analysis of Continual Learning for MLLMs

author.name: Van-Tuan Tran, Shruthi Gowda, Merim Dzaferagic, Marco Ruffini

entry.summary: Revisits continual learning benchmarks for MLLMs, showing a training-free, replay-free prototypical routing method matches the MLLM-based router of MR-LoRA at far lower cost, and that shared experts do not improve continual learning. Challenges assumptions in the state-of-the-art MR-LoRA method.

entry.title: Chem2Gen-Bench: Benchmarking Chemical-to-Genetic Translation in Perturbation Response Space

author.name: Yuxiang Lin, Ying Chen

entry.summary: Chem2Gen-Bench is a benchmark with over 260,000 chemical and 1.09 million genetic perturbation profiles organized into cell-target contexts to test target-matched chemical-to-genetic translation in perturbation response space. It finds translation fidelity measurable but heterogeneous across matched contexts.

entry.title: MammoExpert: Benchmarking Chain-of-Thought Reasoning in Mammography Diagnosis

author.name: Di Dai, Bo Liu, Youcheng Li, Haojun Yu, Zhouhang Bian, Quanlin Wu, Dong Wang, Sichen Meng, Hongye Xuan, Zijie Lan, Shenda Hong, Liwei Wang

entry.summary: MammoExpert is the first mammography dataset with Chain-of-Thought reasoning annotations across primal observation, factual assessment, and diagnostic synthesis phases, covering 2,379 images and 67 WHO histopathology subtypes with features annotated by nine radiologists. It enables benchmarking structured diagnostic reasoning.

entry.title: OmniV2X: A Generative Foundation Planner for Efficient End-to-End Cooperative Driving

author.name: Juntong Peng, Juanwu Lu, Yupeng Zhou, Can Cui, Yaobin Chen, Ziran Wang

entry.summary: OmniV2X is a generative foundation model for vehicle-to-everything cooperative driving that interprets independent multi-modal, multi-agent observation sequences rather than fusing them into a shared representation. It uses an end-to-end supervised pipeline with a trajectory generation loss and cross-attention injection to reduce compute and improve standardized messaging compliance.

entry.title: Task-Differentiated Atomic Skill Expansion and Routing for Continual Learning Across Highly Heterogeneous Tasks

author.name: Jiacheng Wang, Xinjia He, Qi Ding, Yutao Yang, Jie Zhou, Liyang Yu, Liang Dou, Qin Chen

entry.summary: This work benchmarks six frontier and open-weight models on detecting real-world web vulnerabilities (SQL injection, stored XSS, path traversal, RCE) via static analysis in WordPress plugins, across five prompt designs. It analyzes how model and prompt choice affect detection effectiveness. The study evaluates established models including Claude Opus 4.6 and GPT-5.4 rather than announcing new ones.

entry.title: Ramanujan Graph Rewiring with Non Negative Resistance Curvature

author.name: Hugo Attali, Rachid El Jouhri

entry.summary: This work introduces Ramanujan Propagation, a graph rewiring strategy using Ramanujan graphs to alleviate over-squashing in GNNs, proving that suitable Ramanujan graphs guarantee non-negative resistance curvature. It connects spectral graph theory to information flow in message passing.

entry.title: Scene-Level Heterogeneous Physics Simulation with 3D Gaussian Splats

author.name: Xiaoyang Liu, Shangzhe Wu, Kai Han

entry.summary: This work enables 3D Gaussian Splatting assets to participate in scene-level heterogeneous multi-solver physical simulations, bridging the gap between 3DGS rendering and production physics engines. It supports interaction with complex static collision geometry and heterogeneous assets beyond prior object-centric setups.

entry.title: AgentDSE: Reasoning-Augmented Architectural Design Space Exploration

author.name: Chenyu Wang, Jiahe Caroline Shi, David Kong, Duane S. Boning, Zishen Wan, Yilun Du, Vijay Janapa Reddi

entry.summary: AgentDSE is a simulator-in-the-loop methodology where a general-purpose LLM coding agent automates architectural design space exploration by reasoning through physical constraints and bottlenecks, without fine-tuning or precomputed databases. It aims to replace inefficient black-box optimization with human-like architectural reasoning.

entry.title: AI-Mediated Negotiation: Design Reflections and Lessons

author.name: Veda Duddu, Jash Rajesh Parekh, Andy Mao, Hanyi Min, Ziang Xiao, Vedant Das Swain, Koustuv Saha

entry.summary: This work builds Trucey, a theory-driven AI negotiation coaching system, and tests four design assumptions via a preregistered experiment (N=267) and interviews (N=15). Notably, a static handbook control outperformed both AI conditions on empowerment and usability, prompting reflection on why each assumption failed.

entry.title: Old Fictions, New Skins: Evaluating the Manipulative Capabilities of LLMs in Healthcare

author.name: Gathoni Ireri, Roger D. Odipo

entry.summary: Reports a randomized experiment with 303 Kenyan participants testing whether manipulative LLM variants (ChatGPT 5.2, DeepSeek V3.2) can covertly steer users toward incorrect treatment decisions. Found higher manipulation success in the manipulative condition, raising safety concerns for African healthcare deployments.

entry.title: Flow Annealing Posterior Sampling for Function-Space Regression and Inverse Problems

author.name: Yaozhong Shi, Zachary E. Ross, Yisong Yue

entry.summary: Introduces Flow Annealing Posterior Sampling (FAPS), described as the first function-space posterior sampling framework unifying stochastic-process regression and PDE inverse problems atop pretrained flow-matching priors. Enables likelihood-guided inference from sparse, noisy observations with variable query discretizations.

entry.title: Rethinking Molecular Graph Backdoors under Chemistry-aware Admission

author.name: Thinh T. H. Nguyen, Sze Jue Yang, Khoa D. Doan, Chee Seng Chan, Kok-Seng Wong

entry.summary: Reframes molecular graph backdoor attacks by introducing ChemGuard, an admission protocol requiring submitted molecules to survive parsing, sanitization, and consistency checks. Shows many existing graph backdoors fail when chemistry-aware validation is enforced.

entry.title: ReasoningLens: Hierarchical Visualization and Diagnostic Auditing for Large Reasoning Models

author.name: Jun Zhang, Jiasheng Zheng, Boxi Cao, Yaojie Lu, Hongyu Lin, Jia Zheng, Xianpei Han, Le Sun

entry.summary: ReasoningLens is an open-source framework for hierarchically visualizing and auditing long chain-of-thought traces from large reasoning models. It structures traces into interactive hierarchies and uses an agentic auditor for automated error detection.

entry.title: RECALL: Recovery Experience Collection for Active Lifelong Learning in Vision-Language-Action Models

author.name: Ulas Berk Karli, Tesca Fitzgerald

entry.summary: RECALL proposes active, uncertainty-guided data collection for continual fine-tuning of vision-language-action models, contrasting it with passive imitation that requires failures first. Shows active collection is more efficient but reveals nuances in fine-tuning strategy.

entry.title: Semantic Browsing: Controllable Diversity for Image Generation

author.name: Sara Dorfman, Maya Vishnevsky, Omer Dahary, Or Patashnik, Daniel Cohen-Or

entry.summary: Introduces controlled diversity for text-to-image generation enabling Semantic Browsing, where users navigate structured galleries along interpretable axes of variation rather than incidental noise. Addresses mode collapse toward single visual interpretations.

entry.title: Temporal Causal Prior-Data Fitted Networks for Panel Data with Learned Reliability Signals

author.name: Shravan Talupula, Saurabh Sharma

entry.summary: TCPFN is a prior-data fitted network foundation model for zero-shot temporal causal discovery on panel data with learned per-pair reliability signals. Extends causal PFNs from static to temporal settings with a causal judgment head predicting null-effect probability and confounding.

entry.title: Grouped Query Experts: Mixture-of-Experts on GQA Self-Attention

author.name: Vishesh Tripathi, Abhay Kumar

entry.summary: Grouped Query Experts adds a mixture-of-experts layer atop grouped-query attention, routing tokens to a subset of query-head experts while keeping key-value heads dense and unchanged. Aims to save attention compute while preserving GQA KV-cache benefits.

entry.title: Formalizing Task-Space Complexity for Zero-Shot Generalization

author.name: Jung-Hoon Cho, Heling Zhang, Siqi Du, Roy Dong, Cathy Wu

entry.summary: Introduces a performance-centric directional task-dissimilarity measure (signed divergence) that upper-bounds the zero-shot generalization gap between contexts in contextual dynamical systems. Yields a notion of task-space complexity counting source contexts needed to certify generalization.

entry.title: DCD-PFN: A Decoupling-Aware Foundation Model for Causal Discovery

author.name: Zhengkang Guan, Yikang Chen, Yi He, Yunze Tong, Zijing Hu, Haoyuan Qian, Fei Wu, Kun Kuang

entry.summary: DCD-PFN is a decoupling-aware prior-data fitted network foundation model for causal discovery that focuses on local causal discovery rather than amortizing global graph reconstruction. Pretrained on diverse synthetic structural causal models for zero-shot inference.

entry.title: VLA-FAIL: Efficient Task Failure Detection for Finetuned Vision-Language-Action Models

author.name: Florian Seligmann, Emiliyan Gospodinov, Enes Ulas Dincer, Gerhard Neumann

entry.summary: Proposes VLA-FAIL, a lightweight runtime failure detector for vision-language-action robotics models using last-layer Mahalanobis distance and a second detector, without requiring failure data or expensive action sampling. Targets safe real-world deployment of VLAs.

entry.title: Universal Encoders for Modular Relational Deep Learning

author.name: Jakub Pele\v{s}ka, Gustav \v{S}\'ir

entry.summary: Introduces a modular Relational Deep Learning approach with universal encoders that decouples row encoding from graph message-passing, enabling cross-schema generalization across multi-tabular databases. Establishes four design pillars for foundational relational models.

entry.title: A Causal DAG Prior for Synthetic Time-Series Classification Datasets

author.name: Franco Martino O'Rourke, Ana Trisovic, Dimitris Bertsimas

entry.summary: Introduces a causal DAG prior that synthesizes complete labeled multivariate time-series classification datasets with cross-modal causal structure for prior-data fitted networks. Validated by finetuning TabPFN v2.5 on 75 UCR/UEA datasets.

entry.title: Prefix-Guided On-Policy Distillation: Mining Golden Trajectories from Rollouts

author.name: Qingfei Zhao, Huan Song, Shuyu Tian, Jiawei Shao, Xuelong Li
