entry.summary: Circumvents the price-of-adaptivity barrier in stochastic convex optimization by assuming model-loss decomposition and clipping model outputs in tail events relative to a reference model. Achieves improved adaptation bounds.

entry.title: FlowTrain: Flow-Based Decoupled Training for Industrial-Grade Vision-Language Models

author.name: Zhida Jiang, Zhaolong Xing, Yang Pei, Xiaolong Chen, Yuanhang Xiao, Chengzhi Huang, Xiyu Liu, Haopeng Liu, Qingyuan Sang, Lingfeng Zhou, Jiaxing Wang, Zicheng Zhang, Wenzhe Wang, Xinyu Liu, Yan Li, Zhen Chen, Ke Zhang

entry.summary: Presents FlowTrain, a flow-based decoupled training framework for vision-language models using a producer-consumer dataflow over a unified memory pool, letting encoder and backbone progress independently. Improves industrial-scale VLM training efficiency.

entry.title: Quantifying the Agreement Between Data-Influence and Data-Similarity to Understand LLM Behavior

author.name: Christopher J. Anders, Henrique Da Silva Gameiro, Nico Daheim, Mohammad Emtiyaz Khan

entry.summary: Quantifies the agreement between data-influence and data-similarity measures for tracing LLM outputs back to training data by ranking documents and computing overlap. Finds the rankings agree significantly but with an asymmetry between top documents of each measure.

entry.title: On the Limits of Prompt-Conditioned Language Models as General-Purpose Learners

author.name: David Mguni, Julian Ma, Jun Wang

entry.summary: Argues that prompt-conditioned LLMs face a fundamental expressivity floor because language is a capacity-limited interface for conveying tasks, modeling user-system interaction as a bilevel cheap-talk game. Derives PAC-Bayes bounds separating estimation error from irreducible structural limitations.

entry.title: VeriBound: PAC-Bayesian Generalization Bounds for Process Reward Models Trained with Formal Verification Tools

author.name: Amirul Rahman, Mohammed Sabih Alsharari

entry.summary: Proposes VeriBound, a PAC-Bayesian theoretical framework providing generalization bounds for Process Reward Models trained on formal-verification-tool labels (FOVER-style). Explains the empirically observed cross-task generalization from symbolic tasks to reasoning benchmarks.

entry.title: ASCII Art Turns LLMs into VLA Controllers

author.name: Yitao Jiang, Roy Xing, Luyang Zhao, Brian Plancher, Muhao Chen, Devin Balkcom

entry.summary: Shows that a text-only LLM can be adapted into a vision-language-action controller by rendering visual observations as ASCII text, enabling existing LLM training stacks to condition on visual state. Compares fine-tuned LLMs and VLMs across families and scales.

entry.title: Spectrally Safe Neural Operator Warm-Starts for Large-Scale Newton Solvers

author.name: Jaemin Oh, Youngkyu Lee, Jerome Darbon, George Em Karniadakis

entry.summary: Shows that neural operators used to warm-start Newton solvers can produce initial states with indefinite Jacobians despite low average test error, because mean-squared error misses localized physics violations. Diagnoses this for hyperelasticity via predicted volume change dispersion.

entry.title: Any-Body Guard: Universal Safeguarding for Manipulation Policies via Action Masking

author.name: Alex Beaudin, Hanna Krasowski, Kartik Nagpal, Sanjit A. Seshia, Murat Arcak, Negar Mehr

entry.summary: X-Safe proposes a universal action-masking safeguard for robotic manipulation that reasons in configuration space to give formal probabilistic collision-avoidance guarantees that transfer across embodiments. It aims to replace heuristic fallback controllers with a lightweight, transferable safety layer.

entry.title: Chains That See, Answers That Don't: A Multi-Aspect Evaluation Recipe for Forced Chain-of-Thought on Video-MME

author.name: Zhichao Fan, Yanhang Li, Zexin Zhuang

entry.summary: This paper proposes a three-probe evaluation recipe to test whether forced chain-of-thought improves video question answering, applying it to Qwen2.5-VL on Video-MME with counterfactual video-swaps and visual-degradation ladders. It finds CoT chains are video-conditioned yet do not necessarily improve final answers.

entry.title: Incremental Learning in Mirror Flows

author.name: Rapha\"el Berthier, Loucas Pillaud-Vivien

entry.summary: This paper studies mirror flows under a convex quadratic loss and general convex mirror potentials, showing that initialization near the domain boundary yields rescaled trajectories converging to a limiting flow whose potential is the domain indicator. This characterization provides a general mechanism for incremental learning in mirror flows.

entry.title: Storyline Trees: Hierarchical Representations for Long-Form Narratives

author.name: Litu Ou, Mirella Lapata

entry.summary: This work constructs storyline trees, hierarchical representations organizing long-form narratives from global themes to fine-grained events, built via complementary top-down and bottom-up procedures over scene segments. It aims to make implicit narrative structure navigable for long-context models.

entry.title: When to Plan, When to Polish: Noise Level as a Granularity Axis for Diffusion Language Models

author.name: Peihong Li, Yuanjie Shi, Yan Yan

entry.summary: Proposes Noise Dependent Granularity Control for diffusion language models, using noise level as a granularity cue so high-noise steps use coherent token groups for planning while low-noise refines wording. Avoids extra planners or two-stage designs.

entry.title: Beyond Value Benchmarks: Measuring Value-Structure Alignment in Large Language Models via Symmetric Q-Sorts

author.name: Jingting Zheng (TJUNLP Lab, School of Computer Science, Technology, Tianjin University, Tianjin, China), Yuqi Ren (TJUNLP Lab, School of Computer Science, Technology, Tianjin University, Tianjin, China), Linhao Yu (TJUNLP Lab, School of Computer Science, Technology, Tianjin University, Tianjin, China), Yongqi Leng (TJUNLP Lab, School of Computer Science, Technology, Tianjin University, Tianjin, China), Deyi Xiong (TJUNLP Lab, School of Computer Science, Technology, Tianjin University, Tianjin, China)

entry.summary: Proposes a symmetric Q-methodology framework where humans and LLMs sort 140 moral statements into a forced distribution to measure value-structure alignment as a cohesive system. Establishes a three-factor human reference geometry to compare against model rankings.

entry.title: Knowledge-Graph Grounding Helps LLMs Only for Out-of-Training Knowledge: A Controlled Study on Clinical Question Answering

author.name: Madhulatha Mandarapu, Sandeep Kunkunuru

entry.summary: Reproduces a Nature Medicine finding that frontier LLMs beat specialized retrieval tools, flagging a grader bug, and shows knowledge-graph grounding only helps for out-of-training knowledge in clinical QA. Establishes a knowledge-boundary result for when grounding adds value.

entry.title: Same question, different history: language, national identity, and credit in large language models

author.name: William Guey, Pierrick Bougault, Wei Zhang, Vitor D. de Moura, Jos\'e O. Gomes

entry.summary: Analyzes 11 LLMs across 21 disputed inventions in 12 languages (75,896 responses), showing query language systematically affects which claimant is surfaced. Lower-status claimants appear more when asked in their associated language while Anglophone figures stay stable.

entry.title: Towards Root Memories: Benchmarking and Enhancing Implicit Logical Memory Retrieval for Personalized LLMs

author.name: Hongxun Ding, Xiang Yu, Chengbing Wang, Jianfei Xiao, Keqin Bao, Wenjie Wang, Xiangnan He

entry.summary: Constructs IMLogic, the first benchmark for implicit logical memory retrieval in long dialogues where logically critical memories have limited semantic overlap. Introduces root memory, a structured decision-preserving representation, and RootMem to distill reusable personalized logic.

entry.title: Can LLMs Reliably Self-Report Adversarial Prefills, and How?

author.name: Quang Minh Nguyen, Uzair Ahmed, Taegyoon Kim

entry.summary: Introduces EnterpriseClawBench, built from 852 reproducible tasks derived from real proprietary workplace agent sessions with recovered fixtures, role classes, and semantic rubrics. The best configuration (Codex with GPT-5.5) reaches only 0.663, highlighting headroom; data not released for privacy.

entry.title: Cross-National Information Attacks: A Two-Decade Analysis of Troll Behavior in Korea

author.name: Jaehong Kim, Hyeonseung Kim, Jiseon Kim, Alice Oh, Thorsten Holz, Wonjae Lee, Meeyoung Cha

entry.summary: Develops an explainable ML framework for detecting state-linked troll activity in Korean news comments along foreign origin, moral-emotional framing, and target country dimensions. Applied to 112M comments over two decades for longitudinal influence analysis.

entry.title: CogniRoute: Learning to Route Social Evidence in Omni-Modal Models

author.name: Yifan Shen, Pei Tian, Xinzhuo Li, Bowen Fang, Shujun Xia, Bingxuan Li, Ana Jojic, Wenming Ye, Xu Cao, James Matthew Rehg, Ismini Lourentzou

entry.summary: Introduces CogniRoute, a schema-guided Mixture-of-Experts framework for social omni-modal reasoning that routes evidence by cross-modal relation, reasoning demand, and temporal scope. Adds route-aware reinforcement learning for social video QA.

entry.title: SARIF: Segment Anything for Robust Image Forensics

author.name: Dong-Hyun Moon, Ju-Hyeon Nam, Sang-Chul Lee

entry.summary: Proposes SARIF, leveraging the Segment Anything Model with a feedback-guided mask decoder and dual-encoder for robust image forgery localization. Improves cross-domain generalization over benchmark-tuned forensics models.

entry.title: RAPID: A Reproducible Multi-Agent Pipeline for Interpretable Disaster Damage Assessment from Satellite and Street-View Imagery

author.name: Yifan Yang, Wenjing Gong, Kaili Zhang, Lei Zou, Zhengzhong Tu, Hao Li, Zongrong Li, Xinyue Ye

entry.summary: Presents RAPID, a reproducible multi-agent pipeline combining satellite and street-view imagery for interpretable disaster damage assessment, addressing generalization under domain shift and long-tailed distributions. It performs damage-level, damage-type, and reasoning-based assessment.

entry.title: Resolving Multi-Target Association in OFDM-based ISAC via Vision-aided Multi-Modal Learning

author.name: Meng Hua, Chenghong Bian, Deniz Gunduz

entry.summary: Proposes a vision-assisted OFDM-ISAC framework that fuses transmitted street-view imagery (via deep joint source-channel coding) with radar sensing to resolve multi-target association ambiguity in delay-Doppler maps. Tackles a fundamental limitation of peak-searching approaches.

entry.title: Curvature-Adaptive Consistency Flow Matching: Autonomous Trajectory Optimization via Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Songtao Tian, Guhan Chen, Bohan Li, Jingyi Ma, Zixiong Yu

entry.summary: Proposes Curvature-Adaptive Consistency Flow Matching (CACFM), revealing a U-shaped difficulty profile in consistency distillation and using reinforcement learning to dynamically optimize the sampling trajectory. Targets boundary-stage optimization bottlenecks.

entry.title: Gen2Balance: Generative Balancing for Long-Tailed Video Action Recognition

author.name: Prajwal Gatti, Simon Jenni, Fabian Caba Heilbron, Dima Damen

entry.summary: Proposes Gen2Balance, using a text-to-video generative model conditioned on action-grounded prompts to augment long-tailed video action recognition datasets into balanced real-plus-generated sets. Uses a two-stage training strategy to mitigate domain shift.

entry.title: Catching Lies Without Sending the Video: Privacy-Preserving Multimodal Deception Detection

author.name: Nikita Sharma, Pranav Sara, Karan Singla

entry.summary: Demonstrates privacy-preserving multimodal deception detection by extracting a compact on-device digest (transcript, emotion, prosody, facial behavior) instead of streaming raw video, matching frontier model performance (AUC 0.74-0.76) at 7.8x fewer tokens. Tested on the Real-life Trial Deception dataset.

entry.title: READ More than What You See: Reinforcement Learning for Accurate and Coherent Audio Description Generations

author.name: Bo Fang, Xinyao Zhang, Yuxin Song, Hui Zhang, Hang Zhou, Antoni B. Chan

entry.summary: Presents READ, the first reinforcement-learning framework for training-based audio description generation, using sequence-level optimization with reference-matching, length, format, and a context-aware coherence reward. Targets concise narrations for blind and low-vision audiences.

entry.title: LoCC: Detection and Localization of Lip-Syncing Deepfakes via Counterfactual Frame Consistency

author.name: Soumyya Kanti Datta, Shan Jia, Siwei Lyu

entry.summary: Proposes LoCC, a framework for detecting and localizing lip-syncing deepfakes at segment and frame levels by checking whether each frame aligns with a counterfactual estimate generated from temporal neighbors. Real videos show stable consistency while lip-sync deepfakes introduce localized inconsistencies.

entry.title: CoVStream: Edge-Cloud Collaboration for Understanding of Long Video Streams

author.name: Xu Liu, Guikun Chen, Zihao Yan, Kanzhi Wu, Wenguan Wang

entry.summary: Proposes CoVStream, the first edge-cloud collaborative framework for understanding long video streams, where edge nodes distill raw streams into compact features and captions to minimize bandwidth while cloud handles strong reasoning. Addresses the deployment reality of computationally constrained source devices.

entry.title: SPAR: Semantic-Pixel Self-Alignment and Adaptive Routing for Unified Multimodal Models

author.name: Hongxiang Li, Hongxu Chen, Chenyang Zhu, Xiaoshuang Huang, Jiayin Cai, Xiaolong Jiang, Yao Hu, Long Chen

entry.summary: Proposes SPAR, a unified multimodal framework with semantic-pixel self-alignment and adaptive routing to bridge the gap between semantic understanding and pixel-level generation in MLLMs. Aims to give semantic encoders high-fidelity reconstruction without external teachers.

entry.title: Dense Reward for Multi-View 3D Reasoning with Global Maps and Local Views

author.name: Jiho Choi, Seonho Lee, Seojeong Park, Hyunjung Shim

entry.summary: Proposes DR-MV3D, a map-grounded learning framework providing dense, verifiable rewards to supervise multi-view 3D visual question answering, decomposing it into global map construction, view-trajectory planning, and egocentric grounding. Addresses inconsistent cross-view reasoning from sparse answer-level supervision.

entry.title: Pose Anything Anywhere:Model-free Object Poses from Arbitrary References

author.name: Hongli Xu, Jiaqi Hu, Junwen Huang, Boyang Zhong, Peter KT Yu, Nassir Navab, Benjamin Busam, Slobodan Ilic

entry.summary: Presents PANY, a unified model-free framework for estimating 6D pose of unseen objects from one or sparse pose-free reference views, supporting both RGB and RGB-D inputs via a multi-view transformer geometry backbone. Moves beyond pairwise single-anchor matching to handle occlusion and large viewpoint changes.

entry.title: IMAGIN-4D: Image-Guided Controllable Interaction Generation

author.name: Sai Kumar Dwivedi, Federica Bogo, Bu\u{g}ra Tekin, Chenhongyi Yang, Nadine Bertsch, Tomas Hodan, Michael J. Black, Dimitrios Tzionas, Shreyas Hampali

entry.summary: Proposes IMAGIN-4D, a diffusion-based human-object interaction generation method that uses a reference image as a visual specification to resolve ambiguity in grasps, poses, contacts, and layouts that text and trajectories underspecify. Uses per-cue representations rather than a single global image embedding.

entry.title: Non-line-of-sight imaging with arbitrary relay surface geometries via 3D Gaussian Transient Rendering

author.name: Yi Wang, Ziyu Zhan, Yuran Wang, Hao Wang, Qiang Liu, Zuoqiang Shi, Lingyun Qiu, Xing Fu

entry.summary: Proposes a non-line-of-sight imaging pipeline using 3D Gaussian transient rendering that imposes no geometric assumptions on the relay surface and supports both confocal and non-confocal configurations. Addresses real-world NLOS conditions that violate planar-wall and dense-sampling assumptions.

entry.title: Lighting-Consistent Object Transfer Across Radiance Fields

author.name: Nicol\'as Violante, George Kopanas, Linus Franke, Julien Philip, George Drettakis

entry.summary: Introduces a diffusion model that harmonizes lighting when compositing objects between 3D Gaussian Splatting scenes, enabling realistic object transfer for VFX and design. Trained on a mixed synthetic, generated, and real dataset.

entry.title: Geometric Entropy: When Trajectory Diversity Helps and Hurts in Imitation Learning

author.name: Qian Luo, Ruizhe Liu, Pei Zhou, Xunzhe Zhou, Yanchao Yang

entry.summary: Introduces Geometric Entropy, a task-agnostic metric quantifying intrinsic trajectory diversity in demonstrations, and shows an inverted-U relationship between imitation learning success and diversity across architectures and real-robot tasks. Reveals when diversity helps versus hurts.

entry.title: Energy-based Compositional Diffusion Planning

author.name: Tao Sun, Utkarsh Aashu Mishra, Jiaxin Lu, Danfei Xu, Iro Armeni

entry.summary: Proposes Energy-based Compositional Diffuser, showing that heuristic stitching in compositional diffusion planners yields a non-conservative field, and instead formulates global trajectories as minimizers of summed local bridge potentials. Adds a boundary reaction term omitted by stitching.

entry.title: Causal Reward World Models: Zero-shot Reward Design for Automated Skill Generation

author.name: Yang Yang, Yuchuang Tong, Zhengtao Zhang, Xu Ding, Ning Yang, Yifan Zhang, Haipeng Li, Kehu Yang, Miao Xin

entry.summary: The Causal Reward World Model (CRWM) replaces correlation-driven LLM-based automated reward design with explicit modeling of causal relationships between candidate reward components and task-targeted physical variables, enabling zero-shot reward design for automated skill generation. This reduces susceptibility to spurious reward components.

entry.title: BiliVLA: Scene-Aware Vision-Language-Action Model with Reinforcement Learning for Autonomous Biliary Endoscopic Navigation

author.name: Jinsong Lin, Chi kit Ng, Zhiyong Xiong, Zikang Pan, Yihan Hu, Tabassum Tamima, Ziyi Hao, Eddie Cheung, Jiewen Lai, Huxin Gao, Hongliang Ren

entry.summary: BiliVLA is a scene-aware vision-language-action framework with reinforcement learning for autonomous biliary endoscopic navigation during ERCP, formulating cannulation as instruction-conditioned visuomotor learning under specular reflections, occlusions, and tissue contact. It targets reliable autonomy in a safety-critical surgical procedure.

entry.title: On the Asymptotic Inadmissibility of Double Machine Learning Estimators Under Structure-Agnostic Models

author.name: Lin Liu, Rajarshi Mukherjee, James M Robins

entry.summary: Analyzes structure-agnostic models and shows that the popular double machine learning estimators, while minimax for several functionals, are asymptotically inadmissible under these models. It probes the gap between minimax optimality and admissibility for influential causal inference estimators.

entry.title: A dexterous soft hand exoskeleton restores intentional grasping in individuals with severe hand impairment

author.name: Gordon Cheng

entry.summary: Presents a lightweight soft robotic hand exoskeleton, a textile glove with wrist dorsiflexion and an active opposable thumb, that restores intentional grasping in individuals with severe hand paralysis, enabling tasks like self-feeding. Published in Nature Machine Intelligence.

entry.title: Latent Goal Prediction from Language for Model-Based Planning

author.name: Samuel Barbeau, Simon Roy, Giovanni Beltrame, Christian Desrosiers, Nicolas Thome

entry.summary: LAGO predicts intermediate goal states from language instructions and action-conditioned rollouts within a shared latent space for model-based planning. It dynamically decomposes instructions into local subgoals rather than optimizing a single global objective.

entry.title: SPARC: A Multi-Agent System for Electrical Circuit Question Answering

author.name: Mushtari Sadia, Zhenning Yang, Umme Habiba Lamia, Nishat Shawrin, Ang Chen, Amrita Roy Chowdhury

entry.summary: SPARC is a multi-agent system that answers electrical circuit diagram questions by grounding reasoning in executable physics-based simulations, achieving 83% accuracy with up to 58% absolute improvement over baselines. It enables systematic error diagnosis.

entry.title: Simulated Customers Never Walk Away: Decision Fidelity of LLM User Simulators Measured Against Real Purchase Outcomes

author.name: Liang Chen

entry.summary: Argues that existing LLM user simulators measure communicative fidelity but have a blind spot, namely decision fidelity, because assigned goals make user willingness exogenous. Introduces measuring whether simulated populations reproduce real users' decision-state dynamics against actual purchase outcomes.

entry.title: Process-Reward Tactic Evolution for Long-Horizon Bioinformatics Workflows

author.name: Lingzhi Yang, Yubo Fan, Song Wu, Gilchan Park

entry.summary: Process-Reward Tactic Evolution is a Galaxy-based training framework that turns verified bioinformatics workflow rollouts into reusable tactics, with process verifiers scoring workflow construction and biological checks. It targets reliable long-horizon bioinformatics agents.

entry.title: Neurosymbolic Clinical Trial Matching via LLM-Driven Abduction and Logical Verification

author.name: Baiyang Qu, Leonardo Ranaldi, Xi Wang, Marco Valentino

entry.summary: Introduces aNeSy-CTM, an abductive neurosymbolic framework for clinical trial matching that combines LLM reasoning over noisy clinical text with logical verification of eligibility criteria. It substantially outperforms standalone LLM baselines.

entry.title: Coherence Under Commitment: Probing Generalization and Vacuous Memorization in LLM Logical Reasoning

author.name: Noor Islam S. Mohammad, Mahmudul Hasan

entry.summary: Introduces Coherence Under Commitment, a dual-query evaluation revealing that LLMs can achieve logical coherence vacuously by systematically abstaining, satisfying consistency while providing no utility. It contributes a commitment score and a deterministic log-probability elicitation protocol.

entry.title: Translating Inference-Time Control to Radiology Vision-Language Models: Activation Steering for Pneumonia Classification on Chest X-rays

author.name: Eduardo Moreno Judice de Mattos Farina, Mateus A. Esmeraldo, Felipe Akio Matsuoka, Paulo Eduardo de Aguiar Kuriki, Felipe Campos Kitamura

entry.summary: Evaluates whether Contrastive Activation Addition steering can improve pneumonia classification in three frozen chest X-ray VLMs without weight updates, using answer-bias, text-contrast, and image-conditioned steering vectors. Translates inference-time control to radiology.

entry.title: PeerCheck: Enhancing LLM-Generated Academic Reviews Towards Human-Level Quality

author.name: Zeyuan Chen, Ziqing Yang, Yihan Ma, Michael Backes, Yang Zhang

entry.summary: PeerCheck analyzes differences between LLM-generated and human academic reviews, finding LLMs prioritize theory while humans emphasize methodology and experiments, then explores prompt engineering to improve LLM review quality toward human level. Aims to make LLM review assistance more useful.

entry.title: FleetAgent: Teleoperation Assistant for Autonomous Fleets via Vectorized V2N Messages

author.name: Juntong Peng, Qi Chen, Deyuan Qu, Takayuki Shimizu, Yaobin Chen, Ziran Wang

entry.summary: FleetAgent is a cloud-hosted multimodal LLM teleoperation assistant for autonomous fleets that consumes compact vectorized V2N messages and outputs structured natural-language explanations plus an intervention urgency score. VecFormer bridges vector messages to token-based MLLMs.

entry.title: EnTrust: Modeling Inter-Modal Conflict for Trustworthy Multimodal Medical Image Analysis

author.name: Dwarikanath Mahapatra, Abhijit Das, Behzad Bozorgtabar, Zongyuan Ge, Sudipta Roy, Deepak Nayak, Mauricio Reyes, Imran Razzak

entry.summary: EnTrust treats inter-modal conflict as the primary source of predictive uncertainty in multimodal medical segmentation, with an EnFuse module decomposing features into shared consensus, modality-specific cues, and localized conflict. It contrasts with deterministic fusion or decoupled post-hoc uncertainty.

entry.title: Evaluating LLMs for Real-World Web Vulnerability Detection

author.name: Sebastian Neef, Luca Jungnickel, Antonio Benjamin Buchholz, Valene Spence, Vicente Birke Gonzalez

entry.summary: TASER is a continual learning framework for highly heterogeneous task sequences that jointly decides how many new atomic skills to introduce per task and which to activate, using uncertainty-driven capacity expansion and orthogonal routing. It targets catastrophic forgetting under large reasoning and format divergence.

entry.title: Streaming T5-based Text-to-Speech Synthesis with Limited Lookahead

author.name: Muyang Du, Jason Roche, Junjie Lai

entry.summary: S5-TTS is a streaming variant of T5-TTS enabling low-latency word-by-word incremental speech synthesis via encoder-decoder language modeling and monotonic alignment, beginning generation after the first few words. A lookahead-causal masking mechanism and interleaved multi-source distillation preserve quality under limited lookahead.

entry.title: KITE: Decoupling Kinematics and Interaction for Zero-Shot Cross-Embodiment Manipulation

author.name: Qianxu Wang, Kuan Fang

entry.summary: Introduces KITE, which decouples manipulation into embodiment-agnostic task reasoning and embodiment-specific motor control linked by a learned latent of interaction intent based on contact patterns. Enables zero-shot cross-embodiment manipulation without target demonstrations.

entry.title: On the Expressive Power of Weight Quantization in Large Language Models

author.name: Shao-Qun Zhang

entry.summary: Provides a theoretical investigation of LLM expressive power as a function of weight quantization bits, arguing 1.58-bit is the limiting precision via universal approximation and expressive-collapse results. Sheds light on approximation and degradation as bits decrease.

entry.title: Energy-Based Transformers as Predictors of Reading Difficulty

author.name: Jakub Dotlacil, Ece Takmaz

entry.summary: Explores energy-based transformers as predictors of human reading difficulty, linking them to associative memory and Hopfield network theory. First application of an energy-based transformer measure in computational psycholinguistics across reading-time corpora.

entry.title: Evidential Fusion Network for Multimodal Survival Prediction under Missing Modalities

author.name: Yucheng Xing, Hailan Mo, Zi Wang, Ling Huang, Mengling Feng

entry.summary: EMMS performs multimodal survival prediction robust to missing modalities using Dempster-Shafer theory and Gaussian Random Fuzzy Numbers for evidential decision fusion, modeling both aleatoric and epistemic uncertainty without a generative imputation phase. Targets real-world clinical incompleteness.

entry.title: Hierarchical Pooling for Sheaf Neural Networks

author.name: Dionisia Naddeo, Carlo Abate, Pietro Li\`o, Nicola Toschi, Filippo Maria Bianchi

entry.summary: HiSP introduces hierarchical pooling for sheaf neural networks based on local spectral coarsening, enabling multi-resolution representations that existing fixed-resolution sheaf architectures lack. Sheaf diffusion promotes consistency through restriction maps rather than feature similarity.

entry.title: Geometric and Information Compression of Representations in Deep Learning

author.name: Linara Adilova, Henning Petzka, Asja Fischer, Bernhard C. Geiger

entry.summary: Investigates whether low input-representation mutual information necessarily implies geometrically compressed latent spaces in deep nets, using class-wise clustering and CEB networks. Studies the interplay between information-theoretic and geometric compression with generalization.

entry.title: DevoTG: Temporal Graph Neural Networks for Modeling C. elegans Developmental Connectomics

author.name: Jayadratha Gayen, Bradly Alicea

entry.summary: Presents DevoTG, a temporal graph neural network framework applied to C. elegans developmental connectomics using continuous- and discrete-time dynamic graphs of cell lineage and synaptic data. Substantially outperforms static GNNs on lineage prediction.

entry.title: Encoder-Decoder Manifold Alignment for Idempotent Generation

author.name: Dareen Alharthi, Abdul Waheed, Bhiksha Raj

entry.summary: Argues that failures of idempotent generative models stem from geometric mismatch between encoder and decoder manifolds, and proposes encoder-decoder manifold alignment to achieve exact fixed points. Addresses instability and drift under repeated model application.

entry.title: GRADE: Graph Representation of LLM Agent Dependency and Execution

author.name: Yue Zhao

entry.summary: Introduces GRADE, a graph representation of LLM agent runs combining execution edges and graded dependency edges to recover missing reliance information from traces. Shows the dependency layer predicts agent failures across six corpora.

entry.title: DUET: Decentralized Bilevel Optimization without Lower-Level Strong Convexity

author.name: Zhen Qin, Zhuqing Liu, Songtao Lu, Yingbin Liang, Jia Liu

entry.summary: Introduces DUET, a single-loop decentralized bilevel optimization algorithm that eliminates the lower-level strong convexity assumption via diminishing quadratic regularization. Provides convergence guarantees, broadening applicability of decentralized bilevel methods.

entry.title: NAC: Neural Action Codec for Vision-Language-Action Models

author.name: Ahad Jawaid, Yu Xiang

entry.summary: Introduces NAC, a Neural Action Codec for vision-language-action models that treats robot action trajectories as multi-channel 1D signals compressed via a multi-scale RVQGAN audio-codec-inspired architecture. Improves the compression/latency/performance tradeoff of action tokenization.

entry.title: Finite-Sample Performance of Gradient Descent in Logistic Regression with Gaussian Design

author.name: Junren Chen, Arya Mazumdar

entry.summary: Characterizes the finite-sample estimation performance and convergence of gradient descent on logistic loss under Gaussian design, proving linear convergence to a neighborhood of the true parameter with explicit error bounds. Goes beyond existing asymptotic analyses.

entry.title: Deep RL for Fast Long-Horizon Operations Scheduling on NASA's Carruthers Geocorona Observatory Mission

author.name: Alex Zhang, Jackson Craig, Lara Waldrop

entry.summary: Presents a scalable deep reinforcement learning framework deployed for NASA's Carruthers Geocorona Observatory mission, using macro-action activity blocks and dynamic action-masking to generate feasible long-horizon spacecraft schedules under complex constraints. Trains a full cycle in under six hours.

entry.title: IndicGuard: A Multilingual Safety Guard Model and Dataset for Indic Languages

author.name: Parth Bramhecha, Smit Deshmukh, Sairaj Bodhale, Adwait Borate, Raviraj Joshi

entry.summary: IndicGuard introduces a multilingual safety guard model and dataset spanning ten Indic languages, curated to capture region-specific harms, socio-political contexts, and adversarial jailbreaks. It addresses the English-centric bias of existing LLM safety mechanisms.

entry.title: SCOPE: Sequential Conformal Probing for Reliable OOD Rejection in LLM Services

author.name: Zhuoyun Li, Boxuan Wang, Changshun Wu, Xiaowei Huang, Yi Dong

entry.summary: SCOPE is a framework for reliably rejecting out-of-distribution requests in LLM services by selecting a readable hidden layer, building a conformal gate with in-distribution calibration, and using a supermartingale e-process to certify persistent service-boundary evidence. It provides theoretical guarantees and identifies where boundary signals are best encoded inside the model.

entry.title: From Recognition to Understanding: Unlocking Cognitive Time Series Reasoning with LLMs

author.name: Xin Qiu, Junlong Tong, Yao Zhang, Yunpu Ma, Wei Zhang, Xiaoyu Shen

entry.summary: Argues time-series-LLM gains are limited by reducing the task to curve-fitting, and introduces TSCognition, a multimodal benchmark of ~41K QA samples from 15 sources for reasoning-intensive temporal decision-making. Emphasizes semantic and contextual reasoning over low-level prediction.

entry.title: VTOS: Learning to Orchestrate Vision Tools by Co-Searching Solutions and Observers

author.name: Jinchao Ge, Lingqiao Liu, Shuwen Zhao, Lei Wang

entry.summary: Introduces VTOS, a framework for adaptive vision tool orchestration via joint solution-observer search, co-searching executable programs composing tools like Grounding DINO, SAM, and NMS. Aims to overcome brittleness of fixed visual-programming pipelines under occlusion, small targets, and domain shift.

entry.title: Unlimited OCR Works

author.name: Youyang Yin, Huanhuan Liu, YY, Qunyi Xie, Chaorun Liu, Shiqi Yang, Shaohua Wang, Zhanlong Liu, Hao Zou, Jinyue Chen, Shu Wei, Jingjing Wu, Mingxin Huang, Zhen Wu, Guibin Wang, Tengyu Du, Lei Jia

entry.summary: Proposes Unlimited OCR, replacing attention in DeepSeek OCR with a memory-emulating mechanism to avoid KV cache growth and efficiency decline on long-horizon copying. Aims for human-like sustained parsing efficiency.

entry.title: How Well Can Your Video Model Remember? Measuring Memory-Budget Trade-offs in Long Video Understanding

author.name: Yixian Tian

entry.summary: Develops an empirical model quantifying how long-video understanding accuracy degrades with frame budget and temporal distance, fitting a scaling law across ten models. Derives a budget exponent capturing the marginal value of extra frames.

entry.title: Fine-grained Human Motion Understanding with Language Models

author.name: Thomas Markhorst, Zhi-Yi Lin, Jouh Yeong Chew, Jan van Gemert, Xucong Zhang

entry.summary: Proposes an LLM-based model for fine-grained human motion understanding representing motion as timestamped skeletal pose sequences for reasoning about order, duration, and rhythm. Constructs a diverse pose/motion captioning and QA training mixture.

entry.title: ShuffleFlow: Scalable Posterior Inference for Bayesian Inverse Imaging

author.name: Tianao Li, Tjitske Starkenburg, Yu Sun, Emma Alexander

entry.summary: Presents ShuffleFlow, a scalable variational inference framework for Bayesian inverse imaging combining pixel-unshuffling coordinate sampling, a neural field encoder, and conditional normalizing flow. Addresses poor scalability of flow networks for large-scale reconstruction.

entry.title: Adversarial Domain Prompt Tuning and Generation for Single Domain Generalization

author.name: Zhipeng Xu, De Cheng, Xinyang Jiang, Nannan Wang, Dongsheng Li, Xinbo Gao

entry.summary: Proposes adversarial domain prompt tuning and generation for single domain generalization, the first to use pretrained text-to-image foundation models to create out-of-domain training data with learnable prompts. Addresses impracticality of manual prompt design for all domains.

entry.title: Cross-View Yaw Estimation in Location Uncertainty with Line-Aligning Yaw Scoring

author.name: Taeho Kang, Nairan Zhang, Yelin Kim, Yujiao Shi, Youngki Lee

entry.summary: Proposes LAYS, a radially invariant line-consensus voting method for cross-view yaw estimation that disentangles yaw from translation, achieving sub-degree precision without accurate location. Uses 3D voting over candidate poses based on radial invariance.

entry.title: Prompting Diffusion Models for Zero-Shot Instance Segmentation

author.name: Irem Zeynep Alag\"oz, Nils Morbitzer, Andrea Ramazzina, Nassir Navab, Federico Tombari, Stefano Gasperini

entry.summary: Proposes a method for zero-shot instance segmentation that prompts diffusion models with user input during the generation process rather than only post-processing, leveraging generative priors for more accurate segments. Addresses false positives and over-segmentation in promptable segmentation.

entry.title: FedOT: Ownership Verification and Leakage Tracing via Watermarks for Federated LDMs

author.name: Wenlong Cheng, Yuan Gan, Yunqiu Xu, Jiaxu Miao

entry.summary: Proposes FedOT, a watermarking framework for federated latent diffusion models that supports both ownership verification and leakage tracing to specific malicious clients, addressing vulnerabilities of VAE-based watermarks. Targets unauthorized model distribution in federated settings.

entry.title: PHOEBI: An Open-World Benchmark for Bacterial Identification in Phase-Contrast Microscopy

author.name: Aaditya Baranwal, Md Jahid Hasan, Shruti Vyas

entry.summary: Introduces PHOEBI, a wet-lab-prepared benchmark of 120,000 phase-contrast microscopy images covering 40 combinations of six rod-shaped bacterial species, with a leave-combinations-out protocol for open-world multi-label species identification. Tests generalization to unseen polymicrobial mixtures.

entry.title: Arbor: Explicit Geometric Conditioning for Controllable 3D Asset Generation

author.name: Jan-Niklas Dihlmann, Andreas Engelhardt, Simon Donne, Hendrik P. A. Lensch, Mark Boss

entry.summary: Presents Arbor, a trainable attachment for text-conditioned latent 3D generation that introduces constraint meshes (hull, avoidance, and touch regions) as a native 3D control interface for specifying spatial intent. Addresses lack of direct spatial control in current 3D asset generation.

entry.title: DIPBox: A Multi-scale Testing Framework for Tracking Dataset Regeneration

author.name: Tian Dong, Yan Meng, Shaofeng Li, Guoxing Chen, Yuling Chen, Zhen Liu, Haojin Zhu, Hao Chen

entry.summary: Introduces DIPBox, a multi-scale testing framework for detecting unauthorized dataset regeneration, motivated by a measurement study revealing real-world partial replication of public tumor datasets. Designs sample-, set-, and distribution-level similarity metrics to track previously unknown adversarial regeneration.

entry.title: Rotation-Aware Point-Cloud Embeddings for Vision-Based In-Hand Reorientation

author.name: Yashom Dighe, Karthik Dantu

entry.summary: Proposes rotation-aware point-cloud embeddings for vision-based in-hand object reorientation that disentangle object rotation from permutation, resampling, and unstable correspondence in point-cloud goal conditioning. Avoids reliance on explicit pose, dense flow, or privileged teacher distillation used by prior methods.

entry.title: Real-World Deployment of Massively Parallel Sampling-Based MPC for Contact-Rich Manipulation

author.name: Magnus Dierking, Joao Carvalho, An Thai Le, Georgia Chalvatzaki, Jan Peters

entry.summary: Demonstrates real-world deployment of massively parallel sampling-based MPC for contact-rich manipulation using JAX and MuJoCo MJX on a Franka arm via a real-to-sim-to-real pipeline. Shows structured global sampling outperforms unimodal baselines on mode-switching tasks.

entry.title: BayesFP: Posterior Estimation for Flow-Based Policies via Feynman-Kac Sampling

author.name: Sreevardhan Sirigiri, Weiming Zhi, Fabio Ramos

entry.summary: Proposes BayesFP, a retraining-free inference-time sampler that frames constrained trajectory generation for pretrained diffusion and flow-matching policies as Bayesian posterior sampling using the Feynman-Kac corrector. Extends the framework to deterministic flow-matching policies.

entry.title: Flowing With Purpose: Latent Action Guided Flow Matching Policies For Robotic Manipulation

author.name: Bruno Machado, Alexandre Chapin, Emmanuel Dellandrea, Liming Chen

entry.summary: LAFM replaces the fixed isotropic Gaussian source of flow matching policies with an adaptive library of learned prior distributions grounded by latent actions, addressing the structural mismatch with the fragmented, heteroscedastic structure of robotic action spaces. This reduces entangled vector fields and improves training efficiency and policy performance.

entry.title: Learning to See While Learning to Act: Diffusion Models for Active Perception in Robot Imitation

author.name: Kuancheng Wang, Vaibhav Saxena, Shuo Cheng, Yotto Koga, Danfei Xu

entry.summary: See2Act is an imitation learning method that couples action denoising with active viewpoint refinement, conditioning action prediction on actively-inferred camera poses to handle occlusions where robots must both search and act. It learns where to look and how to act jointly from demonstrations with keyframe-anchored camera poses.

entry.title: PEAR: Permutation-Equivariant Adaptive Routing Multi-Agent Debate

author.name: Yang Feng, Ziwei Xu, Xia Hu, Fengxiang He

entry.summary: PEAR introduces an inference-time protocol for multi-agent debate that dynamically reconfigures communication roles and topologies to prevent positional biases and uneven influence. It provides theoretical characterization as an equivariant routing mechanism.

entry.title: SkillHarness: Harnessing Safe Skills for Computer-Use Agents

author.name: Yurun Chen, Biao Yi, Keting Yin, Shengyu Zhang

entry.summary: SkillHarness is a framework for computer-use agents to learn and use reusable skills safely in dynamic environments with adversarial risks like prompt injections and pop-ups. It addresses the gap that existing skill-learning assumes static, safe settings.

entry.title: Expected Free Energy-based Planning as Variational Inference

author.name: Wouter W. L. Nuijten, Thijs van de Laar, Bert de Vries

entry.summary: Shows that Expected Free Energy planning in active inference can be reformulated as Variational Free Energy minimization on a generative model augmented with epistemic priors. This unifies and clarifies a previously specialized class of optimization procedures.

entry.title: DrugBench: Evaluating AI Control Protocols for Medication Harm Mitigation

author.name: Guido Freire, Agust\'in Mart\'inez-Su\~n\'e, Viviana Cotik

entry.summary: DrugBench presents a pipeline and benchmark for evaluating AI control protocols that mitigate medication-related harm in LLM medical question answering. It extends the emerging AI control paradigm to safety-critical medical settings.

entry.title: BioInsight: Multi-Agent Orchestration for Interactive Biomedical Knowledge Discovery

author.name: Jieyi Wang, Bingxuan Li, Nanyi Jiang, Desong Meng, Zirui Fan, Yuxin Guo, Jiayu Liu, Kunlun Zhu, Eddie Yang, Xiusi Chen, Pan Lu, Bingxin Zhao

entry.summary: BioInsight is a multi-agent system that moves from static biomedical reports to interactive evidence-centered interfaces, organizing disease-specific evidence through typed intermediate artifacts like ranked pathways and citation-grounded reports. It supports researchers in inspecting evidence and refining hypotheses.

entry.title: Negative Knowledge as Failure-aware Shared Memory for AutoResearch

author.name: Hanchun Wang

entry.summary: Proposes a negative knowledge memory layer where a curator agent converts failed research attempts into typed records that downstream agents explicitly adopt or reject before proposing new experiments. It outperforms vanilla AutoResearch baselines while using fewer tokens.

entry.title: Balancing Performance and Diversity in GRPO Autoregressive Text-to-Image Post-Training

author.name: Yuanhao Chiang, Hongbo Duan, Chunru Yang, Jiahua Pei, Yi Liu, Xueqian Wang

entry.summary: Studies how the choice of f-divergence (forward KL, reverse KL, JS) for reference-policy regularization affects GRPO-style autoregressive text-to-image alignment, providing theoretical analysis of token-level update reshaping. Finds JS regularization achieves a favorable performance-diversity tradeoff.

entry.title: Robust Zero-Shot Generalization for Open-Vocabulary Action Recognition via Task Arithmetic

author.name: Francesca Morandi, Omayma Moussadek, Federico Venturini, Mauro Suardi, Alessandro Banzatti, Francesco Cannarile, Angelo Porrello, Simone Calderara

entry.summary: Proposes task arithmetic and model merging to achieve robust zero-shot open-vocabulary action recognition without target-domain training, combining task vectors from models fine-tuned on diverse public datasets. Shows superior out-of-distribution performance.

entry.title: Exploiting Neural Audio Codec Latents for Adversarial Audio Attacks

author.name: Sameek Bhattacharya, Bharath Krishnamurthy, Ajita Rattani

entry.summary: Proposes a generative adversarial audio attack framework operating in the continuous latent space of a neural audio codec, enabling single-shot synthesis of attacks against speaker verification with lower latency than iterative or diffusion methods. Targets real-time threat assessment.

entry.title: Peeking Inside LLMs: Leveraging Internal Artifacts of LLMs for Enhancing Reliability in Legal Classification

author.name: Sudipta Santra, Debtanu Datta, Saptarshi Ghosh

entry.summary: Explores using internal artifacts of LLMs (such as hidden features) to build downstream classifiers that detect incorrect or hallucinated outputs in legal-domain classification tasks. Aims to improve reliability in the high-stakes legal domain.

entry.title: Imitation Learning for Elder-Facing Speech Synthesis

author.name: Dongrui Han, Weidong Chen, Jiawen Kang, Mingyu Cui, Helen Meng, Xixin Wu

entry.summary: Proposes an imitation learning framework for elder-facing TTS that learns from expert demonstrations rather than costly preference feedback, improving GRPO with two-stage on-policy reward learning to mitigate reward hacking. Targets older adults' speech comprehension needs overlooked by general TTS.

entry.title: Topological Neural Dynamics: A Neuron-wise Framework for Sequence Modeling

author.name: Borui Cai, Yao Zhao

entry.summary: Topological Neural Dynamics proposes shifting sequence modeling from layer-wise to neuron-wise dynamics, representing a system as a directed neuron graph with local dynamics functions so individual neurons evolve independently. It contrasts with RNNs, LSTMs, and Transformers that share an operator across a layer.

entry.title: TACO: Task-Aware Column Description Generation Using LLMs

author.name: Ting Cai, Rakesh R. Menon, Yiru Chen, Zifan Liu, Yuan Tian, Fei Wu, Anudeep Chimakurthi, Prashanthi Ramamurthy, Sunav Choudhary, Kun Qian, Yunyao Li

entry.summary: TACO generates task-aware column descriptions for tabular data using LLMs, addressing missing or cryptic documentation that hampers NL2SQL, table QA, and entity linking. It tackles abbreviation handling, hallucination, and redundancy that single-prompt approaches struggle with.

entry.title: Gated MLPs as Symmetry-Broken Rank-1 Bilinear Attention

author.name: Nathan Breslow

entry.summary: Shows that the conventional gated MLP can be viewed as a rank-1 approximation to a bilinear attention mechanism, with the nonlinearity breaking exchange and inverse-scaling symmetries. Offers a theoretical lens on why gated MLPs work and how to design future architectures.

entry.title: First-Token Broadcasters: Mechanistic Origins of Language Identity and Distributed Robustness in Transformers

author.name: Arjun Pillai, Christian Hoang, Anjelo Jann Laroza

entry.summary: Introduces Language Identity Head Ablation, a causal intervention zeroing individual attention heads to measure language switch rates, identifying a small set of first-token broadcaster heads (notably L6H1 in GPT-2) that propagate language identity. Shows statistically significant compensatory redistribution when heads are ablated.

entry.title: MMGist: A Comprehensive Multimodal Benchmark for 2027

author.name: Wenzhen Yuan, Jiacheng Ruan, Wutao Xiong, Chengping Zhao, Ting Liu, Yuzhuo Fu

entry.summary: Introduces MMGist, a curated 7,262-item vision-language benchmark across seven capability dimensions, built via text-ablation, cross-model saturation, and anomaly-detection filtering to fix three issues in existing benchmarks (text-solvable items, saturation, anomalies). Evaluated across 27 models.

entry.title: VideoAgent: All-in-One Framework for Video Understanding and Editing

author.name: Hengji Zhou, Lingxuan Huang, Jian Wang, Bing Zhou, Si Wu, Lianghao Xia, Chao Huang

entry.summary: VideoAgent is an all-in-one agentic framework for long-video understanding and editing, orchestrating over thirty specialized editing agents with shot planning and cross-modal retrieval. Targets coherent narrative creation beyond short-segment limitations.

entry.title: War in the Abstract: The Rise and Consequences of Militarized Language in Scientific Communication

author.name: Sovesh Mohapatra, David Lydon-Staley, Dani S. Bassett

entry.summary: Analyzes 21.4 million scientific papers to quantify the rising prevalence of militaristic language in abstracts (up 48% in OpenAlex since 2010), correlating it with global conflict, and runs an experiment on its persuasive effects. Highlights how war metaphors pervade science communication.

entry.title: Polycepta: Object-Centric Appearance Estimation for Multi-Object Tracking

author.name: Mohamed Nagy, Naoufel Werghi, Jorge Dias, Majid Khonji

entry.summary: Polycepta reformulates appearance modeling in multi-object tracking as recursive state estimation rather than frame-wise matching, continuously updating object appearance states. Aims to make appearance cues robust and efficient for real-time tracking.

entry.title: Understanding Latent Flow Models for Tabular Data Synthesis: Targets, Paths, and Sampling

author.name: Bahrul Ilmi Nasution

entry.summary: Empirically studies latent flow models for synthetic tabular data across seven datasets, comparing velocity/score/noise/posterior objectives, OT versus VP paths, ODE versus SDE sampling, and integration budgets. Shows theoretical equivalences diverge under finite-step compute budgets.

entry.title: Continuous-Time Probabilistic Correctors for Uncertainty-Aware Physics-Based Spacecraft Trajectory Forecasting

author.name: Muhammad Bilal Shahid, Zhanhong Jiang, Soumik Sarkar, Cody Fleming

entry.summary: Introduces a predictor-corrector framework augmenting deterministic physics-based spacecraft trajectory propagators with a learned continuous-time probabilistic corrector that models forecast errors and provides calibrated uncertainty. Targets long-horizon space domain awareness and conjunction assessment.

entry.title: Leveraging Similarities in Multi-Armed Bandits

author.name: Khaled Eldowa, Thibaud Rahier, Augustin Cablant, Panayotis Mertikopoulos, Pierre Gaillard

entry.summary: Studies online learning with similarity-structured action sets encoded by a tree, proving an impossibility result that standard one-point bandit feedback cannot leverage tree-induced similarity. Provides unified algorithms adapting to richer feedback models.

entry.title: MAS-PromptBench: When Does Prompt Optimization Improve Multi-Agent LLM Systems?

author.name: Juyang Bai, Laixi Shi

entry.summary: Introduces MAS-PromptBench to study whether, when, and how much prompt optimization improves multi-agent LLM systems, addressing the exponentially growing search space. Examines sensitivity of gains to system configuration.

entry.title: Diffusion-Driven State Space Models

author.name: Jack Ruder, Michael Wojnowicz

entry.summary: Introduces the Diffusion-Driven State Space Model (DDSSM), replacing Gaussian latent transitions with a diffusion model and jointly training an autoencoder and diffusion model on sequential data. Combines expressiveness of diffusion with principled dynamics inference.

entry.title: The Pitfall of Scaling Up: Uncovering and Mitigating Popularity Bias Amplification in Scaling Transformer-based Recommenders

author.name: Weiqin Yang, Yue Pan, Chongming Gao, Sheng Zhou, Xiang Wang, Can Wang, Jiawei Chen

entry.summary: Identifies that scaling transformer-based sequential recommenders amplifies popularity bias even as accuracy improves, tracing the cause to attention aggregation and other core components. Proposes mitigation to enable sustainable model scaling without ecosystem harm.

entry.title: Physics-Informed Eikonal Caging for Whole-Arm Manipulation Planning

author.name: Yan Zhang, Yiming Li, Yifei Dong, Florian T. Pokorny, Sylvain Calinon

entry.summary: Reformulates caging for whole-arm manipulation as a minimum-time escape problem solved via a physics-informed Eikonal equation, yielding a continuous escape-time field suitable for optimization-based planning. Provides robustness to contact-model inaccuracy without precise dynamics.

entry.title: Scalable Physics-Inspired Transformers for Spin Glasses

author.name: Lu Zhong, Wenli Duan, Jing Liu, Pan Zhang, Ying Tang

entry.summary: This paper develops a physics-inspired transformer with interpretable sparse attention and spin-tailored positional embeddings for sampling Boltzmann distributions in frustrated spin glasses, using FlashAttention for parallel ancestral sampling. It achieves up to two orders of magnitude speedup over vanilla approaches and probes scaling behavior.

entry.title: Scaling Diverse Language Generation for 3D Visual Grounding

author.name: Austin T. Wang, Dongchen Yang, Angel X. Chang

entry.summary: ViGiL3D++ scales diverse language generation for 3D visual grounding by combining constraint sampling over scene graphs with LLM language generation to produce varied grounding queries. It addresses the lack of diverse, contrastive descriptions that limits generalization in 3DVG models.

entry.title: MedHal-Loc: Are "Explainable-by-Architecture" Medical Hallucination Detectors Faithful Localizers? A Localization Benchmark

author.name: Minmin Chen, Daojian Lu, Yining Dai, Jvyu Cai, Fengdan Chen

entry.summary: Introduces MedHal-Loc, a benchmark testing whether knowledge-graph-based hallucination detectors actually localize errors to the offending span, rather than just flagging them. Uses 300 PubMedQA-derived statements with injected single-span errors across four error types.

entry.title: Adding Robust Code-Switching Capabilities to High Performance Multilingual ASR

author.name: Enes Yavuz Ugan, Alexander Waibel

entry.summary: Proposes Bayesian factorized adaptation to add robust code-switching capabilities to multilingual ASR without degrading monolingual baselines. Uses small synthetic data, reducing code-switched word errors by 32.87% while improving overall WER.

entry.title: How Does Research Evolve? Tracing Cross-Domain Trajectories in NLP, ML, and CV with Claim-Grounded Typed Citations

author.name: Abdul Muntakim, Md Abdullah Al Hafiz Khan, Sadid Hasan, Yong Pei

entry.summary: Proposes SciTraj, the first claim-grounded typed citation graph linking each citation edge to the specific motivating claim sentence, with four claim-driven relations verified by NLI entailment. Traces cross-domain research trajectories across NLP, ML, and CV.

entry.title: Judgment-Grounded Expansion for Peer Review Generation

author.name: Sheng Lu, Lizhen Qu, Iryna Gurevych

entry.summary: Formalizes judgment-grounded expansion, a human-AI collaboration mode where a reviewer provides an evaluative claim and the system expands it into review comment candidates as a generate-check-refine process. Conducts a user study and develops scalable evaluation and candidate curation methods.

entry.title: WaveDetect: Robust Framework for Machine-Generated Text Detection via Wavelet Transform

author.name: Zhichen Liu, Kaitong Qin, Linhan He, Yang Xu

entry.summary: Proposes WaveDetect, reformulating machine-generated text detection as a time-frequency signal processing task using continuous wavelet transform over probability signals. Targets robustness against adversarial perturbations, cross-domain shifts, and rapid model evolution.

entry.title: Neural Architecture Distributions: A New Paradigm for Stochastic Segmentation

author.name: Conghui Li, Junhao Huang, Chern Hong Lim, Bing Xue, Mengjie Zhang

entry.summary: Introduces neural architecture distributions as a novel stochastic source for segmentation, sampling discrete architectures from a learned distribution rather than latent noise. Makes stochastic sources auditable for safety-critical segmentation.

entry.title: Context-Aware Autoregressive Diffusion for Gloss-Wise Sign Language Production

author.name: JungHoon Sung, Boeun Kim, Chu Xin, Hyung Jin Chang, ChangHo Kim, Sang-Il Choi, Younggeun Choi

entry.summary: Proposes GARD, a gloss-wise autoregressive diffusion framework for sign language production that conditions on both linguistic and kinematic contexts to model coarticulation. Reduces temporal drift and motion blur in longer sentences.

entry.title: Lightweight 3D Feature Pretraining by Bayesian Inversion of 2D Foundation Models

author.name: Marwane Hariat, Gianni Franchi, David Filliat, Antoine Manzanera

entry.summary: Presents Casper3D, a lightweight probabilistic framework converting noisy multi-view 2D foundation-model embeddings into a latent 3D semantic representation via set-based variational inference with pose. Supports open-vocabulary 3D understanding while being backbone-agnostic.

entry.title: UnityShots: Memory-Driven Multi-Shot Audio-Video Generation with Boundary-Aware Gating

author.name: Jiehui Huang, Yuechen Zhang, Bin Xia, Jiahao Wang, Xu He, Zhenchao Tang, Meng Chu, Xin Tao, Pengfei Wan, Jiaya Jia

entry.summary: Investigates what makes distilled datasets effective through discrete visual tokenizers, introducing a structural score measuring adequacy of token compositions rather than global distribution matching. Provides insight into compositional structure in dataset distillation.

entry.title: BAC-JEPA: Label-Efficient Breast Arterial Calcification Segmentation via Synthetic Mammography-Guided Supervision

author.name: Scott Chase Waggener, Lakshman Tamil

entry.summary: Introduces BAC-JEPA, a label-efficient framework for breast arterial calcification segmentation trained on procedurally synthesized calcifications inserted into real mammographic backgrounds with exact masks. Pairs synthetic masks with self-supervised ViT encoders.

entry.title: NegAS: Negative Label Guided Attention and Scoring for Out-of-Distribution Object Detection with Vision-Language Models

author.name: Yingjie Zhang, Shuai Li, Peng Wang

entry.summary: Proposes NegAS, a negative-label-guided attention and scoring method for out-of-distribution object detection with vision-language models, exploiting background regions and addressing sigmoid multi-label output limitations. Takes a first step toward building OOD detection on VLM detectors.

entry.title: BoxCtrl: 3D-Aware Visual Prompting for Geometric Image Editing

author.name: Feifei Wang, Shiyuan Yang, Xiaoyu Li, Jing Liao

entry.summary: Introduces BoxCtrl, a 3D-aware visual prompting framework for geometric image editing that projects RGB-colored 3D bounding boxes onto images to encode position, size, and orientation as in-context visual examples. Enables precise 3D translation, scaling, and rotation in editing.

entry.title: Lift4D: Harmonizing Single-View 3D Estimation for 4D Reconstruction In-the-Wild

author.name: Yehonathan Litman, Xiaoxuan Ma, Manan Shah, Nicolas Ugrinovic, Kris Kitani, Fernando De la Torre, Shubham Tulsiani

entry.summary: Presents Lift4D, a test-time optimization framework for reconstructing dynamic non-rigid objects from monocular video that adapts single-view 3D estimators and continues to leverage priors throughout rather than only at initialization. Targets in-the-wild scenarios with large deformations and occlusions.

entry.title: FlowCodec: One-Step Flow Prior for Generative Image Compression

author.name: Yinhuan Huang, Hao Cao, Pu chen, Wenqi Guo, Zhijin Qin

entry.summary: Proposes FlowCodec, a generative image compression framework that plugs pretrained large-scale text-to-image flow priors (Qwen-image, FLUX.1-dev) into ultra-low-bitrate codecs with a simple decoupled two-stage design. Aims to integrate stronger generative priors without heavy retraining.

entry.title: From Driving Videos to Simulatable Scenarios

author.name: Alexandre Levy, Ernest Valveny Llobet, Antonio Manuel L\'opez

entry.summary: Introduces D-V2S, a two-stage framework that automatically generates simulatable driving scenarios from driving videos by using a VLM to produce natural-language scene descriptions and an LLM to translate them into executable simulator scenarios. Aims for controllable, repeatable, scalable AV safety testing.

entry.title: ZeroGVC: Zero-Shot Generative Video Compression with Autoregressive Diffusion Priors

author.name: Yixin Gao, Xiaohan Pan, Lin Liu, Xin Li, Zhibo Chen, Qi Tian

entry.summary: Proposes ZeroGVC, a zero-shot generative video compression framework that leverages pretrained autoregressive diffusion priors for low-delay reconstruction without additional training, encoding GOP first frames with an image codec and P-frames via codebook-guided autoregressive latent compression. Avoids the retraining required by most generative compression methods.

entry.title: HoloAgent-0: A Unified Embodied Agent Framework with 3D Spatial Memory

author.name: Xiaolin Zhou, Liu Liu, Tingyang Xiao, Wei Feng, Fa Fu, Xinrui Meng, Xinjie Wang, Jialiang Han, Boyang Yu, Yun Du, Wei Sui, Zhizhong Su

entry.summary: Introduces HoloAgent-0, a unified embodied agent framework with 3D spatial memory that converts language instructions into executable skill graphs and schedules robot resources for real-world deployment. Bridges LLM agent loops to physical robots.

entry.title: ReFPO: Reflow Regularization for Flow Matching Policy Gradients

author.name: Ge Wang, Yibo Peng, Fan Feng, Shenhao Yan, Chengsi Yao, Jiahao Yang, Honghao Cai, Yiming Zhao, Xi Li, Jinke Ren, Shuguang Cui, Yatong Han, Zhen Li

entry.summary: Introduces ReFPO, an online RL method adding explicit Reflow regularization to Flow Matching Policy Gradients, revealing that FPO updates act as an implicit advantage-weighted Reflow process. Stabilizes flow-based control with a one-line geometric regularizer.

entry.title: Robot Critics that Sweat the Small Stuff

author.name: Sruthi Sudhakar, Junbang Liang, Sreehari Rammohan, Pavel Tokmakov, Richard Zemel, Carl Vondrick

entry.summary: Introduces a method to fine-tune VLM critics for robot policies using pairwise progress supervision from success/failure rollouts, enabling fine-grained progress reasoning and subtle failure detection. Combines with an action-conditioned video model to predict action effects.

entry.title: Temporal Logic Guidance for Action-Only Diffusion Policies with World Models

author.name: Moritz Zoellner, Anastasios Manganaris, Rohan Paleja

entry.summary: Introduces a guidance method that lets action-only diffusion policies be steered at inference using Signal Temporal Logic via a separate learned world model, enabling differentiable STL robustness evaluation without requiring joint state-action generation. This adds controllable behavior-mode selection for human-robot settings.

entry.title: Distilling Collaborative Dynamics into Latent Space for Implicit Coordination in Decentralized Multi-Agent Manipulation

author.name: Chanyoung Park, Minsung Yoon, Andrew Jeong, Sung-eui Yoon

entry.summary: CLS-DP enables decentralized multi-arm manipulation under partial observability by distilling privileged multi-agent dynamics into a latent space that each agent infers from local RGB observations to condition its diffusion policy. This achieves implicit coordination without shared views or communication.

entry.title: A Watermark for Vision-Language-Action and World Action Models

author.name: Yule Liu, Shuai Liu, Jiaheng Wei, Xinlei He

entry.summary: Proposes keyed latent-provenance verification to watermark and fingerprint VLA and world-action models by controlling the seed of the Gaussian noise vector drawn before generation, protecting these black-box-deployed models as intellectual property. The owner can verify provenance using a keyed seed.

entry.title: Human Decision-Making with AI Assistance under Correlated Features

author.name: Yanru Guan, Naveen Raman, Fei Fang

entry.summary: Studies optimal AI test recommendation policies for human decision-makers when features are correlated, proving that stationary repeated-recommendation policies can perform arbitrarily poorly. Shows optimal policies follow an explore-then-commit structure.

entry.title: RIZZ: Routing Interactions to Near Zero-Interference Zones for Continual Adaptation of Black-Box Agents

author.name: Sonali Goel, Pranav Vaidhyanathan, Lucas Schorling, Natalia Ares, Maike Osborne

entry.summary: RIZZ is a continual adaptation framework for black-box LLM agents that learns through verifier-gated memory, routing, and prompt compilation to prevent cross-task interference. It targets nonstationary streams with sparse feedback without accessing model weights.

entry.title: Confidence Laundering in Agent Systems: Why Uncertainty Needs a Latent Carrier

author.name: Kaiwen Shi, Zheyuan Zhang, Han Bao, Colby Nelson, Yanfang Ye

entry.summary: Identifies confidence laundering, a failure mode where uncertain upstream agent decisions are passed downstream as clean artifacts, amplifying local ambiguity into system-level errors. Argues uncertainty needs a latent carrier to survive component handoffs.

entry.title: Trip+: Benchmarking Agents in Personalized Interactive Travel Planning

author.name: Junle Chen, Wei Chen, Yehong Xu, Zhengjun Huang, Yuqian Wu, Zhoujin Tian, Kai Wang, Lei Wang, Xiaofang Zhou

entry.summary: Trip+ is a benchmark for personalized interactive travel planning where agents generate and revise minute-level itineraries under evolving preferences and disruptions, with an LLM-based simulator evaluating subjective metrics like fatigue. It measures holistic end-to-end travel planning ability.

entry.title: Training the Orchestrator: A Supervised Approach to End-to-End PDDL Planning with LLM Agents

author.name: Rajesh Mangannavar, Zachary Coalson, Pranay Dugar, Prasad Tadepalli

entry.summary: HALO trains a small QLoRA-tuned orchestrator from verifier-certified refinement trajectories so that LLM-based PDDL planning no longer pays a frontier API call at every repair step. It tackles cost efficiency in agentic planning across 11 domains.

entry.title: Reference-Free Assessment of Physical Consistency in World Model-based Video Generation

author.name: Yun Oh, Sukmin Yun

entry.summary: This paper introduces reference-free measures combining relative and absolute physical-consistency assessment for world-model-generated videos, using SLAM and optical-flow tools to quantify inconsistencies without human voting or ground-truth references. Filtering with the relative measure improves downstream robotic task success by over 8%.

entry.title: Code Isn't Memory: A Structural Codebase Index Inside a Coding Agent

author.name: Ishaan Bhola, Adithyan Krishnan, Sravanth Kurmala, Mukunda NS

entry.summary: This ablation study holds the model (Claude Opus 4.7) and harness fixed to isolate whether adding a structural codebase index changes cost or resolution on SWE-PolyBench Verified and SWE-bench Pro, finding large localization gains and a separated resolve gain without cost penalty. It clarifies retrieval design choices for coding agents.

entry.title: Imagine to Ensure Safety in Hierarchical Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Gregory Gorbov, Artem Latyshev, Aleksandr I. Panov

entry.summary: This work combines a learnable world model with high-level and low-level policies to enforce safety in hierarchical reinforcement learning, using imagined rollouts and subgoals that bias exploration toward safe regions in long-horizon tasks. It targets compounding errors in safe exploration.

entry.title: Beyond Templates: Revisiting Zero-Shot Remote Sensing through Meta-Prompting

author.name: Eirini Baltzi, Dionysis Christopoulos, Sotiris Spanos, Valsamis Ntouskos, Konstantinos Karantzalos

entry.summary: Examines zero-shot remote sensing across 17 VLM variants and 12 datasets, showing that meta-prompting and LLM-generated class descriptions are highly sensitive to textual design and do not reliably beat simple domain-adapted CLIP descriptions. Highlights noise introduced by semantically rich descriptions.

entry.title: MMGNN: Multi-level, multi-color graph neural networks for molecular property prediction

author.name: Trung Nguyen, Duc Duy Nguyen

entry.summary: MMGNN is a hierarchical multi-color graph neural network for molecular property prediction that decomposes molecular graphs into atom-type-pair-specific subgraphs while preserving atom-level resolution, with 2D and 3D geometric variants. It avoids mixing interaction-specific signals in a single graph.

entry.title: When Context Misleads: Surprisal, Energy and Attention Entropy as Metrics of Coherence Illusions in LLMs

author.name: Ece Takmaz, Nitin Kumar, Li Kloostra, Jakub Dotlacil

entry.summary: This study tests whether Dutch language models exhibit human-like coherence illusions, where a distractor matching upcoming text makes incoherent discourse seem coherent. It finds surprisal tracks human judgments and identifies attention heads whose entropy differs under coherence versus incoherence.

entry.title: NASDAQ: Normalized Observation Space Dynamics-Augmented Q-Learning

author.name: Xinwei Liu (Sun Yat-sen University, China), Junyuan Liang (Sun Yat-sen University, China), Zicong Hong (EPFL, Switzerland), Jianting Zhang (Purdue University, USA), Wuhui Chen (Sun Yat-sen University, China)

entry.summary: NASDAQ identifies that unbalanced reconstruction losses across observation dimensions degrade observation-predictive RL on low-dimensional tasks, where large-range dimensions dominate. It proposes an online-RL-tailored normalization method to rebalance learning across dimensions.

entry.title: SOHET: Sequence Of Heterogeneous Events Transformer with Self-Supervised Pre-Training

author.name: Kees Jan de Vries, Mustafa Radha, Mathijs de Jong

entry.summary: SOHET is a hierarchical transformer for heterogeneous event streams using event-type-specific tabular encoders with temporal and type embeddings, plus three self-supervised pretraining objectives. It outperforms baselines on a large Booking.com fraud-detection task and the EBES benchmark.

entry.title: Graph-of-Differences: Anatomy-Structured Difference Alignment for Medical Image Re-Identification

author.name: Nichula Wasalathilaka, Abhijit Das, Imran Razzak, Dwarikanath Mahapatra

entry.summary: Graph-of-Differences grounds medical image re-identification in explicit anatomy graphs, computing identity differences over matched named anatomical regions to reduce shortcut learning. A graph-level difference alignment objective anchors retrieval signals in homologous structures for auditability.

entry.title: Generative Robust Optimisation

author.name: Yuhui Yin, Vassilis M. Charitopoulos

entry.summary: Proposes Generative Robust Optimisation (GRO), defining the uncertainty set as the image of a neural decoder over a calibrated latent set to capture nonlinear correlations, asymmetry, and multimodality beyond fixed-geometry sets. Provides a five-point evaluation framework and a Wasserstein adversarial autoencoder instantiation.

entry.title: SteerVTE: Seamless Video Text Editing with Style and Glyph Control

author.name: Kai Zeng, Moran Li, Zhengwei Wang, Yingchen Yu, Yiheng Lin, Ruichuan An, Ming Lu, Qi She, Wentao Zhang

entry.summary: SteerVTE steers a frozen video diffusion model to edit text within videos with stroke-level precision while preserving style and temporal coherence. Tackles the largely unexplored problem of video text editing using lightweight adapters.

entry.title: The Energy Consumption of Transformer Fine-Tuning: A Roofline-Inspired Scaling Model

author.name: Mansour Zoubeirou a Mayaki

entry.summary: Develops a roofline-inspired scaling model for predicting energy consumption of transformer fine-tuning across multiple GPUs, incorporating compute, memory traffic, and hardware-efficiency factors. Derives scaling laws from controlled BERT sweeps.

entry.title: Objective-Behavior Alignment: Diagnostics for MORL Policy Selection

author.name: Antonio Mone, Zuzanna Osika, Florian Felten, Pradeep K. Murukannaiah, Mark Fuge, Frans A. Oliehoek, Luciano Cavalcante Siebert

entry.summary: Provides diagnostic tools for multi-objective RL policy selection by examining objective-behavior alignment, revealing that policies with similar value vectors can exhibit very different trajectories. Helps decision-makers select among Pareto-optimal policies more meaningfully.

entry.title: Learning to Place Guards by Reinforcement: A Geo-Free Neural Policy for the Vertex-Guard Art Gallery Problem

author.name: Domagoj \v{S}everdija, Jurica Maltar, Nathan Chappel, Domagoj Matijevi\'c

entry.summary: Trains a pointer-network RL policy to place guards for the NP-hard vertex-guard Art Gallery Problem using only vertex coordinates without geometric oracles at test time. Examines what neural combinatorial policies actually learn versus what decoders express.

entry.title: Data Pruning: Redundant, Problematic, and Interdependent Samples

author.name: Leon Freese, Marthinus W. Theunissen

entry.summary: Empirically investigates two popular data pruning methods under noisy and noiseless conditions, showing they fail under significant label noise. Identifies redundancy, problematic samples, and inter-sample interdependence as three factors governing pruning success.

entry.title: Learning by Shifting: Temporal View Construction for Time Series Contrastive Learning

author.name: Abdul-Kazeem Shamba, Kerstin Bach, Gavin Taylor

entry.summary: Proposes encoding temporal shift invariance as the basis for positive/negative pairs in time series contrastive learning, challenging reliance on hand-crafted augmentations. Aims to improve generalization across diverse temporal patterns without spurious correlations.

entry.title: Meta-Reinforcement Learning via Evolution for Multi-Objective Combinatorial Supply Chain Optimisation

author.name: Rifny Rachman, Bahrul Ilmi Nasution, Josh Tingey, Richard Allmendinger, Pradyumn Shukla, Wei Pan

entry.summary: Proposes a population-based meta-reinforcement learning framework combining decomposition with evolutionary search over scalarization weights for multi-objective combinatorial supply chain optimization. Maintains a population of weight-associated meta-policies to better cover the Pareto front.

entry.title: Learning a Normal World Model for Few-Shot Boundary-Calibrated Abnormality Detection

author.name: Weizhi Nie, Weichao Liu, Weijie Wang, Yuting Su

entry.summary: Proposes a Hypergraph Entropic Normal-World Model for few-shot abnormality detection that learns normal behavior from abundant normal events and uses few abnormal examples only to calibrate the normality boundary. Represents sensor windows as context-conditioned hypergraphs with entropy-aware energy.

entry.title: Multigrid Training for Molecular Generation using Graph Neural Networks

author.name: Zixuan Ling, Paula Mercurio, Di Liu

entry.summary: Introduces a multigrid training strategy for graph-based and 3D-grid molecular generation that transfers parameters from coarse to fine resolutions via biased random walk upsampling and multi-resolution voxelization. Accelerates learning and improves stability at high resolution.

entry.title: Training-free Task Classification for Multi-Task Model Merging

author.name: Jungyong Son, Jinwook Jung, Sungyong Baik

entry.summary: Proposes a training-free method for routing inputs to task-relevant experts in multi-task model merging, avoiding the need for labeled data or task IDs at inference. Aims to close the gap to individual expert performance.

entry.title: Minimax Quantile Lower Bounds for Interactive Statistical Decision Making with Privacy

author.name: Raghav Bongole, Amirreza Zamani, Tobias J. Oechtering, Mikael Skoglund

entry.summary: Develops a delta-explicit minimax-quantile theory for interactive statistical decision making, providing high-probability Fano and Le Cam converse tools and handling mutual-information privacy in the same framework. Captures rare consequential failures beyond expectation-based criteria.

entry.title: GRIMIP: A General Framework for Instance-Specific Configuration of MIP Solvers Using LLMs

author.name: Yidong Luo, Xuemin Chen, Chenguang Wang, Fangzhou Zhu, Tao Zhong, Tianshu Yu

entry.summary: Introduces GRIMIP, a hybrid framework combining LLM semantic reasoning with sample-efficient search to configure MIP solver hyperparameters per instance. Addresses cold-start and inefficient search in solver tuning.

entry.title: Dynamic estimation of slowly varying sequences

author.name: Prashant Gokhale, Mikhail Khodak, Sandeep Silwal

entry.summary: Introduces a framework for sequentially approximating functions of slowly-varying sequences by reusing past queries, generalizing implicit trace estimation to matrix powers, spectral densities, Monte Carlo integration, and PDE boundary value problems. Reduces overall cost when consecutive elements change little.

entry.title: Inductive Generalization for Robotic Manipulation

author.name: Annabella Macaluso, Haochen Zhang, Ishaan Masilamony, Yingshan Chang, Yonatan Bisk

entry.summary: Argues that robot visuomotor policy generalization should be tested via inductive out-of-distribution task variants rather than unstructured domain shifts, drawing on axis-based LLM evaluation. Proposes inductive generalization benchmarks for manipulation.

entry.title: Compressing Observation History into Agent Memory: Distilling Transformers into Recurrent Transformers

author.name: Philippe Weinzaepfel, Christian Wolf, B\"ulent Mert Sariyildiz, Guillaume Bono, Gianluca Monaci

entry.summary: Distills full-history transformers into recurrent transformers for long-horizon streaming vision and robotics, arguing the performance gap stems from how information is compressed rather than architecture. Targets memory-efficient agent applications like map-free pose estimation.

entry.title: Variance-Tilted Diffusion Models for Diverse Sampling

author.name: Iskander Azangulov, Leo Zhang, Kianoosh Ashouritaklimi

entry.summary: Introduces variance-tilted diffusion models for diverse sampling, using a variance-weighted batch distribution derived as a Doob h-transform of independent diffusion dynamics to favor sample collections with large empirical spread. Yields an interacting-particle sampler with a transparent probabilistic target.

entry.title: Robust Diffusion Models via Divergence-Induced Weighted Denoising

author.name: Lei Li, Yuexiao Dong

entry.summary: This work replaces the standard MSE denoising loss in diffusion models with an f-divergence-induced nonlinear transformation, yielding a robust training surrogate that improves performance under data contamination with minimal overhead. The theory rests on a per-step lognormal likelihood-ratio reduction.

entry.title: RAVEN: Agentic RAG for Automated Vulnerability Repair

author.name: Varun Gadey, Zijie Liu, Alexandra Dmitrienko

entry.summary: RAVEN is an autonomous framework combining agentic retrieval-augmented generation with controlled iterative repair to fix software vulnerabilities, aiming to generalize beyond memory-related and locally repairable bugs across languages. It targets limitations of prior repair frameworks tied to proprietary models.

entry.title: Spectral Gating via Damped Oscillations for Adaptive Implicit Neural Representations
