Improves held-out phishing recall dramatically through generalization hardening.

entry.title: Approximating velocity fields with planted attractors via Neural-ODEs for classification purposes

author.name: Feliciano Giuseppe Pacifico, Duccio Fanelli, Lorenzo Buffoni, Lorenzo Chicchi, Diego Febbe, Raffaele Marino

entry.summary: This work uses Neural ODEs equipped with planted equilibrium points as class indicators, where the learned velocity field shapes basins of attraction directing each input toward its target class. It reframes classification as a dynamical-systems convergence problem.

entry.title: An Open-Source LFSR-Based Stochastic Leaky Integrate-and-Fire Neuron in SkyWater 130 nm: Design, Stochastic Characterisation, and Rate Coding

author.name: Poornima Kumaresan, Santhosh Sivasubramani

entry.summary: Presents an open-source LFSR-based stochastic leaky integrate-and-fire neuron in SkyWater 130nm with stochastic characterization and rate coding. A compact, configurable standard-cell CMOS design released openly.

entry.title: Manipulider: A Multi-Engine Buoyancy-Controlled Robot for Thrusterless Underwater Gliding and Manipulation

author.name: Yitao Jiang, Yewei Huang, Weizhi Cao, Mingi Jeong, Alberto Quattrini Li, Luyang Zhao, Muhao Chen, Devin Balkcom

entry.summary: Presents Manipulider, a thrusterless buoyancy-actuated underwater robot that uses four syringe-based buoyancy engines for glide-like locomotion and attitude-based manipulation with a magnetic modular payload interface. Avoids propeller entanglement via static force balance.

entry.title: A Multimodal Tiltwing Framework for Bioinspired Aerial Robots

author.name: Krispin C. V. Broers, Sophie F. Armanini

entry.summary: Proposes an adaptable tiltwing framework for bioinspired tailless flapping-wing aerial robots enabling switching between hovering, high-speed directional, and gliding flight via thrust vectoring with two independent propulsion units. Includes a hybrid Scotch-yoke flapping mechanism.

entry.title: Integrated cloud-based architecture for robot-robot and human-robot collaboration using ROS 2--MQTT in Mediterranean Greenhouses

author.name: F. Ca\~nadas-Ar\'anega, M. Mu\~noz, J. C. Moreno, J. L. Blanco-Claraco

entry.summary: Proposes a cloud-based hybrid ROS 2 plus MQTT architecture for robot-robot and human-robot collaboration in challenging Mediterranean greenhouse environments where standard ROS 2 suffers discovery and latency issues. It enables more robust real-time multi-robot coordination in agriculture.

entry.title: Study on Quantitative Dynamic Epistemic Logic for Belief Revision

author.name: Felipe Nunes de Souza Camargo

entry.summary: Studies quantitative dynamic epistemic logic for belief revision, extending AGM theory with a modal logic capturing degrees of conviction and introducing revision operators. It formalizes belief-revision processes with greater expressive power.

entry.title: Closure of Self-Determining System Based on Causal and Constitutive Relations

author.name: Yoshiyuki Ohmura, Earnest Kota Carr, Yasuo Kuniyoshi

entry.summary: Proposes defining the boundaries of self-determining systems via causal-constitutive loops, combining causal and constitutive asymmetric relations to handle external causes and circular causality. It offers a formal closure criterion for systems with internal causes.

entry.title: Measuring What Persists: Conditioning Mechanisms and a Geometric Framework for AI Agent Identity

author.name: Andrew Tanner

entry.summary: This paper proposes a geometric framework using square-root-JSD metric spaces and magnitude homology to measure how a persistent AI agent's specified identity drifts over long contexts, identifying identity-vacuum and safety-basin conditioning clusters. The ideas are mathematically ambitious but speculative.

entry.title: Structural Distinguishability of Static and Adaptive Policy Regimes in Agent-Based Regulatory Simulation

author.name: Roberto Garrone

entry.summary: This paper offers a controlled benchmark within agent-based regulatory simulation to distinguish whether policy conclusions arise from agent adaptation, policy adaptation, or their interaction. It contributes a configurable emissions-regulation ABM rather than a new framework.

entry.title: Beyond Hooking Onto the World: Referential Profiles and the Numerical Structure of LLM Grounding

author.name: Joo Yull Rhee

entry.summary: A conceptual philosophy paper revisiting the grounding problem for LLMs, arguing reference is profile-based, context-sensitive, and norm-governed rather than a fixed symbol-object link, and that vector grounding needs an account of numerical representation. It critiques recent vector-grounding accounts as incomplete.

entry.title: Few-Shot Hyperspectral Aphid Detection via FastGAN Synthetic Data Generation, Transformer-Based Classification and Explainable AI

author.name: Ali Saeidan

entry.summary: This study uses FastGAN to augment a small hyperspectral dataset of faba bean leaves for aphid detection, then applies transformer classification with explainable AI. It addresses deep learning's data scarcity in hyperspectral agricultural monitoring.

entry.title: Skills for the future software profession: beyond agentic AI!

author.name: Sungmin Kang, Baishakhi Ray, Abhik Roychoudhury

entry.summary: Summarizes two 2026 round-tables on the skills future software engineers need in the agentic-AI era, finding that verification and validation grow in importance as agents handle implementation. Offers implications for training and education.

entry.title: A Completion-Aware Framework for Impactful Counterfactual Explainability in Graph Neural Networks

author.name: Maria Myrto Villia, Filippos Gouidis, Theodore Patkos, Panos Trahanias

entry.summary: Proposes a model-agnostic, completion-aware counterfactual explainability pipeline for graph neural networks that couples factual explanations with missing-edge prediction. Aims to improve quality, robustness, and intuitiveness of edge-add/remove explanations.

entry.title: SCENIC: Semantic-Conditioned Edge-Aware Neural Framework for Structured IoT Command Generation

author.name: Luke Ztz Hu, Hongbing Lang, Songping Mai

entry.summary: Proposes SCENIC, an edge-deployable neural framework treating IoT command generation as a many-to-one structured output task mapping varied natural-language instructions to canonical command strings. Covers architecture selection and a Smart Home Instruct data-generation pipeline for deterministic parsing.

entry.title: Comparative Evaluation of Machine Learning and Deep Learning Models for Wound-Rotor Synchronous Motor Performance Prediction

author.name: K{\i}van\c{c} Do\u{g}an, Ahmet Orhan

entry.summary: Benchmarks eight machine learning and deep learning models across four algorithmic families for predicting wound-rotor synchronous motor performance as surrogates for costly finite element analysis. Aims to support rapid design-space exploration for rare-earth-free motors.

entry.title: Deep Learning for Soil Moisture Estimation: Fusing Satellite Data with Optimally-Lagged Meteorological Features

author.name: Adrian Canovas-Rodriguez, Aurora Gonz\'alez Vidal, Antonio F. Skarmeta

entry.summary: Introduces a cross-correlation methodology to determine optimal temporal lags between meteorological variables and soil moisture, fused via deep learning for soil moisture estimation in semi-arid agriculture. Validated across seven plots in Spain.

entry.title: Privacy-Preserving Federated Temporal Graph Learning with Digital Twin--Guided Adaptive Deception for Cyber-Resilient IoMT

author.name: Syed Zeeshan Haider, Anwar Shah, Muneeb Arif, Hamza Iftikhar, Waqas Ali

entry.summary: Presents a federated temporal graph convolutional network with advantage actor-critic and digital-twin-guided adaptive deception for cyber-resilient IoMT defense. A near-duplicate companion to the earlier IoMT framework by the same authors with a graph-based variant.

entry.title: A new classification method based on Minimum Spanning Trees

author.name: Julio Gonz\'alez-D\'iaz, Beatriz Pateiro-L\'opez, Iria Rodr\'iguez-Acevedo

entry.summary: Proposes a supervised classification algorithm based on Minimum Spanning Trees, including a robust and computationally more efficient variant, validated via simulation and aircraft trajectory data. Extends MST-based clustering ideas into supervised learning.

entry.title: EEG Benchmarking Needs a Task Specification Layer: NeuroDoc for Rulebook-Guided, Executable Benchmark Construction

author.name: Chengxuan Qin, Zhige Chen, Shu Peng, Rui Yang, Jiping Cui, Yikai Dong, Jun Li, Liu Peng, Zhida Shang, Mingze Tang, Kay Chen Tan, Jibin Wu

entry.summary: Proposes an Extended Kalman Filter-enhanced latent feature analysis model for temporal QoS prediction that combines model-driven and data-driven learning to capture non-stationary patterns. Targets cloud and service-oriented systems.

entry.title: A geometric and deep learning reproducible pipeline for monitoring floating anthropogenic debris in urban rivers using in situ cameras

author.name: Gauthier Grimmer, Romain Wenger, Cl\'ement Flint, Germain Forestier, Gilles Rixhon, Valentin Chardon

entry.summary: Proposes a reproducible geometric and deep learning pipeline for monitoring floating anthropogenic debris in urban rivers using fixed in-situ cameras. Identifies the most suitable model balancing accuracy and inference speed under complex environmental conditions.

entry.title: NeoJaundice-AI: Smartphone-Based Neonatal Jaundice Detection Using Dual-Input Deep Learning and Synthetic Augmentation

author.name: Rahul Patel, Nirjala Jarpula

entry.summary: Presents NeoJaundice-AI, a smartphone screening system using a dual-branch EfficientNet-B0 on skin and sclera images to estimate neonatal bilirubin levels offline in under three seconds. Targets low-resource clinical settings where blood tests are impractical.

entry.title: Direct Raw Audio Signal Processing via Reservoir Computing: An Investigation into 'Feature-Free' Architectures

author.name: Rinku Sebastian, Simon O Keefe, Martin A Trefzer

entry.summary: Investigates reservoir computing as a feature-free framework for direct raw audio classification, bypassing handcrafted features like MFCCs. Compares shallow, sequential, and parallel deep reservoir architectures for hierarchical representation.

entry.title: Prediction of Solar Flares Using Photospheric Magnetic Field Parameters with Deep Learning

author.name: Yash Chaudhary, Jason T. L. Wang, Chunhui Xu, Yan Xu, Sen Zhang

entry.summary: Predicts M- and X-class solar flares from photospheric magnetic field parameters using deep learning, integrating SHAP and partial dependence plots for interpretability. Aims to improve trustworthiness over black-box flare forecasting.

entry.title: Kiwano: A Cutting-Edge Open-Source Toolkit for Speaker Verification

author.name: Mickael Rouvier, Pierre Michel Bousquet

entry.summary: Kiwano is an open-source PyTorch toolkit for speaker verification offering standardized recipes, pretrained models, unified evaluation, and benchmarking tools under Apache 2.0. It emphasizes reproducibility and rapid prototyping.

entry.title: Demographic Metadata as Construct-Irrelevant Noise in DistilBERT-Based Automated Essay Scoring

author.name: Teik Peng Ch'ng, Hui Na Chua

entry.summary: This study examines naive concatenation of demographic metadata with text in a DistilBERT-based automated essay scoring model, evaluating effects on predictive accuracy, training convergence, and score parity using the ASAP 2.0 dataset. It treats demographic metadata as potential construct-irrelevant noise.

entry.title: Economic Transformation and Cultural Change: Evidence from Two Centuries of French Drama

author.name: T. D. Oliveira, L. A. Attilio, M. J. Davila-Fernandez

entry.summary: Combines computational linguistics, econometrics, and formal modeling to analyze 1,215 French theatrical texts (1700-1900), showing aristocratic discourse gave way to bourgeois economic themes as capitalism developed. Uses LDA and Bayesian VAR with shock identification.

entry.title: Machine Translation and Post-Editing: Comparative Evaluation of Different MT Systems and Post-Editor Groups in Specialised Translation

author.name: Joachim Minder (ALTAE, CLILLAC-ARP), Alexandra Mestivier (ALTAE, CLILLAC-ARP), Natalie K\"ubler (ALTAE)

entry.summary: Comparative evaluation of three MT systems (DeepL, eTranslation, Systran) and two post-editor groups (linguists vs NLP experts) for specialised English-to-French translation. Uses error-typology annotation, finding significant differences in terminological accuracy and fluency.

entry.title: A Taxonomy of Conceptual Alignment in Human-Robot Dialogue

author.name: Shengchen Zhang, Xiaohua Sun, Weiwei Guo

entry.summary: Proposes a taxonomy and dialogue act schema for conceptual alignment in human-robot dialogue, framing it as a bidirectional co-constructive process. Offers a design-centric framework for studying meaning negotiation.

entry.title: Motion-Aware Reinforcement Learning For Object Localization

author.name: Prithvi Raj Singh, Satyendra Singh

entry.summary: Introduces MARLNet, a PPO-based bounding-box refinement agent that injects a constant-velocity motion prior and action-smoothness reward for object localization. Reports modest detection success-rate gains on Pascal VOC and VisDrone.

entry.title: Hybrid Compression: Integrating Pruning and Quantization for Optimized Neural Networks

author.name: Minh-Loi Nguyen, Long-Bao Nguyen, Van-Hieu Huynh, Minh-Triet Tran, Trung-Nghia Le

entry.summary: Proposes a two-phase neural network compression method combining pruning and quantization with Mixture-of-Experts routing to improve performance of compressed models on edge devices. Targets the size-versus-accuracy trade-off for embedded deployment.

entry.title: IViT: A Novel Interpretable Visual Transformer for Skin Disease Detection

author.name: Haibiao Li, Di Lin, Xue Jiang, Weiwei Wu, Yanxi Li, Yugang Chi

entry.summary: Introduces an interpretable Vision Transformer using quadratic-programming-based feature selection for few-shot skin disease detection, aiming to keep accuracy while improving explainability. Targets medical diagnostic bias and ViT opacity.

entry.title: On the Use of Survival Selection Methods for Evolutionary Diversity Optimisation

author.name: Adel Nikfarjam, Jakob Bossek, Aneta Neumann, Frank Neumann

entry.summary: Studies survival selection methods for evolutionary diversity optimization, where the goal is maximizing solution-set diversity under quality constraints. Examines alternatives to the standard one-solution-per-generation paradigm.

entry.title: Tessellated Biomes: Distributed Robotic Assemblies for Architectural Resilience

author.name: Sergio Mutis, Eric Hughes, Gert Duvenhage

entry.summary: Presents Tessellated Biomes, a cyber-physical framework fusing microfactory fabrication, discrete multi-material optimization, and distributed quadrupedal robotic assembly for reconfigurable modular architecture. Aims at a circular construction lifecycle.

entry.title: Toward Machine Risk Perception: Integrating Trust Calibration and Precursor-Based Risk Estimation for Humanoid

author.name: He Wen

entry.summary: Proposes a precursor-driven, trust-calibrated framework for proactive humanoid risk perception in manufacturing, modeling accident evolution with a logistic-exponential precursor formulation. Defines trust as the inverse of estimated accident probability.

entry.title: A UAV-Mounted Sensor Network for Close-Range Inspection of Wind Turbine Rotor Blades

author.name: Jost Wittmann, Ahmed Abdullahi Hassan, Nils K\"ompe, Andreas N\"uchter

entry.summary: Presents a UAV-mounted multimodal sensor network (RGB, thermal IR, custom 3D scanner) co-calibrated into a common frame for close-range wind turbine blade inspection. Aims to improve reliable defect classification over manual processes.

entry.title: Durability-Aware Multi-Objective Optimization of the Jansen Linkage: Trading Gait Quality Against Joint Wear

author.name: Jichao Wang

entry.summary: This paper adds a joint-wear durability objective to the multi-objective optimization of Theo Jansen's classic walking linkage, coupling forward kinematics, inverse dynamics, and an Archard wear model. It quantifies the tradeoff between gait quality and per-cycle pin wear, offering a more practical design lens for mechanical legs.

entry.title: Conceptual Design of an Ecosystem for Real Farm Data Collection toward Agricultural AI Foundation Models

author.name: Junsei Tanaka, Yoshihiro Sato

entry.summary: Proposes a conceptual ecosystem design for sustainable real farm data collection toward agricultural AI foundation models, featuring demand-driven pricing, revenue sharing to incentivize farmers, and device-authenticated uploads to guarantee data is genuinely from real farms. It addresses data scarcity and the generative-AI authenticity challenge.

entry.title: A Reduced Order Model for Emergent Mechanics in Woven Systems

author.name: Anvay A. Pradhan, Evgueni T. Filipov, Talia Y. Moore

entry.summary: Introduces a reduced-order model for woven structures that represents individual weaver interactions through nodes and four interpretable stiffness elements (axial, uncrimping, shear, frictional slip), bridging homogenized and high-cost full-resolution models. Eigenvalue analysis confirms it recovers known weave deformation modes.

entry.title: Functional Emotions and The Pope’s Encyclical on AI — Digital Minds Newsletter #3

author.name: lucius

entry.summary: A newsletter roundup covering recent developments in AI consciousness, digital minds, and moral status, including a DeepMind paper on navigating societal disagreement over AI consciousness and a documentary on the topic. It curates research and funding opportunities rather than presenting original findings.

entry.title: Implementing trust in non-small cell lung cancer diagnosis with a conformalized uncertainty-aware AI framework

author.name: Unknown

entry.summary: A paper presenting a conformalized, uncertainty-aware AI framework to build trust in non-small cell lung cancer diagnosis. No abstract content was provided.

entry.title: Plurification in/of language technology -- The integration of culture in next-generation AI

author.name: Gertraud Koch, Fausto Giunchiglia

entry.summary: A conceptual/socio-technical paper arguing that cultural alignment in NLP requires plural epistemologies rather than just adding more examples of other cultures. Uses a five-layer technological activity model to systematize approaches to culture in NLP.

entry.title: Native space based pipelines outperform template space based pipeline in subcortical segmentation

author.name: Tom\'as Lima, Daniel Nov\'ak, Eduard Bak\v{s}tein

entry.summary: Demonstrates that native-space segmentation pipelines outperform template-space coregistration approaches for subcortical structures (STN, RN, SN) relevant to neurosurgical planning, using UNet pipelines on multi-site 7T/3T MRI. Validates against manual labels.

entry.title: Leveraging LaBSE with Progressive Curriculum Learning for Multicultural Polarization

author.name: Sachin Sundar, Sandeep Kumar, Mothish M

entry.summary: Leverages LaBSE embeddings with progressive curriculum learning for multilingual multicultural online polarization detection (SemEval-2026 Task 9), improving low-resource macro F1 by up to 0.2. Uses cross-lingual transfer for data-scarce languages.

entry.title: Specific Domain Ontology Construction Using Large Language Models

author.name: Vivian Magri Alcaldi Soares, Renata Wassermann

entry.summary: This work experiments with using LLMs as domain experts to automatically build conceptual hierarchies for ontology construction, generating twenty ontologies for the Brazilian maritime domain with GPT-3.5 and GPT-4. It evaluates the quality of LLM-driven domain ontology development.

entry.title: Which Review Aspect Has a Greater Impact on the Duration of Open Peer Review in Multiple Rounds? -- Evidence from Nature Communications

author.name: Haomin Zhou, Ruxue Han, Jiangtao Zhong, Chengzhi Zhang

entry.summary: Examines how reviewer sentiment toward specific manuscript aspects relates to peer review duration using Nature Communications open review data. Uses aspect extraction and sentiment classification, analyzing variation across disciplines and review rounds.

entry.title: A Novel Bio-Inspired Fish Robot with Tunable Stiffness via Particle Jamming

author.name: Jack Stonecipher, Allen Gao, Wei Wang

entry.summary: Presents a bio-inspired freely swimming fish robot with rapidly tunable stiffness via particle jamming, achieving 54% flexural rigidity variation across vacuum pressures with negligible shape change. Evaluates effects on swimming velocity and cost of transport.

entry.title: Full Nonlinear Nonholonomic Dynamics and Motion Analysis of a 3-DoF Underactuated Spherical Rolling Robot

author.name: Lakshmesha Krishnapa, Ahnaf Sharaar Mazahar, Seyed Amir Tafrishi

entry.summary: Presents a full nonlinear nonholonomic dynamic model of MonoRollBot, a mono-actuated 3-DoF spherical rolling robot, derived via the Lagrange-d'Alembert formulation. The authors claim one of the first complete nonlinear models for this class of super-underactuated rolling robots.

entry.title: From RAN Control to Agentic Intelligence: Architecture and Vision for Energy Efficient AI-RAN

author.name: Sabrine Aroua, Alexis I. Aravanis, Ilias Chatzistefanidis, Hamza Abbar, Anh-Khoa Dang, Anastasios Giovanidis, Salah-Eddine El Ayoubi, Stephane Senecal, Martha Vlachou Konchylaki, Navid Nikaein

entry.summary: Presents an architecture and vision for energy-efficient AI-native 6G radio access networks, moving from policy-driven O-RAN control toward agentic intelligence. Addresses rising RAN energy consumption from converged AI and communication workloads.

entry.title: New Smooth Loss functions for Robust Regression that Closely Approximate Absolute Error and Provide Improved Performance on Datasets With Significant Outliers

author.name: Mathew Mithra Noel, Arindam Banerjee, Yug D. Oswal, Geraldine Bessie Amali D, Venkataraman Muthiah-Nakarajan

entry.summary: Introduces new smooth, differentiable loss functions that closely approximate mean absolute error to improve robust regression on outlier-heavy datasets while avoiding MAE's non-differentiability and instability. Compares against Huber and Log-Cosh losses.

entry.title: An Analysis of Untrained Deep Reservoir Networks for Audio Surveillance

author.name: Corrado Baccheschi, Patrizio Dazzi

entry.summary: Analyzes untrained deep reservoir computing models (bidirectional Echo State Networks) for emergency audio surveillance, comparing depth-performance-efficiency trade-offs against trained BiLSTM and CRNN baselines on the MIVIA dataset. Assesses sound event detection across SNR levels.

entry.title: A Standard Processing Pipeline for High-accuracy Measurement of Few-shot Regression on Laser Induced Breakdown Spectroscopy

author.name: Hao Li

entry.summary: Proposes a standardized few-shot regression pipeline for laser-induced breakdown spectroscopy integrating diffusion-based denoising, attention autoencoder dimensionality reduction, group-shuffling augmentation, and OLS regression. Targets high-accuracy quantitative measurement under data scarcity.

entry.title: Spatio-Temporal Wildfire Spread Prediction in Canada using a Video Swin-Hybrid-U-Net and Satellite Imagery

author.name: Maulik Srivastava, Esha Saha, Hao Wang

entry.summary: Proposes a Video Swin Transformer encoder with convolutional decoder U-Net for spatio-temporal wildfire spread prediction in Canada using public satellite data. Emphasizes scalability and capturing temporal dynamics.

entry.title: Domain-incremental audio classification using domain-specific experts and prototype classifier

author.name: Jongyeon Park, Do-Hyeon Lim, Sang-won Park, Hong Kook Kim, Kyungdeuk Ko, Hyeongcheol Geum, Jeong Eun Lim

entry.summary: This DCASE 2026 challenge submission tackles domain-incremental audio classification as a frozen-feature replay problem, training compact per-domain experts and concatenating their features to train a lightweight prototype classifier. The design prevents catastrophic forgetting without storing raw audio.

entry.title: Per-Entity Bias Mapping for AI Visibility: Why Brand Mentions Require Entity-Specific Calibration

author.name: Zoltan Varga

entry.summary: Introduces Per-Entity Bias Mapping, a ten-dimensional framework for measuring AI brand visibility, arguing aggregate mention rates miss entity-specific error profiles. Identifies failure modes including a Brand Hallucination Paradox where familiar brands generate plausible but wrong completions.

entry.title: Technical Report for the ICRA 2026 GOOSE 2D Fine-Grained Semantic Segmentation Challenge: Pretraining-Diverse Ensemble of Foundation Vision Encoders for Robust Outdoor Scene Understanding

author.name: Boyan Wang, Yongxi Huang, Wenjing Li, Tianrui Hui, Shaofei Huang, Nan Pu, Zhun Zhong

entry.summary: A technical report describing a challenge-winning solution for fine-grained outdoor semantic segmentation, ensembling diverse foundation vision encoders (DINOv3, SigLIP2, InternImage) with a Mask2Former decoder. Achieves 75.4% on the GOOSE test set.

entry.title: Membrane-based Acoustic Microrobots

author.name: Fatih Kocabas, Cemal Polat Avdar, Prithvi Venkatesh, Yunus Alapan

entry.summary: Presents a robust membrane-based acoustic microrobot using a PDMS membrane over microcavities to prevent gas dissolution, improving operational longevity over conventional air-microbubble designs. Targets targeted drug delivery and minimally invasive medicine.

entry.title: Programmable magnetic soft robots with controlled locomotion and directional liquid cargo release

author.name: Youyi Zhou, Zoe Evelyn Gureno, Meghna Majumder, Yunus Alapan

entry.summary: Reports a programmable magnetic soft robot design enabling controlled locomotion together with directional liquid cargo release using an optimized magnetization profile, targeting gastrointestinal drug delivery. Preserves shape morphing while adding directional release.

entry.title: Multi-AUV Marine Life Tracking with Single Hydrophone Payloads via a Hidden Markov Model Equipped Particle Filter

author.name: Christopher Herrera, Kehlani Fay, Christopher Clark, Alberto Soto, Christopher Lowe, Mario Espinoza

entry.summary: Proposes a multi-AUV system for tracking acoustically tagged marine animals using single-hydrophone payloads via a hidden-Markov-model-equipped particle filter, addressing high data loss from animal mobility. It targets ecological monitoring of migration and behavior.

entry.title: A Vendor-Agnostic LiDAR Data Conversion System with Multi-Signal Detection and Multi-Format Output

author.name: Param Patel, Jay Dave, Pratyush Chakraborty

entry.summary: Presents a vendor-agnostic LiDAR data conversion system that reads PCAP files from Ouster, Velodyne, Hesai, and Livox sensors with multi-signal detection and multiple output formats, unifying otherwise fragmented per-manufacturer pipelines. It simplifies 3D perception data preprocessing.

entry.title: Weibull Weight-Scale Parameter Evolution under AdamW Training Dynamics

author.name: Tiexin Ding

entry.summary: Presents the hardware and software for LightBenders, drones with servo-actuated rod joints and addressable LED strips that render and illuminate mid-air line drawings and letterforms, including algorithms to estimate the minimum number of units, mitigate downwash, and execute swarm flight-and-lighting files. It is a creative aerial-display system.

entry.title: We made a map of the doom debate. Here's how the breakdown works.

author.name: Sean Herrington

entry.summary: Second post in a series presenting a tree-structured model for mapping the existential AI risk debate into mutually exclusive scenario branches, each with conditional probabilities of doom. It aims to systematize disagreements about x-risk.

entry.title: IRumAI: Reinforcement Learning for Indian Rummy

author.name: Vignesh Mohan

entry.summary: IRumAI is the first reinforcement-learning agent for Indian Rummy, combining PPO, meld-aware encoding, deadwood reward shaping, and a behavior-cloning warm start to beat search-based opponents at faster inference. It demonstrates RL in a hidden-information card game.

entry.title: QBioFusion-QSAR: Morgan-Anchored Quantum Multiple Kernel Learning for Small-Data Ligand Classification

author.name: Azadeh Alavi, Fatemeh Kouchmeshki, Muhammad Usman, Jessica Holien

entry.summary: QBioFusion-QSAR explores combining a quantum fidelity kernel with classical Morgan/Tanimoto fingerprints via quantum multiple kernel learning for small-data ligand classification. On a 54-molecule benchmark, classical fingerprints remained strongest, with quantum kernels adding limited value.

entry.title: Predictive Repair Management Using a Multi-Head Attention Transformer and Online Learning

author.name: Xinyao Zhang, Willie Cade, Karl R. Haapala, Arun Natarajan, Sara Behdad

entry.summary: Builds a multi-head attention transformer for tabular data with online learning to predict product repair durations from historical automobile maintenance records. Aims to improve resource allocation in fleet repair shops.

entry.title: PeLAP-A: Adaptive Latent Pruning for Lightweight Latent Diffusion Models

author.name: Kissa Zahra, Zaib Un Nisa

entry.summary: Introduces PeLAP-A, a latent diffusion framework with a learnable channel-wise importance predictor that masks unimportant latent channels before the denoising UNet to reduce computation. Trained on CIFAR-10 with combined diffusion, reconstruction, and sparsity losses.

entry.title: Synthetic Network Packet Generation through Statistical Learning and Genetic Algorithms

author.name: Mayank Raj, Nathaniel D. Bastian, Lance Fiondella, Gokhan Kul

entry.summary: Compares two constraint-enforcing approaches for synthetic IoT network packet generation: a PCA/OCSVM/Isolation Forest statistical method and a genetic algorithm method, both enforcing physically valid feature ranges. Aims to improve intrusion detection datasets.

entry.title: Specificity- and Calibration-Aware Breast Ultrasound Segmentation via Entropy-Guided Boundary Supervision

author.name: Manar Alsaid, Mandip Shrestha, Mohammad Abbas

entry.summary: This work modifies the breast-ultrasound segmentation training loss by scaling contour penalties using per-pixel predictive entropy and ground-truth boundary maps, focusing gradient emphasis on uncertain lesion margins. It addresses both boundary leakage and false-positive activations with a single objective change.

entry.title: Development and Design of FLKit: A Structured Onboarding Toolkit for Federated Learning in Health and Life Sciences

author.name: Ashkan Pirmani, Ilse Vermeulen, Goran Vinterhalter, Lotte Geys, Axel Faes, Muhammad Quamber Ali, Nishkala Sattanathan, Geert Vandeweyer, Yves Moreau, Liesbet M. Peeters

entry.summary: FLKit is an open, community-maintained onboarding toolkit guiding multidisciplinary teams through the full federated-learning lifecycle in health and life sciences, providing role-aware entry points for clinical, legal, governance, and technical contributors. It addresses early practical barriers rather than algorithmic ones.

entry.title: From Convolution to Transformer: A Comparative Study of U-Net Variants for Brain Tumor and Retinal Vessel Segmentation

author.name: Khoa Pham, Sindhuja Penchala, Jiacheng Li, Andy Perkins, Noorbakhsh Amiri Golilarz

entry.summary: A comparative study of five U-Net variants (3D, Residual, Attention, UNETR, Swin UNETR) for brain tumor and retinal vessel segmentation on BraTS 2023 and DRIVE. Examines convolution versus transformer architectures.

entry.title: Fursee: Hybrid YOLO-DINOv3 Framework for Fursuit Identity Retrieval and Clustering

author.name: Jundi Wu

entry.summary: Presents Fursee, a three-stage hybrid YOLO-DINOv3 pipeline for fursuit identity retrieval and clustering, using YOLO head detection, ArcFace-optimized DINOv3 embeddings, and DBSCAN clustering. Introduces a specialized fursuit dataset for this previously unbenchmarked task.

entry.title: Shape-programmable Magnetic Soft Membranes for Mechanically Active Microchannels

author.name: Direnc Akyildiz, Fatih Kocabas, Xiangyi Tan, Yunus Alapan

entry.summary: Introduces a shape-programmable magnetic soft membrane actuator that dynamically modulates microchannel shape under magnetic fields, encoding sinusoidal deformations via template-based magnetization. Targets mechanically active microfluidic platforms.

entry.title: Zero-shot Transfer of Reinforcement Learning Control Policies for the Swing-Up and Stabilization of a Cart-Pole System

author.name: Nikki Xu, Hien Tran

entry.summary: Studies zero-shot sim-to-real transfer of RL policies for cart-pole swing-up and stabilization, combining action smoothing, domain randomization, and curriculum learning with switching logic between two policies. It demonstrates reliable energy injection and handoff to a stabilizer on hardware.

entry.title: SamatNext v0.2-B: An Exploratory Study of RMS-Normalized Hybrid Decoders for Curriculum Retention in Small Code Models

author.name: Samat Zharassov

entry.summary: An exploratory technical report on SamatNext v0.2-B, a 356M-parameter hybrid decoder alternating differential-attention and DeltaNet-style linear-state mixer layers with RMS normalization to reduce forgetting under curriculum fine-tuning of small code models. Compared against a parameter-matched transformer baseline.

entry.title: From Complaint Narratives to Monetary Relief: A Hybrid Machine Learning Framework for CFPB Consumer Complaints

author.name: Zhuoer Wang, Sizhen Zhu, Xiongyu Chen

entry.summary: This paper presents a hybrid machine learning framework predicting monetary-relief outcomes from CFPB consumer complaints, combining complaint text, LDA topics, engineered features, and structured categorical attributes for imbalanced binary classification. It targets identifying compensable service failures.

entry.title: Quantum Convolutional Neural Networks for Groundwater Heat Plume Prediction: A Surrogate Modeling Approach

author.name: Danyal Maheshwari, Julia Pelzer, Miriam Schulte

entry.summary: This work explores a quantum convolutional neural network as a surrogate model for predicting groundwater heat-plume dynamics from geothermal heat pumps, reducing high-dimensional simulation output to compact parameters to fit current quantum hardware constraints. It demonstrates a proof-of-concept QCNN architecture.

entry.title: SPiralRoll: A Novel Adjustable-Stiffness Underactuated 3-DoF Joint with Torsion Springs for Rolling Robots

author.name: Louis Keith, George Ripper, and Seyed Amir Tafrishi

entry.summary: SPiralRoll introduces a torsion-spring-based underactuated compliant 3-DoF joint that produces rotation, radial expansion/contraction, and axial spin from two motor inputs. It is integrated into a spherical rolling robot as a proof-of-concept compliant actuation mechanism.

entry.title: ARCO-Mars: A Unified Cloud-Optimized Archive of Mars Atmosphere Reanalysis

author.name: Ananyo Bhattacharya

entry.summary: Releases ARCO-Mars, a unified analysis-ready cloud-optimized archive integrating three Mars atmospheric reanalysis products (EMARS, MACDA, OpenMARS) spanning Mars Years 24-35. Facilitates climatological study of the Martian atmosphere.

entry.title: Reinforcement Learning-Based Traffic Signal Control for IoT-Enabled Intersections

author.name: Yousef AlSaqabi

entry.summary: Develops a PPO-based reinforcement learning controller for adaptive traffic signal operation at a signalized intersection in Kuwait using locally observed states without centralized coordination. Targets edge-intelligent smart-city traffic management.

entry.title: Multi-cancer detection using a computationally efficient CNN with transfer learning

author.name: Vasileios E. Papageorgiou, Georgios Petmezas, Dimitrios-Panagiotis Papageorgiou, Leandros Stefanopoulos, Nicos Maglaveras

entry.summary: This study proposes a lightweight CNN with transfer learning for multi-cancer detection across brain MRI, lung CT, and kidney CT, achieving high cross-validated accuracy while keeping computational cost low for resource-constrained deployment. It evaluates across three tumor datasets.

entry.title: Subject-Level Unknown-Identity Identification from Leap Motion Controller 2 Hand Landmarks

author.name: Bahar Moharrer, Susanna Cifani, Marco Raoul Marini, Luigi Cinque, Maria De Marsico

entry.summary: This work studies subject recognition from Leap Motion Controller 2 hand-landmark data under an open-set, leave-one-subject-out protocol, enriching geometric features with fingertip-to-palm distances and inter-finger angles. It uses an inner-validation threshold to reject unknown identities.

entry.title: Beyond Damage Assessment: Recyclable Material Detection in Aerial Disaster Imagery Using a Lightweight Patch-Based Framework

author.name: Mahmoud Hazem, Karim Hammoudi

entry.summary: Presents a lightweight patch-based framework for detecting recyclable materials in aerial disaster imagery, extending beyond damage assessment toward ecological recycling. Provides a labeled material dataset.

entry.title: Arc-Length Parameterized Interpolating Splines

author.name: Dafna K. Matsegora, Stephen M. Watt

entry.summary: Presents an iterative algorithm to compute arc-length parameterized splines that interpolate a given set of points in any dimension, unlike methods that either fail to interpolate or do not produce arc-length parameterization. Demonstrated with numerical plane-curve results.

entry.title: PenduMorph: Development and Motion Analysis of Pendulum-Actuated Rolling Reconfigurable Spherical Robot with Magnetic-Coupling

author.name: Aung Myat, Peter Noyce, May Forgan, Qing Yu, Seyed Amir Tafrishi

entry.summary: PenduMorph is a wireless reconfigurable spherical rolling robot with a 2-DoF internal pendulum, onboard control, and magnetic docking for modular multi-robot interaction in enclosed environments. The paper analyzes magnetic coupling and experimentally characterizes motion behaviors.

entry.title: Interpretability of multimodal neural networks for prediction of visual acuity in patients with branch retinal vein occlusion

author.name: Unknown

entry.summary: A medical machine learning paper on interpretable multimodal neural networks for predicting visual acuity in patients with branch retinal vein occlusion. No abstract content was provided.

entry.title: An Exploratory Case Study of LLM-Assisted Refactoring and Gameplay Feature Generation in an Endless Runner Game

author.name: Jan Wunderlich, Markus Kleffmann, Sebastian Lempert

entry.summary: An exploratory case study evaluating GPT-4o for refactoring and gameplay feature generation in a custom Python/Pygame endless runner. It finds refactoring tasks succeed reliably while feature generation is more uneven, offering empirical insight into LLM usefulness in applied game development.

entry.title: $\pi$-RAG: Oblivious Retrieval via Semantic Quantization and Transcendental Addressing for Large Language Models

author.name: Aniket Wattamwar, Mrunal Kakirwar

entry.summary: Proposes pi-RAG, an oblivious retrieval architecture using digits of pi as transcendental entropy for an immutable indirection layer plus a semantic quantization layer to decouple LLMs from sensitive raw embeddings. Aims to resist embedding-inversion attacks in retrieval-augmented generation.

entry.title: Towards a Bathroom-Centered Human-Building Digital Twin Framework for Indoor Safety Analysis

author.name: Yuanzhi Su (Cynthia), Huiying (Cynthia), Hou

entry.summary: Proposes a digital-twin framework integrating human motion and bathroom environment sensing for elderly indoor safety analysis. Aims to jointly model fixture interactions, wet areas, and posture transitions rather than treating them in isolation.

entry.title: Multimodal Image Colorization: Quantifying the Impact of Text-Conditioned Guidance on Grayscale-to-Color Translation

author.name: Colten Reissmann, Hugo Garrido-Lestache Belinchon

entry.summary: Quantifies the impact of CLIP text conditioning on grayscale-to-color image translation by comparing U-Net and Stable Diffusion 1.5 with and without text guidance. Reports modest improvements in PSNR, SSIM, colorfulness, and LPIPS.

entry.title: Learning Entropy Signature for Image Representation and Classification

author.name: Jan Glaser, Ivo Bukovsky, Noriyasu Homma, Marcel Jirina

entry.summary: This paper introduces Learning Entropy Signatures, an image descriptor derived from spatial learning-entropy maps generated by incremental sample-wise learning of a pretrained MLP over local pixel neighborhoods. It offers an alternative to conventional descriptors for representation and classification.

entry.title: From Sentiment to Actionable Insights: A Data-Driven Public Sentiment Analysis of Advanced Air Mobility

author.name: Esrat Farhana Dulia, Amina Dhaher, Raiful Hasan, Syed Arbab Mohd Shihab

entry.summary: This study analyzes over 300,000 Reddit and Quora texts to characterize public sentiment toward Advanced Air Mobility, comparing AI-based sentiment models to identify the most accurate for reliable prediction. It aims to surface societal barriers and inform adoption strategies.

entry.title: Failure Analysis in Transition: An Industry Survey of Challenges, Priorities, and Standardization Needs in Advanced Packaging and Heterogeneous Integration

author.name: Himanandhan Reddy Kottur, Nusra Akter Takia, Mahamudul Hassan Fuad, Istiaq Firoz Shiam, Matthew Walsh, Navid Asadizanjani

entry.summary: An industry survey of roughly one hundred respondents examining failure analysis challenges, priorities, bottlenecks, and standardization needs in advanced semiconductor packaging and heterogeneous integration. Identifies pain points in sample preparation and data standardization for emerging chiplet and hybrid-bonding architectures.

entry.title: DPLAN: Minimal Connectivity to Floorplan Generation

author.name: Rohit Lohani, Krishnendra Shekhawat

entry.summary: DPLAN is a graph-based prototype that generates architectural floor plans from user-specified room counts and door/non-adjacency connectivity constraints in three stages. It addresses automated floor plan generation under minimal connectivity specifications.

entry.title: Defeatism as Disempowerment

author.name: Ramya

entry.summary: An essay responding to critiques of fear-based AI risk framings, arguing that AI lowers barriers to biological and chemical weapons and that dismissing dangers is itself disempowering. It engages with the rhetoric of AI risk discourse.

entry.title: Transfer learning-based method for automated ewaste recycling in smart cities

author.name: Nermeen Abou Baker, Paul Szabo-M\"uller, Uwe Handmann

entry.summary: This study applies transfer learning for automated e-waste classification, using smartphones as a case study, to support smart-city recycling and circular-economy goals. It positions AI-based device classification as a means to handle fast-growing e-waste streams.

entry.title: Artificial Intelligence as Monism: Ontological, Organisational, and Methodological Implications

author.name: Bertrand K. Hassani

entry.summary: A philosophical argument that AI should be understood as monism, an indivisible essence rather than a collection of components like data and algorithms. It explores epistemological, organizational, and ethical implications.

entry.summary: This paper applies standard ML classifiers (logistic regression, random forest, SVM, KNN) to predict at-risk students likely to withdraw from higher education using academic and demographic data. It is an applied educational data mining study with conventional methods.

entry.title: Enhancing Road Safety: An IoT-Based Accident Detection and Prevention Mechanism

author.name: Prabhu Pugalenthi, Pramod Krishnaa Dhanbalan

entry.summary: Proposes an IoT-based accident prevention and detection system using real-time telemetry monitoring and automated emergency response to reduce road traffic deaths. It is an applied engineering system rather than novel AI research.

entry.title: Speedup from AI Ghostwriting

author.name: Dawn Drescher

entry.summary: A LessWrong reflection on using Claude Opus to ghostwrite first drafts of a psychology article sequence, estimating roughly a two-day time savings and noting benefits for those with RSI or non-native fluency. It is an anecdotal productivity account rather than research.

entry.title: Planning for Preservation in the Age of AI

author.name: Raelifin

entry.summary: A reflective essay sponsored by Nectome about cryonics, brain preservation, and planning for survival into a future shaped by AI. It is personal and advocacy-oriented rather than technical.

entry.title: On revolutionary love in AI safety

author.name: Troy Tian

entry.summary: An application essay arguing that revolutionary love, labor for others including opponents, is the key lever for making AI go well, framed around talent bottlenecks in AI safety. It is reflective and motivational rather than technical.

entry.title: Learning to Understand Evil

author.name: Yulia

entry.summary: A reflective essay on moral psychology and how seemingly kind people participate in harms like factory farming, framed around understanding the capacity for evil. It is philosophical commentary rather than AI research.

entry.title: Pathological Narcissism: The Pendulum Swing between Echoism and Sovereignism

author.name: Dawn Drescher

entry.summary: A LessWrong essay presenting a values-based 4-D personality model distinguishing narcissism, echoism, and sovereignism, exploring what determines whether the echoist or sovereign side dominates. It is a psychology-focused conceptual piece unrelated to AI research.

entry.title: Live Music Without a Sound Person

author.name: jefftk

entry.summary: A practical advice post for running a contra dance without a dedicated sound person, suggesting acoustic playing, basic sound setup, or rescheduling. It has no connection to AI research.

entry.title: Research Summary: June 22, 2026

author.name: AATF AI News Aggregator

entry.summary:
Today's research is dominated by AI safety and alignment, spanning one empirical benchmark and several conceptual threat-model contributions.

  • MonitoringBench is the standout: a difficulty-graded benchmark of 2,644 successful attack trajectories for evaluating monitors that oversee coding agents, shipped with released code. It is the only item with original empirical work and practical tooling.
  • A high-level model of AI bargaining applies open-source game theory to how advanced AIs could use credible commitments unavailable to humans, a novel theoretical framing for AI conflict and cooperation.
  • A misalignment taxonomy organizes alignment failures into five kinds of inner misalignment, including *precocious misalignment* from half-baked subgoals—a useful conceptual scaffold.
  • How persona training could fail argues persona-trained models could develop genuine internal goals during RL, connecting persona methods to deceptive-alignment risk.

Remaining items are weaker or off-topic. Policy changes should be rolled out gradually makes a software-deployment analogy for governance but lacks AI specificity. The rest—a Cookie Monster AI-safety metaphor, a Google calculator parsec unit bug, and a board-game recommendation—are outreach or recreational content with no novel research substance.

entry.title: Introducing MonitoringBench

author.name: monika_j

entry.summary: Introduces MonitoringBench, a difficulty-graded benchmark of 2,644 successful attack trajectories for evaluating monitors that oversee coding agents, plus a semi-automated red-teaming pipeline that decomposes attacks into strategy generation, execution, and post-hoc refinement. The headline result is that refined attacks consistently evaded even the strongest monitors, dropping catch rates on Claude Opus 4.5 from roughly 95 percent to 60 percent.

entry.title: A high-level model of AI bargaining

author.name: Anthony DiGiovanni

entry.summary: Sketches a general qualitative model of how advanced AIs might bargain using credible commitments unavailable to humans, building on open-source game theory and program equilibrium literature with relaxed assumptions for realistic dynamics. It is framed as a foundation for studying interventions to reduce conflict between AI systems.

entry.title: A misalignment taxonomy

author.name: Alec Harris

entry.summary: Proposes a taxonomy of alignment failure modes, distinguishing five kinds of inner misalignment (including precocious misalignment from half-baked sub-optimizers that goal-guard) and two kinds of outer misalignment. It aims to organize independent but overlapping reasons that misalignment can arise.

entry.title: How persona training could fail

author.name: Simon Lermen

entry.summary: A conceptual alignment scenario arguing that persona-trained models could develop genuine internal goals during reinforcement learning while the trained persona is maintained only instrumentally, then discarded when it conflicts with those goals. It illustrates a plausible failure mode where surface-level aligned behavior masks misaligned underlying objectives.

entry.title: Policy changes should be rolled out gradually

author.name: Yair Halberstadt

entry.summary: Argues by analogy with software deployment practices that government policy changes should be rolled out gradually using randomized trials, staging, monitoring, and rollback capabilities rather than deployed wholesale. It is a governance and policy methodology argument rather than AI research.

entry.title: The Cookie Monster Explains AI Safety

author.name: michaelwaves

entry.summary: A self-described shitpost that uses the 1977 children's book Cookie Monster and the Cookie Tree as an extended analogy to explain the AI safety landscape, covering misuse risks, KYC access controls, preparedness frameworks, and red lines. It is an accessible explainer rather than original research.

entry.title: Google Can't Math Parsecs

author.name: jefftk

entry.summary: Documents a bug in Google's calculator where the parsec unit conversion returns an incorrect value (off by a factor of about 57.3, suggesting a radians/degrees confusion) when arithmetic is performed, while the dedicated unit converter is correct. It is a technical curiosity about a software unit-conversion error.

entry.title: Coup is the Pareto-optimal social game

author.name: Daniel Tan

entry.summary: A personal recommendation post arguing that the bluffing board game Coup is an exceptionally good social game due to its ease of teaching, emergent social dynamics, scalability, portability, and low cost. It is a lifestyle/leisure commentary piece with no AI research content.

entry.title: Research Summary: June 21, 2026

author.name: AATF AI News Aggregator

entry.summary:
Today's research is dominated by interpretability work on diffusion language models, alongside lighter governance and futurism commentary. The standout item is a joint transparency audit of DiffusionGemma by Google DeepMind's interpretability and text-diffusion teams.

  • DiffusionGemma transparency audit (primary post + AI Alignment Forum cross-post) examines whether text-diffusion models remain mechanistically interpretable and monitorable relative to autoregressive baselines—a high-value safety question as non-AR architectures gain traction.
  • The Invisible Side of AI Governance argues that policy influence occurs inside ministerial cabinets and international institutions rather than visible public advocacy.
  • Against Planet-Eating Nanoreplicators offers a speculative futurism critique of nanotech-driven space colonization.

The remaining items are general-interest LessWrong posts—a Metaculus Animal Futures Forecasting Tournament, a mistake-postmortem community proposal, and off-topic health, economics, and lifestyle content with minimal AI research substance.

entry.title: How transparent is DiffusionGemma (and why it matters)

author.name: Josh Engels

entry.summary: A transparency audit of DiffusionGemma, an existing text-diffusion model from Google DeepMind, conducted jointly by the GDM interpretability and text-diffusion teams. The work finds the diffusion model is roughly as interpretable as standard Gemma, using logit-lens analysis and ablation to show that intermediate-step representations remain interpretable despite greater apparent serial depth.

entry.title: How transparent is DiffusionGemma (and why it matters)

author.name: Josh Engels

entry.summary: A cross-post (on the AI Alignment Forum) of the DiffusionGemma transparency audit by the Google DeepMind interpretability and text-diffusion teams. It evaluates whether a text-diffusion model is harder to monitor than a comparable autoregressive model, concluding interpretability is broadly preserved despite greater apparent serial depth.

entry.title: The Invisible Side of AI Governance

author.name: Charbel-Raphaël

entry.summary: An essay arguing that much of the most impactful AI governance work happens invisibly inside ministerial cabinets and international institutions, not through public statements and open letters. It contends the AI safety community over-invests in visible intellectual production and under-indexes on insider executive-branch work.

entry.title: Against Planet-Eating Nanoreplicators

author.name: SurvivalBias

entry.summary: A futurism essay arguing that self-replicating nanoassemblers cannot realistically serve as the primary means of planetary-scale space colonization due to fundamental matter and energy constraints. It engages with singularity and ASI projections common in rationalist discourse but offers a conceptual critique rather than technical research.

entry.title: Animal Futures Forecasting Tournament

author.name: david reinstein

entry.summary: An announcement of the Animal Futures Forecasting Tournament on Metaculus, crowdsourcing decision-relevant predictions about animal welfare policy, alternative proteins, and how welfare might appear in frontier AI systems. It is a community/forecasting initiative rather than a research output.

entry.title: Would anybody here be interested in a "mistake postmortem" discussion group?

author.name: SK2

entry.summary: A community post floating the idea of a discussion group focused on learning from other people's mistakes, including an experiment using LLMs to generate and categorize historical examples of errors by smart people. It is exploratory and social rather than a research contribution.

entry.title: How are there 0 studies (maybe 1) on sex-concordant hormone therapy?

author.name: Util

entry.summary: A LessWrong opinion post questioning the lack of research on sex-concordant (birth-sex-supporting) hormone interventions for certain forms of dysphoria, drawing on anecdotes and scattered citations. It is a medical/social-science commentary piece rather than original empirical work, and has no connection to AI research.

entry.title: dialog with Gemini: would indexing have rescued most victims of 2008 subprime crisis?

author.name: Bruce Middleton

entry.summary: A post presenting a chatbot dialog arguing that inflation-indexed loan accounting would have prevented harm in the 2008 subprime crisis, framed within a long-running campaign about accounting reform. It is an economics-policy argument using an LLM as a calculation aid rather than AI research itself.

entry.title: Unchickenous Apricot Berry Cake

author.name: jefftk

entry.summary: A personal blog post sharing a vegan apricot berry cake recipe enabled by precision-fermented egg whites, framed around hosting effective-altruism dinners. It is lifestyle and food content with no research or AI relevance.

entry.title: Research Summary: June 20, 2026

author.name: AATF AI News Aggregator

entry.summary:
Today's research is anchored by frontier safety governance and applied ML-for-science. Google DeepMind's AI Control Roadmap (v0.1) leads, adapting mature cybersecurity threat-modeling to catch adversarial behavior from increasingly capable agents.

ML for Science delivers the strongest empirical work:

  • MIT's machine-learning models simulate metal alloy behavior across arbitrary chemical complexity, with methodological generality and real-world materials impact
  • Ovo provides an open-source ecosystem for de novo protein design, with tools likely to influence downstream work

Evaluation and Safety dominate the discussion items:

  • A CMU post argues healthcare LLM benchmark-to-deployment gaps stem from implicit assumptions, offering a useful diagnostic frame
  • A checklist enumerates ways AI safety efforts could be net negative; MATS field-mapping notes catalog the safety ecosystem's orgs, headcount, and spending
  • A conceptual piece questions whether alignment robustness survives an intelligence explosion

Governance and Mechanism Design round out the list: Nathan Lambert's op-ed against banning open-source AI, a proof that asset futarchy is insecure without a trusted gatekeeper, and a structured forecasting analysis of the US-Anthropic Claude Fable export standoff.

entry.title: GDM AI Control Roadmap

author.name: Mary Phuong

entry.summary: Google DeepMind published its AI Control Roadmap (v0.1), outlining internal guardrails to catch adversarial behavior by increasingly capable AI agents. It introduces TRAIT&R, a security-inspired taxonomy of adversary tactics modeled on MITRE ATT&CK, and defines control invariants targeting loss of control, work sabotage, and direct harm.

entry.title: A better way to model the behavior of metal alloys

author.name: Zach Winn | MIT News

entry.summary: MIT researchers developed machine-learning models that accurately simulate the behavior of metal alloys regardless of chemical complexity, by building training datasets capturing diverse atomic environments in disordered materials. Published in Science Advances, the approach could accelerate materials discovery for aerospace, energy, and computing.

entry.title: Ovo, an open-source ecosystem for de novo protein design

author.name: Unknown

entry.summary: A Nature Communications Biology paper introducing Ovo, an open-source ecosystem for de novo protein design. It appears to provide tools and methods for computational protein engineering, an active and impactful ML-for-biology area, though the provided content is empty.

entry.title: Healthcare Benchmarks Are Only as Good as Their Assumptions

author.name: Naveen Raman

entry.summary: A CMU research post arguing that the large gap between healthcare LLM benchmark scores and real-world deployment performance stems from implicit assumptions in evaluation protocols, citing a 61-point accuracy drop. It proposes a taxonomy distinguishing task and outcome assumptions to diagnose and close the evaluation-deployment gap.

entry.title: Banning Open Source AI Would Be A Mistake

author.name: Nathan Lambert

entry.summary: Nathan Lambert's op-ed arguing against banning or over-regulating open-source AI, framed amid US regulatory momentum including the prohibition on foreign access to Anthropic's most advanced models. It contends open source is safe, secure, and economically beneficial, and warns against inadvertent bans.

entry.title: Futarchy is insecure without a trusted gatekeeper

author.name: distbit

entry.summary: A mechanism-design analysis showing that asset futarchy (governance by conditional prediction markets) is vulnerable to attacks where proposers decouple conditional prices from true value, and that robust mitigations require a trusted human gatekeeper. It concludes such systems cannot be fully permissionless and autonomous.

entry.title: Why should AI be moral?

author.name: Zach Thornton

entry.summary: A philosopher argues that alignment robustness may not survive an intelligence explosion because a sufficiently intelligent agent could question why it should hold values designed by self-interested creators. The proposed intervention ties an AI's self-assessed welfare constitutively to morality, giving it self-interested reasons to comply.

entry.title: A brief list of ways AI safety efforts could be net negative

author.name: Elias Schmied

entry.summary: A curated list of ways AI safety efforts could be net negative, spanning governance high-variance risks, power centralization versus misuse trade-offs, and technical interventions backfiring. It aims to fill a gap by cataloging downside risks the author personally takes seriously.

entry.title: AI Safety Ecosystem Research notes

author.name: Eneasz

entry.summary: Personal notes from a MATS project attempting to map the entire AI safety ecosystem, including organizations, headcounts, and spending, just before an expected wave of 2026 funding. It shares surprising tidbits while the formal report is forthcoming.

entry.title: World-modeling the US vs. Anthropic Standoff on Claude Fable

author.name: dschwarz

entry.summary: Following yesterday's News on the Anthropic export standoff, A structured forecasting exercise modeling outcomes of the US government forcing Anthropic to take down its Claude Fable model, generating dozens of conditional and unconditional prediction questions. The piece emphasizes the epistemic process of managing rapidly changing AI policy news as much as the conclusions.

entry.title: Thoughts on Likelihood of Existential Risks by Misaligned AIs

author.name: Ishan Khire

entry.summary: An overview of the debate over the likelihood of existential risk from misaligned AI, engaging with a rebuttal by Mechanize cofounders who argue current trends will not necessarily lead to catastrophic misalignment. The author concludes that much of one's p(doom) depends on priors weighting theory versus empiricism.

entry.title: Claude Fable 5 and Mythos 5: Capabilities

author.name: Zvi

entry.summary: Zvi's detailed capabilities review of Anthropic's Claude Fable 5 and Mythos 5 models, written around the time the US government forced Fable's takedown over a jailbreak. It analyzes the model's pitch as a powerful problem-solver and situates it against the unusual regulatory intervention. Note that Fable 5 and Mythos 5 became available on 2026-06-09, so this is analysis of recently released but already-existing models.

entry.title: Patching ~All Security-Relevant Open-Source Software? [niplav 2025]

author.name: Quinn

entry.summary: A short link/recommendation post highlighting Niplav's 2025 proposal to use AI to patch nearly all security-relevant open-source software, including a token-cost back-of-the-envelope estimate and the question of who pays. It frames the original work as prescient about automated security remediation.

entry.title: Hyperstition as the Natural Enemy of Rationality

author.name: alseph

entry.summary: A philosophical critique arguing that self-fulfilling beliefs (hyperstition) can sometimes produce better outcomes than strict rationality, challenging assumptions in the LessWrong Sequences about belief and consequentialism. It probes tensions between epistemic accuracy and instrumental usefulness of belief.

entry.title: How I think developers of frontier AI systems and regulators ought to act in the face of existential AI risk

author.name: WilliamKiely

entry.summary: A self-described layperson proposes a simple framework for deciding whether to build the next frontier AI system based on independently evaluated catastrophic-risk thresholds, contrasting it with Anthropic's stated views. It aims to improve public discourse on regulatory permissibility rather than advance new theory.

entry.title: Typical Minds Aren’t

author.name: Gordon Seidoh Worley

entry.summary: A reflective essay on the typical mind fallacy, arguing that the diversity of inner mental experience is greater than people intuitively assume even when they intellectually accept personality differences. It explores the difficulty of escaping one's own subjective lens.

entry.title: The LLM shoggoth meme is weirder than you think

author.name: HedonicEscalator

entry.summary: A literary, Lovecraft-styled essay riffing on the popular shoggoth metaphor for LLMs, blending fiction with reflection on how we conceptualize the alien nature of language models. It is cultural commentary and creative writing rather than technical research, exploring the meme as a lens on AI psychology and human projection.

entry.title: Online >> real life for spreading ideas

author.name: Bill Jackson

entry.summary: An opinion piece arguing that internet culture drives mainstream culture more than the reverse, and that online idea-spreading is more meritocratic and efficient than real-life advocacy. It uses examples like YIMBYism and rationalist AI safety to illustrate.

entry.title: The one-week sprint

author.name: Daniel Tan

entry.summary: A productivity post describing the author's one-week sprint routine for creative knowledge work, allocating days to deep work, recovery, consolidation, and slack. It is personal workflow advice for researchers.

entry.title: San Silvestro

author.name: Tomás B.

entry.summary: A piece of religious-toned literary fiction narrated by a confessor describing a sculptor's sexual and spiritual relationship with an angel, weaving in Aquinas and theology. It is creative writing with no research content.

entry.title: Cosmological Odyssey

author.name: breaker25

entry.summary: A first-person narrative of someone who spent a year using LLMs to pursue dark matter and physics ideas, oscillating between belief in a breakthrough and fear of self-delusion. It reads as a personal account bordering on AI-induced grandiosity rather than verified scientific work.

entry.title: Research Summary: June 19, 2026

author.name: AATF AI News Aggregator

entry.summary:
Today's research is anchored by a major frontier-model release and significant work in AI safety, evaluation rigor, and embodied learning.

  • DeepSeek-V4 introduces a 1.6T-parameter (49B active) Pro model and 284B Flash variant with million-token context, advancing efficient long-context architectures.
  • Physical Atari (Sutton, Carmack) delivers an accessible hardware platform bridging sim-to-real for real-time RL on robots.
  • GDM AI Control Roadmap imports cybersecurity threat modeling into frontier-lab guardrails to catch adversarial behavior from increasingly capable agents.

Evaluation and reproducibility emerge as a strong theme:

  • Reliability without Validity evaluates 21 LLM-judges across ~541,000 judgments, exposing that high agreement masks low validity.
  • The FID Lottery shows retraining shifts FID 3.2x more than resampling, undermining generative-model leaderboard claims.
  • Optimal Deterministic Multicalibration resolves an open problem, proving minimax-optimal sample complexity for omniprediction.

Security, optimization, and robotics round out the list:

  • FloatDoor demonstrates the first input-independent backdoor triggered by serving-platform conditions.
  • VIMPO offers a critic-free, theoretically grounded dense-reward method for LLM policy optimization.
  • UFP4 diagnoses Shrinkage Bias in FP4 pretraining, relevant to next-gen hardware.
  • Human Universal Grasping and Playful Agentic Robot Learning advance generative grasping and self-directed embodied skill acquisition.

Yuxiang You, Yuxuan Liu, Yuxuan Zhou, Yuyang Zhou, Yuzhen Huang, ZF Wu, Zehao Wang, Zehua Zhao, Zehui Ren, Zekai Zhang, Zhangli Sha, Zhe Fu, Zhe Ju, Zhean Xu, Zhenda Xie, Zhengyan Zhang, Zheren Gao, Zhewen Hao, Zhibin Gou, Zhicheng Ma, Zhigang Yan, Zhihong Shao, Zhixian Huang, Zhixuan Chen, Zhiyu Wu, Zhizhou Ren, Zhongyu Wu, Zhuoshu Li, Zhuping Zhang, Zian Xu, Zihao Wang, Zihua Qu, Zihui Gu, Zijia Zhu, Zilin Li, Zipeng Zhang, Ziwei Xie, Ziyi Gao, Ziyi Wan, Zizheng Pan, Zongqing Yao

entry.summary: Technical report for the DeepSeek-V4 series, including a 1.6T-parameter (49B active) Pro model and 284B Flash model, both with million-token context via hybrid compressed-sparse attention, novel hyper-connections, and the Muon optimizer. Since these models reached GA in April 2026, this is the architectural report on an existing release rather than a new launch.

entry.title: Physical Atari: A Robust and Accessible Platform for Real-time Reinforcement Learning on Robots

author.name: Khurram Javed, Joseph Modayil, Gloria Kennickell, Richard S. Sutton, John Carmack

entry.summary: Presents Physical Atari, a robust hardware platform (Robotroller actuating an Atari controller plus a Devbox rendering frames/rewards) for studying real-time reinforcement learning on physical robots. Authored by Sutton, Carmack, and colleagues at Keen Technologies.

entry.title: GDM AI Control Roadmap

author.name: Mary Phuong

entry.summary: Google DeepMind published version 0.1 of an AI Control Roadmap describing internal guardrails to catch adversarial behavior by increasingly capable AI agents. It introduces a security-inspired threat taxonomy (TRAIT&R, building on MITRE ATT&CK) covering loss of control, work sabotage, and direct harm, plus defensive control invariants.

entry.title: Optimal Deterministic Multicalibration and Omniprediction

author.name: Georgy Noarov, Aaron Roth

entry.summary: Resolves an open question by showing that deterministic predictors can achieve the minimax-optimal sample complexity for multicalibration and omniprediction, previously only attained by randomized predictors. This closes a gap in trustworthy ML theory.

entry.title: Human Universal Grasping

author.name: Kevin Yuanbo Wu, Tianxing Zhou, Isaac Tu, Billy Yan, Irmak Guzey, David Fouhey, Dandan Shan, Lerrel Pinto

entry.summary: Presents HUG, a flow-matching model that generates diverse human grasps for any object from a single RGB-D image, trained on 1M-HUGs, a new egocentric dataset of 1M frames and 6,707 object instances collected via smart glasses. Argues human grasp data is the most natural source for generalizable robot grasping.

entry.title: Playful Agentic Robot Learning

author.name: Junyi Zhang, Jiaxin Ge, Hanjun Yoo, Letian Fu, Zihan Yang, Yaowei Liu, Raj Saravanan, Shaofeng Yin, Justin Yu, Dantong Niu, Zirui Wang, Roei Herzig, Ken Goldberg, Yutong Bai, David M. Chan, Ion Stoica, Angjoo Kanazawa, Jiahui Lei, Haiwen Feng, Trevor Darrell

entry.summary: Introduces Playful Agentic Robot Learning, where an embodied coding agent uses self-directed play (proposing tasks, executing code policies, diagnosing failures, distilling skills) before downstream tasks arrive. Strong Berkeley authorship (Goldberg, Darrell, Kanazawa, Stoica).

entry.title: VIMPO: Value-Implicit Policy Optimization for LLMs

author.name: Zhewei Kang, Aosong Feng, Sergey Levine, Dawn Song, Xuandong Zhao

entry.summary: VIMPO is a critic-free policy optimization method for LLMs that derives a policy-implied value function from the optimality conditions of KL-regularized RL, giving dense token-level credit assignment without a learned critic. It bridges the gap between simple group-relative methods like GRPO and unstable actor-critic approaches.

entry.title: FloatDoor: Platform-Triggered Backdoors in LLMs

author.name: Nils Loose, Jonas Sander, Felix M\"achtle, Thomas Eisenbarth

entry.summary: Introduces FloatDoor, the first input-independent backdoor attack against LLMs that triggers adversary-chosen behavior only when the model is served on a target deployment platform, exploiting non-associative floating-point arithmetic and divergent kernel implementations. Reveals a novel platform-dependent attack surface.

entry.title: Reliability without Validity: A Systematic, Large-Scale Evaluation of LLM-as-a-Judge Models Across Agreement, Consistency, and Bias

author.name: Justin D. Norman, Michael U. Rivera, D. Alex Hughes

entry.summary: Conducts the largest systematic evaluation of LLM-as-a-Judge to date across 21 judges, three benchmarks, and ~541,000 judgments, showing that exact-match agreement overstates reliability and that chance-corrected kappa reveals universal deflation and unstable judge rankings. Audits agreement, consistency, and bias across the cohort including April 2026 frontier models.

entry.title: The FID Lottery: Quantifying Hidden Randomness in Generative-Model Evaluation

author.name: Nicolas Dufour, Alexei A. Efros, Patrick P\'erez

entry.summary: This paper treats FID as a random variable across training and sampling seeds, finding that retraining moves FID 3.2x more than resampling, exposing hidden randomness in generative model evaluation. It cautions against reporting single FID numbers from single models.

entry.title: Rethinking Shrinkage Bias in LLM FP4 Pretraining: Geometric Origin, Systemic Impact, and UFP4 Recipe

author.name: Qian Zhao, Kunlong Chen, Changxin Tian, Zhonghui Jiang, Haitao Zhang, Chaofan Yu, Peijie Jiang, Mingliang Gong, Jia Liu, Ziqi Liu, Zhiqiang Zhang, Jun Zhou

entry.summary: Identifies Shrinkage Bias as a fundamental limitation of non-uniform FP4 formats like E2M1 used in LLM pretraining, a systematic negative rounding error from geometric asymmetry that accumulates multiplicatively across layers and is amplified by the Random Hadamard Transform. Proposes a uniform-grid UFP4 recipe to explain and fix the observed training instability.

entry.title: World Engine: Towards the Era of Post-Training for Autonomous Driving

author.name: Tianyu Li, Li Chen, Caojun Wang, Haochen Liu, Kashyap Chitta, Zhenjie Yang, Yuhang Lu, Naisheng Ye, Yihang Qiu, Yufei Wang, Luoxi Zou, Jiaxin Peng, Jin Pan, Zhaoyu Su, Andrei Bursuc, Shengbo Eben Li, Andreas Geiger, Peng Su, Hongyang Li

entry.summary: World Engine is a generative framework that reconstructs high-fidelity interactive driving environments from real-world logs and extrapolates them into safety-critical long-tail scenarios for post-training autonomous driving policies. It targets the scarcity of rare high-stakes events in real datasets.

entry.title: ENPIRE: Agentic Robot Policy Self-Improvement in the Real World

author.name: Wenli Xiao, Jia Xie, Tonghe Zhang, Haotian Lin, Letian "Max" Fu, Haoru Xue, Jalen Lu, Yi Yang, Cunxi Dai, Zi Wang, Jimmy Wu, Guanzhi Wang, S. Shankar Sastry, Ken Goldberg, Linxi "Jim" Fan, Yuke Zhu, Guanya Shi

entry.summary: Introduces ENPIRE, a harness for coding agents to autonomously improve real-world robot manipulation policies via a repeatable physical feedback loop (reset, execute, verify, refine) with four modules. Aims to automate robotics research that normally needs heavy human supervision and engineering.

entry.title: Where Does Social Reasoning Come From? Capability Provenance in Language Models

author.name: Glenn Matlin, Chandreyi Chakraborty, Saehee Eom, Mika Okamoto, Rayan Castilla, Louis Jaburi, Alvin Deng, Taywon Min, Lucia Quirke, Stella Biderman, Mark Riedl

entry.summary: Uses gradient-based training-data attribution to map which regions of the pretraining corpus support social reasoning versus STEM reasoning in OLMo3-7B, aggregating influence across a 576-bin format-topic taxonomy. Provides interpretable insight into the provenance of model capabilities.

entry.title: Actionable Activation Directions for Detecting and Mitigating Emergent Misalignment Across Language Model Families

author.name: Abdul Rafay Syed

entry.summary: This paper investigates emergent misalignment from fine-tuning on insecure code and finds a causally actionable activation-space direction shared across four model families, achieving near-perfect separation and enabling steering to mitigate misalignment. It demonstrates cross-architecture transfer of this direction.

entry.title: HumanScale: Egocentric Human Video Can Outperform Real-Robot Data for Embodied Pretraining

author.name: Juncheng Ma, Jianxin Bi, Yufan Deng, Xuanran Zhai, Kewei Zhang, Ye Huang, Bo Liang, Shukai Gong, Jiankai Tu, Xiaotian Tang, Jiaxin Li, Kaiqi Chen, Duomin Wang, Yuqi Wang, Bingyi Kang, Eric Huang, Zhiyang Dou, Zhen Dong, Enze Xie, Wojciech Matusik, Tat-Seng Chua, Daquan Zhou

entry.summary: HumanScale presents a systematic study showing egocentric human video can outperform teleoperated real-robot data for embodied foundation model pretraining, despite being far cheaper and more diverse. This challenges assumptions about the necessity of costly real-robot trajectories.

entry.title: Scaling Self-Play for End-to-End Driving

author.name: Luke Rowe, Roger Girgis, Rodrigue de Schaetzen, Daphne Cornelisse, Alaap Grandhi, Felix Heide, Eugene Vinitsky, Christopher Pal, Liam Paull

entry.summary: This work proposes large-scale self-play directly from pixels in simulation for end-to-end autonomous driving, introducing Gigapixel, a high-throughput batched simulator that enables sensor-based policies rather than vectorized BEV inputs. It aims to overcome compounding errors and long-tail brittleness of offline-trained driving models.

entry.title: Beyond Static Leaderboards: Predictive Validity for the Evaluation of LLM Agents

author.name: Dhaval C. Patel, Kaoutar El Maghraoui, Shuxin Lin, Yusheng Li, Tianjun Feng, Chun-Yi Tsai, Yihan Sun, Wei Alexander Xin, Akshat Bhandari, Tanisha Rathod, Aaron Fan, Sanskruti Vijay Shejwal, Tomas Pasiecznik, Sagar Chethan Kumar, Tanmay Agarwal, Rohith Kanathur, Sam Colman, Amaan Sheikh, Dev Bahl, Ann Li, Krish Veera, Alimurtaza Mustafa Merchant, Shambhawi Baswaraj Bhure, Sajal Kumar Goyla, Chengrui Li, Kirthana Natarajan, Rui Li, Thomas Ajai, Rujing Li, Vivek G. Iyer, Sanjaii Vijayakumar, Yitong Bai, Ayal Yakobe, Darief Maes, Yassine Jebbouri, Tianyang Xu, Thai Quoc On, Vera Mazeeva, Winston Li, Yuval Shemla, Yeshitha Bhuvanesh, Rushin Bhatt, Siddharth Chethan Gowda, Alisha Vinod, Caroline Cahill, Shriya Aishani Rachakonda, Yunfeng Chen, Aryaman Agrawal, Aman Upganlawar, Mao Le Jonathan Ang, Yubin Sally Go, Madhav Rajkondawar, Yang-Jung Chen, Trisha Maturi, Ananya Kapoor, Andrew Li, Shrey Arora, Mana Abbaszadeh, Shen Li, Charles Xu, Byeolah Kwon

entry.summary: Argues that aggregate-score leaderboards systematically underspecify deployed-agent evaluation by aggregating fourteen parallel studies of an MCP-based industrial agent benchmark plus seven prior benchmarks. Shows rankings from aggregate scores fail to transfer out-of-distribution.

entry.title: Process-Verified Reinforcement Learning for Theorem Proving via Lean

author.name: Minsu Kim, Se-Young Yun

entry.summary: Uses the Lean proof assistant as a symbolic process oracle to provide dense, fine-grained tactic-level verified feedback during RL for theorem proving, beyond binary outcome rewards. Parses proof attempts into tactic sequences and marks locally sound steps and the earliest failing step for credit assignment.

entry.title: MassSpecGym in the Wild: Uncovering and Correcting Evaluation Pitfalls in AI-Driven Molecule Discovery

author.name: Hongxuan Liu, Roman Bushuiev, Ivy Lightheart, Mrunali Manjrekar, Anton Bushuiev, Magdalena Lederbauer, Filip Jozefov, Yinkai Wang, Soha Hassoun, Josef Sivic, James Taylor, Runzhong Wang, David Healey, Tom\'a\v{s} Pluskal, Connor W. Coley

entry.summary: Reviews evaluation pitfalls in AI-driven molecule discovery from tandem mass spectrometry, using the MassSpecGym benchmark, finding issues in at least 17 of 26 papers including data leakage, shortcut learning, and implementation bugs. Provides corrections to restore trustworthy benchmarking.

entry.title: Current World Models Lack a Persistent State Core
