entry.summary: Proves that signed pairwise interaction scores conflate uniqueness, redundancy, and synergy using a minimal XOR causal model, and introduces Stochastic Hi-Fi, a retraining-free interventional decomposition estimating per-feature U/R/S profiles with statistical guarantees. Improves interpretability of feature interactions.

entry.title: Low-Burden Data Augmentation for Dysarthric ASR via Zero-Shot Voice Cloning

author.name: Satwinder Singh, Qianli Wang, Zihan Zhong, Clarion Mendes, Hasegawa-Johnson, Waleed Abdulla, Seyed Reza Shahamiri

entry.summary: Investigates zero-shot voice cloning (Higgs Audio V2) as a low-burden data augmentation strategy for dysarthric speech recognition, fine-tuning Whisper-medium on cloned, real, and hybrid data from the TORGO dataset. Cloned and hybrid finetuning nearly match real data and outperform it for moderate-severity speakers.

entry.title: Deep-Unfolded Coordination

author.name: Hunter Kuperman, Minchan Jung, Rahul V. Ghosh, Alex Oshin, Evangelos A. Theodorou

entry.summary: Proposes Deep Coordinator, a deep-unfolding framework that learns to dynamically adjust the hyperparameters of the ADMM-DDP distributed solver at solve-time for multi-agent robotics problems. Claims to be the first deep-unfolding framework for distributed optimization in this context.

entry.title: LaViSA: A Language and Vision Structural Ambiguity Benchmark

author.name: Lee Sangmyeong, Shun Inadumi, Koichiro Yoshino

entry.summary: Introduces LaViSA, a vision-language benchmark for evaluating whether VLMs can resolve syntactic structural ambiguity by leveraging visual scenes, comprising ambiguous and disambiguated sentence pairs with corresponding images across seven ambiguity categories. Provides a comprehensive evaluation of current VLMs on this challenge.

entry.title: AtomMem: Building Simple and Effective Memory System for LLM Agents via Atomic Facts

author.name: Yanyu Yao, Shangze Li, Zhi Zheng, Hui Zheng, Qi Liu, Tong Xu, Enhong Chen

entry.summary: Proposes AtomMem, a long-term memory system for LLM agents that extracts high-value atomic facts from long-form interactions and organizes them into hierarchical event structures for value-dense storage and stable memory evolution across multi-session interactions. Addresses coarse and unstable memory representations in existing systems.

entry.title: JAMER: Project-Level Code Framework Dataset and Benchmark on Professional Game Engines

author.name: Jianwen Sun, Chuanhao Li, Zizhen Li, Yukang Feng, Fanrui Zhang, Yifei Huang, Yu Dai, Kaipeng Zhang

entry.summary: JamSet and JamBench provide the first project-level game code dataset and benchmark on a professional engine (Godot), built from Game Jam open-source projects with deterministic headless evaluation. It addresses the unexplored area of project-level game code engineering.

entry.title: CARE: Competence-Aware Reward Shaping for Adaptive Reasoning Length in Video-MLLMs

author.name: Chengwen Liu, Hao Peng, Jisheng Dang, Hong Peng, Bin Hu, Tat-Seng Chua

entry.summary: CARE is a competence-aware reward shaping framework for video-MLLM reasoning that adapts reasoning length to the model's evolving competence using a smoothed EMA of pass rates to route training through progressive stages. It shifts from exploration-oriented long reasoning to efficient reasoning as competence grows.

entry.title: Timage: A Generative Text-in-Image Paradigm for Fine-Tuning Vision-Language Models

author.name: Yifeng Wu, Huimin Huang, Ruiluo Wu, Chunyi Lin, Guanhua Chen, Xian Wu, Wang Song, Ruize Han

entry.summary: Timage recasts multimodal understanding as input-level alignment by drawing the textual query as a typeset overlay onto the image, using a constrained Schrodinger bridge for placement. It aims to anchor language to correct visual coordinates without rewiring model weights.

entry.title: Holo-World: Unified Camera, Object and Weather Control for Video World Model

author.name: Xiangchen Yin, Wenzhang Sun, Jiahui Yuan, Zijie Liu, Yinda Chen, Wei Li, Dachun Kai, Chunfeng Wang, Xiaoyan Sun

entry.summary: Holo-World is a video world model unifying camera, object, and weather control from a single first frame, introducing HoloStateData to convert diverse videos into unified control samples. It supports preserving the source world or transferring it to a target weather state.

entry.title: HEad and neCK TumOR (HECKTOR) 2025: Benchmark of Segmentation, Diagnosis, and Prognosis in Multimodal PET/CT

author.name: Numan Saeed, Salma Hassan, Shahad Hardan, Lishan Cai, Xinglong Liang, Moona Mazher, Abdul Qayyum, Yansong Bu, Mengye Lyu, Yue Lin, Mingyuan Meng, Chuanyi Huang, Lisheng Wang, Dalal Chamseddine, Shamimeh Ahrari, Beining Wu, Yifei Chen, Fuyou Mao, Hao Zhang, Baixiang Zhao, Surajit Ray, Muzi Guo, Lei Xiang, Jakob Dexl, Michael Ingrisch, Adrien Depeursinge, Arman Rahmim, Mathieu Hatt, Vincent Andrearczyk, Mohammad Yaqub

entry.summary: HECKTOR 2025 is a comprehensive benchmark for automated head-and-neck cancer analysis combining segmentation, recurrence-free survival prognosis, and HPV-status diagnosis from multimodal PET/CT and EHR data. It establishes standardized evaluation for clinically valuable noninvasive prediction tasks.

entry.title: How Fragile Are Training-Free AI-Generated Image Detectors? A Controlled Audit of Score Direction, Preprocessing, and Compression

author.name: Jingwen Zhou, Mingzhe Wang

entry.summary: This audit demonstrates that training-free AI-generated image detectors are fragile, with implementation details like LPIPS backbone choice and preprocessing causing large AUROC swings that masquerade as method differences. It calls for controlled evaluation protocols.

entry.title: TimeProVe: Propose, then Verify for Efficient Long Video Temporal Reasoning in Activities of Daily Living

author.name: Arkaprava Sinha, Dominick Reilly, Siddharth Krishnan, Hieu Le, Srijan Das

entry.summary: TimeProVe is a cost-efficient propose-then-verify framework for long video question answering that uses lightweight modules to generate action-grounded answer-evidence hypotheses and invokes an expensive VLM only for targeted verification. It targets motion-centric evidence missed by caption-based methods.

entry.title: Stable Transformer-Actor-Critic Model Predictive Control: A Contraction Analysis Approach

author.name: Antonio Marino (CAM), Valerio Modugno (UCL), Marco Cognetti (LAAS)

entry.summary: This paper introduces a Transformer-Actor-Critic Model Predictive Control architecture with formal robustness guarantees, proving Transformers can satisfy incremental Input-to-State Stability and using Riemannian contraction theory for closed-loop analysis. Stability bounds are integrated as a training regularizer.

entry.title: Overfitted high-dimensional matrix factorizations via adaptive spectral shrinkage

author.name: Lorenzo Mauri, David B. Dunson

entry.summary: EigenBayes is a fast spectral estimation approach for overfitted high-dimensional matrix factorizations that provides valid uncertainty quantification and automatically selects latent dimension without expensive Bayesian shrinkage priors. It addresses dimension selection in low signal-to-noise factor models.

entry.title: Leveraging tails for adaptation

author.name: Sergios Agapiou, Isma\"el Castillo, Paul Egels

entry.summary: This work analyzes Bayesian posterior contraction with p-exponential tail priors, showing contraction rates improve as p decreases and full adaptation to smoothness is achieved in the p-to-0 regime. Applications include overparametrized shallow ReLU networks adapting to any regularity between 0 and 2.

entry.title: Emergent Alignment

author.name: Martin Kol\'a\v{r}

entry.summary: Proposes giving an LLM a conscience step that reviews its own reasoning plus a DPO-based alignment loss using a frozen copy of itself as judge, enabling online self-correction without a separate stronger or weaker judge. Frames this as a counter to emergent misalignment from fine-tuning.

entry.title: Learning to Prompt: Improving Student Engagement with Adaptive LLM-based High-School Tutoring

author.name: Po-Chin Chang, Nicholas Hogan, Aske Plaat, Michiel T. van der Meer

entry.summary: Develops an adaptive LLM tutoring system with subject-aware prompt routing based on 14 pedagogical features, trained in simulation then deployed for online adaptation with real high-school students. Reports the router beats static baselines and shows sim-to-real transfer in an A/B test with 656 conversations.

entry.title: QMFOL: Benchmarking Large Language Model Reasoning via Quantifiable Monadic First-Order Logic Test Case Generation

author.name: Xinyi Zheng, Ling Shi, Tianlong Yu, Yongxin Zhao, Lorenz Goette, Kailong Wang

entry.summary: Proposes QMFOL, an automated framework that generates monadic first-order logic reasoning tasks with quantifiable, controllable complexity (reasoning depth, width, label types, distractors) using conjunction and disjunction patterns. Addresses benchmarks that lack fine-grained control over logical complexity.

entry.title: How Linear Is a Transformer Feed-Forward Block? Per-Block Linear Recoverability Is Learned, Not Architectural

author.name: Stuart Whipp

entry.summary: Measures the linearity of transformer feed-forward blocks via a closed-form least-squares linear approximation (R-squared linear) across GPT-2, Pythia, and Llama models, finding linearity is highly heterogeneous, non-monotone with depth, and learned rather than architectural. Provides an optimiser-free interpretability probe.

entry.title: Bidirectional Tutoring for Developmental Motor Learning in Robots: Co-Developed Interaction Dynamics Support Stable Learning

author.name: Rui Fukushima, Jun Tani

entry.summary: Studies bidirectional tutoring for robot motor learning, showing that when tutor and learner dynamically adapt to each other, the robot's past experiences act as prior constraints that support stable, coherent learned behaviors. Reframes demonstration learning as mutual rather than unidirectional. Authored by Tani and colleague.

entry.title: Temporal Self-Imitation Learning

author.name: Yinsen Jia, Boyuan Chen

entry.summary: Introduces Temporal Self-Imitation Learning (TSIL), which mines temporally efficient successful trajectories during RL training and converts them into reusable supervision, using temporal efficiency itself as a self-supervision signal for long-horizon manipulation. Prevents forgetting rare efficient behaviors and reward-shaping exploitation.

entry.title: FFinRED: An Expert-Guided Benchmark Generation and Evaluation Framework for Financial LLM Red-Teaming

author.name: Chaeyun Kim, Daeyoung Park, Junghwan Kim, Jinyoung Jeong, Eunji Song, Yongtaek Lim, Minwoo Kim

entry.summary: Introduces FinRED, an expert-guided red-teaming framework and taxonomy for evaluating financial LLM safety, mapping global standards like FATF and EU DORA to threats such as fraud facilitation and regulatory evasion. Fills a gap left by general-purpose safety benchmarks.

entry.title: StreamKL: Fast and Memory-Efficient KL Divergence for Boosting Attention Distillation

author.name: Guangda Liu, Yiquan Wang, Chengwei Li, Wenhao Chen, Jing Lin, Yiwu Yao, Danning Ke, Wenchao Ding, Jieru Zhao

entry.summary: Presents StreamKL, a fused GPU kernel that computes attention KL divergence in one pass without materializing both full attention matrices, eliminating quadratic memory for attention distillation. Enables scalable distillation and sparse-attention training at long context.

entry.title: AutoPass: Evidence-Guided LLM Agents for Compiler Performance Tuning

author.name: Zepeng Li, Jie Ren, Zhanyong Tang, Jie Zheng, Zheng Wang

entry.summary: Presents AutoPass, a multi-agent LLM framework for compiler performance tuning that opens the compiler to the model, querying internal optimization states and analyzing intermediate representation to orchestrate options using runtime feedback. Moves beyond black-box auto-tuning.

entry.title: UltraQuant: 4-bit KV Caching for Context-Heavy Agents

author.name: Inesh Chakrabarti (Advanced Micro Devices, University of California, Los Angeles), David Limpus (Advanced Micro Devices, Purdue University), Aditi Ghai Rana (Advanced Micro Devices), Bowen Bao (Advanced Micro Devices), Spandan Tiwari (Advanced Micro Devices), Thiago Crepaldi (Advanced Micro Devices), Ashish Sirasao (Advanced Micro Devices)

entry.summary: Studies 4-bit KV-cache compression for context-heavy multi-round agents, using rotation and codebook quantization with practical design choices like asymmetric K/V treatment and Walsh-Hadamard rotation, measuring quality, cache residency, and throughput jointly. Authored by an AMD-led team targeting serving efficiency.

entry.title: Efficient Neural Network Model Selection for Few-Class Application Datasets

author.name: Bryan Bo Cao, Abhinav Sharma, Lawrence O'Gorman, Michael Coss, Shubham Jain

entry.summary: Develops a data-side classification-difficulty measure for few-class datasets (fewer than ten classes) to guide efficient model selection, a setting common in practice but rarely studied. The metric enables comparing models and datasets 6 to 29 times faster than repeated training.

entry.title: Matching Markets meet Cumulative Prospect Theory: Towards Optimal and Adversarially Robust Learning

author.name: Ananya Kunisetty, Avishek Ghosh

entry.summary: Studies multi-agent multi-armed bandits in two-sided matching markets under cumulative prospect theory, which weighs rewards nonlinearly to capture human preferences. Derives player-optimal regret bounds and addresses adversarial robustness in this human-centric setting.

entry.title: Data Bias Mitigation under Coverage Constraints & The Price of Fairness

author.name: Bruno Scarone, Alfredo Viola, Ren\'ee J. Miller

entry.summary: Extends a bias-mitigation framework to incorporate coverage constraints enforcing sufficient representation across groups including intersectional subgroups, addressing both bias measurement and underrepresentation. Analyzes the price of fairness, trading small approximation errors for greater data efficiency rather than requiring exactly zero bias.

entry.title: Full-Self Diagnostics (FSD): Physics-Grounded Visual Biomarker Inference from Smartphone Video via Inverse Problems and Operator Learning

author.name: Jonathan Thomas, Harsh Thaker

entry.summary: Presents Full-Self Diagnostics, a physics-grounded framework using inverse problems and operator learning to recover physiological biomarkers from short smartphone facial videos, integrating a radiative-transfer forward model with identifiability guarantees. Targets accessible health diagnostics from consumer hardware.

entry.title: Closing the Calibration Gap in Semantic Caching

author.name: Aditeya Baral, Radoslav Ralev, Iliya Sotirov Zhechev, Srijith Rajamohan, Jen Agarwal

entry.summary: Argues that PR-AUC is a misleading metric for semantic caching of LLM responses because it ignores usability at fixed thresholds, and introduces P-CHR AUC and Calibration Retention Rate as cache-aware, deployment-relevant metrics. Decomposes the offline-to-deployed quality gap into recoverable calibration components.

entry.title: Semantic-Anchored Evidential Fusion for Domain-Robust Whole-Slide Survival Analysis

author.name: Yucheng Xing, Ling Huang, Pei Liu, Jingying Ma, Jiaqing Xu, Kai He, Mengling Feng

entry.summary: Proposes SAEFS, a semantic-anchored evidential fusion framework for domain-robust whole-slide-image survival analysis that derives high-level pathology semantic anchors rather than relying on domain-sensitive pixel features. Aims to generalize across clinical centers with varying staining and scanner hardware.

entry.title: CacheWeaver: Cache-Aware Evidence Ordering for Efficient Grounded RAG Inference

author.name: Kaizhen Tan, Rong Gu, Mingyuan Li

entry.summary: Presents CacheWeaver, a lightweight prompt-layer method that reorders retrieved evidence to maximize reusable prefix overlap for prefix caching in RAG serving engines like vLLM, using a prefix tree and greedy walk. Lowers median prefill cost without changing the serving engine or retrieved evidence set.

entry.title: Source-Grounded Data Generation for Text-to-JSON Learning

author.name: Sunghee Ahn, Guijin Son, Youngjae Yu

entry.summary: Proposes STAGE, a spreadsheet-grounded data generation pipeline for text-to-JSON learning that uses LLMs to synthesize reports and JSON schemas while validating ground-truth values against underlying spreadsheets. Addresses the challenge of building reliable, scalable structured-extraction training data.

entry.title: Gender Bias in LLM Hiring Decisions: Evidence from a Japanese Context and Evaluation of Mitigation Strategies

author.name: Serena A. Hoffstedde, Machiko Hirota, Akshara Nadayanur Sathis Kanna, Rihito Kotani, Ujwal Kumar, Gabriele Trovato, Phan Xuan Tan

entry.summary: This study examines gender bias in LLM hiring decisions in a Japanese context using counterfactual rirekisho resumes and over 43,000 API calls across five models, evaluating prompt-instruction and privacy-filter mitigations. It finds pro-female bias extends beyond Western contexts.

entry.title: Learning When to Denoise: Optimizing Asynchronous Schedules for Latent Diffusion

author.name: Bingshuo Qian, Xiang Cheng

entry.summary: This paper proposes learning the asynchronous denoising schedule for multi-representation diffusion models via a schedule-corrected objective and a convex-monotone parametric class, using a cheap joint probe. It reports improved ImageNet 256x256 generation with under 1% extra training compute.

entry.title: SurgVista: Long-Horizon Surgical World Modeling with Plausible Instrument-Tissue Dynamics

author.name: Wentao Pan, Wuyang Li, Shengyuan Liu, Xinyu Liu, Hengyu Liu, Yixuan Yuan

entry.summary: SurgVista is a long-horizon surgical world model that mitigates spatial interaction incoherence and temporal fidelity collapse via deformation consistency regularization and other training recipes. It generates action-conditioned future surgical frames to support safe policy learning.

entry.title: SpatialSV: Internalizing Interpretable 3D Spatial Awareness in MLLMs via Task-Oriented Visual Supervision

author.name: Jiayu Tang, Yuchen Zhou, Chao Gou

entry.summary: SpatialSV internalizes interpretable 3D spatial awareness in MLLMs via task-oriented visual supervision, compelling the model to actively lift 2D features into explicit 3D representations rather than using external tools or opaque distillation. It offers inherent interpretability with geometric constraints.

entry.title: Distill Once, Adapt Life-Long: Exploring Dataset Distillation for Continual Test-Time Adaptation

author.name: Hyun-Kurl Jang, Jihun Kim, Hyeokjun Kweon, Kuk-Jin Yoon

entry.summary: DO-ALL is a plug-and-play framework for continual test-time adaptation that uses dataset distillation to produce compact privacy-conscious synthetic anchors summarizing the source distribution before deployment. It mitigates instability and catastrophic forgetting in source-free long-term adaptation.

entry.title: Cinematic Compositing Using Character-Environment-Harmonized Video Generation Models

author.name: Tianyi Xiang, Mingming He, Li Ma, Jing Liao

entry.summary: This work presents an end-to-end video diffusion framework for cinematic compositing that jointly models character-to-environment physical interactions and environment-to-character lighting harmonization using a tri-mask-guided architecture with RGB-D joint denoising. It integrates green-screen characters into novel environments with physical and photometric realism.

entry.title: Fast Human Attention Prediction for Fixation-guided Active Perception in Autonomous Navigation

author.name: Fatma Youssef Mohammed, Grzegorz Malczyk, Kostas Alexis

entry.summary: GazeLNN is a lightweight scanpath prediction model using Liquid Neural Networks and MobileNetV3 to predict human visual attention fixations for active perception in robot navigation. It achieves state-of-the-art results at only 0.61 GFLOPs.

entry.title: Motor Angular Speed Preintegration for Multirotor UAV State Estimation

author.name: Mat\v{e}j Petrl\'ik, Filip Nov\'ak, Robert P\v{e}ni\v{c}ka, Martin Saska

entry.summary: This work proposes preintegration of accelerations from motor angular speeds for multirotor UAV state estimation, avoiding IMU degradation from propeller vibrations. It shows motor-speed-derived accelerations can support state propagation independently with better precision than IMU.

entry.title: LIT-GS: LiDAR-Inertial-Thermal Gaussian Splatting for Illumination-Robust Mapping

author.name: Shikuan Shi, Chunran Zheng, Jiaming Xu, Tianyong Ye, Tao Yu, Yukang Cui

entry.summary: LIT-GS is a LiDAR-inertial-thermal Gaussian Splatting framework that injects LiDAR-derived plane geometry as an explicit constraint to achieve illumination-robust mapping in texture-deficient scenes where RGB-based pipelines fail. It uses cross-modal anchors for thermal-LiDAR association.

entry.title: TaCauchy: An Extensible FEM Framework for Vision-Based Tactile Simulation

author.name: Hengfei Zhao, Yifan Xie, Junhao Gong, Yue Sun, Kai Zhu, Weihua He, Shoujie Li, Haohuan Fu, Wenbo Ding

entry.summary: TaCauchy is an extensible Finite Element Method framework integrating physics-based force computation into Isaac Sim for high-fidelity vision-based tactile sensor simulation. It directly computes Cauchy stress tensors from hyperelastic laws to provide mechanical ground truth for reinforcement learning.

entry.title: Analyzing the Narration Gap in LLM-Solver Loops

author.name: Zunchen Huang, Songgaojun Deng

entry.summary: Examines the overlooked narration step in LLM-solver pipelines (SAT/SMT), where a formally sound solver output is translated into a user answer and soundness can be lost. Models the LLM-solver loop and analyzes failures in this narration gap.

entry.title: BrainG3N: A Dual-Purpose Tokenizer for Controllable 3D Brain MRI Generation

author.name: Max Van Puyvelde, Ibrahim Gulluk, Wim Van Criekinge, Olivier Gevaert

entry.summary: Introduces BrainG3N, a volumetric masked-autoencoder tokenizer for 3D brain MRI latent diffusion that decouples encoder and decoder so embeddings retain clinical information while reconstructions stay anatomically faithful. Targets controllable generative modeling for augmentation and privacy-preserving data sharing.

entry.title: Human-on-the-Loop Orchestration for AI-Assisted Legal Discovery

author.name: Anushree Sinha, Srivaths Ranganathan, Abhishek Dharmaratnakar, Debanshu Das

entry.summary: Studies autonomous LLM agents in legal e-discovery, defining a failure mode called trajectory collapse where an early misclassification silently propagates and invalidates privilege review. Contributes a taxonomy of agentic legal-IR failures and a four-layer verification architecture with human-on-the-loop orchestration.

entry.title: Autonomous Event-Driven Multi-Agent Orchestration for Enterprise AI at Scale

author.name: Harsh Rao Dhanyamraju, Leonidas Raghav, Aaron Lee

entry.summary: Evaluates DAG Plan-and-Execute and ReAct multi-agent orchestration across 208 production-derived enterprise scenarios at three scales and introduces a Task Manager for continuous event-driven operation via priority inference, event merging, and preemption. Finds scale rather than task complexity dominates orchestration performance, with agent-discovery noise as the bottleneck at enterprise scale.

entry.title: Residual-Space Evolutionary Optimization via Flow-based Generative Models

author.name: Zhuo Cao, Lena Krieger, Fernanda Nader, Xuan Zhao, Hanno Scharr, Ira Assent

entry.summary: Proposes residual-space evolutionary optimization, a model-agnostic framework combining flow-based generative editing with evolutionary algorithms for settings with non-differentiable or black-box objectives. Exploits conditional flow matching to disentangle condition-controlled factors from instance-specific residuals and searches in residual space.

entry.title: Navigating Unreliable Parametric and Contextual Knowledge: Explicit Knowledge Conflict Resolution for LLM Inference

author.name: Huang Peng, Jiuyang Tang, Weixin Zeng, Hao Xu, Xiang Zhao

entry.summary: Addresses knowledge conflicts in LLM inference both between parametric and contextual knowledge and among multiple external contexts, where both sources may contain errors. Proposes explicit conflict resolution rather than privileging one source over the other.

entry.title: FlowEdit: Associative Memory for Lifelong Pronunciation Adaptation in Flow-Matching TTS

author.name: Harshit Singh, Ayush Pratap Singh, Nityanand Mathur

entry.summary: Presents FlowEdit, a lifelong adaptation framework for frozen flow-matching TTS that learns pronunciation corrections as latent conditioning edits rather than weight updates, storing them in a Modern Hopfield Network as content-addressable episodic memory. Enables fuzzy morphological retrieval to fix out-of-vocabulary proper-noun errors at inference.

entry.title: How Do Instructions Shape Speech? Cross-Attention Attribution for Style-Captioned Text-to-Speech

author.name: Nityanand Mathur, Hamees Sayed, Wasim Madha, Apoorv Singh, Sameer Khurana, Akshat Mandloi, Sudarshan Kamath

entry.summary: Automates generation of SKILL.md skill libraries for computer-using agents by mining GUI interaction trajectories through segmentation, clustering into candidate skills, and training a skill-aware policy. Finds mined clusters are readable (high purity) but readability does not translate into downstream transfer, with GRPO yielding minimal accuracy gains.

entry.title: PerceptionDLM: Parallel Region Perception with Multimodal Diffusion Language Models

author.name: Yueyi Sun, Yuhao Wang, Jason Li, Ye Tian, Tao Zhang, Jacky Mai, Yihan Wang, Haochen Wang, Jinbin Bai, Ling Yang, Yunhai Tong

entry.summary: Proposes PerceptionDLM, a multimodal diffusion language model optimized for efficient parallel region perception, using structured attention masking to caption multiple image regions simultaneously rather than autoregressively. Leverages the parallel decoding nature of diffusion LLMs.

entry.title: Formal Verification of Learned Multi-Agent Communication Policies via Decision Tree Distillation

author.name: Ahmad Farooq, Kamran Iqbal

entry.summary: Presents an end-to-end framework for formally verifying learned multi-agent communication policies by distilling neural policies into interpretable decision trees, verifying them, and confirming properties transfer back to the networks. Targets safety guarantees for drone swarms and autonomous vehicle fleets.

entry.title: Beyond Uniform Forgetting: A Study of Sequential Direct Preference Optimization Across Preference Settings

author.name: Pranav Bhandari, Nicolas Fay, Amitava Datta, Usman Naseem, Mehwish Nasim

entry.summary: Studies sequential Direct Preference Optimization across four preference settings (distributional conflict, multi-attribute interaction, strong safety signal, compatible objectives), finding forgetting is non-uniform and depends on the relationship between objectives. Uses Llama-3.1-8B with LoRA adapters.

entry.title: Large Language Models Do Not Always Need Readable Language

author.name: Jiayi Zhu, Haoxuan Peng, Junxi Wang, Liang Ke, Chen Zhang, Linfeng Zhang

entry.summary: Investigates whether LLMs can encode and recover semantic information in compact, non-human-readable text representations (BabelTele) intended for model-to-model communication. Probes the limits of readability versus recoverability in LLM-targeted prompts.

entry.title: Confidence Calibration for Multimodal LLMs: An Empirical Study through Medical VQA

author.name: Yuetian Du, Yucheng Wang, Ming Kong, Tian Liang, Qiang Long, Bingdi Chen, Qiang Zhu

entry.summary: Provides the first comprehensive study of confidence calibration in multimodal LLMs for medical visual question answering, proposing a multi-strategy interrogation method with auxiliary expert LLM assessment that cuts calibration error by ~40%. Targets the safety-critical mismatch between model confidence and accuracy.

entry.title: Variable-Length Tokenization via Learnable Global Merging for Diffusion Transformers

author.name: Dong Hoon Lee, Seunghoon Hong

entry.summary: Proposes a variable-length tokenizer for diffusion transformers that modulates token count via learnable global merging rather than sequence truncation, preserving representational alignment across lengths. Enables a single diffusion model to flexibly trade quality for compute.

entry.title: Frequency-Aware Flow Matching for Continuous and Consistent Robotic Action Generation

author.name: Jianing Guo, Fangzheng Chen, Zihao Mao, Wong Lik Hang Kenny, Zhenhong Wu, Yu Li, Yishuai Cai, Yuanpei Chen, Yikun Ban, Kai Chen, Qi Dou, Yaodong Yang, Xianglong Liu, Huijie Zhao, Simin Li

entry.summary: Proposes Frequency-Aware Flow Matching for robotic action generation, transforming discrete action sequences into the frequency domain via DCT to produce continuous, temporally consistent actions robust to heterogeneous control frequencies. Addresses brittleness of discretized action chunks in flow/diffusion policies.

entry.title: SPOT-E: Test-Time Entropy Shaping with Visual Spotlights for Frozen VLMs

author.name: Bo Yin, Xiaobin Hu, Chengming Xu, Ruolin Shen, Mo Yang, Jiangning Zhang, Peng-Tao Jiang, Cheng Tan, Shuicheng YAN

entry.summary: Presents ScholarQuest, a large-scale taxonomy-guided benchmark for agentic academic paper search built from over 1,000 CS topics and four research intent types, with a shared retrieval backend for reproducible evaluation. Targets the lack of realistic benchmarks for LLM-based literature search agents.

entry.title: CRAX: Fast Safe Reinforcement Learning Benchmarking

author.name: Tristan Tomilin, Mourad Boustani, Mickey Beurskens, Thiago D. Sim\~ao

entry.summary: Introduces CRAX, a JAX/MuJoCo-XLA-based safe reinforcement learning benchmark with realistic 3D physics achieving up to ~100x speedups over CPU-based safety benchmarks, with six environment suites and graded difficulty. Enables large-scale, rapid safe-RL experimentation.

entry.title: Does Text Actually Help? Uncovering and Resolving Text Collapse in Multimodal Time Series Forecasting

author.name: Huu Hiep Nguyen, Minh Hoang Nguyen, Dung Nguyen, Hung Le

entry.summary: Identifies a text-collapse failure mode in multimodal time-series forecasting where the text branch converges to a content-independent transformation contributing negligible signal. Attributes it to asymmetry between strongly autocorrelated numerical inputs and underused text, and proposes a fix.

entry.title: Convex training of Lipschitz-regularized shallow neural networks

author.name: Chao Yin, Antoine Lesage-Landry

entry.summary: Introduces a convex restriction to the non-convex Lipschitz-regularized training of shallow networks that can be solved to global optimality, promoting adversarial robustness. It works as a post-processing step guaranteed to be no worse than the pretrained initialization.

entry.title: On the Oracle Complexity of Interpolation-Based Gradient Descent

author.name: Dongmin Lee, William Lu, Anuran Makur

entry.summary: Proposes piecewise polynomial interpolation-based gradient descent, which approximates full gradients by querying the oracle at equidistant data-domain points to build interpolants over data patches. Analyzes oracle complexity for strongly convex and non-convex losses leveraging smoothness in the data rather than parameters.

entry.title: Kolmogorov-Arnold Reservoir Computing

author.name: Juntian Huang, Jurgen Kurths, Ying Tang

entry.summary: Kolmogorov-Arnold Reservoir Computing replaces trainable or recurrence-free reservoirs with explicit basis-function expansions inspired by the Kolmogorov-Arnold representation theorem for forecasting dynamical systems. It is shown to be a lightweight design of KANs preserving expressivity while avoiding rapid feature-dimension growth.

entry.title: Constrained hybrid modelling to predict microbial dynamics and organic matter turnover in soil systems

author.name: Paul Collart, Juergen Gall, Andrea Schnepf, Holger Pagel, Lars Doorenbos

entry.summary: Presents the first hybrid modeling framework deriving biokinetic parameter values of a process-based soil organic matter turnover model from metagenome-inferred functional traits. It constrains microbial dynamics predictions for soil carbon cycling using genomic data, addressing an unsolved genome-to-process mapping problem.

entry.title: Variational Consensus Monte Carlo for Bayesian Mixture

author.name: Julie Fendler, Francesca L. Crowe, Tom Marshall, Sylvia Richardson, Paul D. W. Kirk

entry.summary: Develops Variational Consensus Monte Carlo for Bayesian mixture models in a federated setting where data cannot be pooled, extending prior work to handle unknown cluster numbers and mixture parameters. Motivated by privacy constraints in health data.

entry.title: Prompt, Plan, Extract: Zero-Shot Agentic LLMs Workflows for Lung Pathology Extraction from Clinical Narratives

author.name: Aman Pathak, Cheng Peng, Mengxian Lyu, Ziyi Chen, Reema Solan, Sankalp Talankar, Yasir Khan, Hiren Mehta, Aokun Chen, Yi Guo, Yonghui Wu

entry.summary: Develops a zero-shot agentic LLM workflow to extract 13 College of American Pathologists synoptic fields from lung resection pathology reports, evaluating five open-source LLMs against a supervised NLP baseline. Demonstrates clinical information extraction without expensive manual annotation.

entry.title: Stochastic Linear Contextual Bandits with Bounded Noise: A Set-Membership Approach

author.name: Haonan Xu, Yingying Li

entry.summary: Studies stochastic linear contextual bandits with bounded reward noise, proposing SME-OFU that leverages set-membership estimation with optimism in the face of uncertainty to exploit the extra information in bounded (rather than sub-Gaussian) noise. Provides regret guarantees under this more informative assumption.

entry.title: Beyond Global Replanning: Hierarchical Recovery for Cross-Device Agent Systems

author.name: Shu Yao, Yuhua Luo, Qian Long, Jingru Fan, Zhuoyuan Yu, Yuheng Wang, Lin Wu, Yufan Dang, Huatao Li, Chen Qian

entry.summary: H-RePlan is a hierarchical replanning framework for cross-device agent systems that distinguishes device-local repairable failures from those needing cross-device replanning. It models the device-local strategy space across unified API/CLI/GUI execution.

entry.title: Occ-VLM: Occupancy Grounded Vision Language Model for Indoor Scene Understanding

author.name: Jianing Li, Zhou Fang, Yijiang Liu, Li Du

entry.summary: Occ-VLM is a vision-language framework for 3D indoor scene understanding that operates purely on posed RGB images, using occupancy grounding to unify 3D geometry with vision-language semantics rather than decoupling them via separate 3D encoders. It targets embodied intelligence applications.

entry.title: 3D-PLOT-LLM: Part-Level Object Tokens for 3D Large Language Models

author.name: Jintang Xue, Xinyu Wang, Yixing Wu, Jingwen Chen, C. -C. Jay Kuo

entry.summary: 3D-PLOT-LLM makes object parts directly addressable in 3D multimodal LLMs by reorganizing the token stream with per-region markers and reserved vocabulary tokens, avoiding heavy segmentation decoders. It enables part-level naming and reasoning at low parameter cost.

entry.title: FrozenDrive: Zero-Shot Text-Guided Driving Scene Generation and Data Augmentation with Parameter-Free Frozen Diffusion Model

author.name: Yuhwan Jeong, Hyeonseong Kim, Daehyun We, Seonkyu Song, Jinnyeong Yang, Hyun-Kurl Jang, Youngho Yoon, Kuk-Jin Yoon

entry.summary: FrozenDrive is a controllable generative framework for driving scene synthesis and data augmentation that keeps a pretrained diffusion model frozen (parameter-free) while achieving multi-view and temporal consistency through knowledge-preserving spatiotemporal conditioning. It improves robustness to adverse weather and rare classes.

entry.title: Pixel-Level Residual Diffusion Transformer: Scalable 3D CT Volume Generation

author.name: Zhenkai Zhang, Markus Hiller, Krista A. Ehinger, Tom Drummond

entry.summary: PRDiT is a pixel-level residual diffusion transformer for scalable 3D CT volume generation, using a two-stage architecture with an MLP-based local denoiser for low-frequency structures and a memory-efficient global residual transformer for high-frequency details. It synthesizes high-resolution volumes directly at voxel level.

entry.title: SA-VIS: Sparse frame Annotations for training Video Instance Segmentation

author.name: Edoardo Mello Rella, Ajad Chhatkuli, Shipra Jain, Ender Konukoglu, Luc Van Gool

entry.summary: SA-VIS proposes a Past-frames Feature Propagation module enabling video instance segmentation training with sparse rather than dense frame annotations, arguing effective instance modeling does not require densely annotated frames. It reduces both annotation and compute costs.

entry.title: CUPID: Reconstructing UV Texture Maps for Interpretable Person-of-Interest Deepfake Detection

author.name: Giovanni Affatato, Sara Mandelli, Edoardo Daniele Cannas, Paolo Bestagini, Stefano Tubaro

entry.summary: CUPID is an interpretable person-of-interest deepfake detector that reconstructs UV texture maps from 3D face reconstructions and combines them with a masked autoencoder, requiring no deepfake videos or the specific target person in training. It aims to combine robustness, efficiency, and interpretability.

entry.title: VisDom: Sparse Novel View Synthesis with Visible Domain Constraint

author.name: Mariia Gladkova*, Tarun Yenamandra*, Edmond Boyer, Robert Maier, Tony Tung, Daniel Cremers

entry.summary: VisDom introduces a learning-free geometric constraint for sparse novel view synthesis that augments visual hull carving with a minimum multi-view visibility requirement, reducing floating artifacts. It improves geometric consistency where silhouette consistency alone fails.

entry.title: CalTennis: Large Multi-View Tennis Video Dataset and Benchmark of Monocular-to-3D Pose Estimation

author.name: Ilona Demler, Xinran Xie, Blake Werner, Anna Szczuka, Pietro Perona

entry.summary: CalTennis is a large-scale multi-view tennis video benchmark (11M frames, 40 players) for evaluating monocular-to-3D pose estimation in the wild, ten times larger than existing in-the-wild datasets. The multi-view setup enables inexpensive label-free evaluation of expert athletic motion.

entry.title: Proprioceptive Invariant State Estimation for Humanoid Robots on Non-Inertial Ground

author.name: Falak Mandali, Zijian He, Yan Gu

entry.summary: This paper presents an invariant extended Kalman filter for real-time state estimation of humanoid robots on non-inertial (moving) ground using only onboard proprioceptive sensing. It exploits stance-foot kinematic constraints via foot-mounted IMUs without external sensors.

entry.title: Safe, Real-Time Active Model Discrimination and Fault Diagnosis for Nonlinear Systems via Differentiable Reachability

author.name: Xinpei Ni, Melkior Ornik, Glen Chou, Samuel Coogan

entry.summary: This work presents a safe real-time algorithm for active fault diagnosis and model discrimination in uncertain nonlinear systems using differentiable reachability and interval over-approximations. It robustly enforces safety constraints while driving the system to produce diagnostically distinguishing measurements.

entry.title: Belt-Finger: An Affordable Soft Belt-Driven Gripper for Dexterous In-Hand Manipulation

author.name: Boya Zhang, Andreas Zell, Georg Martius

entry.summary: Belt-Finger is an affordable soft belt-driven gripper module that upgrades parallel-jaw grippers with three additional in-hand degrees of freedom (translation, pitch, roll) while preserving standard opening/closing. It is engineered for inexpensive manufacturing and easy integration.

entry.title: Autonomous Driving with Priority-Ordered STL Specifications Under Multimodal Uncertainty

author.name: Taha Bouzid, Shuhao Qi, Mircea Lazar, Sofie Haesaert

entry.summary: This paper proposes an uncertainty-aware trajectory planning framework for autonomous driving that incorporates a lexicographic priority ordering over Signal Temporal Logic specifications remaining valid under multimodal uncertainty. It handles safety-critical scenarios where requirements cannot all be satisfied simultaneously.

entry.title: Calibration without labels in multiple testing

author.name: Adway S. Wadekar, Jake A. Soloff

entry.summary: This work shows how empirical Bayes probability claims in large-scale multiple testing can be interpreted as approximately calibrated forecasts of the null hypothesis, addressing the challenge that ground truth labels are never revealed. It constructs pseudo-labels from spacings of ordered statistics to assess calibration indirectly.

entry.title: Your Model Organisms Might Be Fried

author.name: Daniel Tan

entry.summary: From the model-motivations team at Arcadia Alignment, this post argues that deliberately inducing pathologies (reward hacking, secret loyalties, sandbagging) to create model organisms can inadvertently damage models, making them incoherent and unrepresentative of real deployment systems. It calls for more natural model organisms to keep alignment auditing and interpretability testbeds valid.

entry.title: DeXposure-Claw: An Agentic System for DeFi Risk Supervision

author.name: Aijie Shu, Bowei Chen, Wenbin Wu, Cathy Yi-Hsuan Chen, Fengxiang He

entry.summary: Introduces DeXposure-Claw, an agentic supervision system for DeFi credit risk that routes LLM decisions through a graph time-series forecasting model, deterministic monitors, and confidence gates to reduce false alarms. Targets regulator-aligned risk supervision where general LLM agents over-react to weak evidence.

entry.title: AgentFinVQA: A Deployable Multi-Agent Pipeline for Auditable Financial Chart QA

author.name: Aravind Narayanan, Shaina Raza

entry.summary: Presents AgentFinVQA, a multi-agent pipeline for auditable financial chart question answering that decomposes queries into planning, OCR, legend grounding, visual inspection, and verification with a traceable evaluation packet. Improves 7.68 points over a matched backbone on FinMME while supporting on-premise deployment.

entry.title: Advancing DialNav through Automatic Embodied Dialog Augmentation

author.name: Leekyeung Han, Sangwon Jung, Hyunji Min, Jinseong Jeong, Minyoung Kim, Paul Hongsuck Seo

entry.summary: Tackles training-data scarcity in dialog-based embodied navigation (DialNav) by introducing an automatic generation pipeline that converts existing VLN datasets into multi-turn dialog, producing RAINbow with 238K episodes versus prior 2K. Adds complementary methods to leverage the augmented data.

entry.title: ScaffoldAgent: Utility-Guided Dynamic Outline Optimization for Open-Ended Deep Research

author.name: Zhibang Yang, Xinke Jiang, Yuzhen Xiao, Ruizhe Zhang, Yue Fang, XinFei Wan, Zhengxing Song, Yuxuan Liu, Yuheng Huang, Xu Chu, Junfeng Zhao, Yasha Wang

entry.summary: Presents ScaffoldAgent, a utility-guided framework that dynamically optimizes report outlines for open-ended deep research via expansion, contraction, and revision operations modeled as a structured decision process. Addresses scaffold drift and delayed feedback in fixed or locally refined outlines.

entry.title: Exposing the Unsaid: Visualizing Hidden LLM Bias through Stochastic Path Aggregation

author.name: Matteo Pelossi, Rita Sevastjanova, Thilo Spinner, Mennatallah El-Assady

entry.summary: Introduces TreeTracer, a visual analytics tool that aggregates hundreds of stochastic LLM generations into syntax-aligned hierarchical structures to expose biases hidden in low-probability generation branches. It matters because standard single-output audits miss distributional biases that only surface across many samples.

entry.title: CTS-MoE: Implicit Terrain Adaptation via Mixture-of-Experts for Perceptive Locomotion

author.name: Francisco Affonso, Matheus P. Angarola, Ana Luiza Mineiro, Aditya Potnis, Marcelo Becker, Girish Chowdhary

entry.summary: Proposes CTS-MoE, a dense mixture-of-experts actor with perception-based gating for perceptive legged locomotion over discontinuous terrain, balancing skill sharing and task separation in multi-task RL. Avoids the tradeoffs of monolithic policies and hierarchical sub-policies.

entry.title: Token Factory: Efficiently Integrating Diverse Signals into Large Recommendation Models

author.name: Xilun Chen, Shao-Chuan Wang, Baykal Cakici, Lukasz Heldt, Lichan Hong, Raghu Keshavan, Aniruddh Nath, Li Wei, Xinyang Xi

entry.summary: Introduces Token Factory, a framework that transforms traditional recommendation signals into compressed soft tokens directly processable by transformer-based Large Recommendation Models, avoiding long prompts and high memory costs. Google authorship targeting industry-scale recommendation.

entry.title: QueryGaussian: Scalable and Training-Free Open-Vocabulary 3D Instance Retrieval

author.name: Xiuyuan Zhu, Ke Lu, Zijie Yang, Chao Yue, Jian Xue, Dongming Zhang

entry.summary: Proposes QueryGaussian, a training-free framework for scalable open-vocabulary 3D instance retrieval that avoids the memory bottleneck of distilling high-dimensional semantics into every primitive, enabling city-scale retrieval without out-of-memory failures. Uses an instance-level rather than scene-level embedding paradigm.

entry.title: Towards Engineering Scaling Laws with Pretraining Data Composition

author.name: Jan-Lucas Uslu, Kevin Greif, Daniel Whiteson, Benjamin Nachman

entry.summary: Shows that pretraining data composition can be engineered to influence neural scaling laws in particle physics, exploiting cheap high-fidelity simulators to favor data-over-parameters regimes for classifying hadronic jets. Demonstrates scaling-law manipulation enabled by synthetic data abundance.

entry.title: ROSE: Benchmarking the Perception-to-Action Gap in Multimodal Models

author.name: Yihao Wang, Zijian He, Jie Ren, Keze Wang

entry.summary: Introduces ROSE, a controlled benchmark that holds the visual scene fixed while varying task context to measure whether multimodal models reliably convert the same visual evidence into context-appropriate actions. Probes the perception-to-action gap via coupled counting and coordinate tasks.

entry.title: Finetuning Vision-Language-Action Models Requires Fewer Layers Than You Think

author.name: Gia-Binh Nguyen, Trong-Bao Ho, Thien-Loc Ha, Khoa Vo, Philip Lund M{\o}ller, Quang T. Nguyen, Long Dinh, Tuan Dam, Vu Duong, Tung M. Luu, Trung Le, Tran Nguyen Le, Minh Vu, An Thai Le, Ngan Le, Daniel Sonntag, James Zou, Jan Peters, Duy M. H. Nguyen, Ngo Anh Vien

entry.summary: Introduces SPOT-E, a test-time entropy-shaping method with visual spotlights and low-entropy anchors for frozen VLMs, using answer-span prediction entropy as internal feedback to verify that highlighted evidence is actually used. Improves grounding on evidence-intensive tasks without retraining.

entry.title: Robust $Q$-learning for mean-field control under Wasserstein uncertainty in common noise

author.name: Mathieu Lauri\`ere, Ariel Neufeld, Kyunghyun Park

entry.summary: Presents a robust Q-learning algorithm for discrete-time mean-field control under Wasserstein uncertainty in common noise, combining quantization-projection with dual reformulation, and establishes convergence with finite-time bounds. Demonstrates on systemic risk and epidemic models.

entry.title: SARLO-80: Worldwide Slant SAR Language Optic Dataset 80cm

author.name: Sol\`ene Debuys\`ere, Nicolas Trouv\'e, Nathan Letheule, Elise Colin, Georgia Channing

entry.summary: Presents SARLO-80, a worldwide very-high-resolution SAR-optical-text dataset preserving complex-valued SLC measurements and native acquisition geometry built from open Umbra spotlight acquisitions. Fills a gap in physically grounded multimodal SAR resources for foundation model training.

entry.title: When to Trust, How to Distill: Multi-Foundation Model Guidance for Lightweight, Robust Scientific Time Series Forecasting

author.name: Rupasree Dey, Abdul Matin, Nathan Orwick, Yao Zhang, Shrideep Pallickara, Sangmi Lee Pallickara

entry.summary: Proposes Guard, a gated uncertainty-aware multi-teacher distillation framework that extracts latent structural knowledge from misaligned time-series foundation models to train lightweight specialized forecasters via instance-wise routing. Targets distributional misalignment and compute cost when deploying TSFMs in scientific edge settings.

entry.title: A Hybrid GNN-FEM Framework for Phase-Field Fracture Simulation. Physics-Preserving Hybridization for Generalizable Surrogate Modeling

author.name: Hyeonbin Moon, Yongjin Choi, Seunghwa Ryu

entry.summary: Proposes a hybrid graph-neural-network and finite-element-method framework to accelerate phase-field fracture simulations while preserving physical consistency. The GNN surrogate handles the costly nonlinear, history-dependent solves, aiming for generalizable crack-evolution prediction.

entry.title: Understanding Key Features of Time Series Foundation Models from Epidemic Forecasting

author.name: Alireza Jafari, Judy Fox, Geoffrey C. Fox, Madhav Marathe, Aniruddha Adiga

entry.summary: Systematically evaluates modern forecasting architectures, including time-series foundation models, on regional US influenza surveillance data under temporal and spatial generalization for 1-4-week-ahead prediction. Characterizes which features of foundation models matter for epidemic forecasting.

entry.title: Federated Bilevel Performative Prediction

author.name: Liangxin Qian, Chang Liu, Xuanyu Cao, Jun Zhao, Kwok-Yan Lam

entry.summary: Studies federated bilevel optimization under performativity, where deployed decisions reshape client data distributions, formalizing a federated bilevel performatively stable point under a decoupled-risk view. Provides algorithmic and convergence analysis for client-dependent decision-dependent shift.

entry.title: Adversarial Bandit Optimization with Globally Bounded Perturbations to Convex Losses

author.name: Zhuoyu Cheng, Kohei Hatano, Eiji Takimoto

entry.summary: Extends globally-budgeted post-action adversarial perturbation bandit optimization from linear losses to general convex and beta-smooth losses with adversarial perturbations bounded by a global budget. Establishes expected regret guarantees explicitly characterizing the perturbation-budget effect.

entry.title: Integrating national forest inventory, airborne lidar, and satellite imagery for wall-to-wall mapping of forest structure with computer vision

author.name: Luke J. Zachmann, David D. Diaz, Vincent A. Landau, Chelsey Walden-Schreiner, Tony Chang, Nathan E. Rutenbeck, Katharyn A. Duffy, Kiarie Ndegwa, Andreas Gros, Scott Conway, Guy Bayes

entry.summary: Introduces VibrantForests, a framework integrating national forest inventory, airborne lidar, and satellite imagery to produce wall-to-wall annually updated maps of forest structure across the contiguous US. It trains a satellite-based model on lidar-derived samples to support forest and wildfire planning.

entry.title: Train, Retrieve, or Both? A Four-Arm Head-to-Head for Correct Statutory Citation on the Ontario Residential Tenancies Act

author.name: Ali Asaria, Tony Salomone, Deep Gandhi

entry.summary: Runs a four-arm head-to-head comparison (base zero-shot, LoRA SFT-only, RAG-only, SFT+RAG hybrid) on Qwen2.5-7B for producing correct statutory citations on Ontario tenancy law. Finds retrieval is essential, drives hallucination to zero by construction, and the hybrid performs best, answering whether fine-tuning alone suffices.

entry.title: Marginal Advantage Accumulation for Memory-Driven Agent Self-Evolution

author.name: Mingyu Yang, Keye Zheng, Congchao Cheng, Yujie Liu, Xingkang Lu, Fan Jiang, Yefei Zheng

entry.summary: Proposes Marginal Advantage Accumulation, a post-processing method for memory-driven agent self-evolution that accumulates signed evidence per memory operation across batches to distinguish stably effective operations from accidental hits. It reports strong results across multiple benchmarks for agent memory distillation.

entry.title: Doeblin Curves

author.name: Dongmin Lee, William Lu, Anuran Makur, Japneet Singh

entry.summary: Introduces Doeblin curves, a finer-grained generalization of Doeblin coefficients that yields non-vacuous information-contraction guarantees even for channels whose Doeblin coefficient is zero. Builds on nonlinear information contraction theory for multi-way contraction characterization.

entry.title: EFIQA: Explainable Fundus Image Quality Assessment via Anatomical Priors

author.name: Pengwei Wang, Jos\'e Morano, Qian Wan, Hrvoje Bogunovi\'c

entry.summary: Proposes EFIQA, an explainable fundus image quality assessment framework requiring no quality-related supervision that learns what anatomy should be present via anatomical priors and produces spatial quality maps. Improves generalization across datasets and adds explainability over label-trained classifiers.

entry.title: Light-weight Pronunciation Assessment via Discrete Speech Token Surprisal

author.name: Syeda Faiza Ahmed Sara, Shammur Absar Chowdhury

entry.summary: Proposes a lightweight pronunciation assessment framework trained only on native speech, discretizing learner speech with an SSL encoder and K-means codebook and using token-language-model surprisal plus a transcript-guided alignment module to derive error-sensitive features. Avoids costly labeled non-native corpora via unsupervised or lightly calibrated training.

entry.title: A Layered Security Framework Against Prompt Injection in RAG-Based Chatbots

author.name: Gulshan Saleem, Nisar Ahmed, Muhammad Imran Zaman, Ali Hassan

entry.summary: This work presents a three-layer security framework to defend RAG chatbots against both direct and indirect prompt injection, addressing the gap where isolated input/output filters fail against poisoned knowledge-base documents. Layers combine rule-based screening with deeper inspection.

entry.title: Mix-QVLA: Task-Evidence-Aware Mixed-Precision Quantization of Vision-Language-Action Models

author.name: Navin Ranjan, Andreas Savakis

entry.summary: Mix-QVLA is a task-evidence-aware mixed-precision post-training quantization framework for vision-language-action models, anchoring quantized variants to full-precision action decisions and measuring evidence distortion at functional boundaries. It models sensitivity across task-execution phases.

entry.title: Training-Free Metrics for Synthetic Object Detection Data: A Proxy for Detector Performance

author.name: Myeongseok Nam, Donghoon Yeo, Seungwook Kim

entry.summary: This paper introduces CCDM, a pre-computable training-free metric family that serves as a proxy for the downstream utility of synthetic object-detection datasets without training a detector. It addresses the expense of evaluating synthetic data for dense detection annotations.

entry.title: GEN-Guard: Correcting Generalization Failures for Deployable Federated Surgical AI

author.name: Julia Alekseenko, Pietro Mascagni, AI4SafeChole Consortium, Nicolas Padoy

entry.summary: GEN-Guard is a post-hoc framework for federated surgical AI that detects and corrects generalization failures via client-blocked evaluation, identifying performance leakage where models overfit federation data and fail on unseen institutions. It improves deployment model selection.

entry.title: PCFootprint: A Large-Scale Dataset and Benchmark for Vectorized Building Footprint Extraction from Aerial LiDAR Point Clouds

author.name: Haoyuan Shen, Kuihao Wang, Ruisheng Wang, Yujun Liu

entry.summary: PCFootprint is the first large-scale public dataset (33,000 tiles) for vectorized building footprint extraction from airborne LiDAR point clouds, addressing limitations of optical imagery such as occlusion and lack of elevation. It enables LoD building modeling from point clouds.

entry.title: FrequencyFormer: A Co-Designed Sensor-to-Processor Pipeline for Frequency-Domain Vision Transformer Inference

author.name: Chengwei Zhou, Ovishake Sen, Xuming Chen, Rishith Paramasivam, Shaahin Angizi, Swarup Bhunia, Baibhab Chatterjee, Gourav Datta

entry.summary: FrequencyFormer is a co-designed sensor-to-processor pipeline using a multi-scale DCT tokenizer to exploit frequency-domain compactness for efficient vision transformer inference on edge devices. It reduces sensor-to-processor data movement and energy cost.

entry.title: MMD-SLAM: Structure-Enhanced Multi-Meta Gaussian Distribution-Guided Visual SLAM

author.name: Fan Zhu, Ziyu Chen, Peichen Liu, Yifan Zhao, Zhisong Xu, Hui Zhu, Hongxing Zhou, Sixun Liu, Chunmao Jiang

entry.summary: MMD-SLAM is a structure-enhanced visual SLAM framework using 3D Gaussian Splatting guided by the Atlanta World assumption and point-line fusion for photorealistic mapping with improved tracking robustness. It exploits structural regularities that existing 3DGS-SLAM systems underuse.

entry.title: SCAN-Planner: Spatial Collision-Aware Local Planning for Route-Guided Long-Range Quadruped Navigation

author.name: Han Zheng, Zhe Chen, Yiwen Fu, Ming Yang, Tong Qin

entry.summary: SCAN-Planner is a spatial collision-aware local planner for long-range quadruped navigation that uses a yaw-aware twin-cylinder footprint and projected A* search to handle tight spaces and overhanging structures. It enables whole-body collision evaluation in 3D occupancy maps.

entry.title: An Infrastructure-less, Control-Independent Solution to Relative Localisation of a Team of Mobile Robots using Ranging Measurements

author.name: Paolo Golinelli, Tommaso Faraci, Daniele Fontanelli

entry.summary: This work presents a decentralized cooperative localization algorithm for robot teams that is anchor-less and, unlike most approaches, does not require controlling robot motion for observability, relying only on odometry, sparse ranging, and short-range communication. It enables fast flexible deployment without fixed infrastructure.

entry.title: ARC: Adaptive Robust Joint State and Covariance Estimation

author.name: Alexandre Hadji-Thomas, Andrew Stirling, James R. Forbes

entry.summary: ARC is a unified Block-Coordinate Descent framework that jointly performs robust state estimation and measurement covariance estimation in the presence of outliers and non-Gaussian noise, combining a norm-aware adaptive robust loss with iteratively reweighted least squares. It integrates two previously separate capabilities.

entry.title: Uncertainty Decomposition for Clarification Seeking in LLM Agents

author.name: Gregory Matsnev

entry.summary: Proposes a prompt-based decomposition of uncertainty for black-box LLM agents that separates action confidence from underspecification, enabling proactive clarification-seeking without logprobs, multi-sampling, or training. Targets deployment constraints like API-only access and latency.

entry.title: AURA: Adaptive Uncertainty-aware Refinement for LLM-as-a-Judge Auditing

author.name: Zilong Zhang, Yi-Ting Hung, Weiyi He, Junxi Zhang, Lei Ding, Chi-Kuang Yeh

entry.summary: Proposes AURA, an adaptive uncertainty-aware refinement framework for auditing pairwise LLM-as-a-judge decisions without assuming a pre-existing clean subset or abundant human verification. Addresses fragile assumptions in existing judge-auditing pipelines.

entry.title: The Hidden Evolution of Disguised Visual Context inside the VLM

author.name: Wish Suharitdamrong, Tony Alex, Muhammad Awais, Sara Atito

entry.summary: Provides a controlled comparison of how VLM integration architectures (in-context visual tokens versus layer-wise injection) transform visual information internally under identical training across image, multi-image, and video benchmarks. Offers analysis of an underexplored architectural design choice.

entry.title: HilDA: Hierarchical Distillation with Diffusion for Advancing Self-Supervised LiDAR Pre-trainin

author.name: Maciej Wozniak, Jesper Ericsson, Hariprasath Govindarajan, Truls Nyberg, Thomas Gustafsson, Patric Jensfelt, Olov Andersson

entry.summary: Proposes HilDA, a self-supervised LiDAR pretraining framework that distills layer-wise semantic structure and global context from vision foundation models using hierarchical distillation with diffusion, rather than treating teachers as black boxes. Targets annotation scarcity in autonomous driving perception.

entry.title: Contagion Networks: Evaluator Bias Propagation in Multi-Agent LLM Systems

author.name: Zewen Liu

entry.summary: Introduces Contagion Networks, a formal framework measuring how LLM evaluator biases propagate across interacting agents in multi-agent systems, finding consistent bias contagion even within the same underlying model and identifying propagation regimes via spectral radius. Uses a controlled three-agent DeepSeek experiment.

entry.title: Physics-Informed Discovery of Yield Functions in Plasticity via Convex Neural Representations

author.name: Hyeonbin Moon, Donghyuk Cho, Jecheon Yu, Jeong Whan Yoon, Seunghwa Ryu

entry.summary: Proposes a physics-informed framework discovering anisotropic yield functions from full-field displacement and reaction-force data without stress observations or a prescribed parametric form, using convex neural representations embedded in elastoplastic stress integration. Addresses the difficulty of calibrating yield surfaces in plasticity.

entry.title: An Information Theoretic Framework for Graph Novelty Generation via Latent Mixture Modeling

author.name: Itsuki Nakagawa, Kenji Yamanishi

entry.summary: Presents an information-theoretic framework for generating graphs that are novel relative to existing patterns while preserving global structural consistency, using latent mixture models and the Minimum Description Length principle. Novelty and reliability are enforced as description-length conditions with theoretical analysis.

entry.title: Physics-Informed Neural Network with Squeeze-Excitation-like Attention

author.name: Yun-Fei Song, Long-Gang Pang, Fu-Peng Li, Jun-Jie Zhang

entry.summary: SEA-PINN incorporates a squeeze-excitation-like attention mechanism into physics-informed neural networks to dynamically recalibrate neuron importance across layers. It achieves highly stable initialization with low variance and competitive accuracy without Fourier features or periodic activations.

entry.title: Adaptive Distance-Aware Trunk Deep Operator Learning for Long-Span Roadway Bridges

author.name: Bilal Ahmed, Diab W. Abueidda, Waleed El-Sekelly, Tarek Abdoun, Mostafa E. Mobasher

entry.summary: Proposes an adaptive-trunk DeepONet for predicting localized structural responses in long-span bridges under vehicular loading, dynamically building a load-dependent learning domain via kNN and distance-aware trunk features. It targets expensive repeated FE analysis for influence-surface generation and structural digital twins.

entry.title: The Significance of Style Diversity in Annotation-Free Synthetic Data Generation

author.name: Zahra Abbasiantaeb, Zeno Belligoli, Omar Essam, Mohammad Aliannejadi

entry.summary: Proposes a framework for annotation-free synthetic dialogue generation for intent classification using only intent definitions, with topic and style attributes and two post-hoc stylization models (Univ and Exam) to diversify utterances. Uses LLM-as-a-judge filtering to enhance data quality for fast-paced industrial settings.

entry.title: A fast direct solver based neural network for solving PDEs

author.name: Jashwanth Reddy Kadaru, Vaishnavi Gujjula

entry.summary: Presents a neural network that learns the inverse operation of HODLR (hierarchical off-diagonal low-rank) matrices based on the Ambikasaran-Darve fast direct solver, and extends the architecture to learn nonlinear PDE solution operators. Combines fast numerical linear algebra structure with neural operator learning.

entry.title: Investigating Human-Model Discrepancies in Speech Quality Assessment via Acoustic and Prosodic Perturbations

author.name: Masato Takagi, Masaya Kawamura, Reo Shimizu, Yuma Shirahata

entry.summary: Investigates discrepancies between human and MOS-prediction-model judgments of speech quality using controlled acoustic, prosodic, and speaker-characteristic perturbations. Finds models track acoustic degradation but are insensitive to prosodic errors and exhibit double dissociations on speaker features.

entry.title: CATCH-ME if you RAG: a dataset of Contextually Annotated multi-Turn Counterspeech against Hate and Misinformation Exchanges

author.name: Helena Bonaldi, Genoveffa Martone, Marco Guerini

entry.summary: CATCH-ME introduces the first large-scale, expert-curated, multilingual, multi-turn dataset of counterspeech against the intersection of hate speech and misinformation. It addresses the gap in prior single-turn English-only resources for LLM-assisted counterspeech.

entry.title: DiffMath: Symbol- and Graph-Aware Latent Diffusion Transformer for Handwritten Mathematical Expression Generation

author.name: Wei Pan, Xuhan Zheng, Yilin Shi, Huiguo He, Hiuyi Cheng, Dezhi Peng, Minghui Liao, Lianwen Jin

entry.summary: DiffMath is a symbol- and graph-aware latent diffusion transformer for handwritten mathematical expression generation that uses LaTeX hierarchical structure as a prior, eliminating the need for symbol-level bounding-box supervision. It distills MathML trees into compact triplet sequences.

entry.title: SketchKeyAnime: Reference-anchored Sparse Key-Sketch Animation Synthesis

author.name: Meixi Li, Xianlin Zhang, Yue Zhang, Xueming Li

entry.summary: SketchKeyAnime is a video diffusion framework that generates controllable, appearance-consistent, temporally coherent animations from a single reference image and a few sparse key sketches via a dual-branch conditioning mechanism. It targets low-cost animation production.

entry.title: ARTEMIS: Agent-guided Reliability-aware Temporal Mask Evolution for Imperfectly Supervised Video Polyp Segmentation

author.name: Tong Wang, Siwen Wang, Yaolei Qi, Jinxing Zhou, Yuting He, Guanyu Yang, Yutong Xie

entry.summary: ARTEMIS is a unified framework for imperfectly supervised video polyp segmentation that uses agent-guided reliability-aware temporal mask evolution to refine SAM2-generated masks, addressing boundary leakage and underused temporal consistency. It learns dense temporally consistent masks from weak or sparse supervision.

entry.title: BAFIS: Dataset + Framework to assess occupational Bias and Human Preference in modern Text-to-image Models

author.name: Thomas Klassert, Adrian Ulges, Biying Fu

entry.summary: BAFIS is a dataset and framework assessing occupational gender and ethnicity bias plus human preference across five text-to-image models including Midjourney, SD3, DALL-E 3, Playground, and FLUX. It complements established metrics with human preference feedback.

entry.title: Single-Stage Hierarchical Rectification for Weakly Supervised Histopathology Segmentation

author.name: Duc T. Nguyen, Hoang-Long Nguyen, Thanh-Ha DO, Huy-Hieu Pham

entry.summary: SSHR is a single-stage hierarchical rectification framework for weakly supervised histopathology segmentation that replaces the standard multi-stage CAM-refine-retrain paradigm to reduce computational cost and prevent error propagation from shallow-layer texture biases. It actively rectifies activations during training rather than post-hoc.

entry.title: Contour-Constrained Deformable Registration with Parameter Characterization for Head and Neck Surgical Guidance

author.name: Qingyun Yang, Jon S. Heiselman, Ayberk Acar, Morgan J. Ringel, Michael I. Miga, Matthieu Chabanas, Michael C. Topf, Jie Ying Wu

entry.summary: This work presents a biomechanics-driven deformable registration framework that corrects post-resection tissue shrinkage to relocate positive surgical margins on the resection bed during head and neck cancer surgery. It registers 3D specimen meshes to intraoperative point clouds.

entry.title: Simulating Robotic Locomotion in Sand: Resistive Force Theory in an Open-Source Physics Engine

author.name: Ryan Walker Brown, Laura K. Treers, Kathryn A. Daltorio

entry.summary: This work implements 3D Granular Resistive Force Theory in the MuJoCo physics engine to simulate robotic locomotion in sand without modeling individual grains. It verifies that key trends in end-effector shape, speed, and loading are preserved for stable walking simulation.

entry.title: TIDY: Thermal Infrared Image Denoising via Wavelet Domain Entropy and Directional Stripe Index

author.name: Tai Hyoung Rhee, Dong-Guw Lee, Ayoung Kim

entry.summary: TIDY is a lightweight wavelet-domain denoiser for thermal infrared images using entropy and a directional stripe index, trained on real clean-noisy pairs rather than synthetic noise, achieving a good accuracy-efficiency tradeoff for online robotics. It targets severe fixed-pattern and stochastic noise especially indoors.

entry.title: AK-MCS-C2 : Active Kriging Monte Carlo Simulation method with conformal certification for failure probability estimation

author.name: Edgar Jaber (CB, ENS Paris Saclay), Vincent Chabridon (EDF R\&D PRISME), Mathilde Mougeot (CB, ENSIIE, ENS Paris Saclay)

entry.summary: AK-MCS-C2 integrates Active Kriging Monte Carlo simulation with conformal prediction for failure probability estimation in structural reliability, providing distribution-free guarantees on prediction errors via an adaptive cross-conformal strategy for small samples. It improves classification of samples near the limit-state surface.

entry.title: BIM-Edit: Benchmarking Large Language Models for IFC-Based Building Information Modeling

author.name: Bharathi Kannan Nithyanantham, Clemens Kujat, Tobias Sesterhenn, Stefan Telgmann, J\"orn Pl\"onnigs, Stefan L\"udtke, Christian Bartelt

entry.summary: Introduces BIM-Edit, a benchmark for evaluating LLMs on natural-language editing of Building Information Models in the IFC format, requiring scene understanding, correct edits, and preservation of semantics and relations rather than just new geometry. Provides a challenging editing-focused CAD testbed.

entry.title: FlowFake: Liquid Networks for Audio Deepfake Detection

author.name: Shivaay Dhondiyal, Divyansh Sharma, Dinesh Kumar Vishwakarma

entry.summary: Proposes FlowFake, a compact Liquid Time-Constant (ODE-based) architecture for audio deepfake detection that resolves both spectral (10ms) and prosodic (2s) cues via per-neuron adaptive time constants. Targets the cross-dataset generalization failure of fixed-window detectors.

entry.title: Data Standards for Humanoid Robotics: The Missing Infrastructure for Physical AI

author.name: Shaoshan Liu, Xiugong Qin, Xuan Wu, Xuan Xia, Ning Ding, Jialu Liu, Jie Tang

entry.summary: Argues that data standards are foundational infrastructure for Physical AI, drawing on the authors' work developing ISO/WD 26264-1 for humanoid robot datasets, emphasizing embodied interaction data and physical coherence across robots, tasks, and time. Position piece on enabling experience to accumulate across humanoid robots.

entry.title: Hierarchical Control in Multi-Agent Games: LLM-based Planning and RL Execution

author.name: Jannik H\"osch, Alessandro Sestini, Florian Fuchs, Amir Baghi, Joakim Bergdahl, Konrad Tollmar, Jean-Philippe Barrette-LaPierre, Linus Gissl\'en

entry.summary: Proposes a hierarchical architecture where a pretrained LLM acts as a strategic controller selecting among specialized RL skill policies for a team of agents in a competitive game, with RL handling low-level execution. Compares against behavior tree and flat RL baselines.

entry.title: From Texts to Scores: Tracing the Emergence of Essay Quality Representations in Large Language Models

author.name: Jiaxu Zuo, Mu You, Kaixin Lan, Tao Fang, Yujia Huo, Henghua Shen, Lidia S. Chao, Derek F. Wong

entry.summary: Analyzes hidden representations of eight LLMs across English and Portuguese essay datasets using linear probing and neuron-level analysis, finding essay-quality information is linearly accessible and emerges progressively across layers. Sheds light on the internal mechanisms of LLM-based automated essay scoring.

entry.title: Evaluating and Enhancing Negation Comprehension in Remote Sensing MLLMs

author.name: Haochen Han, Jue Wang, Alex Jinpeng Wang, Fangming Liu

entry.summary: Introduces RS-Neg, the first benchmark for negation understanding in remote sensing multimodal LLMs, revealing models struggle to identify what is absent or false, with a data generation pipeline and dynamic visual focus module. Highlights a deployment-critical comprehension gap for emergency-response use cases.

entry.title: ELVA: Exploring Ranking-Driven Universal Multimodal Retrieval

author.name: Yuhan Liu, Pei Fu, Hang Li, Yukun Qi, Chao Jiang, Jingwen Fu, Zhen Liu, Bin Qin, Zhenbo Luo, Jian Luan, Jingmin Xin

entry.summary: Proposes ELVA, a ranking-driven approach to universal multimodal retrieval that addresses grain blindness by treating negative samples differently according to similarity rather than as uniform binary classes. Aims to better handle fine-grained complex queries in MLLM-based retrieval.

entry.title: Learning universal approximations for partial differential equations with Physics-Informed Broad Learning System

author.name: Zhiwen Yu, Derong Yang, Liujian Zhang, Kaixiang Yang, Peilin Zhan, Jianmin Lv, Jane You, C. L. Philip Chen

entry.summary: Proposes the Physics-Informed Broad Learning System, a backpropagation-free framework reformulating PDE solving as direct least-squares optimization to overcome PINN convergence instability. Extends the method to nonlinear PDEs with a universal approximation proof.

entry.title: Self-Adaptive Scale Handling for Forecasting Time Series with Scale Heterogeneity

author.name: Xu Zhang, Zhengang Huang, Yunzhi Wu, Xun Lu, Erpeng Qi, Yunkai Chen, Zhongya Xue, Peng Wang, Wei Wang

entry.summary: Proposes a self-adaptive scale-handling module for forecasting time series with scale heterogeneity, where series differ by orders of magnitude but share temporal patterns. It learns input-tailored adaptive scale factors that preserve semantic discriminability, avoiding the pitfalls of global or window-based scaling.

entry.title: Predicting gestational age at birth in the context of preterm birth from multi-modal fetal MRI

author.name: Diego Fajardo-Rojas, Megan Hall, Daniel Cromb, Mary A. Rutherford, Lisa Story, Emma C. Robinson, Jana Hutter

entry.summary: Develops a bespoke ML pipeline (data imputation, feature selection, regression) to predict gestational age at birth from multimodal fetal MRI in 333 controls and 93 preterm cases. Classifies predictions into term and preterm categories with ablation validation of the pipeline design.

entry.title: Quantum-classical physics-informed Kolmogorov-Arnold networks for PDEs

author.name: Xiang Rao, Yuxuan Shen

entry.summary: Develops QCPIKAN, a quantum-classical physics-informed Kolmogorov-Arnold network combining Chebyshev-polynomial KAN layers with parameterized quantum circuits to solve PDEs. Theory shows accelerated high-frequency error convergence and reduced numerical dispersion, validated on porous-media seepage scenarios.

entry.title: Towards Modality-imbalanced Federated Graph Learning: A Data Synthesis-based Approach

author.name: Zhengyu Wu, Hongchao Qin, Xunkai Li, Zekai Chen, Rong-Hua Li, Guoren Wang

entry.summary: Formalizes modality-imbalanced multimodal federated graph learning as a graph-aware latent semantic synthesis problem, addressing both client-level missing modalities and node-level missing attributes. Proposes a data-synthesis approach to recover missing modal semantics within the graph structure.

entry.title: PASQA: Pitch-Accent-Focused Speech Quality Assessment Model Trained on Synthetic Speech with Accent Errors

author.name: Masaya Kawamura, Yuma Shirahata, Kentaro Mitsui, Reo Shimizu

entry.summary: Proposes PASQA, a speech quality assessment model explicitly targeting pitch-accent correctness, trained on a controlled Japanese accent-error dataset generated by an accent-controllable TTS system. Uses mora-conditioned fusion, ranking loss, and accent-error localization to outperform conventional naturalness MOS models on accent sensitivity.

entry.title: Statistical Properties of Training & Generalization

author.name: Itay Lavie, Noam Levi, Yonatan Kahn

entry.summary: A physics-informed review of deep learning's surprising statistical behavior, covering neural scaling laws and their interplay with inductive biases and constraints when applying ML to physics problems. Aims to explain how deep learning evades classical statistical intuitions.

entry.title: LEAP: Layer-skipping Efficiency via Adaptive Progression for Vision Transformer Distillation

author.name: Jiaqi Zhang, Ashton Lee, Anthony Wong, John Zou, Sami BuGhanem, Randall Balestriero

entry.summary: LEAP is a training curriculum for ViT feature-based knowledge distillation that treats a teacher's intermediate feature maps as progressively harder targets to mitigate the teacher-student capacity gap. It targets distilling vision foundation models like DINOv2 for edge deployment.

entry.title: QG-MIL: A Gated Transformer Aggregator for Domain-Agnostic Multiple Instance Learning in Medical Imaging

author.name: Luca Zedda, Davide Antonio Mura, Cecilia Di Ruberto, Maurizio Atzori, Muhammed Furkan Dasdelen, Carsten Marr, Andrea Loddo

entry.summary: QG-MIL is a gated transformer aggregator for domain-agnostic multiple instance learning in medical imaging that combats attention concentration via RMSNorm, per-head QK normalization, fine-grained output gating, and SwiGLU modules. It distributes attention more uniformly without auxiliary losses across six benchmarks.

entry.title: FUSE: Frequency-domain Unification and Spectral Energy Alignment for Multi-modal Object Re-Identification

author.name: Xuanhao Qi, Tom H. Luan, Yukang Zhang, Jinkai Zheng, Zhou Su, Shuwei Li, Lei Tan

entry.summary: FUSE is a frequency-domain framework for multi-modal object re-identification that disentangles low/mid/high-frequency subspaces and aligns spectral energy across modalities, addressing the over-reliance on low-frequency cues. It recovers geometric and textural identity-discriminative details.

entry.title: Geometry-Preserving in 3D Gaussian Splatting for LiDAR-Camera Extrinsic Calibration

author.name: Kyoleen Kwak, Daeho Kim, Jeong Woon Lee, Hyoseok Hwang

entry.summary: This paper proposes a geometry-preserving 3D Gaussian Splatting framework for targetless LiDAR-camera extrinsic calibration, addressing how rendering-focused 3DGS proxies drift from true LiDAR structure. It preserves metric geometry within the differentiable calibration framework.

entry.title: CMDS-AD: Cross-Modal Dual-Stream Decoupling for Few-Shot Anomaly Detection

author.name: Junhao Cai, Deyu Zeng, Junhao Pang, Junyu Chen, Qiwei Liang, Xiaopin Zhong, Zongze Wu

entry.summary: CMDS-AD is a cross-modal dual-stream framework for few-shot anomaly detection that decouples stable macroscopic structures from high-frequency localized defect signals and uses LoRA-guided diffusion to augment RGB samples and a diffusion-based 3D normal estimator. It addresses cross-modal misalignment and high false-positive rates.

entry.title: SAFE-Cascade: Cost-Adaptive Vision-Language Routing for Chart Question Answering
