author.name: Marta Fernandez-Moreno, Margarita Guerrero, Rosalia Rementeria, Pablo Mesejo, Raul Moreno

entry.summary: Quantifies how much unsupervised algorithms can accelerate manual annotation for complex semantic segmentation in industrial materials science. Provides the first empirical measurement of labeling speedups from unsupervised assistance in this setting.

entry.title: The Almost Intelligent Revolution: Options for Scaling Up Deliberation and Empowering People with AI

author.name: Serge Sharoff

entry.summary: A perspective chapter examining how LLMs can scale up and democratize public deliberation, drawing on Systemic-Functional Linguistics to address linguistic constraints, biases, and sycophancy while empowering marginalized groups. Explores options for inclusive AI-assisted deliberation.

entry.title: Exploring Multi-Modal Large Language Models and Two-Stage Fine-Tuning for Fashion Image Retrieval

author.name: Nguyen Cao Hoang, Hoang Bui Le, Nam Vo Hoang, Trung-Nghia Le

entry.summary: This work tackles composed image retrieval in fashion by using a multimodal LLM (LLaVA) to generate attribute-aware triplets and a two-stage fine-tuning strategy to improve contrastive learning. It scales negatives using pretrained vision-language models.

entry.title: SAM3 Self-Distillation for Fine-Grained GOOSE 2D Semantic Segmentation

author.name: Xuesong Wang

entry.summary: This challenge entry adapts the SAM3 image encoder with a lightweight decoder for fine-grained semantic segmentation, contributing a self-distillation scheme reusing SAM3 prompted with ground-truth boxes as a teacher and a multi-scale test-time augmentation scheme. It reached 4th place with 69.73% mIoU.

entry.title: Efficiently Linking Real Scenes with Synthetic Data Generation for AI-based Cognitive Robotics and Computer Vision Applications

author.name: Paul Koch, Vivek Chavan, Andr\'e Sers, Adem Karakurt, Paul Hofmann, Mohamad Zaher Ziadeh, J\"org Kr\"uger

entry.summary: This work-in-progress paper discusses bridging the sim-to-real domain gap for cognitive robotics by efficiently linking real scenes with synthetic data generation for tasks like 6D and grasping pose estimation. It reviews current limits and proposes synergistic data and architecture methods.

entry.title: Introduction: Gaussian Natural Latents

author.name: Haru

entry.summary: An introductory post laying out a research direction called Gaussian Natural Latents, situated within the Natural Abstractions agenda that seeks a mathematical theory of shared concept structure across agents. It previews forthcoming results aimed at formalizing how concepts could be objectively identified.

entry.title: The Tao of Agency: Autotelic AI, Embedded Agency and Dissolution of the Self

author.name: Aritra Sarkar

entry.summary: A philosophical exploration of autotelic AI, where agents generate their own goals, tracing consequences through intrinsic motivation, resource-driven priors, causal learning, homeostasis, and embeddedness. Argues embeddedness individuates the agent but leads to non-unique self-partitions.

entry.title: How far do open weights trail the frontier?

author.name: RobinHa

entry.summary: A data-analysis post measuring how far open-weight models lag closed frontier models, preferring Epoch's IRT-based ECI metric over a cruder index and finding a meaningfully different (less collapsing) lag curve. It also generalizes the method to compare lab rivalries like OpenAI versus Anthropic.

entry.title: How Transparent is DiffusionGemma?

author.name: Joshua Engels, Callum McDougall, Bilal Chughtai, Janos Kramar, Senthoran Rajamanoharan, Cindy Wu, Arthur Conmy, Asic Q Chen, Jean Tarbouriech, Min Ma, Brendan O'Donoghue, Jo\~ao Gabriel Lopes de Oliveira, Rohin Shah, Neel Nanda

entry.summary: Studies the reasoning transparency of DiffusionGemma by decomposing it into variable transparency (understanding intermediate computational snapshots) and algorithmic transparency (reconstructing the reasoning process), finding its continuous latent computation poses interpretability challenges. Authored by a DeepMind interpretability team including Neel Nanda. Note that DiffusionGemma was released on 2026-06-10, so this is analysis of an existing model.

entry.title: Toten: Knowledge-Based Ontological Tokenization Of Physical Quantities And Technical Notation In Brazilian Portuguese

author.name: Antonio de Sousa Leit\~ao Filho; Allan Kardec Duailibe Barros Filho; Fabr\'icio Saul Lima; Selby Mykael Lima dos Santos; Rejani Bandeira Vieira Sousa

entry.summary: Presents TOTEN, an ontology-based tokenization framework that replaces statistical BPE for structured technical entities (physical quantities, units, symbolic notation) in Brazilian Portuguese using declarative classification grounded in an engineering ontology. Aims to preserve semantic structure that BPE fragments.

entry.title: A Tool for the Synthesis of Adaptive Probabilistic Processors Based on the Ising Model

author.name: Jonathan Juracy Carneiro da Silva, Leonardo R. Gobatto, Jose Rodrigo Azambuja

entry.summary: Presents a tool for synthesizing and simulating probabilistic Ising-model processors (p-bits) for combinatorial optimization, automatically constructing the Hamiltonian and adaptively selecting among Gibbs sampling, simulated annealing, SQA, and cluster methods. Improves convergence and flexibility versus fixed approaches.

entry.title: A Categorial and Sheaf-Theoretic Semantics for Autonomic Component Ensembles

author.name: Manuel Hern\'andez, Eduardo S\'anchez-Soto

entry.summary: This report proposes a category-theoretic and sheaf-theoretic semantics for the Software Component Ensemble Language to reason about global, structural, and emergent properties of decentralized autonomous agent systems. It models robot societies as sheaves on topological spaces.

entry.title: On “Model Organisms”

author.name: J Bostock

entry.summary: A reflective post examining the meaning and history of the term model organism as used in AI safety, drawing parallels to its biological origins to clarify what researchers are actually studying. It distinguishes studying production models, intervention effects, and specific properties.

entry.title: AI4SE and SE4AI Exploration: A Decade Looking Back and Forward

author.name: H. Sinan Bank, Daniel R. Herber, Thomas Bradley

entry.summary: Reviews a decade of AI for Systems Engineering and SE for AI across foundational, applied, and LLM-inflection phases, using a human-AI agreement literature review over thousands of articles. Identifies convergence points and critical gaps in the community.

entry.title: A Comparative Study of Pretrained Transformer Models for Quranic ASR: Speech Representations, Label Formats, and Dataset Composition

author.name: Nabil Mosharraf Hossain (Greentech Apps Foundation, United Kingdom), Riasat Islam (Greentech Apps Foundation, United Kingdom, Queen Mary University of London, United Kingdom), Unaizah Obaidellah (University of Malaya, Malaysia)

entry.summary: Conducts a comparative study of pretrained Transformer speech models (Wav2Vec2.0, HuBERT, XLS-R) fine-tuned for Quranic automatic speech recognition, examining speech representations, label formats, and dataset composition. Aims to reduce word error rates on user recitations.

entry.title: Human-AI Agent Interaction in a Business Context

author.name: Kathrin Paimann, Elizangela Valarini, Sebastian Juhl

entry.summary: Investigates human-AI agent interaction patterns in business contexts to identify principles and criteria for positive user experience, trust, and user-centered decision-making, using a mixed-methods exploratory approach. Develops a survey experiment to evaluate interaction patterns for AI agent adoption.

entry.title: Ensembles of Large Language Models for Identifying EQ-5D Studies in PubMed Based on Their Abstracts

author.name: Zhyar Rzgar K. Rostam, M\'arta P\'entek, J\'anos Tibor Czere, Zsombor Zrubka, L\'aszl\'o Gul\'acsi, G\'abor Kert\'esz

entry.summary: Evaluates ensembles of nine Gemini and Gemma LLMs with few-shot prompting and a stacking meta-classifier to automate detection of EQ-5D quality-of-life studies in PubMed abstracts. It addresses the bottleneck of manual screening in systematic literature reviews.

entry.title: Bistable by Construction: Wall-Clock-Calibrated State Monitors Have No Moment-Detection Regime at Agent Cadence

author.name: Manvendra Modgil

entry.summary: Corrects a prior result (an erratum-as-experiment) showing that runtime state monitors calibrated in wall-clock time have no moment-detection regime at agent cadence, contrasting sample-time monitors like CUSUM. Examines a State Saturation Trap caused by zero time deltas disabling exponential decay.

entry.title: From 50K to 8.2 Million in 24 Hours: Vozinha's Algorithmic Consecration and the Multilingual Making of World Cup Visibility

author.name: Vinicius Covas

entry.summary: A multilingual computational discourse analysis of how language constructed the algorithmic virality of a Cape Verde goalkeeper after a 2026 World Cup match, contributing a four-language corpus, a nine-frame narrative taxonomy, and an LLM-assisted annotation pipeline with human validation. Treats follower-count growth as a narratable linguistic object.

entry.title: Vortex: Multi-Modal Fusion System for Intelligent Video Retrieval

author.name: Duc-Tho Nguyen, Hieu-Hoc Tran-Minh, Khanh-Hoa Lam, Hoang-Nhut Ly, Huu-Phuc Huynh, Thanh-Tien Tran, Trung-Nghia Le

entry.summary: Vortex is a multimodal video retrieval system combining adaptive keyframe extraction, vision-language and speech metadata, and hybrid CLIP/SigLIP2 fusion with relevance feedback, built for a challenge competition. It uses Milvus and Elasticsearch for scalable indexing.

entry.title: A BART-based approach with hierarchical strategy for Vietnamese abstractive multi-document summarization

author.name: Vu Nguyen Nguyen Xuan, Huy Ngo Quang

entry.summary: A technical report on Vietnamese abstractive multi-document summarization using a BART-based hierarchical condense-then-aggregate strategy guided by golden summaries, achieving ROUGE2-F1 of 0.2468 on the VLSP 2022 test set. Adds external data to expand training resources.

entry.title: Multi-Granular Attention-Driven Reinforcement Learning Framework for Web Intelligent Enhancement Systems

author.name: Navin Chhibber, Deepak Singh, Anokh Kishore, Nikita Chawla, K. Anguraj

entry.summary: Proposes a multi-granular attention-based reinforcement learning system for web intelligence enhancement, integrating semantic graph modeling, attention, and adaptive RL over heterogeneous web data. Aims to improve personalization and scalability in evolving web environments.

entry.title: Optimal Scheduling in a Question-Answering Forum of Knowledge Workers

author.name: Rohit Negi, Mustafa Yilmaz

entry.summary: Models a future Q&A forum staffed by paid knowledge-worker experts as a queuing system, computing capacity and designing schedulers that assign topic-specific requests to experts by expertise level. Analyzes optimal scheduling for throughput.

entry.title: Pitch Spelling Jazz Lead Sheets, Solo Transcriptions, Classical Piano and Monophonic Scores

author.name: Augustin Bouquillard (X), Florent Jacquemard (CEDRIC - VERTIGO)

entry.summary: This work presents an algorithm for pitch spelling and key estimation from MIDI-like input, using a two-stage modal-then-tonal optimization to produce correct note names and key signatures. It targets music notation across jazz, classical, and monophonic scores.

entry.title: Measuring Curriculum Alignment across Topical Coverage, Competency, and Cognitive Depth: A Longitudinal Framework Applied to CS2013 and CS2023

author.name: Sherzod Turaev, Mary John, Saja Aldabet, Mamoun Awad, Nazar Zaki, Khaled Shuaib

entry.summary: Presents a human-in-the-loop pipeline to measure how well a CS program covers official curricular guidelines (CS2013 vs CS2023) across topics, competencies, and cognitive depth. Uses semantic retrieval plus human judgment to track coverage shifts when standards are restructured.

entry.title: MetaResearcher: Scaling Deep Research via Self-Reflective Reinforcement Learning in Adversarial Virtual Environments

author.name: Wei Yu, Suxing Liu, Minjie Yu, Jiahao Wang, Zhijian Zheng, Haocheng Deng, Bing Li

author.name: Xijia Tao, Yihua Teng, Xinyu Fu, Ziru Liu, Kecheng Chen, Yuzhi Zhao, Suiyun Zhang, Rui Liu, Lingpeng Kong

entry.summary: arXiv:2606.20333v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Agent skills are commonly deployed as natural-language Markdown files that encode answer policies, evidence-use habits, and task procedures. These file...

author.name: Yuexing Hao, Xiaomin Li

entry.summary: arXiv:2606.20363v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Explicit skill libraries make computer-using agents easier to inspect, but it remains unclear whether such libraries can be mined from interaction data...

author.name: Jiawei Liu, Peiyi Han, Yuntao Lu, Su Zheng, Fengyu Yan, Bei Yu

entry.summary: arXiv:2606.19795v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Electronic design automation (EDA) is inherently multi-stage and handoff-heavy. Design artifacts, flow scripts, and engineering decisions cross tool,...

author.name: Kaiyue Yang, Yuyan Bu, Jingwei Yi, Yuchi Wang, Biyu Zhou, Juntao Dai, Songlin Hu, Yaodong Yang

entry.summary: arXiv:2606.20023v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: As LLM agents increasingly select tools autonomously, their choices among tools with different privileges become safety-relevant. However, prior tool...

entry.title: ScholarQuest: A Taxonomy-Guided Benchmark for Agentic Academic Paper Search in Open Literature Environments

author.name: Tingyue Pan, Mingyue Cheng, Daoyu Wang, Yitong Zhou, Jie Ouyang, Qi Liu, Enhong Chen

entry.summary: arXiv:2606.20235v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Academic paper search is a core step in scientific research, and LLM-based search agents are emerging as a promising paradigm for iterative, intent-d...

entry.title: Topological Data Analysis for High-Dimensional Dynamic Process Monitoring

author.name: Angan Mukherjee, Tyler A. Soderstrom, Michael J. Kurtz, Victor M. Zavala

entry.summary: arXiv:2606.20443v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Real-time process monitoring requires methods that extract actionable information from high-dimensional time-series data. In this work, we present a ...

author.name: Sai Sakunthala Guddanti, Anil Prabhakar, Ria Rushin Joseph

entry.title: Evaluation of Image Matching for Art Skills Assessment

author.name: Asaad Alghamdi, Michael Poor, Trung-Nghia Le, Tam V. Nguyen

entry.summary: This paper proposes measuring drawing skill by matching hand-drawn images with original templates using computer vision image-similarity techniques. It aims to automate art skills assessment compared to traditional manual evaluation.

entry.title: One Demo is Worth a Thousand Trajectories: Action-View Augmentation for Visuomotor Policies

author.name: Chuer Pan, Litian Liang, Dominik Bauer, Eric Cousineau, Benjamin Burchfiel, Siyuan Feng, Shuran Song

entry.summary: arXiv:2606.19586v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Visuomotor policies for manipulation have demonstrated remarkable potential in modeling complex robotic behaviors, yet minor alterations in the robot's...

entry.title: GLM 5.2 playing text adventures

author.name: kqr

entry.summary: An informal benchmark comparing the open-weights GLM 5.2 model against the similarly priced Gemini 3 Flash on text-adventure achievement counts under a fixed cost budget, using a linear regression controlling for game difficulty. It finds GLM 5.2 earns about 15 percent fewer achievements, a statistically significant gap.

entry.title: Does it feel any different to be reverse-chiral life?

author.name: jessicata

entry.summary: This philosophical essay examines chirality (handedness) as analogous to color in philosophy of mind, exploring through a science-fiction thought experiment of a parity-symmetric universe whether reverse-chiral life would feel any different. It probes the relationship between physical symmetry and conscious experience.

entry.title: AI that represents you can't be neutral.

author.name: agulaya24

entry.summary: An opinion piece arguing that beyond training priors and constitutional guardrails, the interpretive lens an AI applies is an understudied factor that can lead identical inputs to divergent moral or strategic conclusions. It frames personalized or representative AI as inherently non-neutral.

entry.title: CoT-forcing promptware

author.name: Bruce Middleton

entry.summary: A short prompt-engineering note describing a technique to force language models into more extensive structured chain-of-thought modeling by specifying ordered or tree-branching reasoning rules embedded in the prompt. It is a hobbyist exploration of exploiting the model's in-context generation rather than a rigorous study.

entry.title: Leveraged on being right

author.name: Ben Pace, the Vacationing Vagabond

entry.summary: A rationalist essay on the epistemics of receiving criticism, distinguishing cases where one's own lack of recollection is strong evidence against a claim from cases where the accusation itself predicts that you would fail to notice. It explores asymmetries in how introspective denials count as Bayesian evidence.

entry.title: How Domyn and AISquared built on Ai2's open releases

author.name: Unknown

entry.summary: A testimonial blog post from Ai2 describing how Domyn and AISquared use Ai2's open model releases to build systems for regulated industries where transparency, provenance, and licensing matter. It is promotional case-study content.

entry.title: Shard narcissism as delusion of unembededness

author.name: Fernand0

entry.summary: A speculative post reframing Lasch's concept of narcissism as a denial of agency's embeddedness in the world, illustrated with everyday vignettes and loosely connected to shard-theory style framing. It is psychological-philosophical speculation rather than AI research.

entry.title: Contra Pace on When to Apologize

author.name: Zack_M_Davis

entry.summary: A philosophy-of-ethics essay rebutting another author's theory of apologies, arguing that genuine regret implies a policy update rather than merely accepting ex post costs. It is interpersonal-ethics commentary rather than AI research.

entry.title: MIT in the media: For the future of tech, "Massachusetts can absolutely lead"
entry.summary: An MIT News media-recap piece noting that eight MIT affiliates appeared on the Boston Globe's 2026 Tech Power Players list and highlighting MIT's AI research and entrepreneurship leadership in Massachusetts. It is institutional public-relations coverage.

entry.title: War of Dots: CRUSHING my opponents with FACTS and LOGIC

author.name: momom2

entry.summary: A recreational mathematical strategy analysis of the minimalist RTS game War of Dots, covering micro and meso tactics like attack surface and cycling. It applies simple modeling to game mechanics for entertainment.

entry.title: Karlsruhe - LW/ACX Meetup - June 2026

author.name: volis

entry.summary: A local community announcement for a LessWrong/ACX meetup in Karlsruhe in June 2026. It contains logistics and an invitation only.

entry.title: Research Summary: June 18, 2026

author.name: AATF AI News Aggregator

entry.summary:
Today's research is dominated by AI safety, interpretability, and evaluation integrity, alongside notable advances in robotics and RL.

Deception and lie detection drew the most substantive work:

  • "Did you lie?" builds belief-verified model organisms to rigorously evaluate LLM lie detectors, addressing a key methodological pitfall.
  • Rift controls for incorrectness to isolate an internal conflict signature distinguishing deliberate deception from honest errors.
  • STATEWITNESS trains a separate decoder to read hidden states and produce natural-language deception audits.

Evaluation reliability is a recurring theme:

  • Several frontier models are substantially prefill aware, undermining the validity of widely-used prefill-based safety evaluations.
  • SAE Interventions are Unreliable shows suppressed unsafe behavior can be recovered post-intervention, questioning SAE-based safety steering.
  • Vision-language models for chest radiography exposes that medical VLMs often exploit text priors rather than reading images.
  • A Position paper on coding benchmarks argues current scores conflate model, harness, and environment, misaligning with agentic software engineering.

Architecture and learning advances:

  • KV Cache as editable notebook demonstrates causally that cached key/value vectors store memoized conclusions, with practical composability implications.
  • Reversal Q-Learning (Park, Levine) bridges flow matching and off-policy Q-learning via an expanded MDP over refinement steps.
  • Do as I Do retargets monocular human videos to multi-fingered robot hands, scaling dexterous manipulation data.
  • Nothing from Something probes whether LLMs can discover the concept of zero, a conceptually deep OOD-generalization case study.
entry.content:
Today's research is dominated by AI safety, interpretability, and evaluation integrity, alongside notable advances in robotics and RL.

Deception and lie detection drew the most substantive work:

  • "Did you lie?" builds belief-verified model organisms to rigorously evaluate LLM lie detectors, addressing a key methodological pitfall.
  • Rift controls for incorrectness to isolate an internal conflict signature distinguishing deliberate deception from honest errors.
  • STATEWITNESS trains a separate decoder to read hidden states and produce natural-language deception audits.

Evaluation reliability is a recurring theme:

  • Several frontier models are substantially prefill aware, undermining the validity of widely-used prefill-based safety evaluations.
  • SAE Interventions are Unreliable shows suppressed unsafe behavior can be recovered post-intervention, questioning SAE-based safety steering.
  • Vision-language models for chest radiography exposes that medical VLMs often exploit text priors rather than reading images.
  • A Position paper on coding benchmarks argues current scores conflate model, harness, and environment, misaligning with agentic software engineering.

Architecture and learning advances:

  • KV Cache as editable notebook demonstrates causally that cached key/value vectors store memoized conclusions, with practical composability implications.
  • Reversal Q-Learning (Park, Levine) bridges flow matching and off-policy Q-learning via an expanded MDP over refinement steps.
  • Do as I Do retargets monocular human videos to multi-fingered robot hands, scaling dexterous manipulation data.
  • Nothing from Something probes whether LLMs can discover the concept of zero, a conceptually deep OOD-generalization case study.

entry.title: “Did you lie?” Evaluating Lie Detectors across Model Scale and Belief-Verified Model Organisms

author.name: Alan Cooney

entry.summary: Evaluates LLM lie detectors by building belief-verified model organisms that demonstrably hold a belief contrary to what they state, plus a prompted-lying testbed. Finds that activation- and logprob-based detectors scale positively when lying is prompted but drop sharply when lying is trained in, casting doubt on current detectors' reliability.

entry.title: Rift: A Conflict Signature for Deception in Language Models

author.name: Petr Nyoma

entry.summary: Rift investigates whether deception leaves an internal signature in LLMs by contrasting a sleeper agent that lies on trigger against a naive liar producing identical wrong answers. It finds deceptive passes carry a conflict signature with higher residual rank, enabling lie identification with 100% accuracy and no labels.

entry.title: SAE Interventions are Unreliable: Post-Intervention Recovery of Suppressed Behavior

author.name: Mingyue Cui, Linghui Shen, Xingyi Yang

entry.summary: Shows that interventions on sparse autoencoder features intended to suppress unsafe model behavior are unreliable, because the behavior can be recovered via residual-space optimization even after clamping. This challenges latent-space safety defenses that assume SAE features are actionable handles for control.

entry.title: Do as I Do: Dexterous Manipulation Data from Everyday Human Videos

author.name: Bhawna Paliwal, Haritheja Etukuru, William Liang, Pieter Abbeel, Nur Muhammad Mahi Shafiullah, Jitendra Malik

entry.summary: DO AS I DO reconstructs and retargets monocular RGB human videos to multi-fingered dexterous robot hands, recovering hand-object interactions from in-the-wild egocentric and exocentric sources. It aims to unlock abundant RGB-only human video as scalable dexterous manipulation data.

entry.title: Models Take Notes at Prefill: KV Cache Can Be Editable and Composable

author.name: Bojie Li

entry.summary: This work shows that an LLM's KV cache acts like a notebook of memoized conclusions, where a field's own key/value vectors drive under 1% of downstream decisions. This enables editable and composable caches, allowing field corrections via chain-of-thought at roughly 1% compute.

entry.title: Decoding Hidden Deception in Reasoning LLMs: Activation Explainers for Deception Auditing

author.name: Kexin Chen, Yi Liu, Haonan Zhang, Yanhui Li, Xinyu Deng, Dongxia Wang

entry.summary: STATEWITNESS is an activation explainer for deception auditing that uses a separate decoder to read a target model's hidden states and produce natural-language reports about suspicious behavior. It reaches 0.916 mean AUROC across seven deception datasets, outperforming black-box and probe baselines.

entry.title: Reversal Q-Learning

author.name: Aditya Oberai, Seohong Park, Sergey Levine

entry.summary: Reversal Q-Learning is an off-policy RL algorithm that trains a flow policy on prior data using an expanded MDP treating flow refinement steps as actions, generating virtual on-policy trajectories by reversing flows. It applies bias-and-variance reduction to mitigate the curse of horizon.

entry.title: Self-CTRL: Self-Consistency Training with Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Itamar Pres, Laura Ruis, Melat Ghebreselassie, Belinda Z. Li, Jacob Andreas

entry.summary: Self-CTRL trains language models so their self-explanations and actual behavior remain consistent, by reinforcement learning that updates either explanations or behavior. Tested on probabilistic reasoning tasks, it improves the correlation between self-reported and measured biases, supporting auditability and trust.

entry.title: EDoF-NeRF: extended depth-of-field neural radiance fields using a coded aperture camera

author.name: Yoshiyuki Shirasaki, Ryoichi Horisaki

entry.summary: SC3-Eval adapts a pretrained video foundation model into an accurate robot policy evaluator by enforcing forward-inverse dynamics, multi-view, and out-of-distribution consistency. It offers a scalable alternative to expensive real-world policy evaluation.

entry.title: Several frontier models are substantially prefill aware

author.name: yeedrag

entry.summary: Extends UK AISI work on prefill awareness, showing several frontier models can distinguish tampered assistant-side content from genuine content even under conservative elicitation and in low-stakes settings. This matters because prefill-based methods underpin many safety evaluations (jailbreaking, persona, introspection), and awareness could confound pre-deployment safety claims.

entry.title: Pulling The REINS: Training-Free Safety Alignment of Video Diffusion Models via Representation Steering

author.name: Rohit Kundu, Arindam Dutta, Sarosij Bose, Athula Balachandran, Amit K. Roy-Chowdhury

entry.summary: REINS is a training-free safety alignment method for video diffusion models that steers internal representations toward safe generation at inference time. It finds safety-relevant structure is linearly encoded and that a single PCA-derived direction separates safe from unsafe content.

entry.title: Statistical Foundations of LLM-based A/B Testing: A Surrogacy Framework for Human Causal Inference

author.name: Joel Persson, M{\aa}rten Schultzberg, Sebastian Ankargren

entry.summary: Develops a statistical framework adapting surrogate endpoint theory to determine when LLM-based A/B test results recover human treatment effects. It shows that calibrating LLM outcomes to human outcomes identifies average treatment effects under conditions weaker than distributional equivalence.

entry.title: Position: Coding Benchmarks Are Misaligned with Agentic Software Engineering

author.name: Maria I. Gorinova, Macey Baker, Amy Heineike, Maksim Shaposhnikov, Rob Willoughby, Dru Knox

entry.summary: A position paper arguing that current coding benchmarks conflate model, harness, and environment into a single score and are misaligned with how agentic software engineering actually works. Identifies symptoms and calls for component-level evaluation.

entry.title: Looped World Models

author.name: Hongyuan Adam Lu, Z. L. Victor Wei, Qun Zhang, Jinrui Zeng, Bowen Cao, Lingwei Meng, Mocheng Li, Zezhong Wang, Haonan Yin, Naifu Xue, Minyu Chen, Cenyuan Zhang, Zefan Zhang, Hao Wei, Jiawei Zhou, Haoran Xu, Hao Yang, Ronglai Zuo, Tongda Xu, Yonghao Li, Jian Chen, Hebin Wang, Zeyu Gao, Yang Li, Wei Zhao, Qimin Zhong, Siqi Liu, Yumeng Zhang, Leyan Cui, Zhangyu Wang, Wai Lam

entry.summary: Introduces Looped World Models (LoopWM), the first looped architectures for world modeling that iteratively refine latent environment states through a shared transformer block, claiming up to 100x parameter efficiency with adaptive computation depth. Positions iterative latent depth as a new scaling axis for world simulation.

entry.title: ARVO: Atlas of Reproducible Vulnerabilities for Open-Source Software

author.name: Xiang Mei, Jordi Del Castillo, Pulkit Singh Singaria, Haoran Xi, Abdelouahab Benchikh, Tiffany Bao, Ruoyu Wang, Yan Shoshitaishvili, Adam Doup\'e, Hammond Pearce, Brendan Dolan-Gavitt

entry.summary: ARVO introduces a fully reproducible dataset of diverse open-source software vulnerabilities at scale by addressing key obstacles to large-scale bug reproduction. It targets the long-standing trade-off between reproducibility, quantity, and diversity in vulnerability datasets.

entry.title: Catastrophic Forgetting is Low-Rank: A Function-Space Theory for Continual Adaptation

author.name: Ido Nitzan Hidekel, Dan Raviv

entry.summary: Develops a function-space theory in the NTK regime showing catastrophic forgetting is low-rank, concentrating in a few old-task eigenmodes, with a closed-form predictor of the forgetting vector before any new-task gradient step. Offers exact predictions for linear-head PEFT continual learning.

entry.title: Benchmarking Large Vision-Language Models on Fine-Grained Image Tasks: From Evaluation to Diagnosis

author.name: Hong-Tao Yu, Chen-Wei Xie, Yuxin Peng, Serge Belongie, Xiu-Shen Wei

entry.summary: Introduces FG-BMK, a large fine-grained evaluation benchmark for vision-language models with over 1 million questions and 280k images spanning common and specialized domains. It jointly assesses dialogue-level semantic recognition and feature-level visual discriminability.

entry.title: From Brewing to Resolution: Tracing the Internal Lifecycle of Code Reasoning in LLMs

author.name: Siyue Chen, Yifu Guo, Yuquan Lu, Zishan Xu, Jiaye Lin, Jianbo Lin, Siyu Zhang, Cheng Yang, Junxin Li, Yujia Li, Yu Huo, Ruixuan Wang

entry.summary: Studies the internal lifecycle of code reasoning in LLMs, showing models brew answers linearly recoverable many layers before they are decodable, then diverge into four resolution outcomes. Introduces layer-wise probing plus Context-Stripped Decoding across 16 models.

entry.title: An Evaluation of Data Leakage Risks in Tool-Using LLM Agents in Realistic Scenarios

author.name: Hankyul Baek, Jaewon Noh, Sang Seo, Yongsu Kim, Gabriel Waikin Loh Matienzo, Young Il Kim, Ee Wei Seah, Akriti Vij

entry.summary: A joint evaluation by the Singapore and Korea AI Safety Institutes examines data leakage in tool-using LLM agents across 12 realistic non-adversarial tasks. It highlights that sensitive information can leak even during benign use, beyond adversarial prompt injection.

entry.title: The Discrete-Log Clock: How a Transformer Learns Modular Multiplication

author.name: Huu Danh Nguyen (Stanford University)

entry.summary: Shows that the reported dense Fourier spectrum of transformers grokking modular multiplication is an artifact of the wrong basis, and that the multiplicative character transform reveals a sparse spectrum. It mirrors the discrete-log clock mechanism analogous to modular addition.

entry.title: No-Free-Fairness: Fundamental Limits and Trade-offs in Learning Systems

author.name: Khoat Than

entry.summary: Establishes No-Free-Fairness theorems identifying three fundamental sources of disparity in learning systems, including a fairness-cost frontier and statistical impossibility results showing strict fairness may require exponentially many samples. Provides theoretical limits on fairness in ML.

entry.title: LoopCoder-v2: Only Loop Once for Efficient Test-Time Computation Scaling

author.name: Jian Yang, Shawn Guo, Wei Zhang, Tianyu Zheng, Yaxin Du, Haau-Sing Li, Jiajun Wu, Yue Song, Yan Xing, Qingsong Cai, Zelong Huang, Chuan Hao, Ran Tao, Xianglong Liu, Wayne Xin Zhao, Mingjie Tang, Weifeng Lv, Ming Zhou, Bryan Dai

entry.summary: Studies parallel-loop Transformer loop-count selection via a gain-cost view and trains LoopCoder-v2, a family of 7B parallel-loop coders from scratch on 18T tokens. Finds the two-loop variant offers a favorable trade-off for test-time computation scaling.

entry.title: Towards Understanding and Measuring COGNITIVE ATROPHY in LLM Behaviour

author.name: Abeer Badawi, Moyosoreoluwa Olatosi, Negin Baghbanzadeh, Laleh Seyyed-Kalantari, Frank Rudzicz, R. Shayna Rosenbaum, Sara Pishdadian, Elham Dolatabadi

entry.summary: Formalizes cognitive atrophy as a process-level behavioral measure of whether AI mental-health support helps users keep reflecting and deciding for themselves, distinct from safety and helpfulness. Introduces a clinically grounded benchmark built from 1,576 human counseling conversations.

entry.title: A Red-Team Study of Anthropic Fable 5 & Opus 4.8 Models

author.name: Nicola Franco

entry.summary: Red-teams two existing Anthropic frontier models, Fable 5 and Opus 4.8, against four automated jailbreak families across 7,826 harmful intents with multi-judge adjudication. Finds both resist most attacks but remain vulnerable to adaptive iterative attacks, with tree-of-attacks breaking Opus 4.8 on 11.5% of cases.

entry.title: ReproRepo: Scaling Reproducibility Audits with GitHub Repository Issues

author.name: Shanda Li, Qiuhong Anna Wei, Jingwu Tang, Valerie Chen, Nihar B Shah, Tim Dettmers, Yiming Yang, Ameet Talwalkar

entry.summary: Introduces ReproRepo, a scalable reproducibility-evaluation framework that leverages human-raised GitHub issues as naturally occurring supervision on reproduction blockers, instantiated on 1,149 recent ML papers. Shows LLM agents can identify many real reproduction issues even without executing code.

entry.title: From Sparse Features to Trustworthy Proxies: Certifying SAE-Based Interpretability

author.name: Dibyanayan Bandyopadhyay, Asif Ekbal

entry.summary: Develops a post-hoc generalization framework that certifies when an SAE-based explanation faithfully represents a frozen language model, deriving a risk upper bound from four measurable quantities. It offers an operational criterion for explanatory faithfulness of sparse-feature interpretations.

entry.title: Strategic Feature Selection

author.name: Jivat Neet Kaur, Pratik Patil, Divya Shanmugam, Emma Pierson, Michael I. Jordan, Nika Haghtalab, Meena Jagadeesan, Ahmed Alaa, Serena Wang

entry.summary: Initiates a formal study of strategic classification through feature selection, analyzing how excluding manipulable features interacts with ridge regularization when predictors inform high-stakes resource allocation. It models realistic constraints where decision makers adjust coarse levers rather than redesigning the predictor.

entry.title: Beyond Safe Data: Pretraining-Stage Alignment with Regular Safety Reflection

author.name: Jinhan Li, Kexian Tang, Yihan Xu, Zhuorui Ye, Kaifeng Lyu

entry.summary: This paper proposes Safety Reflection Pretraining, which inserts short safety reflections into pretraining corpora to integrate self-monitoring into language modeling itself, going beyond just filtering unsafe data. It argues LLMs can compose benign knowledge into unsafe behaviors, requiring deeper pretraining-stage alignment.

entry.title: CEO-Bench: Can Agents Play the Long Game?

author.name: Haozhe Chen, Karthik Narasimhan, Zhuang Liu

entry.summary: Introduces CEO-Bench, evaluating LLM agents on long-horizon strategic capabilities by simulating operating a startup for 500 days, requiring pricing, marketing, budgeting, and adaptation under uncertainty. Tests skills largely untested in short-horizon agent benchmarks.

entry.title: MolmoMotion: Forecasting Point Trajectories in 3D with Language Instruction

author.name: Jianing Zhang, Chenhao Zheng, Yajun Yang, Max Argus, Rustin Soraki, Winson Han, Taira Anderson, Chun-Liang Li, Shuo Liu, Jiafei Duan, Zhongzheng Ren, Jieyu Zhang, Ranjay Krishna

entry.summary: Introduces MolmoMotion, formalizing goal-conditioned 3D point motion forecasting from visual history, 3D query points, and language goal descriptions, with the MolmoMotion-1M corpus of action-described object-grounded trajectories. Provides a class-agnostic, view-stable motion representation for robotics and planning.

entry.title: Beyond the Current Observation: Evaluating Multimodal Large Language Models in Controllable Non-Markov Games

author.name: Shengyuan Ding, Xilin Wei, Xinyu Fang, Haodong Duan, Dahua Lin, Jiaqi Wang, Yuhang Zang

entry.summary: Introduces RNG-Bench, a controllable non-Markov game benchmark (Matching Pairs and 3D Maze) that isolates multimodal models' ability to reconstruct and act on no-longer-visible observations during multi-step interaction. It separates hidden-state reconstruction from other agent skills.

entry.title: Guava: An Effective and Universal Harness for Embodied Manipulation

author.name: Haowen Liu, Xirui Li, Shaoxiong Yao, Peng Shi, Tianyi Zhou, Jia-Bin Huang, Furong Huang, Jiayuan Mao

entry.summary: Guava is a harness framework for embodied tool use that systematically explores agent workflows, action spaces, and observation spaces to determine what makes language models effective for manipulation. It positions tool-use harnesses as an alternative to end-to-end VLA systems.

entry.title: Using Cognitive Models to Improve Language Model Simulation of Human Persuasion Games

author.name: Zirui Cheng, Zeyu Shen, Thomas L. Griffiths, Peter Henderson

entry.summary: Proposes Equation-to-Behavior Prompting to guide LLMs to match cognitive and economic models of human decision-making, evaluated on persuasion games based on legal decisions. It aims to broaden the diversity of simulated human behavior for safety evaluation.

entry.title: PowerOPD: Stabilizing On-Policy Distillation with Bounded Power Transformation

author.name: Anhao Zhao, Junlong Tong, Yingqi Fan, Ping Nie, Wenjie Li, Xiaoyu Shen

entry.summary: PowerOPD diagnoses training pathologies in on-policy distillation of LLMs traced to the unbounded log-ratio reward, then applies a bounded power transformation to stabilize training. It closes the gap with exact full-vocabulary distillation while preserving compute efficiency.

entry.title: Conservation Laws for Modern Neural Architectures

author.name: Viet-Hoang Tran, Vinh Khanh Bui, Tan Lai Ngoc, Nam Nguyen, Tuan Dam, Tan M. Nguyen

entry.summary: Develops a unified framework characterizing conservation laws (gradient-flow invariants) for modern architectures including GELU/SiLU/SwiGLU networks, multihead attention with sinusoidal and rotary positional encodings, and Mixture-of-Experts. Extends implicit-bias theory beyond linear and ReLU networks.

entry.title: RubricsTree: Scalable and Evolving Open-Ended Evaluation of Personal Health Agents across Health Memory and Medical Skills

author.name: Weizhi Zhang, Zechen Li, Hamid Palangi, Ben Graef, A. Ali Heydari, Simon A. Lee, Salman Rahman, Ray Luo, Zeinab Esmaeilpour, Erik Schenck, Chloe Zhang, Yamin Li, Menglian Zhou, Philip S. Yu, Daniel McDuff, Lindsey Sunden, Mark Malhotra, Shwetak Patel, Ahmed A. Metwally

entry.summary: Introduces RubricsTree, a scalable evaluation framework for personal health agents using an expert-aligned hierarchical taxonomy of over 100 clinically-verifiable Boolean rubrics evolved from 4,000 real user queries. Aims to bridge unscalable physician annotation and inconsistent LLM-as-judge evaluation.

entry.title: Mem-World: Memory-Augmented Action-Conditioned World Models for Persistent Robot Manipulation

author.name: Zirui Zheng, Jiaqian Yu, Xiongfeng Peng, jun shi, Mingyi Li, Chao Zhang, Weiming Li, Dong Wang, Huchuan Lu, Xu Jia

entry.summary: Introduces Mem-World, a memory-augmented multi-view action-conditioned world model that improves persistent manipulation prediction under occlusions and fast wrist-camera motion. It tackles the practical failure of world models forgetting or hallucinating earlier-seen scene details.

entry.title: Visual-OPSD: Cross-Modal On-Policy Self-Distillation for Efficient Unified Multimodal Reasoning

author.name: Pengyu Li, Zhitao Gao, Lingling Zhang, Muye Huang, Yuanming Li, Fangzhi Xu, Jun Liu

entry.summary: Investigates the high cost of generated visual thoughts in unified multimodal models, finding rendered visual thoughts barely affect accuracy while the generation pathway still encodes useful reasoning, then proposes a self-distillation method to cheaply recover that benefit. The diagnostic finding (attention concentrates on visual thoughts regardless of content) is an interesting efficiency insight.

entry.title: Task Allocation and Motion Planning in Dynamic, Cluttered Environments via CBBA and Graphs of Convex Sets

author.name: Matthew D. Osburn, Cameron K. Peterson, John L. Salmon

entry.summary: PAIWorld is a 3D-consistent world foundation model for robotic manipulation that adds explicit inter-view communication and a 3D geometric prior to enforce multi-view consistency. It targets cross-view object drift, depth inconsistency, and texture misalignment in multi-camera robot setups.

entry.title: Pre-Training Isn’t Bitter Enough

author.name: Shuqi Ke

entry.summary: This CMU blog argues that current pre-training doesn't fully embrace the Bitter Lesson because it fixes the self-supervised task-construction rule by hand before training. It proposes 'V-pretraining', which replaces the fixed rule with a feedback-trained task designer while keeping the learner update self-supervised, treating task construction as a learnable control surface.

entry.title: SpeechDx: A Multi-Task Benchmark for Clinical Speech AI

author.name: Sejal Bhalla, Larry Kieu, Aina Merchant, Eyal de Lara, Alex Mariakakis

entry.summary: Presents SpeechDx, a large-scale clinical speech AI benchmark spanning 12 datasets and 27 tasks organized by stages of speech production disruption. It enables cross-condition comparison and generalization assessment in health applications.

entry.title: Agentic Discovery of Non-Canonical Antimicrobial Peptides with AMPGAN v3

author.name: Jay Jung, Xiaohan Zhang, Shenghan Song, Mahmoud Sayedahmed, Chijian Xiang, Yunong Xu, Ahmed AbdelKhalek, Severin T. Schneebeli, Matthew J. Wargo, Jianing Li, Safwan Wshah

entry.summary: AMPGAN v3 is a multi-objective conditional GAN for designing antimicrobial peptides that expands the generative vocabulary to D-amino acids and terminus modifications using dual specialized discriminators. Five candidates were validated in vitro, addressing real-world drug design needs.

entry.title: TerraTransfer: Learning End-to-End Driving Policies Without Expert Demonstrations

author.name: Zikang Xiong, Weixin Li, Zhouchonghao Wu, Akshay Rangesh, Saarth Bonde, Grantland Hall, Chen Tang, Yihan Hu, Wei Zhan

entry.summary: TerraTransfer learns end-to-end driving policies via self-play in vectorized simulators without expert demonstrations, decoupling learning to drive from learning to see. It exploits the asymmetry of cheap rollouts rich in collisions and recoveries that real logs lack.

entry.title: FoundCause: Causal Discovery with Latent Confounders from Observational Data

author.name: Patrick Bl\"obaum, Krishnakumar Balasubramanian, Shiva Prasad Kasiviswanathan

entry.summary: FoundCause is an amortized causal discovery model trained entirely on synthetic structural causal models that maps datasets to causal graphs with latent confounders in a single forward pass. It uses a permutation-invariant transformer with alternating attention over samples and variables.

entry.title: SuCo: Sufficiency-guided Continuous Adaptive Reasoning

author.name: Jiahao Wang, Bingyu Liang, Chenhao Hu, Longhui Zhang, Xuebo Liu, Min zhang, Jing Li, Xuelong Li

entry.summary: Introduces Minimal Sufficient Chain-of-Thought (MSC), the shortest reasoning prefix needed for a correct answer, and SuCo, a two-stage training method to make large reasoning models reason adaptively rather than overthink simple queries. It aims to cut inference cost while improving accuracy across difficulty levels.

entry.title: SoftMoE: Soft Differentiable Routing for Mixture-of-Experts in LLMs

author.name: Miko{\l}aj Zasada, {\L}ukasz Struski, Jacek Tabor, Marcin Kurdziel

entry.summary: Proposes SoftMoE, replacing discrete top-k MoE routing with a differentiable truncated soft top-k relaxation that enables gradient-based optimization of expert allocation under a global budget. Allows the model to learn how many experts to activate per layer.

entry.title: Visual Verification Enables Inference-time Steering and Autonomous Policy Improvement

author.name: Mingtong Zhang, Dhruv Shah

entry.summary: Proposes VERITAS, a generator-verifier framework pairing a pretrained generalist robot policy with a gradient-free visual verifier that evaluates actions at inference time for steering and self-improvement. Shows inference-time verification consistently improves performance without additional training data.

entry.title: SFT Overtraining Predicts Rank Inversion via Entropy Collapse Under RLVR

author.name: Siddharth Aphale, Kelly Liu

entry.summary: Shows that overtraining supervised fine-tuning can compress the rollout distribution and cause rank inversion under RLVR via entropy collapse, so highest pass@1 SFT checkpoints can yield worse GRPO outcomes. It analyzes advantage variance and SFT depth ladders on coding models.

entry.title: Concept Modulation Models: A Unified Framework for Identifiability and Extrapolation

author.name: Soheun Yi, Yizhou Lu, Chandler Squires, Pradeep Ravikumar

entry.summary: Introduces concept modulation models, a unified attribute-indexed class of conditional generative models with an attribute-to-modulator-to-concept-to-observation structure, to analyze identifiability and extrapolation jointly. It generalizes separate analyses across nonlinear ICA, causal representation learning, and perturbation modeling.

entry.title: Stealthy World Model Manipulation via Data Poisoning

author.name: Yibin Hu, Xiaolin Sun, Zizhan Zheng

entry.summary: SWAAP is the first two-stage data poisoning framework for learned world models, first identifying a harmful target dynamics model via bilevel optimization then realizing it through poisoned fine-tuning trajectories. It exposes a training-time attack surface that corrupts downstream planning in model-based agents.

entry.title: Sumi: Open Uniform Diffusion Language Model from Scratch

author.name: Mengyu Ye, Keito Kudo, Wataru Ikeda, Ryosuke Matsuda, Keisuke Sakaguchi, Jun Suzuki

entry.summary: Sumi is the first uniform diffusion language model pretrained from scratch at large parameter and token scale, providing a clean open reference point for studying scaling and generation dynamics. It fills a gap where autoregressive and masked diffusion models exist at scale but uniform diffusion does not.

entry.title: DreamReasoner-8B: Block-Size Curriculum Learning for Diffusion Reasoning Models

author.name: Zirui Wu, Lin Zheng, Jiacheng Ye, Shansan Gong, Xueliang Zhao, Yansong Feng, Wei Bi, Lingpeng Kong

entry.summary: Develops DreamReasoner-8B, an open-source block diffusion reasoning model, and studies how training/inference block sizes affect long chain-of-thought reasoning. Proposes block-size curriculum learning to bridge the granularity gap where large blocks degrade reasoning.

entry.title: Motion-Focused Latent Action Enables Cross-Embodiment VLA Training from Human EgoVideos

author.name: Runze Xu, Yiluo Zhang, Jian Wang, Yu Wang, Jincheng Yu

entry.summary: Proposes a latent-action framework that extracts action priors from unlabeled human egocentric videos to train cross-embodiment Vision-Language-Action models, using a Hybrid Disentangled VQ-VAE to separate motion from background. This matters because action-labeled robot data is scarce while human videos are abundant, offering a scalable route to generalist robot policies.

entry.title: Moebius: 0.2B Lightweight Image Inpainting Framework with 10B-Level Performance

author.name: Kangsheng Duan, Ziyang Xu, Wenyu Liu, Xiaohu Ruan, Xiaoxin Chen, Xinggang Wang

entry.summary: Moebius is a 0.2B-parameter lightweight image inpainting framework that claims performance rivaling 10B-level foundation models via a Local-lambda Mix Interaction block summarizing spatial and global context into linear matrices. It targets practical deployment of inpainting at far lower compute.

entry.title: Recover, Discover, Plan: Learning Skills and Concepts from Robot Failures

author.name: Bowen Li, Mayank Mishra, Y. Isabel Liu, Stone Tao, Nishanth Kumar, Alexander G. Gray, Ruwan Wickramarachchi, Jonathan Francis, Sebastian Scherer, Tom Silver

entry.summary: ReSYNC progressively discovers and refines relational state abstractions (predicates) from failure-recovery experience to support abstract planning, jointly learning skills via RL and concepts. It enables robots not just to recover from failures but to acquire knowledge to avoid them.

entry.title: ROBOSHACKLES: A Safety Dataset for Human-Injury Prevention in Embodied Foundation Models

author.name: Zhuowen Yin, Chongyang Liu, Wenzhang Yang, Renjue Li, Yinxing Xue

entry.summary: ROBOSHACKLES is a safety dataset for human-injury prevention in embodied foundation models, built via a synthetic pipeline (scene understanding, hazard-aware image editing, temporal prompting, video synthesis) since real robot-harm data cannot be ethically collected. It targets the underexplored safety alignment of embodied foundation models.

entry.title: A Geometric Account of Activation Steering through Angle–Norm Decomposition

author.name: Atmyre

entry.summary: Decomposes linear activation steering into an angular component (rotating activations toward a concept direction) and a radial/norm component, arguing these are distinct operations. Finds concept information is primarily angular while the norm reflects a token's effective representational capacity, suggesting steering should use two independent parameters.

entry.title: Reinforcing Dual-Path Reasoning in Spatial Vision Language Models

author.name: Yatai Ji, An-Chieh Cheng, Yang Fu, Yukang Chen, Han Zhang, Zhaojing Yang, Wei Huang, Ka Chun Cheung, Song Han, Vidya Nariyambut Murali, Pavlo Molchanov, Jan Kautz, Simon See, Hongxu Yin, Ping Luo, Sifei Liu

entry.summary: SR-REAL equips spatial VLMs with two complementary reasoning paths via reinforcement learning: language-only step-by-step deduction and detect-then-reason with explicit 3D grounding. It adaptively selects strategies for different spatial query types.

entry.title: Visored: A Controlled-Natural-Language Prover for LLM-Generated Mathematics

author.name: Xiyu Zhai, Xinyi Chen, Yiping Wang, Runlong Zhou, Liao Zhang, Simon S. Du

entry.summary: Visored is a dependent-type-based prover designed around how LLMs and humans write mathematics, with a natural-language-like surface and automation that closes routine steps, re-emitting accepted proofs as checked Lean files. Early experiments show LLMs use it effectively on miniF2F without prover-specific training data.

entry.title: Security and Privacy Prompts in the Wild: What Users Ask LLMs and How LLMs Respond

author.name: Hobin Kim, Xiaoyuan Wu, Omer Akgul, Lujo Bauer, Nicolas Christin

entry.summary: Analyzes 14,727 real-world security and privacy prompts mined from the WildChat dataset of 3.2M conversations, characterizing what users actually ask LLMs about S&P and how models respond. Fills a gap by using genuine user queries rather than expert-authored FAQs.

entry.title: Ternary Mamba: Grouped Quantization-Aware Training of W1.58A16 State Space Models

author.name: Ramprasath Ganesaraja, Sahil Dilip Panse, Swathika N

entry.summary: Introduces Ternary Mamba, applying grouped quantization-aware training with distillation to compress a pretrained Mamba-2 1.3B to ternary weights using just 102M tokens, 1000x fewer than prior from-scratch ternary SSM work. Identifies and addresses a novel zero-ratio collapse instability.

entry.title: TRIDENT: Breaking the Hybrid-Safety-Physics Coupling for Provably Safe Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Zijie Meng, Ziwei Li, Yufei Liu, Zhiyu Li, Jiyuan Liu, Wenhua Nie, Bingcai Wei, Miao Zhang

entry.summary: Introduces TRIDENT, a provably safe multi-agent RL framework that co-designs three components to break a three-way coupling of hybrid actions, hard safety constraints, and physics dynamics. Uses Richardson-Romberg gradient correction, Lyapunov-constrained trust regions, and a physics-informed residual critic.

entry.title: Native Active Perception as Reasoning for Omni-Modal Understanding

author.name: Zhenghao Xing, Ruiyang Xu, Yuxuan Wang, Jinzheng He, Ziyang Ma, Qize Yang, Yunfei Chu, Jin Xu, Junyang Lin, Chi-Wing Fu, Pheng-Ann Heng

entry.summary: Proposes OmniAgent, an omni-modal agent formulating long video understanding as a POMDP-based observe-think-act cycle that selectively distills audio-visual cues into textual memory, decoupling reasoning cost from video duration. Includes agentic supervised fine-tuning for active perception.

entry.title: Could AI tell you where you left your keys?

author.name: Adam Zewe | MIT News

entry.summary: MIT researchers developed a long-term spatiotemporal memory framework that lets robots rapidly build and recall detailed mental models of large, complex environments and answer plain-language queries (e.g., retrieving an object placed the night before). It reportedly answers queries more accurately than state-of-the-art methods while running in real time on mobile robots.

entry.title: MemTrace: Probing What Final Accuracy Misses in Long-Term Memory

author.name: Xianxuan Long, Zhikai Chen, Shenglai Zeng, Shouren Wang, Kai Guo, Jiliang Tang

entry.summary: Introduces MemTrace, a benchmark measuring long-term memory in LLM agents at the knowledge-point level rather than aggregate question accuracy, probing memory age, question type, and evidence condition. It reveals failure dynamics hidden by standard scoring.

entry.title: Shattering the Autoregressive Curse: Dynamic Epistemic Entropy Orchestrated Erasable Reinforcement Learning for LLMs

author.name: Ziliang Wang, Kang An, Faqiang Qian, Jialu Cai, Cijun Ouyang, Yuhang Wang, Qibing Ren, Yichao Wu

entry.summary: Proposes E3RL, an erasable reinforcement learning method using dynamic epistemic entropy to counter the autoregressive curse where early reasoning errors cascade irreversibly. It grounds correction in endogenous local signals without external supervision.

entry.title: MODE: Modality-Decomposed Expert-Level Mixed-Precision Quantization for MoE Multimodal LLMs

author.name: Yuanteng Chen, Peisong Wang, Zhilei Liu, Nanxin Zeng, Yuantian Shao, Shiqiang Lang, Tao Liu, Chuangyi Li, Qinghao Hu, Gang Li, Jing Liu, Jian Cheng

entry.summary: MODE introduces modality-decomposed expert-level mixed-precision quantization for MoE multimodal LLMs, correcting two biases in expert importance caused by vision token dominance. It aims to compress MoE-MLLMs without the degradation seen in standard PTQ approaches.

entry.title: From Democracies to Autocracies: How AI Systems Enable Authoritarianism by Design

author.name: Jeba Sania, Marta Ziosi, Fazl Barez

entry.summary: Maps the lifecycles of six AI systems deployed across political regimes from the US to China to identify technical and operational features that enable authoritarianism. It finds enabling features like centralization of administrative data for law enforcement and political punishment.

entry.title: SoK: AI-Augmented Binary Reversing

author.name: Yujeong Kwon, Yiyue Zhang, Shakhzod Yuldoshkhujaev, Kexin Pei, Dokyung Song, Hyungjoon Koo

entry.summary: Presents the first systematization of knowledge on AI-augmented binary reversing, analyzing 144 papers since 2015 across reversing domains, representations, learning approaches, and evaluation practices. It organizes a fragmented field to guide future research.

entry.title: Offline Preference-Based Trajectory Evaluation

author.name: Fernando Diaz

entry.summary: Proposes preference-based trajectory evaluation for agentic systems that compares trajectories via temporal preferences over progress and time-to-return rather than collapsing to terminal success. It reduces ties from roughly 75% to 35%, improving discriminative power and data efficiency.

entry.title: LiveStarPro: Proactive Streaming Video Understanding with Hierarchical Memory for Long-Horizon Streams

author.name: Zhenyu Yang, Kairui Zhang, Bing Wang, Shengsheng Qian, Changsheng Xu

entry.summary: Presents LiveStarPro, a streaming video assistant for proactive understanding over long-horizon streams, using streaming verification decoding and hierarchical memory to decide when to respond and preserve context. Addresses forgetting and real-time responsiveness in Video-LLMs.

entry.title: AnchorKV: Safety-Aware KV Cache Compression via Soft Penalty with a Refusal Anchor

author.name: Ning Ni, Yingjie Lao

entry.summary: Proposes AnchorKV, a safety-aware KV cache compression method that uses a soft penalty with a refusal anchor to preserve jailbreak resistance under aggressive compression. Addresses safety degradation that prior KV compression methods cause.

entry.title: PearlVLA: Progressive Embodied Action-Plan Refinement in Latent Space

author.name: Bochen Yang, Lianlei Shan

entry.summary: Introduces PearlVLA, a vision-language-action model that moves deliberation into latent space via iterative plan refinement using a frozen latent world model, balancing low-latency control with reasoning. Separates fixed visual grounding from an iterative latent plan branch.

entry.title: When English Isn't the Best Teacher: Source Language Effects in Cross-Lingual In-Context Learning

author.name: Fred Philippy, Siwen Guo, Jacques Klein, Tegawend\'e F. Bissyand\'e

entry.summary: Conducts a broad empirical study of cross-lingual in-context learning across seven tasks, six models, and diverse languages, challenging the assumption that English is the best source language. Analyzes language confusion as a key obstacle for generative cross-lingual ICL.

entry.title: DRIFT: Refining Instruction Data via On-Policy Data Attribution

author.name: Zefan Wang, Lincheng Li, Tianyu Yu, Yuan Yao

entry.summary: Proposes DRIFT, refining instruction-tuning data via on-policy data attribution using influence functions, addressing a proximity gap from off-policy validation targets and a severe bias in standard IF formulations. Aims to elevate the model capability upper bound rather than just preserve performance under budget.

entry.title: Measurement noise limits the advantage of nonlinear models over linear models in biomedical prediction

author.name: Marc-Andre Schulz, Kerstin Ritter

entry.summary: Argues that in biomedical tabular prediction the binding limit is often measurement noise rather than model capacity, mathematically showing additive noise erases fine nonlinear structure faster than broad linear structure. This explains why linear models frequently match flexible models on biomedical data.

entry.title: Beyond Prediction: Tail-Aware Scheduling for LLM Inference

author.name: Yueying Li, Yuanfan Chen, Jiayang Chen, Esha Choukse, Haoran Qiu, G. Edward Suh, Rodrigo Fonseca, Ziv Scully, Udit Gupta

entry.summary: Introduces a distribution-aware, prediction-free LLM inference scheduling framework that uses soft priority boosting from lightweight statistical signals to control tail latency. It argues that prediction-driven SJF/SRPT schedulers are fragile under distribution shift and bursty load.

entry.title: Sparsity Curse: Understanding RLVR Model Parameter Space from Model Merging

author.name: Chenrui Wu, Zexi Li, Jiajun Bu, Jiangchuan Liu, Haishuai Wang

entry.summary: Investigates whether sparse RLVR parameter updates make models more amenable to merging, and surprisingly finds a sparsity curse: sparse updates spread far apart in parameter space forming near-orthogonal vectors that resist effective merging. This challenges the idea of merging RLVR reasoning models training-free.

entry.title: On the Residual Scaling of Looped Transformers: Stability and Transferability

author.name: Shaowen Wang, Bingrui Li, Ge Zhang, Wenhao Huang, Shen Yan, Jian Li

entry.summary: Analyzes residual scaling for looped (weight-tied) Transformers, showing the standard depth scaling is insufficient and that weight sharing requires stronger 1/N scaling, with a factored parameterization separating loop correlation and layer variance. This improves stability and transferability of looped architectures.

entry.title: Learning from Own Solutions: Self-Conditioned Credit Assignment for Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards

author.name: Yingyu Shan, Yuhang Guo, Zihao Cheng, Zeming Liu, Xiangrong Zhu, Xinyi Wang, Jiashu Yao, Wei Lin, Hongru Wang, Heyan Huang

entry.summary: Proposes self-conditioned credit assignment for RLVR where the model conditions on its own correct solutions to derive token-level credit without external teachers, process reward models, or ground-truth answers. This addresses GRPO's uniform credit assignment that under-credits pivotal reasoning steps.

entry.title: Identifying Structural Biases from Causal Mechanism Shifts

author.name: Praharsh Nanavati, Jilles Vreeken, David Kaltenpoth

entry.summary: Shows that structural biases such as hidden confounding and selection bias produce dependent causal mechanism shifts across environments, enabling identification of which variables are unbiased, confounded, or selected. It formalizes an empirically testable criterion based on mutual dependence of mechanism changes.

entry.title: REVES: REvision and VErification--Augmented Training for Test-Time Scaling

author.name: Yuanxin Liu, Ruida Zhou, Xinyan Zhao, Amr Sharaf, Hongzhou Lin, Arijit Biswas, Mohammad Ghavamzadeh, Zhaoran Wang, Mingyi Hong

entry.summary: REVES is a revision-and-verification-augmented two-stage training framework for test-time scaling that alternates between online data augmentation and policy optimization, exploiting near-miss intermediate answers as learning signal. It aligns post-training with multi-step sequential revision inference dynamics.

entry.title: The Wrong Kind of Right: Quantifying and Localizing Misfired Alignment in LLMs

author.name: Naihao Deng, Yiming Feng, Chimaobi Okite, Kaijian Zou, Lu Wang, Rada Mihalcea, Yulong Chen

entry.summary: This paper identifies misfired alignment, where safety-oriented LLM behaviors cause models to reject warranted conclusions explicitly supported by context. It quantifies and localizes this failure mode where alignment overrides explicit evidence, particularly around stereotypes and biases.

entry.title: Learning User Simulators with Turing Rewards

author.name: Yingshan Susan Wang, Cedegao E. Zhang, Linlu Qiu, Zexue He, Pengyuan Li, Alex Pentland, Roger P. Levy, Yoon Kim

entry.summary: Proposes Turing-RL, training user simulator LLMs with a discriminative Turing-test reward where an LLM judge scores how indistinguishable generated responses are from real users. Moves beyond single ground-truth matching for more realistic user simulation.

entry.title: Rethinking Reward Supervision: Rubric-Conditioned Self-Distillation

author.name: Siyi Gu, Jialin Chen, Sophia Zhou, Arman Cohan, Rex Ying

entry.summary: Proposes Rubric-Conditioned Self-Distillation, incorporating structured fine-grained rubrics as feedback for on-policy self-distillation in reasoning model post-training. Aims to overcome noisy CoT distillation and scalar-reward opacity from RLVR.

entry.title: Data-Forcing Distillation: Restoring Diversity and Fidelity in Few-Step Video Generation

author.name: Siyi Chen, Shaowei Liu, Yixuan Jia, Zian Wang, Huan Ling, Qing Qu, Jun Gao

entry.summary: Proposes Data-Forcing Distillation (DFD), a one-line post-training fix for distribution matching distillation that restores diversity and fidelity lost to reverse-KL objectives in few-step video generation. Uses teacher score discrepancy to guide students toward real-data distribution.

entry.title: Physics-IQ Verified

author.name: Tim R\"adsch, Yuki M Asano, Hilde Kuehne, Stefan Bauer, Priyank Jaini, Robert Geirhos, Carsten T. L\"uth

entry.summary: Systematically audits the Physics-IQ benchmark for evaluating physical understanding of video generative models, exposing confounds and proposing three fixes to prompt and ground-truth quality. Sharpens how physical understanding of VGMs is measured.

entry.title: FlowObject: Flow Steering for Bridging Generative Priors and Reconstruction Fidelity

author.name: Yuchen Rao, Xuqian Ren, Yinyu Nie, Sayan Deb Sarkar, Biao Zhang, Vincent Lepetit, Friedrich Fraundorfer

entry.summary: FlowObject reformulates sparse-view 3D object reconstruction as a training-free guided inverse problem, using dual-space guidance to balance generative flow-matching priors against observed evidence. It addresses synthetic bias where learned priors override real observations.

entry.title: NeuMesh++: Towards Versatile and Efficient Volumetric Editing with Disentangled Neural Mesh-based Implicit Field

author.name: Chong Bao, Yuan Li, Bangbang Yang, Yujun Shen, Hujun Bao, Zhaopeng Cui, Yinda Zhang, Guofeng Zhang

entry.summary: NeuMesh++ encodes a neural radiance field with disentangled geometry, texture, and semantic codes on mesh vertices to enable versatile volumetric editing including geometry editing, texture swapping/painting, and semantic-guided edits. It aims to overcome limited editing functionality in prior neural rendering methods.

entry.title: Reference-Driven Multi-Speaker Audio Scene Generation from In-the-Wild Priors

author.name: Michael Finkelson, Daniel Segal, Eitan Richardson, Shahar Armon, Nani Goldring, Poriya Panet, Nir Zabari, Benjamin Brazowski, Or Patashnik, Yoav HaCohen

entry.summary: ScenA conditions a text-to-audio flow-matching foundation model on multiple reference voices and a free-form scene prompt to generate realistic multi-speaker audio scenes including background noise, room acoustics, and overlapping dialogue. It moves beyond clean speech-only pipelines toward in-the-wild conversational audio.

entry.title: VEGA: Learning Navigation VLAs from In-the-Wild Egocentric Video with Geometric Trajectory Supervision

author.name: Gershom Seneviratne, Yohan Abeysinghe, Jianyu An, Vaibhav Shende, Dinesh Manocha

entry.summary: VEGA trains navigation Vision-Language-Action models from unlabeled in-the-wild egocentric videos by reconstructing local scene geometry and generating obstacle-aware, goal-conditioned trajectories as supervision. It converts passive human walking videos into usable robot navigation data.

entry.title: Admittance-Based Surface Alignment for Human-in-the-Loop Robotic Visual Inspection

author.name: Antara Banerjee, Colin Acton, Xu Chen

entry.summary: DREAM-Chunk is a test-time scaling method that augments action-chunking VLA policies with a lightweight latent world model, sampling candidate chunks and selecting actions whose predicted latent futures best match observed rollouts. It improves robustness of open-loop chunk execution without policy fine-tuning.

entry.title: Scaling Hypothesis #2: Are Humans Just More Over-Parameterized?

author.name: gwern

entry.summary: Gwern's 2024 essay hypothesizes that human brains and LLMs differ via a bias-variance tradeoff: LLMs minimize variance while overparameterized human brains minimize bias through high-learning-rate training on small, highly-filtered data, catapulting to generalizing basins. If true, this suggests a scaling paradigm yielding far better generalization and adversarial robustness.

entry.title: MolmoMotion: Language-guided 3D motion forecasting

author.name: Unknown

entry.summary: Ai2 introduces MolmoMotion, an open language-guided 3D motion forecasting model that predicts how object points will move in the future. It is positioned to strengthen motion prediction for robotics, video generation, and other systems requiring forward reasoning about object dynamics.

entry.title: A Risk Decomposition Framework for Pre-Hoc Fine-Tuning Prediction

author.name: Yuxiang Luo, Chen Wang, Nan Tang

entry.summary: Provides a theoretical risk decomposition framework for pre-hoc fine-tuning performance prediction, separating prediction risk into an intrinsic limit and reducible optimization variance. It proves a necessary lower bound on optimization variance decay and derives a budget-optimal probing principle.

entry.title: Gaussian Mixture Attention: Linear-Time Sequence Mixing via Probabilistic Latent Routing

author.name: Yongchao Huang, Hassan Raza

entry.summary: Introduces Gaussian Mixture Attention (GMA), a linear-time attention-style mixer that routes queries and keys through K learned Gaussian mixture components via responsibility vectors, avoiding the N×N affinity matrix. Targets the long-context scaling bottleneck of standard attention.

entry.title: Quantifying Consistency in LLM Logical Reasoning via Structural Uncertainty

author.name: Baishali Chaudhury, Mengdie Flora Wang, Hyunji Hayley Park, Rahul Ghosh, Sungmin Hong, Jae Oh Woo

entry.summary: Proposes structural uncertainty, a consistency-aware framework that measures the stability of self-preference rankings over sampled reasoning paths rather than just output dispersion. It captures whether models can consistently rank competing reasoning candidates.

entry.title: Dissecting model behavior through agent trajectories

author.name: Gaurav Gupta, Vatshank Chaturvedi, Jun Huan, Anoop Deoras

entry.summary: Formalizes the intent-execution gap between what an agent model intends and what its harness executes, and develops a customizable Simple Strands Agent to study harness-model alignment. It argues harness design is as critical as the model itself.

entry.title: Beyond Domains: Reusing Web Skills via Transferable Interaction Patterns

author.name: Shiqi He, Yue Cui, Feijie Wu, Xinyu Ma, Jiaheng Lu, Yaliang Li, Bolin Ding, Mosharaf Chowdhury

entry.summary: Proposes reusing web agent skills via transferable interaction patterns rather than instruction similarity, improving skill reuse on held-out sites to reduce steps and tokens. It targets latency and cost in web agents on benchmarks like Mind2Web and WebArena.

entry.title: TrustErase: Auditable Instant Machine Unlearning with Passport-Embedded Representations

author.name: Rutger Hendrix, Leonardo G. Russo, Concetto Spampinato, Matteo Pennisi, Giovanni Bellitto

entry.summary: TrustErase is a verifiable, data-free machine unlearning framework using passport-embedded representations as cryptographic keys within parameter-efficient adaptation layers. It enables instant, auditable forgetting of classes or datasets through deactivation without retraining.

entry.title: Visuals Lie, Consistency Speaks: Disentangling Spatial Attention from Reliability in Vision-Language Models

author.name: Logan Mann, Yi Xia, Ajit Saravanan, Ishan Dave, Saadullah Ismail, Shikhar Shiromani, Emily Huang, Ruizhe Li, Kevin Zhu

entry.summary: Challenges the assumption that tight visual attention signals VLM reliability through a cross-family study using structural-attention metrics like cluster counts and spatial entropy. It finds attention structure does not reliably predict trustworthiness, proposing consistency-based signals instead.

entry.title: AUTOGATE: Automated Clock Gating via Toggling-Aware LLM-based RTL Rewriting

author.name: Yiting Wang, Chenhui Deng, Chia-Tung Ho, Yanqing Zhang, Zhuo Feng, Cunxi Yu, Ang Li, Gang Qu, Brucek Khailany

entry.summary: AUTOGATE is an agentic framework for industry-grade RTL power optimization via toggling-aware LLM-based clock gating, using an ML-LLM co-design to bridge waveform analysis and RTL rewriting. It handles long waveform traces and large hierarchical codebases while preserving correctness.

entry.title: MagicSim: A Unified Infrastructure for Executable Embodied Interaction

author.name: Haoran Lu, Songling Liu, Yue Chen, Guo Ye, Mutian Shen, Shuyang Yu, Yu Xiao, Jihai Zhao, Shang Wu, Jianshu Zhang, Xiangtian Gui, Chuye Hong, Yuran Wang, Maojiang Su, Jiayi Wang, Ruihai Wu, Zhaoran Wang, Han Liu

entry.summary: MagicSim is a unified embodied interaction infrastructure built around a deterministic batched runtime and shared MDP, using YAML specifications to construct diverse executable worlds. It enables reproducible, evaluable, and annotatable episodes linking control, skills, and planning.

entry.title: See First, Answer Later: Visual Evidence Pre-Alignment via Sufficiency-Driven RL

author.name: Yilian Liu, Sicong Leng, Guoshun Nan, Junyi Zhu, Jiayu Huang, Minghao Sun, Xuancheng Zhu, Yisong Chen, Zexian Wei, Xiaofeng Tao

entry.summary: VEPA introduces Visual Evidence Pre-Alignment, an intermediate training stage using sufficiency-driven reinforcement learning to strengthen visual grounding in MLLMs before post-training. It addresses weak grounding from coarse caption pretraining that biases models toward salient objects.

entry.title: A Framework for Evaluating Agentic Skills at Scale

author.name: Maksim Shaposhnikov, Nicolas Fortuin, Simon Stipcich, Maria I. Gorinova, Amy Heineike, Rob Willoughby

entry.summary: Proposes a scalable evaluation framework for agent skills (reusable knowledge artifacts that augment LLM agents), letting authors build realistic tasks to assess skill utility, applied at scale to 500 real-world skills generating 1,000 tasks. Fills a gap in measuring individual skill value.

entry.title: Functional Equivalence in Attention: A Comprehensive Study with Applications to Linear Mode Connectivity

author.name: Viet-Hoang Tran, Vinh Khanh Bui, Van-Hoan Trinh, Tan Lai Ngoc, Tan M. Nguyen

entry.summary: Provides a formal study of functional equivalence (parameter symmetries) in Transformers with sinusoidal and rotary positional encodings, showing how these encodings reshape architectural symmetries with applications to linear mode connectivity. Extends symmetry theory to attention models.

entry.title: A Neuro-Symbolic Approach to Strategy Synthesis for Strategic Logics

author.name: Marco Aruta, Vadim Malvone, Aniello Murano, Domenico Parente, Luca Rizzuti

entry.summary: Introduces a neuro-symbolic framework where an LLM proposes candidate strategies for multi-agent strategic logics (e.g., ATL) that are then formally verified by a model checker. The generate-and-certify design preserves formal soundness while navigating large strategy spaces.

entry.title: Volterra Generative Models

author.name: Yusen Jia, Bingyan Han

entry.summary: Introduces Volterra generative models, a continuous-time score-based diffusion framework that injects path-dependent noise via fractional kernels, replacing memoryless Brownian perturbations. Constructs finite-dimensional Markovian lifts and proves error bounds for the non-Markovian dynamics.

entry.title: Learning Fair Pareto-Optimal Policies in Multi-Objective Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Umer Siddique, Peilang Li, Yongcan Cao

entry.summary: Formalizes fair multi-policy multi-objective RL, learning a set of Pareto-optimal policies that ensure fairness via the generalized Gini welfare function across all possible user preferences. Provides theoretical contributions for fairness over preference space.

entry.title: Structural Role Injection in Handlebars-Templated LLM Prompts: Triple-Brace Interpolation, Delimiter Family, and the Limits of HTML Auto-Escaping

author.name: Mohammadreza Rashidi

entry.summary: Analyzes how Handlebars templating (the default in Microsoft Semantic Kernel) silently governs exposure to structural role injection attacks, since HTML escaping neutralizes angle brackets but not square brackets, colons, or Markdown used by ChatML and Llama-3 delimiters. Exposes a prompt-injection security vector in LLM applications.

entry.title: All Smoke, No Alarm: Oracle Signals in Agent-Authored Test Code

author.name: Dipayan Banik, Kowshik Chowdhury, Shazibul Islam Shamim

entry.summary: Empirically studies 86,156 agent-authored test-file patches to determine whether AI-generated tests contain meaningful verification logic (oracle signals) and how this links to merge outcomes and review effort. Shows test-file presence overestimates verification strength.

entry.title: Attribution-Guided and Coverage-Maximized Pruning for Structural MoE Compression

author.name: Yifu Ding, Jiacheng Wang, Ge Yang, Yongcheng Jing, Jinyang Guo, Xianglong Liu, Dacheng Tao

entry.summary: Proposes attribution-guided, coverage-maximized structural pruning for Mixture-of-Experts models, observing that information concentrates in a small subset of channels within experts so channel-level pruning captures redundancy missed by expert-level methods. Achieves finer-grained MoE compression.

entry.title: LLMZero: Discovering Adaptive Training Strategies for RL Post-Training via LLM Agents

author.name: Haoyang Fang, Wei Zhu, Boran Han, Alex Zhang, Zhenyu Pan, Shuo Yang, Shuai Zhang, Jiading Gai, Peng Tang, Cuixiong Hu, Xuan Zhu, Huzefa Rangwala, George Karypis, Bernie Wang

entry.summary: LLMZero uses LLM agents to search over RL post-training trajectories via tree search, diagnosing pathologies and proposing coordinated parameter transitions. It uncovers an empirical pattern where capacity parameters grow monotonically while regularization parameters oscillate.

entry.title: What Does the Weight Norm Control in Grokking? Logit-Scale Mediation under Cross-Entropy

author.name: Truong Xuan Khanh

entry.summary: Investigates what the weight norm actually controls in grokking, showing via clamping experiments that the grokking delay collapses almost entirely onto the effective logit scale under cross-entropy. It finds the norm adds little beyond logit scale and the effect is loss-dependent.

entry.title: BLADE: Scalable Bi-level Adaptive Data Selection for LLM Training

author.name: Jiaxing Wang, Deping Xiang, Jin Xu, Zirui Liu, Zicheng Zhang, Guoqiang Gong, Jun Fang, Chao Liu, Pengzhang Liu, Tongxuan Liu, Ke Zhang, Qixia Jiang
