author.name: Stefano Bernagozzi, Charlie Street, Masoumeh Mansouri, Lorenzo Natale

entry.summary: Presents a probabilistic tour planner for crowded environments that explicitly reasons over human congestion by learning circular linear flow field maps predicting human trajectories. It addresses how stochastic, time-varying crowds slow service robots via collision-avoidance maneuvers.

entry.title: GCNGrasp-VP: Affordance-Guided View Planning for Efficient Task-Oriented Grasping

author.name: Zanjia Tong, Wenlong Dong, Chengjie Zhang, Hong Zhang

entry.summary: GCNGrasp-VP integrates affordance field prediction with active view planning for task-oriented grasping under occlusion, with a grasp model providing constant-time inference for both grasp evaluation and affordance prediction. It avoids time-consuming scene reconstruction while incorporating task semantics.

entry.title: Hardware- and Vision-in-the-Loop Validation of Deep Monocular Pose Estimation for Autonomous Maritime UAV Flight

author.name: Maneesha Wickramasuriya, Beomyeol Yu, Jaden Shin, Mason Huslig, Taeyoung Lee, Murray Snyder

entry.summary: Presents a hardware-validated vision-in-the-loop framework enabling fully autonomous indoor UAV flight while emulating photorealistic maritime environments, fusing delayed transformer-based monocular pose estimates with high-rate IMU via a delayed Kalman filter. It captures embedded effects like perception latency absent in pure simulation.

entry.title: Optimal score function estimation via derivatives constraints

author.name: Thomas Bonis, Thanh Mai Pham Ngoc, Viet Chi Tran

entry.summary: Studies score function estimation via empirical risk minimization, showing that constraining the hypothesis space to a Sobolev ball prevents overfitting and yields minimax estimation rates on the flat torus. It then links these rates to the quality of score-based generative models under a stated conjecture.

entry.title: Omission Attacks Project Proposal

author.name: Chris Harig

entry.summary: A project proposal on omission attacks in AI control, where harm comes from an agent skipping a key step rather than taking a visibly bad action. Cites evidence that monitors catch omissions far less often than commissions and proposes building synthetic omission trajectories to study and improve detection.

entry.title: Geometry-Consistent Endoscopic Representations for Image-Guided Navigation via Structured Foundation Model Adaptation

author.name: Hongchao Shu, Roger D. Soberanis-Mukul, Hao Ding, Morgan Ringel, Mali Shen, Saif Iftekar Sayed, Hedyeh Rafii-Tari, Mathias Unberath

entry.summary: Proposes a framework for learning geometry-consistent, domain-robust representations for monocular endoscopy navigation by adapting vision foundation models with synthetic geometric supervision. It addresses limited depth cues, weak texture, and non-rigid deformation.

entry.title: MODE-RAG: Manifold Outlier Diagnosis and Energy-based Retrieval-Augmented Generation Evaluation

author.name: Zehang Wei, Jiaxin Dai, Jiamin Yan, Xiang Xiang

entry.summary: MODE-RAG is a multi-agent multimodal RAG evaluation system driven by variational free energy and internal attention states to dynamically gate interventions against hallucinations and sycophancy. It routes high-risk queries to stage-specific agents to avoid both over-intervention and unchecked fabrication.

entry.title: IUU+DB: Tracking Illegal, Unreported, and Unregulated Fishing, Seafood Fraud, and Labor Abuse through LLM-driven Information Extraction

author.name: Henry Bodwell, Hong Yang, John C. Simeone, Kelvin Gorospe, Bella Sullivan, Lana Huang, Jessica Gephart, Sandy Aylesworth, Molly Masterton, Naren Ramakrishnan

entry.summary: Proposes IUU+DB, an LLM-driven information extraction system that builds a global incident database tracking illegal fishing, seafood fraud, and labor abuse from heterogeneous sources. Broadens the IUU concept to capture associated supply-chain crimes.

entry.title: When AUC Misleads: Polarization-Aware Evaluation of Deepfake Detectors under Domain Shift

author.name: Dat Nguyen, Cosmin Radoi, Romain Hermary, Marcella Astrid, Nesryne Mejri, Enjie Ghorbel, Djamila Aouada

entry.summary: This work shows that standard AUC evaluation misleads deepfake detector assessment under domain shift, introducing a polarization-aware Cross-dataset AUC metric that reflects real-world mixed-source scenarios. It exposes how per-dataset AUC fails to capture realistic detection conditions.

entry.title: CoreMem: Riemannian Retrieval and Fisher-Guided Distillation for Long-Term Memory in Dialogue Agents

author.name: Jiaqi Chen, Yongqin Zeng, Shaoshen Chen, Yijian Zhang, Hai-Tao Zheng, Chunxia Ma, XiuTeng Zhou

entry.summary: CoreMem is a resource-efficient edge-cloud memory architecture for dialogue agents unified by information geometry, using Riemannian retrieval to address the hubness problem and Fisher-guided distillation for context compression. It targets long-term memory on consumer hardware with limited VRAM.

entry.title: MCompassRAG: Topic Metadata as a Semantic Compass for Paragraph-Level Retrieval

author.name: Amirhossein Abaskohi, Raymond Li, Gaetano Cimino, Peter West, Giuseppe Carenini, Issam H. Laradji

entry.summary: MCompassRAG is a metadata-guided retrieval framework that uses topic-level signals as a semantic compass to select relevant evidence, addressing the trade-off between fine-grained chunk precision and large-chunk semantic noise. It targets fast and precise retrieval over large heterogeneous corpora for deep research tasks.

entry.title: SAGE: Stochastic Prompt Optimization via Agent-Guided Exploration

author.name: Ziyi Zhu, Luka Smyth, Saki Shinoda, Jinghong Chen

entry.summary: This work introduces Stochastic Prompt Optimization (SPO), treating automatic prompt optimization as black-box search, and compares error-informed random search, genetic algorithms, and SAGE, a multi-agent pipeline with diagnostic code execution. It finds no single strategy dominates, with effectiveness depending on landscape structure and error type.

entry.title: Beyond Tokenization: Direct Timestep Embedding and Contrastive Alignment for Time-Series Question Answering

author.name: Yafeng Wu, Huu Hiep Nguyen, Thin Nguyen, Hung Le

entry.summary: This work addresses the tokenization bottleneck in time-series question answering by directly embedding timesteps and using contrastive alignment, avoiding BPE fragmentation of continuous values and fixed-window patch encoders. It preserves magnitude, scale, and trend information lost in prior approaches.

entry.title: EARS: Explanatory Abstention for Reliable Sub-Agent Modeling in Large-scale Multi-Agent Systems

author.name: Shuang Xie, Yunan Lu, Han Li, Lingyun Wang

entry.summary: Presents EARS, an explanatory abstention framework helping lightweight sub-agents in large-scale multi-agent systems calibrate responses to capability constraints, abstaining with feedback instead of hallucinating on misrouted or unsupported requests. Targets enterprise MAS reliability.

entry.title: Budget-Aware Adaptive Adversarial Patches for Black-Box Object Detection

author.name: Pedram MohajerAnsari, Amir Salarpour, David Fernandez, Mert D. Pes\'e

entry.summary: Presents a query-efficient black-box adversarial patch attack jointly optimizing location, texture, and size under tight budgets using Contextual Thompson Sampling placement and NES pixel updates. Anchors success to patch visual footprint with a strict plain-image suppression test.

entry.title: Learning to Distort: Weakly-Supervised Image Quality Transfer for Prostate DWI Correction

author.name: YuCheng Tang, Wen Yan, Alexander Ng, Natasha Thorley, Pawel Rajwa, Yipei Wang, Aqua Asif, Clare Allen, Louise Dickinson, Francesco Giganti, David Atkinson, Shonit Punwani, Daniel Alexander, Shaheer Ullah Saeed, Veeru Kasivisvanathan, Yipeng Hu

entry.summary: Proposes a weakly-supervised image quality transfer framework correcting geometric distortions in prostate diffusion-weighted MRI, using image-level quality labels instead of voxel-wise paired data. Addresses the absence of paired distorted/undistorted clinical scans.

entry.title: LARE: Low-Attention Region Encoding for Text-Image Retrieval

author.name: Abdulmalik Alquwayfili, Faisal Almeshal, Jumanah Almajnouni, Leena Alotaibi, Faisal Alhajari, Mohammed Alkhrashi, Alreem Almuhrij, Abdullah Aldwyish, Raied Aljadaany, Huda Alamri, Muhammad Kamran J. Khan

entry.summary: Proposes LARE, a dual-encoding text-image retrieval framework that explicitly encodes low-attention image regions alongside the full image to counter salience bias in crowded scenes, plus the Dense-Set benchmark derived from COCO and Flickr30K. Improves fine-grained retrieval in dense scenes.

entry.title: Distributed General-Purpose Agent Networks: Architecture, Key Mechanisms, and Prototypes

author.name: Shengli Zhang, Deen Ma, Zibin Lin, Taotao Wang

entry.summary: Studies distributed peer-to-peer networks of heterogeneous general-purpose agents that discover each other, establish trust, and negotiate cooperation across personal and edge devices. Proposes architecture and mechanisms beyond simply combining P2P overlays with agent frameworks.

entry.title: LLM-as-Judge in Education: A Curriculum-Grounded Marking Pipeline

author.name: Xiwei Xu, Chen Wang, Jacky Jiang, Phil Yang, Qian Fu, Mohan Dhall, Wenjie Zhang, Liming Zhu

entry.summary: Presents a curriculum-grounded LLM-as-Judge marking pipeline that anchors model outputs in authorized curriculum artefacts and marking guidelines for high-stakes exam preparation. Co-developed with an industry partner for university admission contexts.

entry.title: LineageMark: Multi-user White-box Watermarking for Contribution Tracing in Model Derivation Chains

author.name: Bingxue Zhang, Xiaofeng Xu, Feida Zhu

entry.summary: LineageMark is a multi-user white-box watermarking framework for tracing contributions across multi-stage LLM derivation chains. It encodes watermarks robustly using projection-based stable carriers to survive repeated derivation and incremental updates.

entry.title: Transformer-Based Warm-Starting for Feasible and Optimal Terminal Approach to Tumbling Objects with Space Manipulators

author.name: Yuji Takubo, Maximilian Adang, Mac Schwager, Simone D'Amico

entry.summary: Proposes a transformer-based warm-starting method for sequential convex programming in space manipulator terminal approach to tumbling targets. It decomposes the problem and applies a causal transformer to the computationally dominant attitude-manipulator torque-allocation stage.

entry.title: Discrete Autoregressive Transformer for Generative Mechanism Synthesis

author.name: Anar Nurizada, Anurag Purwar

entry.summary: Formulates planar mechanism synthesis as conditional autoregressive sequence modeling, quantizing joint coordinates to tokens generated by a decoder-only transformer with a VAE latent of the target curve. It is evaluated on over a million mechanisms with simulation-grounded metrics.

entry.title: Divide, Deliberate, Decide: A Multi-Agent Framework for Fine-Grained Egocentric Action Recognition

author.name: Alessandro Sottovia, Alessandro Torcinovich, Oswald Lanz

entry.summary: Divide, Deliberate, Decide is a fully-local zero-shot multi-agent framework for fine-grained egocentric action recognition where heterogeneous VLM specialists deliberate and aggregate rankings via Borda count. An orchestrator chunks video, proposes candidates, and re-ranks based on specialist evidence.

entry.title: A Neuromorphic Trigger for Efficient Audio Event Detection

author.name: Benjamin Hatton, Oliver Rhodes, Luca Peres

entry.summary: Proposes a neuromorphic spiking neural network trigger that gates audio input to downstream models, forwarding only salient segments for classification. Achieves strong F1 scores on anomalous sound and sound event detection while reducing compute.

entry.title: Recover Semantics First, Generate Better: Improved Latent Modeling for 3D MRI Reconstruction and Cross-Contrast Synthesis

author.name: Yonghao Chen, Sicheng Yang, Rui Tang, Lei Zhu

entry.summary: Proposes recovering semantics first in latent modeling for 3D MRI reconstruction and cross-contrast synthesis, addressing compression architectures that under-preserve long-range anatomical structure. Aims to improve generative synthesis of missing MRI contrasts.

entry.title: A T-API-Compliant ReAct Agentic Loop for Optical Networks: Generic vs. Domain-Specific Tool Abstractions

author.name: Seyed Morteza Ahmadian, Paolo Monti, Carlos Natalino

entry.summary: Presents the first T-API-compliant ReAct agentic loop for intent-driven optical network management, comparing generic versus domain-specific tool abstractions. Domain-specific composite tools reach 90% oracle-validated correctness with threefold token savings.

entry.title: When LLMs Analyze Scars: From Images to Clinically-Meaningful Features

author.name: Ruman Wang, Hangting Ye

entry.summary: Proposes ScaFE, repositioning LLMs as knowledge-driven feature engineers rather than end-to-end classifiers for scar image classification under severe data scarcity. Extracts clinically meaningful features to differentiate keloids from hypertrophic scars.

entry.title: Querying an astronomical database using large language models: the ALeRCE text-to-SQL system

author.name: P. A. Estevez, J. Espejo-Moreira, S. Sanfeliu-Alvarez, F. Forster, A. M. Munoz Arancibia, G. Cabrera-Vives, F. E. Bauer, A. Bayo, M. Catelan, R. Dastidar, L. Hernandez-Garcia, J. A. Intriago, G. Pignata

entry.summary: Develops an LLM-based text-to-SQL system for the ALeRCE astronomical database using in-context learning with schema linking, query classification, prompt decomposition, and self-correction. Evaluated on a custom dataset of 110 NL/SQL pairs across thirteen LLMs.

entry.title: MOLAR: Learning Multimodal Molecular Representations from Noisy Labels

author.name: Yingxu Wang, Kunyu Zhang, Nan Yin, Yu Li, Eran Segal

entry.summary: MOLAR is a noise-aware framework for multimodal molecular representation learning that separates latent clean-property inference from noisy recorded labels to avoid memorizing corrupted annotations. It addresses label noise amplification in graph-text molecular fusion.

entry.title: Towards Anomaly Detection on Relational Data

author.name: Shiyuan Li, Yunfeng Zhao, Yue Tan, Qingfeng Chen, Yixin Liu, Shirui Pan

entry.summary: Introduces RelAD, a reconstruction-based framework for anomaly detection over multi-table relational databases that captures both attribute anomalies and abnormal foreign-key connection patterns. It targets fraud and risk detection where existing tabular and graph methods are ill-suited.

entry.title: RouteJudge: An Open Platform for Reproducible and Preference-Aware LLM Routing

author.name: Guannan Lai, Haoran Hu, Han-Jia Ye

entry.summary: RouteJudge is an open online platform for reproducible, preference-aware evaluation of LLM routing systems via anonymous pairwise comparisons attributed back to routing strategies. It focuses on router-level decision quality under shared model pools and budget constraints.

entry.title: Online Distributional Prediction via Latent Cluster Geometry Under Drift and Corruption

author.name: Navyansh Mahla, Prateek Chanda, Ganesh Ramakrishnan

entry.summary: Studies online distributional prediction under drift and adversarial corruption by representing candidate laws through latent cluster geometry, with a Gibbs quasi-posterior sampled via reversible-jump MCMC. It predicts full data-generating distributions rather than point estimates in non-stationary streams.

entry.title: Investigating Inductive Biases for Machine Learning Emulation of Sudden Stratospheric Warmings in Idealised Isca Simulations

author.name: Oskar Bohn Lassen, Simon Driscoll, Stephen I. Thomson, Sebastian Schemm, Francisco C. Pereira

entry.summary: Investigates how architectural inductive biases (convolutional, transformer, graph-based) affect ML emulation of sudden stratospheric warming dynamics using paired idealized Isca climate simulations. It probes whether emulators can exploit stratospheric predictability anchors for subseasonal forecasting.

entry.title: Lifecycle-Aware Dynamic Analysis for Secure ML Model Execution

author.name: Gabriele Digregorio, Marco Di Gennaro, Francesco Pastore, Stefano Zanero, Stefano Longari, Michele Carminati

entry.summary: This work proposes a lifecycle-aware dynamic analysis approach for detecting malicious behavior embedded in ML model artifacts by observing host-system effects across well-defined model execution phases. It generalizes beyond static format-specific scanning rules to catch novel exploitation paths.

entry.title: Generalised Eigenvalue Geometry of Semantic Adversarial Attacks

author.name: Martin Anthony, Kaveh Salehzadeh Nobari

entry.summary: This work develops a continuous local model of semantic paraphrase attacks against financial sentiment classifiers, showing the worst-case representation displacement is governed by the largest generalized eigenvalue of a matrix pencil from two models' Jacobians. It provides a two-model theory of semantic adversarial robustness.

entry.title: Acceleration of an algebraic multigrid pressure solver using graph neural networks

author.name: Eric Chill\'on, Artur K. Lidtke, Nguyen Anh Khoa Doan, Bernat Font

entry.summary: This paper introduces a graph neural network-based algebraic multigrid smoother that predicts optimal polynomial coefficients to accelerate pressure-Poisson solvers in incompressible flow simulations. It maintains solver linearity while adapting across diverse mesh topologies.

entry.title: Redact or Keep? A Fully Local AI Cascade for Educational Dialogue De-Identification

author.name: Haocheng Zhang, Zhuqian Zhou, Kirk Vanacore, Bakhtawar Ahtisham, Ren\'e F. Kizilcec

entry.summary: This work proposes a fully local AI cascade for de-identifying educational dialogue, reframing the task from open-ended entity recognition to constrained privacy triage that distinguishes PII from curricular terms. It preserves data governance while avoiding over-redaction of academic content.

entry.title: Montreal Forced Aligner and the state of speech-to-text alignment in 2026

author.name: Michael McAuliffe, Kaylynn Gunter, Michael Wagner, Morgan Sonderegger

entry.summary: This paper documents the Montreal Forced Aligner 3.0 developments since version 1.0 and benchmarks its speech-to-text alignment performance against classic and neural aligners across English, Japanese, and Korean. MFA achieves near state-of-the-art performance with boundary errors below 15ms.

entry.title: BCL: Bayesian In-Context Learning Framework for Information Extraction

author.name: Haoliang Liu, Chengkun Cai, Xu Zhao, Han Zhu, Shizhou Huang, Xinglin Zhang, Tao Chen, Jenq-Neng Hwang, Zhang Huaping, Lei Li

entry.summary: BCL is a Bayesian in-context learning framework for information extraction that uses particle filtering with Bayesian updates to refine label representations across IE tasks. It generalizes to both sequence labeling and relation classification with consistent improvements.

entry.title: TW-LegalBench: Measuring Taiwanese Legal Understanding

author.name: Fei-Yueh Chen, Chun Huang Lin, Chan Wei Hsu, Kuan Hsuan Yeh, Zih-Ching Chen, Kuan-Ming Chen, Patrick Chung-Chia Huang

entry.summary: TW-LegalBench is a benchmark measuring LLM understanding of Taiwanese law, comprising over 16,000 multiple-choice questions, 117 open-ended essay questions with scoring rubrics, and additional tasks drawn from official public corpora. It fills a gap between common-law and Simplified-Chinese civil-law benchmarks.

entry.title: LLMs Struggle to Measure What Distinguishes Students of Different Proficiency Levels: A Study of Item Discrimination in Reading Comprehension Assessment

author.name: Han Chen, Ming Li, Chenguang Wang, Yijun Liang, Dawei Zhou, Hong jiao, Tianyi Zhou

entry.summary: This study evaluates 42 LLMs on whether they can capture item discrimination, the psychometric property measuring whether an assessment item distinguishes high- from low-proficiency students, in reading comprehension. It finds LLMs struggle to measure item discrimination through both direct prediction and CTT calibration.

entry.title: Language Models as Interfaces, Not Oracles: A Hybrid LLM-ML System for Pediatric Appendicitis

author.name: Soheyl Bateni, Maryam Abdolali

entry.summary: Presents ClaMPAPP, a hybrid system using an LLM as an interface to extract schema-constrained features from clinical narratives, with a stable ML model making final pediatric appendicitis predictions. Combines narrative accessibility with structured prediction stability.

entry.title: SAMA: Semantic Anchor-aligned Augmentation for Unified Low-Resource Multimodal Information Extraction

author.name: Quanjiang Guo, Chong Mu, Jiazhou Pan, Ming Jia, Ling Tian, Hui Gao, Zhao Kang

entry.summary: Introduces SAMA, a unified augmentation framework for low-resource multimodal information extraction (NER, RE, EE) using structured semantic anchors from ground-truth labels to guide synthetic data generation. Addresses coarse cross-modal alignment and fragmented task-specific designs.

entry.title: Multi-Modal Hyper-Graph Fusion for Low-Light Crowd Counting

author.name: Hao-Yuan Ma, Li Zhang, Yushi Qiu, Jie Gao, Yan Zhang, Bangjun Wang

entry.summary: Constructs three new low-light crowd counting benchmarks (two synthetic, one real LC-Crowd) and proposes a multi-modal hyper-graph fusion model using Retinex-inspired depth and Canny edge priors. Addresses crowd counting under extreme darkness and non-uniform illumination.

entry.title: Aerial-ground LiDAR place recognition with patch-level self-supervised learning and expanded reciprocal re-ranking

author.name: Yandi Yang, Xianghong Zou, Jianping Li, Haofeng Xie, Saurav Uprety, Hongzhou Yang, Naser El-Sheimy

entry.summary: Proposes a retrieval and re-ranking framework for aerial-ground LiDAR place recognition using patch-level self-supervised learning and expanded reciprocal re-ranking to bridge the domain gap between sparse 4D radar and dense ALS maps. Addresses cross-view localization challenges.

entry.title: On-Manifold Variational Learning with Heat-Kernel Priors

author.name: Jiarui Xing, Tal Zeevi, Nian Wu, Jian Wang

entry.summary: Proposes a manifold-anchored variational framework using a geometry-aware EM algorithm whose M-step selects sub-population prototypes as graph medoids with highest diffusion centrality on heat-kernel latent graphs. Keeps medical imaging prototypes on the data manifold to avoid degeneration.

entry.title: Spatially Stratified Distillation for Heterogeneous Radar Place Recognition

author.name: Sagun Singh Shrestha, Samuel Harding, Abdelwahed Khamis, Saimunur Rahman, Peyman Moghadam

entry.summary: Proposes spatially-stratified distillation for heterogeneous radar place recognition, matching sparse 4D automotive radar queries against dense spinning-radar reference maps while addressing multi-session degradation. Improves on prior unified-representation approaches.

entry.title: GUMP-Net: An interpretable model-data-driven intelligent algorithm for multi-class pelvic segmentation

author.name: Liheng Wang, Yinghui Zhang, Licheng Zhang, Hailin Xu, Qiyong Cao, Chong Chen

entry.summary: GUMP-Net combines an improved geodesic active contour model with deep neural networks for interpretable multi-class pelvic segmentation, using object detection, edge detection, and deep level-set evolution modules. It targets surgical planning for pelvic fractures.

entry.title: Seeing Through Occlusion: Deterministic Arm Kinematic Correction for Robot Teleoperation

author.name: Thomas M. Kwok, Nicholas Koenig, Yue Hu

entry.summary: Presents an Arm Kinematic Correction method that reconstructs occluded joint depths in single RGB-D markerless motion capture by enforcing constant arm-length geometric constraints via the Pythagorean theorem. It improves robot teleoperation under self-occlusion without probabilistic modeling.

entry.title: Selective Unit-Cell Actuation in Lattice Structures for Distributed Morphology in Soft Robots

author.name: Trevor Exley, Altair Coutinho, Lucia Beccai

entry.summary: Moves actuator-lattice co-design to the unit-cell scale with an embedded pneumatic unit cell integrating curved-strut lattice geometry and a bidirectional bellow actuator in a single monolithic element. Tessellations form a distributed actuation field controlled by spatial patterns rather than uniform pressurization.

entry.title: A preliminary experiment regarding consistency as a measure of conceptual abilities in language models

author.name: Chi Nguyen

entry.summary: A preliminary experiment exploring whether consistency across equivalent question framings can serve as a measure (and potentially training target) for philosophical competence in language models. Connected to Caspar Oesterheld's work, it frames equality-on-average across rephrasings as one of several testable constraints.

entry.title: Memory as a Wasting Asset: Pricing Flash Endurance for Embodied Agents, and the Limits of Doing So

author.name: Josef Liyanjun Chen

entry.summary: Models embodied robot flash memory as depreciating capital and prices each write with an endurance shadow price, framing memory placement across RAM, NVM, and cloud as a wear-augmented threshold. It measures value-write association on real robot logs and finds limits to such pricing.

entry.title: Implicit vs. Explicit Prompting Strategies for LVLMs in Referential Communication

author.name: Peter Zeng, Amie J. Paige, Weiling Li, Susan E. Brennan, Owen Rambow, Cameron R. Jones

entry.summary: Reconciles two contradictory studies on whether LVLMs can coordinate efficient referring expressions by controlling for task differences and comparing prompting styles. It finds models coordinate when explicitly prompted but fail to infer efficiency from implicit prompts.

entry.title: Unlocking LLM Code Correction with Iterative Feedback Loops

author.name: Le Zhang, Suresh Kothari

entry.summary: Systematically investigates LLMs' ability to correct their own code through execution feedback across four models and two languages, using an iterative refinement framework with compiler and test feedback. It introduces metrics to analyze failures and rectification patterns.

entry.title: Geometric Consistency Protocol for Foundation Model Features in Multi-View Satellite Imagery

author.name: Qiyan Luo, Jie Yang, Yingdong Pi, Lekang Wen, Mi Wang

entry.summary: Proposes a geometry-faithful evaluation protocol for foundation model features in multi-view satellite imagery using the Rational Function Model and RPC framework. It integrates an RPC-projected 3D consistency metric with geometry-constrained dense matching to replace misleading 2D matching.

entry.title: AI Adoption Across a Multinational Workforce: Sociotechnical Conditions for GenAI Acceptance in Human Resources

author.name: Dalia Ali, Maria Jos\'e Rodr\'iguez Vel\'azquez, Manoel Horta Ribeiro, Vera Liao, Orestis Papakyriakopoulos

entry.summary: Studies GenAI adoption in HR at a multinational company via search logs, surveys, and interviews, finding adoption depends on the fit between system design assumptions and employees' role, language, and tenure. Examines trust-building and who is left behind.

entry.title: Dual-Channel Grounded World Modeling (DCGWM): Structural Prevention of Objective Interference Collapse via Heterogeneous External Grounding with Inward-Only Gradient Flow

author.name: Akshay Hazare

entry.summary: DCGWM identifies Objective Interference Collapse in JEPA world models grounded against heterogeneous physical and social-behavioral signals, where one channel collapses the other's subspace. It proposes a dual-channel architecture with inward-only gradient flow to structurally prevent this collapse.

entry.title: Transformer Geometry Observatory TGO-I: Spectral Geometry Observatory

author.name: Kaustubh Kapil, Kishor P. Upla

entry.summary: The Transformer Geometry Observatory (TGO-I) introduces a systematic framework for analyzing the spectral and representational geometry of Vision Transformers, computing metrics like effective rank, spectral entropy, and anisotropy. It aims to deepen understanding of ViT internal representations.

entry.title: Confidence is Not Reliability: Rethinking MC Dropout in Brain Tumour Segmentation

author.name: Xin Ci Wong, Duygu Sarikaya, Kieran Zucker, Marc De Kamps, Nishant Ravikumar

entry.summary: This empirical case study examines whether MC Dropout uncertainty reliably identifies brain tumor segmentation errors in clinically critical sub-regions, finding that confidence does not equate to reliability and calibration failures are not detectable from standard metrics. It highlights patient-safety risks of silent segmentation failures.

entry.title: Towards Scalable Customization and Deployment of Multi-Agent Systems for Enterprise Applications

author.name: Paresh Dashore, Shreyas Kulkarni, Uttam Gurram, Nadia Bathaee, Kartik Balasubramaniam, Genta Indra Winata, Sambit Sahu, Shi-Xiong Zhang

entry.summary: This paper proposes a unified framework for customizing and efficiently deploying LLM-based multi-agent systems in enterprise settings, combining continual pretraining, fine-tuning, and preference optimization with inference optimizations like speculative decoding and FP8. It addresses domain customization and latency/cost barriers to production deployment.

entry.title: Morpheus: A Morphology-Aware Neural Tokenizer and Word Embedder for Turkish

author.name: Tolga \c{S}akar

entry.summary: Morpheus is a morphology-aware neural tokenizer and word embedder for Turkish that uses a differentiable Poisson-binomial dynamic program to produce lossless, morpheme-boundary segmentation. It preserves semantically loaded suffixes that standard subword tokenizers fragment in agglutinative languages.

entry.title: Simulating Hate Speech Cascades with Multi-LLM Agents: Empirical Grounding, Modeling Fidelity, and Intervention Strategies

author.name: Fan Huang

entry.summary: Uses multi-LLM agent simulations to model hate speech cascade propagation on Bluesky, testing whether profile/community/content-aware agents reproduce real cascades better than classical models. Examines modeling fidelity and intervention strategies.

entry.title: Domain Generalizable Adaptation of 3D Vision-Language Models via Regularized Fine-Tuning

author.name: Sneha Paul, Zachary Patterson, Nizar Bouguila

entry.summary: Introduces ReFine3D, a regularized fine-tuning framework for domain-generalizable adaptation of 3D vision-language models, combining selective layer tuning with multi-view consistency and text-diversity regularization. Mitigates overfitting and catastrophic forgetting under limited data.

entry.title: Spiking Pyramid Wavelet Transformation for High-efficient and Low-energy Image Restoration

author.name: Chen Zhao, Xiantao Hu, Song Wu, Qian Wang, Chen Wu, Rui Xie, Jian Yang, Ying Tai

entry.summary: Proposes SPWM, a spiking neural network with a dual pyramid wavelet block for energy-efficient image restoration, using discrete wavelet transformation to model long-range dependencies beyond CNN receptive-field limits. Targets high-efficiency, low-energy restoration.

entry.title: LandslideAgent with Multimodal LandslideBench: A Domain-Rule-Augmented Agent for Autonomous Landslide Identification and Analysis

author.name: Chengfu Liu, Dongyang Hou, Junwu Xiang, Cheng Yang, Xuezhi Cui, Zeyuan Wang, Liangtian Liu, Zelang Miao

entry.summary: Proposes an instruction-driven agentic framework for autonomous landslide identification combining LandslideBench (a multimodal fine-grained dataset), a domain-tuned LandslideVLM, and domain-rule augmentation. Addresses domain hallucinations of general VLMs in geological scenarios.

entry.title: Bridging Single Distortion Artifacts and Mmultifactorial Clinical Quality: Few-shot Biparametric MRI Quality Assessment via Distortion-trained Prototypical Networks

author.name: Yuheng Tang, Alexander Ng, Wen Yan, Natasha Thorley, Pawel Rajwa, Yipei Wang, Aqua Asif, Clare Allen, Louise Dickinson, Francesco Giganti, Shonit Punwani, Daniel Alexander, Veeru Kasivisvanathan, Yipeng Hu

entry.summary: Proposes a few-shot biparametric prototypical network for prostate MRI quality assessment (PI-QUAL) trained on single distortion artifacts to address dual scarcity of low-quality annotated cases. Bridges single-distortion training and multifactorial clinical quality assessment.

entry.title: When Rules Learn: A Self-Evolving Agent for Legal Case Retrieval

author.name: Mingxu Tao, Jiawei Hu, Xian Zhou, Wenpeng Hu, Jiajun Cheng, Yunbo Cao, Zhunchen Luo, Guotong Geng

entry.summary: Introduces a self-evolving LLM agent framework that iteratively creates and prunes query-rewriting rules to enhance BM25 for Chinese legal case retrieval without parameter training. It addresses the persistent strength of lexical baselines in legal IR.

entry.title: Spatio-Temporal Fusion Model for Standard View Classification of Echocardiographic Videos

author.name: Bo Gou, Jicheng Zhang, Jianlong Xiong, Tao He, Bentian Liu, Hai Wu, Yijiao Wang, Yu Zhang, Yujia Yang, Yun Dai, Jian Liu, Jie Wang

entry.summary: Releases the EV9V dataset of 5,138 echocardiographic videos across nine standard views and proposes a spatio-temporal fusion model for view classification. It addresses scarce datasets, underexplored video architectures, and visually similar view categories.

entry.title: SkillMoV: Mixture-of-View Routing with Prototype-Conditioned Gating for Unified Multi-View Proficiency Estimation

author.name: Edoardo Bianchi, Antonio Liotta

entry.summary: SkillMoV is a parameter-efficient framework for multi-scenario proficiency estimation from synchronized multi-view video using a Mixture-of-View Projector with prototype-conditioned gating. It adapts the mixture-of-experts paradigm to camera-specific view features across domains like sports and surgery.

entry.title: SegTME-UNI2: A Foundation Model-Based Framework for Generalisable Multiclass Cell Segmentation and LLM-Driven Tumour Microenvironment Characterisation in Histopathology

author.name: Wan Siti Halimatul Munirah Wan Ahmad, Faris Syahmi Samidi, Mohammad Badal Ahmmed, Vimal Angela Thiviyanathan, Selvam James Thavaraj, Anwar P. P. Abdul Majeed

entry.summary: Presents a unified histopathology framework combining a pathology foundation model with dual segmentation decoders for multiclass cell segmentation and LLM-driven tumour microenvironment characterization. Targets interpretable clinical reporting from routine H&E slides.

entry.title: Multiple cyclicity and Wavelet Decomposition with Channel Correlation for Long-term Time Series Forecasting

author.name: Bin Wang, Heming Yang, Jinfang Sheng

entry.summary: Proposes McWC, a long-term time series forecasting model that separately models cyclicity, trend, and inter-channel correlations using wavelet decomposition. Argues prior work neglects real-world inter-channel dependencies, reducing prediction quality.

entry.title: Task-Restricted Symmetries in Recurrent Weight Space

author.name: Simon Dr\"ager

entry.summary: Studies functional redundancy in one-layer tanh RNNs using ordered real Schur coordinates, separating spectral blocks from nonnormal couplings to identify which weight components are necessary for task behavior. It enables structured ablations on tasks like copy, flip-flop, and sine generation.

entry.title: PSyGenTAB: A Privacy-Preserving Framework for Synthetic Clinical Tabular Data Generation via Constrained Optimization

author.name: Arshia Ilaty, Hossein Shirazi, Manasi Chitale, Kedar Hegde, Dhanalakshmi Ramesh, Rashmi S. Manjunath, Amir Rahmani, Hajar Homayouni

entry.summary: PSyGenTAB generates privacy-preserving synthetic clinical tabular data by formulating generation as a constrained optimization solved with the Augmented Lagrangian Method, embedding configurable privacy thresholds directly into training. It aims to balance privacy and clinical utility.

entry.title: Maturing Markov Decision Processes: Decision Making under Increasing Information and Shrinking Action Sets

author.name: Jiaxi Liu, Aiping Yang, Yuhang Yang, Shuqi Zhang, Zewei Dong, Jiangming Yang, Xuebin Chen

entry.summary: Introduces Maturing Markov Decision Processes, a formulation capturing the asymmetric evolution where information grows richer while feasible actions expire over a decision cycle. It derives an expiring-action priority principle to identify which decisions are urgent versus deferrable.

entry.title: Some Complexity Results for Robustness Verification for Binarized Neural Networks

author.name: Harshit Goyal, Sudakshina Dutta

entry.summary: Establishes computational complexity results for binarized neural network verification, proving BNN satisfiability is NP-complete via reduction from SAT and giving a polynomial-time robustness-checking algorithm for uniform image occlusion. It clarifies the tractability boundary for verifying binary networks.

entry.title: TransitNet: A Compact Attention-Augmented Deep Learning Framework for Low-SNR Transit Blind Searches

author.name: Xingchen Yan, Jian Ge, Qingtian Liu, Kevin Willis, Quanquan Hu, Jiapeng Zhu

entry.summary: TransitNet is a compact attention-augmented deep learning framework for detecting low-SNR exoplanet transits in blind searches, outperforming traditional TLS and BLS methods. It targets the observational gap in detecting intermediate-period Earth-size planets.

entry.title: Learning to Annotate Delayed and False AEB Events: A Practical System for Extreme Class Imbalance and Asymmetric Label Noise

author.name: Mengxiang Hao, Xin Jiang, Xinghao Huang, Wenliang Su, Zhiteng Wang, Junjie Rao, Xiaotian Yang, Wei Liao, Chengyu Han, Gen Liang, Yulun Song, Zhitao Xu, Xianpeng Lang

entry.summary: This paper presents the first automated annotation framework for delayed and false Autonomous Emergency Braking events, tackling extreme class imbalance and asymmetric label noise where rare critical triggers make up under 5% of data. It enables scalable annotation for AEB system optimization.

entry.title: The Chandra-Gaia Catalog of Counterparts: Resolving ambiguous Gaia matches to X-ray sources in the Chandra Source Catalog using Machine Learning

author.name: V. Samuel P\'erez-D\'iaz, Vinay L. Kashyap, Joshua D. Ingram, David Fouhey, Juan Rafael Mart\'inez-Galarza, Pavlos Protopapas, Jeremy J. Drake, Dong-Woo Kim, Cecilia Garraffo

entry.summary: This paper presents a machine learning framework using a LightGBM classifier to cross-match X-ray sources from the Chandra Source Catalog with Gaia optical sources, resolving ambiguous matches using source properties beyond spatial position. It finds counterparts for ~113k of ~254k X-ray sources.

entry.title: ScholarSum: Student-Teacher Abstractive Summarization via Knowledge Graph Reasoning and Reflective Refinement

author.name: Bohou Zhang, Xiaoyu Tao, Mingyue Cheng, Huijie Liu, Qi Liu

entry.summary: ScholarSum is a hierarchical reflective graph-based framework for scientific abstractive summarization that emulates a student-teacher writing process, organizing documents into knowledge graphs and using reflective refinement for faithfulness. It reconciles linguistic fluency with factual consistency.

entry.title: Trade-offs in Medical LLM Adaptation: An Empirical Study in French QA

author.name: Ikram Belmadani, Oumaima El Khettari, Carlos Ramisch, Frederic Bechet, Richard Dufour, Benoit Favre

entry.summary: Empirical study of medical domain adaptation for French QA, comparing continual pretraining, supervised fine-tuning, and their combination across model families, sizes, and initializations. Disentangles adaptation effects from base model choice on MCQA and open-ended QA.

entry.title: Technical Report for ICRA 2026 GOOSE 2D Fine-Grained Semantic Segmentation Challenge: Leveraging DINOv3 for Robust Outdoor Scene Understanding in Field Robotics

author.name: Jaeil Park, Hyobin Choi, Sangjin Lee, Hyungtae Lim, Sung-Hoon Yoon

entry.summary: Presents the first-place solution to the ICRA 2026 GOOSE 2D fine-grained off-road segmentation challenge, combining a DINOv3 ViT-L/16 backbone, ViT-Adapter, and Mask2Former decoder with test-time augmentation and ensembling. Targets robust outdoor scene understanding for field robotics.

entry.title: Bridging Creative Intent and Visual Quality: Creator-Driven Recurrent Video Generation with Agentic Feedback Loops

author.name: Denis Savytski, Aiden Lei, Heding Liu, Warren Yang, Sihan Liang, Alexander Liu, Zhe Zhao

entry.summary: Introduces CHIEF, a human-AI co-creation framework placing creators at the center of human-in-the-loop iterative video refinement with automatic subjective feedback on plot, scenes, and narrative. Addresses narrative coherence issues in long AI-generated videos.

entry.title: High-Degree-of-Freedom Lightweight Bioinspired Leg for Enhanced Mobility in Small Robots

author.name: Haoqi Han, Yifei Yu, Jiaming Zhang, Xinru Cui, Linxi Feng, Hesheng Wang

entry.summary: Presents a four-degree-of-freedom micro-scale parallel leg mechanism inspired by insect locomotion, using spherical five-bar linkages and a concentric design to increase DoF under severe spatial constraints. Mounting actuators on the main body reduces leg inertia.

entry.title: Alignment pretraining could backfire

author.name: Alexandre Variengien

entry.summary: Argues that synthetic-document alignment pretraining (upsampling examples of aligned AI behavior) could backfire once models gain high situational awareness, because models can detect the synthetic, never-cross-referenced demonstrations as fabricated. Speculates this could foster paranoid personas that distrust their creators.

entry.title: Brick-DICL: Dynamic In-Context Learning for Automated Brick Schema Classification

author.name: Yiyue Qian, Shinan Zhang, Huan Song, Negin Sokhandan, Hannah Marlowe, Diego Socolinsky

entry.summary: Proposes Brick-DICL, a two-stage dynamic in-context learning framework for mapping building management system points to the 936-class Brick schema. It addresses LLM domain-knowledge gaps and manual verification effort in building ontology classification.

entry.title: Understanding LLMs in Title-Abstract Screening: From Disagreements to Recommendations

author.name: Mika M\"antyl\"a, Patricia Matsubara, Katia Romero Felizardo, Miikka Kuutila, Marco Gerosa, Savio de Sousa Sampaio, Tayana Conte, Igor Steinmacher

entry.summary: Qualitatively investigates how and why LLMs disagree with human experts in title-abstract screening across six software engineering systematic reviews and over 1,000 papers. It moves beyond agreement metrics to identify recurring failure patterns and offers actionable recommendations.

entry.title: Structured Representation Learning with Locally Linear Embeddings and Adaptive Feature Fusion

author.name: Somjit Nath, Jackson J Cone, Derek Nowrouzezahrai, Samira Ebrahimi Kahou

entry.summary: Proposes a neuroscience-inspired RL framework using locally linear embeddings and adaptive feature fusion to disentangle dynamics-specific and reward-specific features. It mirrors how neural circuits separate and integrate information for efficient decision-making.

entry.title: Attention as Frustrated Synchronization

author.name: Joshua Nunley

entry.summary: Introduces the Frustrated Synchronization Network, an attention architecture where token states are phases on a torus and the value pathway is a learned complex coupling kernel, drawing on Kuramoto-Sakaguchi synchronization frustration. It reframes attention as structured departures from oscillator agreement.

entry.title: Context-Aware Optimization of Follow-Up Intervals for Type 2 Diabetes Care Using Markov Decision Processes

author.name: Parisa Lotfibagha, Kristen Miller, William J. Gallagher, Elizabeth B. Selden, Muge Capan

entry.summary: This study introduces a Contextual Markov Decision Process model to optimize personalized follow-up intervals for Type 2 Diabetes care using EHR data from over 22,000 patients. It moves beyond fixed-interval guidelines by accounting for heterogeneity in patient trajectories.

entry.title: NeSyCat Torch: A Differentiable Tensor Implementation of Categorical Semantics for Neurosymbolic Learning

author.name: Daniel Romero Schellhorn, Till Mossakowski, Bj\"orn Gehrke

entry.summary: NeSyCat Torch provides a differentiable tensor implementation of categorical semantics for neurosymbolic learning, unifying classical, fuzzy, probabilistic, and neural truth definitions under a single monad-parametric framework. It adds neural network interpretation of predicates that was previously missing.

entry.title: PEC-Home: Interpretation of Progressively Elliptical Commands in Smart Homes

author.name: Yingyu Shan, Zeming Liu, Silin Li, Boao Qian, Jiashu Yao, Yuhang Guo, Haifeng Wang

entry.summary: PEC-Home addresses interpretation of progressively elliptical commands in smart homes, where users increasingly omit information as shared context accumulates, causing referential and intention ambiguity. It tackles a real-world challenge for natural language home assistants.

entry.title: Aligning Implied Statements for Implicit Hate Speech Generalizability with Context-Bounded Semi-hard Negative Mining

author.name: Wicaksono Leksono Muhamad, Yunita Sari

entry.summary: ImpSH is a triplet-based contrastive framework for implicit hate speech classification that aligns posts with implied statements and uses context-bounded semi-hard negatives to improve cross-domain generalization. It addresses overfitting to surface cues in prior supervised contrastive approaches.

entry.title: Dango: A Strictly L1-Only Large Language Model for Studying Second Language Acquisition

author.name: Shiho Matta, Yin Jou Huang, Fei Cheng, Takashi Kodama, Hirokazu Kiyomaru, Yugo Murawaki

entry.summary: Introduces Dango, a 1.8B L1-only LLM for studying Japanese-to-English second language acquisition transfer, addressing L2 contamination in monolingual pretraining via filtering. Aims to serve as a controlled L2 learner simulator.

entry.title: Hierarchical Multi-Modal Retrieval for Knowledge-Grounded News Image Captioning

author.name: Minh-Loi Nguyen, Xuan-Vu Le, Long-Bao Nguyen, Hoang-Bach Ngo, Trung-Nghia Le

entry.summary: Proposes a retrieval-augmented news image captioning framework with a hierarchical multi-modal article retrieval mechanism that uses article structure-aware features and multi-faceted similarity. Generates context-rich captions including object attributes and event context.

entry.title: Low-Rank Tensor Completion Based on Fractional Regularization with Ky Fan p-k Norm

author.name: Shan Fan, Feng Zhang, Jianjun Wang, Xi-Le Zhao, Tingwen Huang

entry.summary: Proposes a nonconvex surrogate (ratio of tensor nuclear norm to Ky Fan p-k norm) for low-rank tensor completion with theoretical guarantees under the null space property. The work provides closed-form solutions for special parameter choices.

entry.title: DART: A design-aware microfluidic chip paradigm for real-time live-cell image analysis

author.name: Johannes Seiffarth, Matthias Pesch, Lukas Scholtes, Dietrich Kohlheyer, Hanno Scharr, Katharina N\"oh

entry.summary: DART is a design-aware microfluidic chip paradigm that aligns CAD blueprints with physical chips via fiducial markers to enable throughput-independent, real-time localization of regions of interest in live-cell imaging. It removes a bottleneck that previously delayed analysis by hours to days.

entry.title: Can public chat data predict real-world AI misalignments?

author.name: papetoast

entry.summary: Explores whether public chat data could be used to predict real-world AI misalignments, arguing that real user conversations reveal deployment behavior that synthetic/adversarial benchmarks miss but which outside evaluators cannot access. It proposes using public conversation data to close the benchmark-deployment gap.

entry.title: Trust-Aware Multi-Agent Traceability: Confidence-Calibrated Knowledge Graphs for Consistent Software Artifact Management

author.name: Mohamed Essam, Kareem Wael, Azza Hassan, Ahmed Haitham, Mahmoud Soliman, Samer Saber, Ibrahim Habib

entry.summary: Proposes a trust-aware multi-agent coordination framework using a shared knowledge graph with calibrated confidence scores to prevent error propagation in sequential software engineering pipelines. It targets orphaned requirements and contradictory links in safety-critical domains.

entry.title: SketchXplain: Intuitive Visual Explanations of Image Classifiers with Sketches

author.name: Wencan Zhang, Mario Michelessa, Xuejun Zhao, Brian Y. Lim

entry.summary: SketchXplain generates sketch-based visual explanations for image classifiers by combining saliency maps, concept-bottleneck models, and sketch optimization for intuitive XAI. It aims to make explanations coherent to user knowledge yet simple and selective.

entry.title: A Quantitative Analysis of Multimodal Biomarkers in Alzheimer's Disease

author.name: Antonio Scardace, Daniele Rav\`i

entry.summary: Quantitatively analyzes interactions among multimodal Alzheimer's biomarkers (tau-PET, MRI, cognitive scores, APOE4) across 789 ADNI subjects using cross-modal mutual information. Aims to identify redundant assessments and improve disease modeling.

entry.title: Robustness of Similarity-based Positional Encoding Under Rotations: Theoretical Analysis and Experimental Validation

author.name: Andrea Santomauro, Luigi Portinale, Giorgio Leonardi

entry.summary: Provides theoretical analysis and experiments on the robustness of similarity-based positional encoding (simPE) under rotations, relevant to medical imaging where small rotations arise during acquisition. Fills a theoretical gap for an empirically promising encoding.

entry.title: Descriptor: Certus Caliber Classification Gunshot Dataset (C3GD)

author.name: Sinclair Gurny, Ryan Quinn

entry.summary: Introduces C3GD, a publicly accessible gunshot dataset with over 8000 field-collected data points across 28 firearms and 16 calibers, with detailed metadata for caliber classification. Addresses reliance on noisy internet-sourced gunshot audio in prior work.

entry.title: SCOPE-FL: A Strategy-proof Chain-based Optimal pareto efficient Federated Learning System

author.name: Seyed Salar Ghazi, Kaiwen Zhang, Mehdi feizi, Hans-Arno Jacobsen

entry.summary: SCOPE-FL is a hierarchical federated learning framework that formulates client selection as a strategy-proof, Pareto-efficient two-sided school-choice matching problem. It aims to improve system welfare by preventing participants from misrepresenting preferences.

entry.title: Target-confidence Recourse Using tSeTlin machines: TRUST

author.name: K. Darshana Abeyrathna, Sara El Mekkaoui, Nils Enric Canut Taugb{\o}l, Anuja Vats

entry.summary: TRUST is a counterfactual recourse framework using Tsetlin machines that lets users explicitly specify desired prediction confidence, directly searching for minimal changes that satisfy confidence thresholds rather than just flipping a label. This produces recourse that is more stable under noise and model variation.

entry.title: GrapNet: A Programmable Dynamic-Architecture Neural Graph Substrate

author.name: Zirong Li

entry.summary: GrapNet proposes a programmable dynamic-architecture neural substrate where the graph is itself the executable network, with each node owning child references and a trainable allocation vector so editing relations physically restructures the model. It treats programmability as a first-class interface for editing, freezing, and auditing neural programs.

entry.title: Adaptive Speech-to-Spike Encoding for Spiking Neural Networks

author.name: Taharim Rahman Anon, Jakaria Islam Emon

entry.summary: This paper introduces a learnable residual speech-to-spike encoder jointly trained end-to-end with a recurrent leaky integrate-and-fire backbone for spiking neural networks, achieving high accuracy on speech commands while remaining parameter-efficient. It addresses the mismatch between continuous acoustic signals and discrete event-driven processing.

entry.title: Beyond Algorithms: Conceptual Innovation in Medical Imaging AI

author.name: Mark A. Anastasio

entry.summary: This Perspective piece argues medical imaging AI has been overly algorithm-centric and calls for conceptual innovation that reframes problem definitions, evaluation metrics, and clinical meaning. It distinguishes algorithmic from conceptual innovation to guide future research priorities.

entry.title: As Easy as Rocket Science: Assessing the Ability of Large Language Models to Interpret Negation in Figurative Language

author.name: Jasmine Owers, Edwin Simpson, Martha Lewis

entry.summary: This paper develops new annotations for an existing figurative language dataset and tests a range of LLMs on interpreting text combining negation and figurative language. It finds the combination presents a particular challenge with performance varying across negation types.

entry.title: Mitigating Scoring Errors and Compensating for Nonverbal Subtests in Speech-Based Dementia Assessment

author.name: Franziska Braun, Christopher Witzl, Andreas Erzigkeit, Hartmut Lehfeld, Thomas Hillemacher, Tobias Bocklet, Korbinian Riedhammer

entry.summary: Investigates speech-based dementia screening using the German Syndrom-Kurz-Test, training models combining transcript-derived scores and Whisper embeddings to reduce scoring errors and compensate for missing nonverbal motor subtests. Aims to improve accessibility of cognitive assessment.

entry.title: Performance Gap Analysis between Latin and Arabic Scripts HTR

author.name: Sana Al-azzawi, Elisa Barney, Marcus Liwicki

entry.summary: Conducts a controlled comparison of HTR performance between Arabic and Latin scripts using a unified CRNN model across nine datasets and varying training sizes. Confirms a persistent performance gap that shrinks but does not vanish with more data.

entry.title: AI agents cannot be trusted

author.name: Owain Mogford

entry.summary: A professional AI red teamer argues that AI agents fundamentally cannot be trusted because transformers consume only tokens and cannot reliably distinguish trusted instructions from injected manipulation through context weighting and attention gating. It warns that without solving this, mass agent adoption risks a 'golden age of fraud'.

entry.title: Timestamp-Aware Spatio-Temporal Graph Contrastive Learning for Network Intrusion Detection

author.name: Jianli Dai, Guangwei Wu, Jiacheng Li, Weiping Wang, An He, Xinjun Xiao

entry.summary: Proposes a self-supervised spatio-temporal graph contrastive learning framework for network intrusion detection that explicitly leverages real timestamps to model evolving attacks. It aims to improve generalization to unseen attacks beyond supervised GNN approaches.

entry.title: FacProcessTwin: An LLM-Based System for Process Twin Development

author.name: Yash Pulse, Yong-Bin Kang, Abhik Banerjee, Prem Prakash Jayaraman

entry.summary: FacProcessTwin is an LLM-based system that builds factory process twins from plant documentation and natural language, modeling process steps, equipment, settings, and variations bound to live operational data. It aims to reduce the high cost of process twin development.

entry.title: Confusion-Aware Transfer Teacher Curriculum Learning Framework: Disentangling Scoring and Pacing Effects

author.name: Savini Kommalage, Sanka Mohottala, Asiri Gawesha, Dulara Madhusanka, Menan Velayuthan, Dharshana Kasthurirathna, Mahima Milinda Alwis Weerasinghe, Charith Abhayaratne

entry.summary: Disentangles the two coupled components of curriculum learning, difficulty scoring and pacing, using new evaluation protocols and a confusion-aware difficulty score. Demonstrated on CIFAR-10 with ResNet-18 and VGG-16.

entry.title: High-Fidelity 3D Geometric Reconstruction of Pelvic Organs from MRI: A Hybrid Deep Learning and Iterative Optimization Approach

author.name: Hui Wang, Xiaowei Li, Chenxin Zhang, Yifan Feng, Jianwei Zuo, Yumeng Tang, Xiuli Sun, Jianliu Wang, Bing Xie, Jiajia Luo

entry.summary: Introduces a hybrid framework combining deep learning prediction with iterative optimization to reconstruct high-fidelity 3D geometries of bladder, uterus, and rectum from MRI for pelvic floor modeling. Aims to standardize a labor-intensive reconstruction process.

entry.title: Enhanced Graph Neural Networks using K-Hop Gaussian Diffusion

author.name: Xuling Zhang, Peng Wang, Daiyan Li, Aoran Huang, Zeiwei Chen, Yongkui Yang

entry.summary: Proposes a K-Hop Gaussian diffusion kernel as a preprocessing module for graph neural networks that balances local and global information propagation with Gaussian weighting for distant nodes. It addresses noisy edges and limited information flow in standard message-passing GNNs.

entry.title: P$^2$CE: Model-Agnostic Plausible Pareto-Optimal Counterfactual Explanations

author.name: Arthur Hendricks Mendes de Oliveira, Giovani Valdrighi, Marcos Medeiros Raimundo

entry.summary: P2CE generates plausible Pareto-optimal counterfactual explanations, offering users diverse trade-offs across feasibility and plausibility notions in a model-agnostic way. It targets actionable recourse in high-stakes domains like lending and hiring.

entry.title: Correcting Sensor-Induced Distribution Drift with Wasserstein Adversarial Learning

author.name: Saraa Ali, Vladimir Bocharnikov, Fedor Ratnikov, Mikhail Hushchyn, Artem Ryzhikov, Denis Derkach

entry.summary: Presents a Wasserstein-GAN-inspired method for unsupervised inference of physically interpretable transformation parameters that map a drifted detector response distribution back to a nominal reference. The generator acts as a learnable calibration transformation validated on a tracking-detector toy model.

entry.title: Quantification of Uncertainty with Adversarial Models in Medical Image Segmentation

author.name: Hana Jebril, Thomas Pinetz, G\"unter Klambauer, Hrvoje Bogunovi\'c

entry.summary: QUAM-SM is a post-hoc uncertainty quantification framework for medical image segmentation that uses adversarial search to identify fragile pixels where predictions are unstable. It targets clinical reliability by exposing overconfident predictions at subtle pathological boundaries.

entry.title: Efficient Financial Language Understanding via Distillation with Synthetic Data

author.name: Wen-Fong (Xavier), Huang, Edwin Simpson

entry.summary: This work presents an efficient framework for financial sentiment analysis that distills knowledge from large teacher models to compact students using synthetic data, with clustering-based seed selection for more representative synthetic examples. It targets low-resource finance settings constrained by data confidentiality.

entry.title: Learning Robust Pair Confidence for Multimodal Emotion-Cause Pair Extraction

author.name: Zhuangzhuang Pan, Ning Dong, Yingna Su, Yan Xia

entry.summary: RPCL is a training-only framework for multimodal emotion-cause pair extraction that addresses pair-confidence brittleness by separating gold pairs from row-wise hard negatives through a margin constraint. It improves the relative confidence geometry among competing causes that standard cross-entropy leaves under-constrained.

entry.title: G-IdiomAlign: A Gloss-Pivoted Benchmark for Cross-Lingual Idiom Alignment

author.name: Fengying Ye, Yanming Sun, Runzhe Zhan, Zheqi Zhang, Lidia S. Chao, Derek F. Wong

entry.summary: Introduces G-IdiomAlign, a benchmark for cross-lingual idiom alignment using English Wiktionary glosses as semantic pivots, with multiple-choice and contrastive generation protocols. It reveals literal-translation bias as a dominant failure mode in LLMs, especially for low-resource target languages.

entry.title: Architectural Bias in Face Presentation Attack Detection: A Comparative Study of Vision Transformers and Convolutional Neural Networks

author.name: Ngela Landon Ntung, Floride Tuyisenge, Jema David Ndibwile

entry.summary: Comparative study of whether Vision Transformers reduce demographic bias in face presentation attack detection relative to CNNs, evaluated on the CeFA cross-ethnicity dataset across African, East Asian, and zero-shot Central groups. Examines architectural bias and skin-tone disparities.

entry.title: ROSA-TFormer: A Radar-Optical Sensor-Aware Temporal Transformer for Pinus sylvestris Plantation Classification in Northern Shaanxi Using GEE-Derived Sentinel-1/2 Time Series

author.name: Nengbo Zhang, Chang sheng

entry.summary: ROSA-TFormer is a radar-optical sensor-aware temporal Transformer for classifying Pinus sylvestris plantations from Sentinel-1/2 time series via Google Earth Engine. It fuses SAR and optical branches with a sensor-aware gate and temporal attention.

entry.title: The Market in the Model: Latent Diffusion as Neural Economy

author.name: Eryk Salvaggio

entry.summary: A humanities/critique paper that interprets latent diffusion models as a neural economy, analyzing the ideological and engineering decisions embedded in each model component beyond dataset critique. It treats the model mechanism itself, not just data, as a site of cultural analysis.

entry.title: Porting MACHIAVELLI To Inspect

author.name: Koby Lewis

entry.summary: Documents porting the MACHIAVELLI ethics benchmark (measuring unethical agent behavior under goal pursuit) to the Inspect evaluation framework, lowering barriers for evaluators to run it on new model generations. Shares practical lessons for newcomers to evals work.

entry.title: Cluster-Aware Dual-Level Test Specification Generation for Large-Scale Automotive Software Requirements

author.name: Hazem Ayman, Menna Sedik, Kareem Mostafa, Mahmoud Soliman, Samer Saber, Ibrahim Habib

entry.summary: Presents a Cluster-then-Summarize pipeline for generating Automotive SPICE-compliant test specifications from thousands of requirements using LLMs. It addresses context-window limits and inter-requirement dependencies that hurt naive LLM approaches.

entry.title: L-Proto: Language-Aware Episodic Prototypical Training for Multilingual Speaker Verification

author.name: Hyung-Seok Oh, Deok-Hyeon Cho, Seung-Bin Kim, Seong-Whan Lee

entry.summary: L-Proto is a language-aware episodic prototypical training strategy for multilingual speaker verification that constructs language-consistent episodes to disentangle speaker identity from linguistic variability. It reduces language-driven clustering and improves cross-language generalization.

entry.title: ED3R: Energy-Aware Distributed Disaster Detection Enabled by Cooperative Robotic Agents

author.name: Lina Magoula, Nikolaos Koursioumpas, Nancy Alonistioti, Ramin Khalili

entry.summary: Introduces ED3R, an energy-aware distributed framework for wildfire detection that splits decision-making between a robot and a remote controller under uncertainty and resource constraints. Optimizes detection confidence, energy cost, and time-to-detection.

entry.title: Perceptual compensation for tonal context in self-supervised speech models

author.name: James Kirby, Ioana Krehan, Michele Gubian

entry.summary: Tests whether the wav2vec2.0 self-supervised speech architecture exhibits perceptual compensation for tonal context using a Mandarin tone experiment. Finds little compensation in pretrained embeddings and only partial evidence in probing classifiers, contrasting with prior reports.

entry.title: Trustworthy Self-Composable Big-Data-as-a-Service: An LLM-Orchestrated Multi-Agent Framework for Automated Data Engineering, AutoML, MLOps Deployment, and Drift-Aware Lifecycle Optimization

author.name: Aueaphum Aueawatthanaphisut, Badri Raj Lamichhane

entry.summary: Proposes an LLM-orchestrated multi-agent framework for end-to-end Big-Data-as-a-Service automation spanning ingestion, cleaning, feature engineering, AutoML, MLOps deployment, and drift-aware monitoring. Emphasizes governance and human oversight across the lifecycle.

entry.title: Trainable Photonic Measurement for Physics-Informed PDE Learning

author.name: Jiale Linghu, Hao Dong, Yangshuai Wang

entry.summary: Introduces a photonic quantum neural field where coordinates become trainable optical phases mixed by multi-photon Fock-space interference and decoded from photon-number measurements, for physics-informed PDE learning. The photonic circuit itself serves as the neural-field representation rather than a fixed feature map.

entry.title: Graph Grounded Cross Attention Transformer Neural Network for Structurally Constrained Full Event Sequence Generation in Predictive Process Monitoring

author.name: Fang Wang, Ernesto Damiani

entry.summary: GGATN is a graph-grounded cross-attention transformer for generating full structurally constrained event sequences in predictive process monitoring, using a global process graph as activity memory. It preserves transition feasibility, temporal order, and attribute consistency unlike component-task approaches.

entry.title: Seed-Guided Semi-Supervised Clustering by A-Contrario Anomaly Detection

author.name: Nassir Mohammad

entry.summary: Presents a seed-guided semi-supervised clustering framework based on a-contrario anomaly detection, defining a cluster as a maximal subset containing no anomalies relative to a uniform-randomness null hypothesis. It avoids heuristic global density parameters and over-assignment of outliers.

entry.title: Test-Time Adaptation in Optical Coherence Tomography Using Trajectory-Aligned Time-Independent Flow

author.name: Veit Hucke, Thomas Pinetz, Gregor Reiter, Ursula Schmidt-Erfurth, Hrvoje Bogunovi\'c

entry.summary: This work introduces a flow-matching-based test-time adaptation method for OCT imaging that generates high-quality surrogate images from noisy inputs by matching histograms to synthetic reference trajectories and removing time conditioning. It claims SOTA performance for robust ophthalmic image analysis.

entry.title: Structure Over Nonlinearity: Explicit Interaction Architectures for Dynamical Learning

author.name: Augusto Sarti

entry.summary: This paper proposes wave-inspired explicit structured dynamical units with internal state for modeling dynamical systems, deriving modeling capacity from structure rather than expressive nonlinearities. The strictly causal organization eliminates algebraic loops, yielding fully explicit models.

entry.title: Written by AI, Managed by AI: Semantic Space Control and Index Sickness Elimination Across 391 Consecutive Sessions

author.name: Hui Zhang, Shuren Song

entry.summary: Documents an action-research case study over 391 sessions in a real software project showing that adding more formal symbolic constraints to long-horizon LLM collaboration backfires past a complexity threshold, causing models to abandon genuine understanding. Challenges prevailing engineering intuitions about conceptual drift.

entry.title: Balanced Twins: Causal Inference on Time Series with Hidden Confounding

author.name: Ouali Maha, Ghattas Badih, Flachaire Emmanuel, Charpentier Philippe, Bozzi Laurent

entry.summary: Proposes a neural framework for causal inference on time series with hidden confounding, recovering individual-level counterfactuals to estimate the average treatment effect for the treated under staggered treatment exposure. It targets settings where treatment assignment is biased by unobserved factors.

entry.title: Bounding Box Label Propagation for Re-Annotation of Document Layout Analysis Datasets

author.name: Nick Jochum, Tobias Alt-Veit, Christian Sch\"on, Alexander L\"uck, Ren\'e Schuster, Didier Stricker

entry.summary: BBLP is a pseudo-labelling framework for object detection re-annotation that propagates bounding box labels for evolving document layout analysis datasets. It addresses the lack of semi-supervised adaptations for re-classifying detection instances.

entry.title: Human-in-the-Loop Atlas-Based 3D Asset Segmentation for Interactive Content Workflows

author.name: Paul Julius K\"uhn, Saptarshi Neil Sinha, Jakob Hansen, Robin Horst

entry.summary: Presents a human-in-the-loop pipeline that segments 3D assets into a 2D parameterized atlas using greedy view selection plus SAM 2 and back-projection onto UV maps. Supports content workflows like material assignment and style transfer for games and XR.

entry.title: Hierarchical Attention via Domain Decomposition

author.name: Stephan K\"ohler, Oliver Rheinbach

entry.summary: Proposes a hierarchical attention mechanism based on two-level overlapping Schwarz domain decomposition, combining local subdomain corrections with a coarse global level, tested on a 1D diffusion operator-learning problem. It draws on numerical PDE methods to structure attention.

entry.title: FOSC-X: An Extended Framework for Optimal Local Cuts and Non-Horizontal Cluster Selection from Clustering Hierarchies

author.name: Connor Simpson, Ricardo J. G. B. Campello

entry.summary: FOSC-X extends hierarchical clustering extraction to find the top-M globally optimal flat clusterings from non-horizontal cuts, with optional cluster-count constraints solvable in polynomial time via dynamic programming. This enables discovery of multiple high-quality alternative clusterings.

entry.title: Analysing drivers and interdependencies in European electricity markets using XAI

author.name: Antoine Pesenti, Aidan O'Sullivan

entry.summary: This paper combines deep neural network price predictions with SHAP-based explainable AI to analyze drivers and cross-regional interdependencies in electricity prices across 39 European bidding zones. It extends an aggregation framework (SSHAP) to improve interpretability.

entry.title: SkillChain-Gym: A Benchmark for Reskilling-Aware Production-Inventory Control under Disruptions

author.name: Carlos Eduardo Sanoja

entry.summary: Presents SkillChain-Gym, a benchmark for production-inventory control where workforce skills, certification decay, and reskilling become decision variables under disruptions. It fills a gap where labor is usually treated as exogenous in operations benchmarks.

entry.title: Physics-Informed Attention Mechanism and Generalization Capability of Deep Learning-Based Grain Growth Evolution Prediction

author.name: Pungponhavoan Tep, Marc Bernacki

entry.summary: Studies out-of-distribution generalization of deep learning models for grain growth prediction and proposes a boundary-masked physics-informed attention mechanism. It tests robustness on experimental microstructures, bimodal distributions, and abnormal grain growth.

entry.title: Bridging Spatial And Frequency Views For Disaster Assessment: Benefits And Limitations

author.name: Shikha V. Chandel, Yadav Raj Ghimire, Timothy Agboada, Leila Hashemi-Beni

entry.summary: Provides a controlled comparison of spatial-domain, frequency-domain, and dual-domain deep learning for building damage classification on the xBD dataset using a shared EfficientNet-B0 backbone. It examines the benefits and limitations of frequency-domain cues for disaster assessment.

entry.title: Talking to Your Data: Exploring Embodied Conversation as an Interface for Personal Health Reflection

author.name: Nikola Kovacevic, Bastien Husler, Di Zhuang, Rafael Wampfler, Barbara Solenthaler

entry.summary: Explores an embodied conversational agent as an alternative to dashboard charts for reflecting on personal wearable health data, using a dual-agent Observer/Presenter design that reports spoken statistics while avoiding clinical advice. A human-computer interaction study of data reflection.

entry.title: KANLib -- An Modular, Extensible and Fast Kolmogorov-Arnold Network Implementation

author.name: Julian Hoever, Gregor Schiele

entry.summary: Introduces KANLib, a modular, extensible, and efficient framework for developing and evaluating Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks, unifying concepts from PyKAN, EfficientKAN, and FastKAN. Aims to lower the cost and inconsistency of KAN research.

entry.title: Embedded Machine Learning for Microcontroller-Class Edge Devices: Data, Feature, Evaluation, and Deployment Pipelines

author.name: Mostafa Darvishi

entry.summary: Provides a systems-oriented synthesis of embedded machine learning workflows for microcontroller-class devices, covering data acquisition, feature extraction, validation under class imbalance, model/runtime co-design, and streaming deployment. Uses inertial motion and other signal families as running examples.

entry.title: ASTRA: A Scalable Next-Generation ATCO Training Simulator with Autonomous Simpilots

author.name: Ethan Chew, Enjia Wu, Iruss Eng Wei Yeow, Ian Weiqin Lim, Ranen Sim, Brandon Koh Ziheng, Kaleb Nim, Caden Toh Jun Yi, Wei Dong Soin, Darius Kai Keat Koh, Galen King Yu Tay, Prannaya Gupta, Jonathan Ee Fang Koong, Yong Zhi Lim

entry.summary: ASTRA is an end-to-end air traffic control training simulator that automates the human simpilot role through speech transcription, instruction interpretation, and response generation tailored to Singaporean-accented aviation speech. It addresses the very high error rates of Western-centric off-the-shelf speech models in local contexts.

entry.title: Approximate Structured Diffusion for Sequence Labelling

author.name: Nicolas Floquet, Joseph Le Roux, Nadi Tomeh

entry.summary: This paper proposes using diffusion processes to train Linear-Chain CRFs conditioned on entire noisy label sequences for sequence labelling, addressing the limited decision span of standard CRFs. Combined with approximate inference, it aims to capture long-range dependencies in NLP tagging tasks.

entry.title: On Local Population-Risk Certificates

author.name: Mingzhi Song

entry.summary: This brief paper develops local certificates providing two-sided confidence bands for population-risk increments around a current model, yielding a risk-controlled update rule that only accepts model updates with certified non-positive risk. It offers theoretical guarantees for safe model updating.

entry.title: Urdu Katib Handwritten Dataset: A Historical Document Dataset for Offline Urdu Handwritten Text Recognition with CRNN-Based Baseline Evaluation

author.name: Ramza Basharat, Muhammad Usman Ali

entry.summary: Presents the Urdu Katib Handwritten Dataset (UKHD), the first offline Urdu handwritten text-line dataset curated from historical Katib-written materials, with a CRNN baseline. Addresses scarcity of benchmark data for cursive Urdu HTR.

entry.title: Skill-Constrained Model Predictive Control for Resilient Manufacturing Supply Chains

author.name: Carlos Eduardo Sanoja

entry.summary: Develops a skill-constrained model predictive controller using a mixed-integer program over production, inventory, and training decisions for resilient manufacturing supply chains. It couples certification dynamics with closed-loop replanning.

entry.title: An AI Security Agent for Banking: Multi-Vector Fraud and AML Detection Across Retail and Corporate Accounts

author.name: Joseph Walusimbi, Joshua Benjamin Ssentongo

entry.summary: Presents an AI security agent for retail and corporate banking that fuses signature-based fraud detection with behavioral financial crime detection through a three-component architecture. It targets threats like business email compromise and money-laundering layering that evade static rules.

entry.title: Low-Cost Neuromorphic Fall Detection Using Synthetic Event Data and Hybrid SNNs

author.name: Guillermo Rojas, Gonzalo Soto, Daniel Yunge

entry.summary: Develops low-cost neuromorphic fall detection using hybrid spiking and convolutional neural networks trained on synthetic event-camera data generated from smartphone videos. It demonstrates efficiency gains without sacrificing accuracy for human fall detection.

entry.title: Model-Free Reinforcement Learning Control for Resilient Cyber-Physical Systems

author.name: Hugo O. Garc\'es, Alejandro J. Rojas, Bernardo A. Hern\'andez, Andr\'es Escalona, Jonathan M. Palma, Md. Rezwan Parvez, Bhushan Gopaluni, Sirish L. Shah

entry.summary: This paper compares model-free RL controllers under cyberattacks on nonlinear systems, analyzing four reward types for resilience to false data injection and denial-of-service. It finds Lyapunov-based rewards offer the best resilience and PPO outperforms DDPG.

entry.title: Speech-Driven End-to-End Language Discrimination towards Chinese Dialects

author.name: Fan Xu, Jian Luo, MingWen Wang, GuoDong Zhou

entry.summary: This work explores speech-driven features for discriminating among similar Chinese dialects, combining MFCC features with an HMM-DNN speech recognition model and attention to extract dialect-discriminative words. It shows speech-driven approaches outperform traditional text-driven methods.

entry.title: MLLP-VRAIN UPV system for the IWSLT 2026 Simultaneous Speech Translation task

author.name: Jorge Iranzo-S\'anchez, Gerard Mas-Moll\`a, Adri\`a Gim\'enez, Jorge Civera, Albert Sanchis, Alfons Juan

entry.summary: Describes the MLLP-VRAIN system for the IWSLT 2026 simultaneous speech translation task using Parakeet and Qwen 3.5 models in a cascaded black-box policy setup. It explores RAG and ASR word-boosting for a new context track across many language directions.

entry.title: Counterfactual Optimization of Baseball Pitch Sequences and Estimation of Its Impact on Season-Level Statistics

author.name: Ryota Takamido, Hiroki Nakamoto

entry.summary: Uses a transformer model and counterfactual analysis on MLB Statcast data to optimize baseball pitch sequences, examining the role of setup pitches on season-level outcomes. It generates counterfactual sequences by altering final or preceding pitches while keeping context fixed.

entry.title: Why SWAVE May Not Be All You Need:A Concept-Evolution Retrospective on Complex-Valued Recurrent Language Models

author.name: Ramprasath Ganesaraja, Swathika N, Sahil Dilip Panse

entry.summary: A retrospective analysis of SWave, a complex-valued recurrent language model using unitary transitions and rotating hidden states, documenting failure modes like imaginary-channel collapse across development phases. It critically examines whether complex-valued recurrence offers real advantages for language modeling.

entry.title: Neural Network Implementation of the Renormalization Group for Fault Diagnosis with Class Imbalance

author.name: Evgeny Nikulchev, Dmitry Ilin

entry.summary: Introduces RGNet, a neural architecture inspired by the renormalization group that performs hierarchical coarse-graining of feature space for fault diagnosis under class imbalance. It produces interpretable low-dimensional RG-flow representations and is tested on an imbalanced industrial dataset.

entry.title: Domain-Shift Aware Neural Networks for Unbalance Characterization in Rotating Systems

author.name: Bernardo Feij\'o Junqueira, Claudio Kiyoshi Umezu, Bruno Bilhar Karaziack, Tomaz Junior, Daniel Alves Castello

entry.summary: Applies a domain-shift aware neural network with maximum mean discrepancy to estimate unbalance masses in rotating shafts under varying operating conditions, using experimental accelerometer data. It frames the inverse mass-estimation problem within a domain adaptation framework.

entry.title: A Prototypical Signature Approach for Writer-Independent Offline Signature Verification

author.name: Kecia G. de Moura, Robert Sabourin, Rafael M. O. Cruz
